text:
Mert explains why Zcash is one of the best-positioned cryptocurrencies to handle quantum computing threats

“The first reason is because Zcash is very limited in scope”

“It's literally just a store of value. It's not programmable in the same way that an Ethereum is. It just does one thing and it does it really well and so the risk is reduced”

“This is also why I'm against shielded assets in terms of stablecoins on Zcash or something, is because we want to minimize the risk surface”

“This is also the exact reason why Zcash, even like a year and a half to two years ago, we were talking about how it's the best positioned for quantum”

“Having the best cryptographers in crypto sort of has its benefits in that these people are constantly thinking about these theoretical risks”

“It's going to be much easier when you have limited scope and you built the entire network with sort of these edge cases in mind to begin with”

1. 给claude code绑好银行卡；

2. 建一个temp folder临时文件夹，把所有关于任务相关的文档、表格、报表、图表、报告、sqlite、access数据库、pdf扫描件、数据、markdown、代码、图片、资料、指令、prompt、config等等一大堆东西，全放在里面；

这是绝大多数不在大厂、不做核心Agent业务、对AI没信仰、不在AI startup、甚至连他妈代码都写不利索的人，

The demand for portfolio margin is there, but the USDC supply can't match it. The delta between supply and demand is too tight at the moment which means we are seeing these rate spikes more often.

I'm a big believer in the borrow rate needing to be as low as possible for the foreseeable future to help fuel the next leg of @HyperliquidX growth. 

Some possible options;

a) Incentivize USDC supply with HYPE "emissions". USDC supply will come rushing in which means more USDC will be held on-chain which means more buybacks via AQAv2.

b) Give HIP-3/4 deployers the ability to OTC their 500k HYPE requirements from the remaining HYPE supply. They could get a discount for a locking commitment, ie, 3 years locked as a deployer and then the proceeds from the OTC go straight into the USDC earn as protocol owned liquidity.

Both options would help distribute the remaining supply whilst also having a direct impact on the activity of the protocol as a whole rather than just the HYPE/USDC spot order book.

text:
Pre market thoughts 20 Oct 26

Yields about 2bps higher across the session. In Asia trading, KOSPI was hit hard, being down about 4.3% while NKY is down about 1.3%. This is off the back of a rather sanguine US session last night.

Memory stocks like $00660 were hit quite hard, being down 4.8%. $SNDK was also punished in overnight trading while $MU also is weighted down. $MU strikes are also another factor potentially for the weight on the stock.

In US session, some notable moves yesterday was $META fading the entire rip pre market into the open. This may be a sign of nerves ahead of earnings.

Neoclouds as a sector remain ground zero for fear. $CRWV fears are getting amplified, however some savvy shops are fanning the flames and selling CDS on the back of it.  

Overall, what happened on Monday was a mild reversal of Friday's moves with a tech rebound and defensives being punished. However, what we saw on Friday had the look of a cross sector contagion/unwind. These things historically have taken a few days to play out and i anticipate the market to further test those positions.

The july lows for $CRWV have already been broken and i would be looking at the breaks of these lows for $NBIS, $SNDK, $MU and $SOXL.

In crypto, $BTC continues to remain firm vs alts especially. The weakness of the original leaders like $ZEC, $VVV has mostly passed and they now trade in line with their respective betas. Instead, the weakness has migrated towards the shiny new coins that got artificially driven up. 

On $PAPER - some changes are happening. To summarize, there will be a "on hours" and "off hours". During "on hours" with more liquidity, presumably there will be less charge on winnings because it will be much more expensive to manipulate the BBO vs "off hours" that are more illiquid. This atm will only affect positions within 6bps during on hours and 10bps within off hours.

$PAPER minting will also change to minting 0.1% of supply per 1M loss - this is roughly ~ 8.8 PAPER per $1 loss at current supply vs 10 PAPER per $1 loss. However instead of a convergent supply model, now $PAPER will tend towards an expansionary supply model. 

This is obviously BAD for early minters and good for late farmers. Essentially, the meta for farming $PAPER is no longer about prioritising speed. The cost of $PAPER matters far more.

Gambit Terminal now also allows you to trade momentum on Papertrade. (https://t.co/bfHUu64ODR) - You can put stop orders in to take advantage of the momentum effect in crypto and also preset in take profit levels so that you do not have to be on the desk to manually tp or stop out. Stopping out is far more advantageous because getting liquidated has an additional liquidation charge.

Good luck!

观察硅谷这几年的致富之路，对于科技从业者，路径还是很明确

Level-1:  有技术 + 去卖铲子/卖工具，例如LLM数据，Env，公司工具，自媒体工具，求职工具等等，做得好的，营收增长得很快。有些人会选择回购投资人的股份，把这部分完全变成自己的生意。又或者赶紧卖掉，去找更大的机会。我观察最踏实，最可行的一条，自己造血才是王道，做好了也可能上市，mercor/zoom/snowflake/etc

Level-2: 有技术 + 会攒局 + 会hype。创始人都有比较强大的融资，学术或者商业关系，团队人员背景也很好，做的东西能在非常垂直的一个小领域位居世界前列。不去硬做商业，被收购变成大公司的一个部门，是上上之选。

Level-3: 赌未来，搞OpenAI/Anthropic/SpaceX这种究极未来科技，上市拿最大结果。很有意思的是，看创始人背景，基本都是前2种拿到结果了，手里有些积累了，然后来一起拥抱梦想，改变世界吧

而金明第一期的《黄金时代》访谈，跟神鱼聊了 37 分钟，神鱼：好资产不需要持续新叙事，目前仓位只有$BTC、$TSLA、$ETH ......仍然建议大家看看原视频

下面是访谈中提到的几个关键点：

───

• AI 时代的最大杠杆：

神鱼：后端落地成本被 AI 打到了零。人类知识全面被高密度压缩，人的意志和“那个原始冲动”反而成了最稀缺的资产

• 日常信息输入：
神鱼：早就不读一手碎片新闻了。3 个 AI Agent（理性、感性、挑盲区）用进化论机制杂交筛选全网长文，压缩成框架直接喂给我

• 独创“三层仓位管理法”：
神鱼：好资产不需要持续新叙事
① 观察仓（<2%）：发现异常先锋逻辑，花时间彻底吃透；
② 配置仓（<10%）：逻辑印证成立，逐步升仓；
③ 核心仓（~20%）：必须“信仰跃迁”，同时满足巨型 TAM + 绝对垄断 + 强劲增长

• 神鱼目前底仓最核心的 3 个标的：
神鱼：目前只有 $BTC、$TSLA、以太坊（SpaceX 还在观察；以太坊最近在讨论要不要降级）

• 以太坊的反直觉终局：
神鱼：以太坊未来根本不是给人用的，而是给 Agent 机器网络用的！普通人操作门槛太高，AI Agent 才是跑在去中心化网络上的真正用户

• 打破“多元化分散”迷信：
神鱼：市场上根本不存在真正的负相关资产，系统性危机时所有资产都会双杀。我坚决不搞盲目分散，只集中在自己 100% 搞懂的顶级资产上。

text:
Sorry, but regardless of what chain it's on, a so-called "tokenized deposit"  from J.P. Morgan is more of a PR stunt than it is something useful. 

The liability of a fractionally reserved bank must be whitelisted to current bank customers forever. The only thing they can do with it is send it to another bank customer. 

This is called a book transfer, and even the least tech forward bank could offer it with a vanilla ledger. Outsourcing book transfers to an external network that will always have lower capacity and more technical lift is  dubious. At best it's a PR stunt.

JPMD can't be used in DeFi. It can't be atomically swapped for any other asset that is not a direct liability of the same bank. JPM has the right to veto any transaction it is a party to, increasingly settlement risk.

Those who want to forgo this risk and have the freedom to do what they want with their money (without a junior compliance officer getting a veto) will use Genius-regulated stablecoins. 

Regulated stablecoins will always be more safe, less restricted, and more interoperable than a bank deposit.

text:
Today I'm launching CellProof, the first project of its kind from Hasky Labs in Copenhagen.

The problem: hospitals and lab-software companies are training AI to spot abnormal blood cells, including early signs of leukemia. That AI learns from thousands of microscope images. But today, almost nobody can prove those images are real.

AI can now generate blood cell images that look exactly like the real thing. A single changed pixel, a swapped image, or one relabelled cell can quietly teach a medical AI the wrong answer. A 2026 study in the Journal of Medical Internet Research estimates that this kind of data poisoning in healthcare AI often goes unnoticed for 6 to 12 months or more.

CellProof is an antivirus for medical AI training data:

1. Sign: every image and its labels get a cryptographic fingerprint and signature the moment they are captured.
2. Verify: before training, every image is checked against its signature.
3. Catch: anything edited, generated or relabelled is rejected before it reaches the AI.

It builds on the same kind of cryptography as C2PA, the standard camera makers use to prove where a photo came from, and brings it into blood analysis.

Try the live demo with a real blood smear. Change one pixel, paste in a fake cell, or relabel a white blood cell, and watch CellProof catch it:
https://t.co/S5A26m1hmJ

This is an early prototype, and I'm looking for people to build it with:
- people working in hematology, digital pathology or lab software who can tell me where this hurts most
- medical AI teams who want to test it on their own data
- investors interested in trust and safety for healthcare AI

If that's you, or you know someone, send me a message at  hello@cellproof.io

Farming Season is a pixel-art farming simulation game, billed as "the first RWA-driven farming game."

Players build farms, grow crops, raise animals, upgrade buildings, fight monsters, and join clans. There are also mines for gold and silver, and oil wells producing oil. The prices of these resources are tied to real commodity markets.

The economic systems in traditional farming games are entirely fictional, making them easy to manipulate or lacking a sense of realism. This project directly ties in-game gold, silver, and oil prices to real market prices, so real-world commodity news and price fluctuations directly affect players' strategies—players can stockpile goods and wait for prices to rise before selling. It also tries to create a more sustainable token economy through a "play-to-burn" model, rather than pure inflationary P2E.

SEASON token utility: the primary in-game currency. All costs and rewards are fixed in USD, then displayed converted at the real-time SEASON price. Spending tokens (upgrading buildings, buying animals, energy, feeding, etc.) usually burns half and sends half to the reward pool. Deposits incur a 3% fee, withdrawals a 5% fee, and all energy purchase fees go into the reward pool. Spending and rewards settle on-chain approximately every 10 minutes and can be tracked on a block explorer. Early gameplay has already burned nearly 2% of the supply.

The player count has quickly reached 2,000+, and it has now reportedly surpassed 3,500 farmers.

text:
关于 Binance AI Pro 的产品反馈与改进建议：

上午用来尝试做了一些事情，暂时用的免费版，模型是 deepseek V4.1 flash 说实话这个模型也挺强的，

比如创建一些定投策略、构建信号监控机制这些完全没问题，而且智能程度在交易构建上，没毛病。

如果需要更复杂的事情也可以充值每个月20刀；

所以整体来讲，我认为 Binance AI Pro 是一个值得期待的产品，

你看我们之前无法完成策略建立，有了 GPT 后，这类通用型 AI 也需要先构建逻辑，后面才能有策略，

Binance Pro 最大的意义，应该是让普通用户不需要掌握编程，他会引导你思考和构建，也有机会建立自己的交易策略。

目前比较认可的几个方向：

1️⃣降低使用门槛。 用自然语言生成策略、可视化展示执行逻辑，比传统量化交易工具友好很多。
2️⃣模拟交易与实盘分离。 用户可以先观察策略表现，再决定是否投入真实资金。
3️⃣独立子账户。 资金需要手动划转、策略需要用户批准，这种权限隔离对资产安全非常重要。

但我觉得还有几个值得优先改进的地方：

第一，补齐历史回测功能。

目前可以模拟交易，但缺少完整的历史回测。
希望未来支持跨牛熊周期回测，展示最大回撤、收益风险比、交易费用、滑点，以及不同市场环境下的表现。

第二，强化自动交易的安全机制。

这是我认为最重要的一点。
我看了一下，当 AI 使用额度耗尽时，策略会暂停，但已有仓位和挂单可能继续保留。
看下是不是增加独立于 AI 模型额度的风控机制，包括资金损失上限、异常交易熔断、策略失效预警，以及策略暂停时的持仓处理选项。

第三，提高数据的透明度和可验证性。

AI 给出市场判断时，希望能看到数据来源、更新时间、计算方法，以及哪些结论属于推测，目前给的来源和策略依据不明确，
特别是链上数据、ETF 资金流、市场指标等，如果无法获取可靠数据，应明确告知，而不是生成一个看起来合理的答案。

第四，希望强化长期投资者的使用场景。

目前产品主要强调自动化交易，但我觉得我本人，实际上更需要资产监控、风险预警、投资研究和定期报告。
例如让我可以建立自己的长期投资框架，让 AI 持续跟踪 BTC、ETH 的关键指标，在达到预设条件时提醒我，由我来决定是否交易。
BTW，我用 GPT 大多做的也是这类事情。
所以建议提供更加明确的“只读研究模式”和“仅提醒、不交易”模式，并支持跨账户或跨平台的只读资产分析。

最后一个建议：

我个人认为 Binance AI Pro 最大的机会，不只是帮助用户更方便地交易，也不是构建交易系统，
而是帮助用户建立一套能够持续运行、可以验证、风险可控的投资决策系统。

如果未来能把策略回测、可靠数据、风险管理和长期资产监控做好，这款产品的长期价值可能会远远超过普通的 AI 交易机器人。

很期待它后续的进化。

text:
科技股基金一周流出47.5亿美元，投资者开始担心AI烧钱太快

截至10月14日的一周，全球科技股基金净流出 47.5亿 美元，同期全球股票基金却净流入 200.1亿 美元。资金虽然还在进入股市，但投资者对科技股，尤其是靠借钱扩张的AI企业，开始变得谨慎。

原因主要是建数据中心、买芯片，都要先把钱花出去，等机房建好、客户开始使用，才能逐步收回现金。手里有订单当然是好事，但完成这些订单还需要继续投入。投资者现在担心的是，收入还没收到，债务和利息已经先增加了。

CoreWeave 就是一个例子，债务已经达到约 350亿 美元，后续扩张仍然需要大量资金。而 9月 全球 AI 相关债务发行只有 230亿 美元，不到 8月 的一半，融资已经有所放缓。在借钱成本较高的时候，如果企业拿不到足够的钱，建设进度就可能放慢，原本预计的收入也要往后推。

金融时报近日报道，今年美国至少有 47 个大型数据中心项目被推迟、撤回或者阻止。Bernstein 估计，美国规划中的数据中心项目，只有约 35% 的建设计划比较可信。融资、供电、审批和当地居民的反对，都在拖慢建设。

这就会影响股价。投资者此前愿意买入，是看好这些企业未来能赚更多的钱，现在发现，要实现这些增长，还得继续借钱、支付更多利息，最终能留下多少利润就需要重新计算。对融资依赖越强、回本时间越长的企业，资金就越容易先减仓。

长鑫预盈超1300亿元仍大跌，半导体正在重新评估增长预期

长鑫科技预计今年前三季度营收达到 2,650 亿至 2,700 亿元，去年同期只有 320.84 亿元，归母净利润预计达到 1,310 亿至 1,325 亿元，去年同期还是亏损 52.8 亿元。这样一份业绩预告公布后，10月19日股价盘中仍然一度下跌超过8%。

在看最近全球半导体行业的走势来看，整体都并不乐观，费城半导体指数已经连续八个交易日下跌，当天跌幅约3.8%。台积电第三季度营收同比增长50.9%，净利润同比增长68.7%，达到7,630.6亿元新台币，但财报公布后也仍然是下跌的状态。

而导致半导体行业整体下跌的主要原因是来自投资者对 AI 投入能否持续、未来利润能否兑现的担忧。

存储芯片涨价，让长鑫这类生产商赚到了更多钱，但到了手机、电脑和零售商那里，就变成了更高的进货成本。 TrendForce 在9月底预计，第四季度常规 DRAM 合约价格还会上涨 10% 至 15% ，但零售渠道已经越来越难接受高价 NAND ，一些电脑品牌也开始减少主流机型的 SSD 容量来控制成本。

美光、SK海力士和三星也要面对同样的问题，投资者买入时，也会提前把未来的利润增长算进股价。如果股价已经涨了很多，一份漂亮的财报可能只是兑现了之前的预期。此时，只要市场担心芯片涨价放缓，或者客户减少采购，就可能下调对未来利润的判断，也不再愿意用之前的价格买入。

这就会出现公司赚得更多，股价却下跌的情况。

到了10月下旬，真正的方向选择快来了！

bitcoin:native 在8万守住上升趋势线重新回到8.2万上方，这证明多头防线还在，但价格没有收复上一轮下跌高点，MACD也没有真正转强。#OKX

4小时持仓量随反弹回升，资金费率持续为正，当前上涨仍有合约资金推动，现货接力并不明显。

日线两个红圈看着都是横盘，性质却不一样，左侧7.6万-8.2万完成换手后放量突破；右侧从8.74万回落以来，高点不断下移，下跌放量、反弹缩量，说明8.3万-8.6万仍有不少筹码等着兑现。

ETF的反馈更直接。
过去两周 ETF累计净流出约9.07亿美元，10月16日再次流出8240万美元，机构没有彻底离场，但也谈不上抢筹。

宏观同样矛盾。
十月加息概率已经降至约12%至15%，美债收益率也从高位回落；但9月CPI升至3.7%，十二月加息预期接近89%，短期压力缓解，不代表流动性重新宽松。

我的判断：十月剩余时间先看反弹修复，暂时不看直接主升。

站稳8.3万，继续看8.4万-8.5万；日线放量收复8.5万，同时ETF恢复持续流入，才有资格挑战8.65万-8.74万。

如果反弹无法突破8.4万，随后跌破8.15万，大概率再次测试8万，日线收盘失守7.97万，下方看7.8万，极端情况防守7.6万。

8万决定防守，8.5万决定进攻，在这个区间里，耐心等确认，比急着判断牛熊更重要。

text:
先说明，我手里确实拿着不少 $TSLA 和 $SPCX，也一直对马斯克正在铺的这盘大棋极其看好。但今天刚看完 ARK 发布的这份特斯拉最新估值模型，我实在忍不住想吐个槽：这饼画的，未免有点太离谱了。🧐

ARK 预测，到 2031 年特斯拉每股能冲到 4400 美元，牛市甚至看到 5000 美元，对应17.5 万亿美元的恐怖市值！🤔

📝咱们先看看 ARK 怎么算的：

• 东西卖多少：到 2031 年要卖出 810 万辆 Robotaxi、1020 万辆普通电动车、100 万台 Optimus 机器人，外加 2278 GWh 的储能。

• 钱从哪里来：总营收要做到 1.45 万亿美元。其中 Robotaxi 拿大头，贡献 7530 亿美元（占 52%）；汽车销量占 3200 亿；Optimus 占 2120 亿；储能占 1630 亿。

• 利润有多夸张：EBITDA干到9020 亿美元，利润率高达 61%！

• 估值核心支撑：Robotaxi 一项就占了特斯拉估值的 80%，Optimus 占 14%。ARK 觉得人形机器人这块市场能搞出 26 万亿美元市场，比他们给 Robotaxi 设的 10 到 15 万亿还要夸张。

• 无人驾驶成本：他们算出来 Cybercab 每英里的运营成本比 Waymo 下一代产品低 40%。

• 算力投入：到 2031 年 AI 基础设施累积要烧掉 2250 亿美元，包括和 SpaceX 一起搞的 Terafab。

更夸张的是，ARK 甚至还顺带附赠了一个神级假设：如果 SpaceX 和特斯拉合并，2031 年合并营收 3.8 万亿，EBITDA 2.74 万亿，市值直接破 50 万亿美元。

说实话，这么远期的数学模型我自己没算过。但我一直坚信 SpaceX 未来会成为全球市值第一的公司，甚至第一个冲到 100 万亿美元市值，两家合并也确实是通往终局的最佳路径。两个月前 $SPCX 才 110美元的时候，我就在自己社群中喊大家买了。

但看好归看好，咱们得讲点现实吧？

你知道 2025 年特斯拉营收多少吗？大概 950 亿美元。

ARK 的意思是，5 年内收入要翻 15 倍以上，利润率还得做到顶级 SaaS 软件公司都眼红的水平。而且 80% 的估值，全押在一个还没真正大规模商业化的 Robotaxi 上。

我们再看好自动驾驶、AI、机器人，也得承认，相信未来，和赌未来 5 年一步都不犯错，完全是两码事。

• 自动驾驶技术落地
• 各国监管审批
• 大规模量产的供应链
• Optimus 真正商业化
• 几千亿美元的 AI 基建

哪一样不是得一步一步啃下来？

最搞笑的是，ARK 的熊市情景，2031 年市值还有 13.4 万亿美元。我就想问，从什么时候开始，13.4 万亿能叫悲观预期了？😂

虽然我也是马斯克死忠粉，也极度看好特斯拉和SpaceX，但对于木头姐这个数据📊模型，真的有点难消化，一级市场画饼可以理解，二级市场还能画这么大的饼，我也是挺佩服木头姐的，DYOR🙏(报告放在评论区👇)

text:
The velocity of code changes for engineers this year has 10x’d, quickly moving the bottleneck to code review and testing.

Greptile solves this for the most technically challenging codebases like Nvidia (core CUDA code is reviewed on Greptile), Coinbase, Datadog, OpenClaw and 22,000 more customers.

Many people think the model layer will eat code validation, but I don’t think it will. Code review within organizations is a more context-bound task than an intelligence-bound. The most intelligent AI can be wrong because it breaks an assumption in one API endpoint another service relies on. Large codebases can quickly accumulate a lot of technical debt your coding harness won’t reliably remember every time. Greptile does.

Instead of having a frontier model harness review your code which can quickly cost $20+/review, Greptile does a much better job for much cheaper, leveraging the smartest models when needed but the GLM/Kimi/DeepSeeks when needed to. And it also runs, tests and takes a video of what your change did. 

Over time, organizations treat a 5/5 rated change by Greptile as a guarantee this won’t break anything in prod. And it shows. Their growth has been off the charts.

Incredibly fortunate to partner with this a company. 

Fun fact: Elon once posted Greptile's growth graph with "it's so over" pointing to 2024 to show AI's acceleration.

流量负责获客，Step 提供金融服务入口，未来再探索投资、加密交易与 DeFi。

Tucked inside the October 19 proxy statement is a clear signal that Tesla is moving well beyond lab experiments. 

The company confirmed it is actively building its first dedicated Optimus production lines, scaling the compute clusters needed to train end-to-end neural networks, and transferring years of FSD breakthroughs directly into general-purpose humanoid robotics.

The standout detail sits right in the compensation disclosures. Tesla explicitly added "Optimus production and deployment" as an operational milestone required for performance stock awards granted to key non-executive talent.

That means execution isn't just riding on Elon Musk’s headline pay structure. The engineers, manufacturing leads, and specialists on the ground now have direct, serious upside tied to getting physical units off the assembly line. When an engineering culture aligns individual equity directly with shipping physical hardware, timelines tend to shrink fast.

Optimus might not be a standalone voting proposal at this year’s shareholder meeting, but make no mistake: it has officially shifted from speculative moonshot to an incentivized industrial program. The ramp-up is going to be wild to watch.

刚刷到这个有点意思 - AI时代很多东西现在可以被分析，被摊在桌面上供人“审视”

我记得我上学那会，“大数据”这个词儿很火，但当时没有AI，很多数据你也许能拿到，但分析不出个所以然，或者说需要花大价钱大力气才能有个结果

AI时代简单多了，比如这个“全美58个外国出生的联邦终身法官的判决数据”

博主声称花了45天，烧了10亿 tokens，梳理超过100万件案件，对全美所有58名在任的外国出生的联邦Article III法官做了审计

里面43个是奥巴马和拜登任命的，14个特朗普任命，一个小布什任命

结论基本上一句话就能说清楚 - 这帮吊人基本是依据“出身文化”而非美国法律来做判决的

然后还给了四张点状图柱状图的论据 - 横轴是判刑有多轻，纵轴是多爱卡边境执法。

结果非常清晰——拜登和奥巴马任命的那批，大多集中在“又轻判又爱拦边境”的右上角，反边境率能到70-90%，量刑低于指南的比例也明显高于全国平均。（这帮人很多人之前是做公设辩护人或者移民维权律师的，职业路径更偏向为被告和移民辩护）

特朗普任命的那批之前多是检察官背景，点就明显偏左下

网站还做了对比表和个人档案，点进去能看每个法官具体咋判的。

我理解作者这里说的“出身文化”不单指出生地和文化，而是更偏任命背景和职业路径

但不管怎样，断案这种东西，在大数据+AI的加持下，估计可预测性大幅提高。

忽然让我想到以前看的一部电影 《Runaway Jury - 失控陪审团》，讲的就是有人专门针对陪审员的背景、性格、生活经历去研究和操控，用各种数据、背景调查去挑和影响陪审员，让案子往有利于自己的方向走

现在有了AI的帮助，是不是法官也可以去“研究和操控”一下了🤔

text:
Your coding agent is the shittiest 1st time visitor your website will ever have.

Why? You're asking it to unbiasedly test the site it just built itself.

If you're vibe coding right now, steal this prompt for a fresh session. It reads your site like a stranger at 10, 30, and 60 seconds, then scores where you lost them.

"Open [site URL] as a 1st time visitor who knows nothing about this product. Don't read the codebase, edit anything, or use past context or memory.

Scroll slowly, dismiss popups, and screenshot each screen at 1440px and 390px wide. Judge only what you've seen so far:

First screen: What is it, who's it for, and what could it be mistaken for?

3 screens: What would make you leave?

6 screens: Explain it in one sentence. What's confusing?

Full page: What looks fake? Where did interest drop? Do the asks compete? Does it feel like a clear user journey or repeated templates? Any odd button placements or layouts?

Phone: What's cramped, wrapped, cut off, or overflowing?

Score clarity, trust, and next step 1-10. Score harshly: under 9 means not ready to launch. Please name the one major idea you'd remember tomorrow.

Then plan up to 5 of the most immediate surgical fixes, highest impact first, with replacement copy. Don't pad the list, and never invent facts or numbers."

text:
我其实不太愿意拿 tensorcash:native 和 $PRL 做比较，尤其不想把这种比较变成拉踩，因为我个人也挺喜欢 PRL，毕竟我也是中文区很早就参与珍珠头矿也赚到钱了。

但研究了这么多项目，我还是认为，它们确实是最有可比性的两个，只是两家技术路线不同。

PRL 是把 AI 计算中的矩阵乘法转化为 PoW 工作量；TSC 则是把 AI 模型推理过程转化为 PoW 工作量，并让这一过程变得可核验。

一个从底层数学运算切入，一个从模型推理过程切入，本质上都在尝试让同一份 AI 计算，既服务用户，又参与区块链记账。

所以，我选择建设 TSC，并不需要以否定 PRL 为前提。

至于为什么选择 TSC，原因有很多。其中一个很重要、也很个人的原因是：现在参与 PRL，相当于我是成熟企业的普通员工；但现在参与 TSC，我就是这家初创的 OG，并且我很认可这家公司的理念和骨干成员。

道理很简单：我想要拿到更大结果，也想成为推动结果发生的元老，享受做成一件大事的爽感，所以我愿意承担对应的风险和挑战。

另外 POUW 是未来的大趋势，我之前就反复发过，只有能与数据中心融合的POW才有未来，所以未来绝对不会只有一个赢家，而大概率会像早期POW1.0时代一样，百花齐放，格局放大，一起让挖矿再次伟大。

text:
Today at @money2020 we launched Logos. @TomZschach and I have been building it in stealth this year.

Moving tokenized assets has come a long way. Accepting them and then actually doing useful work with them is where most of the work is left.

Take tokenized gold. Imagine a lender is asked to accept $10M of it as collateral. If I were building that workflow, I'd want more than an issuer's statement that the gold exists. I'd want an independent auditor's attestation of what gold they inspected, where and when, alongside custody records and redemption terms.

Those pieces of evidence answer different questions. An inspection of gold in a vault still leaves the legal rights and redemption terms to establish. The source, scope and date of each claim matter.

I don't think every institution that wants to receive these assets should have to start from scratch to answer those questions. In a world of many thousands of tokenized assets, I don't even think today's processes survive.

This is why we're building Logos: the evidence layer institutions need to put more tokenized assets and stablecoins to work.

There's a simple idea behind the architecture: N × M → N + M. A hundred evidence publishers and a hundred institutions, each connecting to every other, is 10,000 connections to build and maintain. Each connecting once through a shared interface is 200.

The arithmetic is the easy part. Making evidence reusable means being able to establish who supplied it, their authority and whether it's current enough for the decision. And N + M describes the connections; every institution still makes its own policy checks.

That independence matters. A custodian and a lender can look at the same evidence and reach different decisions. We want to make the shared work reusable while keeping each institution's judgment and accountability intact.

We've closed our seed round with backing from @ParaFiCapital and @vaneck_us, and we're working toward our first production workflows with @Paysend and @Securitize as initial design partners. Thank you to our team and everyone helping us get this off the ground.

If you're the person chasing this evidence or connecting these systems at a custodian, lender or payment institution, I'd love to hear where you spend your time. That's the work we want to make easier.

Discuss a design partnership: https://t.co/TVDnQmdaTv

text:
一支港股ETF竟然走出了土狗的气势，港股高息精选配上美股高成长现金流，聊聊南方东西精选这支ETF。之前聊过港股的机会不在指数里，而在具体的行业里。如果讨论一直停留在“港股便宜”“什么时候估值修复”，投资就很容易变成等待。买入时觉得估值低，跌下来觉得更便宜，最后能否赚钱，很大程度上取决于什么时候有人愿意给出更高的价格。

换一个角度，问题会具体很多。
我理解的“使用港股的正确角度”，就是把其中合适的资产挑出来，放进全球组合里，承担一个明确的功能。

最近关注到了南方东西精选这支港股ETF，发现这提供了一个值得研究的样本。按照现行指数规则，它把约60%的权重配置给港股高股息组合，约40%配置给美国现金流精选组合。港股部分关注现金分派，美国部分引入另一组有现金创造能力的企业。这个搭配，比单独讨论“看多港股还是看多美股”更有意思。从这个角度，值得把它放进配置观察清单里。

这支ETF截至当下近一年回报35%，上市一年半以来回报超过80%，最大回撤－7.9%，夏普比率2.82，算是很稳健了，也能给希望增加不同收益来源的投资人提供了一种新的选择

而把南方东西精选（03441）的持仓拆开看，最值得展开聊的其实是一个问题：港股在我们的资产组合里，到底应该承担什么角色？

60%的持仓给到港股
指数先筛分红，再按规模选出23只符合条件的香港股票，持仓有中银香港、银河娱乐、香港中华煤气、中电控股、电能实业、海丰国际、港铁公司、万洲国际、九龙仓置业、长江基建集团等。这就是一组经过分红和规模筛选的成熟经营资产，绝大部分都是港股里稳健经营的价值股，即使业务增长不快，只要分红有经营支撑、买入价格合理，也可能是一笔有价值的投资。如果盈利改善，再叠加估值修复，回报还可能超过单纯收息。

这让港股投资多了一条回报路径，少一点对整个市场重新估值的依赖。

40%持仓留给美股，保留了另一种增长来源。
美国部分关注自由现金流规模，并结合质量与风险筛选。持仓中既有苹果、微软、Meta、博通等美股高成长科技股，也有伯克希尔哈撒韦、礼来、强生、埃克森美孚、Visa等强现金流的价值股。这些企业产生现金后，可以回馈股东，也可以继续投入业务。新增投资如果有较高回报，就有机会推动每股价值增长。

这种搭配最值得研究的地方，是不同企业的盈利驱动有差别。港股端更偏公用事业、金融和传统经营业务；美股端更多科技、医疗及其他大型企业。

经过测算近五年周度回报相关性约0.25，整体加权平均股息率5.04% 。对科技仓位较重的账户，增加不同经营类型的公司，有机会改善分散程度。指数还会按规则恢复港美目标比例，给仓位调整加上一点纪律。

个人角度，这是一只以香港分红股票为主体、用美国大型现金流企业补充增长和行业分散的权益配置工具。它的优势是组合思路清晰：
1）港股部分偏向现金分派，美国部分保留现金创造能力和增长空间，避免全部依赖单一市场或单一科技主线；
2）低相关性与规则化再平衡，为改善持有体验提供了合理基础，选股规则也比只看股息率更有层次。

对希望增加分红取向，又不愿完全放弃企业增长机会的人，它值得认真比较研究和关注。对于大A投资人还有一个好的点是，这支ETF可以直接通过港股通账户无限额、无溢价买到，相对大A上那些限额严重、溢价也很高的美股纳指的QD基金来说更友好了。

选择它的合理理由应当是自己确实有意配置港股资产，也认可其美国现金流规则，希望用一只产品持续维护这种结构。

港股调整，之后的机会会在哪里？还是要在具体行业里看。最近港股很萎靡，9月恒生指数累计下跌3.73%，恒生科技指数下跌7.92%。但把行业和公司拆开看表现差异很大：AI-bio就是一个例子，过去两个月恒生生物科技指数涨了30%多，港股这个板块里成份股票过去两个月走势都很强。强势也会伴随剧烈波动，上周7号恒生生物科技指数一度跌超 3%。

个人角度，看港股的投资价值，需要把视线从指数往下移。市场整体调整，并不会让公司的研发和商业化进程同时停下来。有些业务还在增长，有些新产品正在接受验证，也有新的公司进入公开市场。

先看 AI-bio 和创新药。
这条线吸引的地方是 AI 已经开始进入真实的药物研发流程，后续可以用临床数据和客户付款来检验价值。药明康德、金斯瑞、石药、翰森、再鼎等多次创新高。驱动跨国药企对中国管线的BD授权、部分公司中报由亏转盈或高增、国内医药工业规划强化创新定位，以及海外AI制药进展带来的情绪催化。摩根大通则表态对生物科技和CXO相对不那么担心利率冲击，当然短期过于拥挤还是会有调整的。

AI算力硬件链条（相对最清晰的产业趋势）
全球云厂商资本开支仍在上修，需求外溢到高层数PCB、覆铜板、电子布、光模块和部分接口芯片。港股这一块有不少可验证订单和涨价的公司。建滔积层板、建滔集团、胜宏科技、广合科技、长飞光纤等在9–10月反复走强，逻辑是AI服务器PCB层数和用量跳升、上游材料短缺带动提价、国内厂商满产并抢份额。高盛等对AI相关CCL需求到2028年给出较高复合增速。

可以把注意力放在订单能否持续、产品定价有没有改善，再看扩产后的折旧和现金流压力。港股里的半导体机会，需要落到具体公司的产品和客户结构上，单靠一个行业标签还不够。

高股息与现金流资产
银行、电信运营商、部分公用事业和能源股在高利率环境下提供股息缓冲。当然逻辑是估值和派息对冲波动，并不是高成长。成长股看未来业务能做多大，分红型公司则可以更多围绕现金回报来估值。不同类型的资产放在同一个市场里，给了投资者更大的选择空间。

还有一块值得留意，就是新股市场。
港交所数据显示，2026 年前八个月，香港市场 IPO 募资约 3,424 亿港元，同比增长 153%。新股发行持续活跃，也在不断补充二级市场里可以研究的公司。当然近期港股打新也没上半年收益率那么高了。

但对投资者来说，打新的价值，在于多了一个评估公司、参与定价的机会。
市场调整的时候，正好可以把这些方向重新梳理一遍。至于什么时候买，仍然要落到具体公司和价格上。研究范围扩展到港股，接下来就会碰到一个很现实的问题：账户和资金通道有没有准备好？

尤其对手里持有 USDT、USDC 的人，想参与港股，往往还得先解决钱怎么进证券账户。如果需要另办境外银行卡、安排跨境汇款，准备工作也会占用时间。

BIT证券这次上线港股，对这类用户就比较实用。
看公告10月12日， @BITstocks_CN 将正式开放港股交易，一个证券账户同时覆盖美股和港股。有几个点值得聊聊：
1）已经开通美股账户的用户无需重复开户，可以直接开通港股。支持稳定币USDT / USDC 7×24 小时出入金，秒级到账。**港币和美元可以在账户内直接互换。

2）这次一起接进来的还有港股IPO打新。稳定币入金后在账户内兑换成港币，就可以提交新股申购。 对本来就持有稳定币的人，这条路径省去了另行准备海外银行账户的步骤。
BIT还同时支持融资打新，融资倍数最高10倍，1个月内融资认购手续费及额度内的认购利息限时双免，每笔新股认购最高40万港币的免息融资额度。当然对于投资人来说也要注意风险控制。

3）也是真实股票，BIT港股交易由香港证监会持牌券商Atomic Vaults Asia提供，稳定币用于入金和资金兑换。用户按持仓及相关规则享有分红、投票等股东权益，美港股都支持股票转仓。

4）BIT支持内地身份注册和KYC，身份证就可以做地址证明，无需额外准备。而且BIT是不丹主体，不丹是不CRS的，这个对很多朋友来说都很友好了。

对本来就在研究港股、手里又持有一部分稳定币的人，BIT 这次更新提供了一个可以了解的交易入口。行业和公司可以持续跟踪，账户与入金路径也可以提前准备。等到出现自己看得懂、价格合适的机会，再决定如何参与。

text:
Papertrade is slowly rugging its own users🚨

The situation with $PAPER is getting ridiculous

For those unfamiliar, Papertrade launched on HyperEVM just 10 days ago, allowing users to trade with 1,000x leverage

every time you lost money or got liquidated, you received $PAPER

You could then stake those tokens to earn USDC from the protocol’s revenue

Well, in its first few days, Papertrade generated $1T in trading volume, with traders losing $54M and $45M distributed in staking rewards

Some people were even deliberately losing money to farm PAPER

One wallet lost $979K to mint 252M PAPER and received $1.87M in staking rewards within days

But yesterday, the team announced some pretty significant changes

First, $PAPER won’t be transferable anytime soon

Actually, the team said they have no plans to enable transfers outside the protocol at this stage

(Remember that users were farming this token expecting it to eventually become tradable)

Paragon, which had paid around $45K to secure the PAPER ticker on Hyperliquid’s HIP-3 infrastructure, immediately shut down its market

Aster did the same

The team is also changing PAPER’s emission model

Previously, the initial rate was 100 PAPER for every $1 lost

Under the new system, each $1M in eligible losses will mint approximately 0.1% of the existing supply

Meaning that as supply grows, more PAPER gets created for the same amount of losses

(existing holders get diluted)

The team literally acknowledged this in its announcement

So imagine being one of the earliest users, losing money to farm PAPER, and suddenly discovering that:

- You can’t transfer or sell your tokens
- The pre-market where people were trading them has disappeared
- Your share of future staking rewards will gradually be diluted
- The protocol is changing its fee structure too

Now, to be fair, the team has an explanation

They argue that allowing people to short PAPER externally could make attacks against the protocol’s liquidity pool profitable

But here’s my problem

If making PAPER transferable creates such a serious threat to the protocol, why wasn’t that risk properly addressed before people started farming it?

And why should early participants accept dilution after taking the biggest risks?

Especially when those people have no way to exit their positions
author: StarPlatinum_
quoted_text:
A note on transferability.

Papertrade is a complicated primitive, and managing it from a risk standpoint is a complicated problem. The PAPER token is far more integrated into the economics of the primitive than most tokens are in their respective protocols today, and, broadly, was designed to act as a counter insolvency incentive coupled with a rebate mechanism to losing traders. Market makers and exchanges are by far the two most profitable businesses in crypto, and our goal was to try and externalise as much of their margins back to users as possible. We are now just over a week into the life of papertrade and we are becoming increasingly confident that this is both possible, but also a likely outcome as agentic led software becomes the norm. 

As it stands, the paper token traded as a perp becomes a leveraged bet on bankroll solvency - and being able to short bankroll solvency materially changes the payoff curve of a manipulation attack. The target number goes from the bankroll, to the bankroll + short side exposure on paper. We can, and do limit bankroll size specifically to control this payoff curve and ensure it never becomes existentially problematic, but external perp markets are not something we would have any control over if left to float of their own accord. For example, if our bankroll is $10m, an attack costing $15m manipulating the price of bitcoin or ether is not viable. You simply lose money. If however you were also able to put on $10m of PAPER short side exposure, suddenly an attack costing $15m is very viable indeed.

If we were to make the token transferable at this point, we are confident we would quickly enter a state too dangerous to allow any material exposure to be taken on papertrade, an end result that benefits no party beyond the wolves who have done the math on the short and are waiting in the wings with sharpened knives.

We would also like to thank the various perps teams who have reached out about pre-market listings for their understanding and patience regarding this issue, and especially to the paragon team who, despite jumping the gun on us, have behaved with the utmost integrity and transparency once a dialogue was opened.

Perps on PAPER will always act as a self-limiting exposure ceiling for a token with this type of utility, and we think it would be a shame to limit the growth of papertrade to the extent that allowing perps would necessitate. As such, at this juncture we do not have plans to allow off-contract token transferability.

Structurally, papertrade is limited by the quality of the data it receives from hyperliquid, but we strongly believe that hyperliquid has a very large part to play in the future of global exchanges, and expect their books to continue to thicken and strengthen over time.

A note on fees.

Papertrade launched with a deadband fee from entry of 0.2bps. This means you don't earn anything until the price has moved by 0.002% in your favour. Over the months before launch, we played around with many different curves and fee structures affecting exclusively positions closed very close to entry price in order to try and devise a structure that removed the edge against the bankroll low time frame scalp bots have, whilst also minimally impacting the traders around which and for whom the product was devised. We were never able to find anything we were absolutely happy with and so decided to stay with the 0.2bp deadband fee through launch. This has however meant we have had to be very restrictive when it came to certain parameters, such as OI caps.

Now, however, we have enough live data to fully understand exactly which strategies work, and to make the necessary changes to stop them. The changes we are making will have an on hours and off hours fee mode to account for the relative differences in liquidity the hyperliquid books see between these two time periods, and the ease with which low time frame moves are signalled. The changes we are making will only affect positions closed within 6bps of entry (0.06%) in on hours, and 10bps (0.1%) in off hours. Any trades closed above these threshold price shifts will see no change to their fees at all. On a look back to launch basis, these changes affect the profitability of bot strategies roughly 15x more than they do normal traders, for whom a very small proportion of overall winnings come from within this band.

These changes should serve to flatten much of the edge our microfee structure necessarily creates on low time frames, and will help with long term exchange sustainability. This should hopefully allow us to open up parameters such as OI caps a little more so those of you who wish to can put on the size you want to, when you want to.

It is possible these changes are still too lax, and that further revisions to this structure may be necessary going forwards. If so, we will notify users ahead of time.

A note on paper tokenomics. 

In conjunction with the fee changes, we will also be implementing a change to the token issuance curve.

Going forward, every $1 lost mints a fixed share of PAPER's supply at that moment, roughly 0.1% of supply per $1M lost (the exact number depends on the mint rate at the time the contracts are upgraded). PAPER minting in and near insolvency will also change, switching from a flat 100 per $1 of loss, to a time weighted multiplier on the curve growing over time, effectively acting as the house running a discounted auction on its own future cash flows. This change also removes the risk of the paper-mint-straddle-attack, temporarily pushing the protocol insolvent by closing only the winning side of a large straddle position and then attempting to mint as much paper as possible. 

In the immediate term these changes will only have a very subtle effect on PAPER minting, but in the long run will structurally change the outlook of the system beyond the first few weeks, serving to slowly dilute out older holders and leaving more recent users with an advantage. Reconstituting the PAPER system into something much closer to the exchange rakeback it was intended to be.

We have been very reticent to touch this particular aspect of the system for obvious reasons, but ultimately we believe that these changes provide all users with the optionality to take a smaller piece of a potentially much larger pie than the current dynamic might necessarily allow.

Other, miscellaneous notes.

These contract upgrades will include a few other contract changes, including the addition of builder codes so that builders can utilise papertrade in whatever capacity they choose to. This will be a whitelist only to begin with and we will have more for you later in the week on where/how this will be rolled out. A small change to contract permissions on the reward distributor and a change on how below bust closes are processed by the exchange are also included, largely to block gas griefing attacks. 

These changes will be pushed to docs in full over the coming day, and we will further announce once the changes are queued into the timelock pending final security passes, scheduled to go live 24 hours after that point.

Final note.

We'd like to thank everyone that has tried out papertrade over the last 10 days. It has been a labour of love building this product and both of us have been taken aback at all of the positive feedback we have received. We'd also like to thank all those of you who have spent considerable time musing on the system we have built, and much of your advice has been taken onboard and will likely affect the colour of what papertrade becomes going forward. We know some of these changes will be unpopular with some, but we would not be making them if we did not feel them to be absolutely necessary.

- blurr, jez

text:
지금 미국에서는 대형 AI 데이터센터 47곳이 줄취소되고, 빚내서 엔비디아 칩을 사 모으던 AI 기업들은 이자가 연 15%까지 치솟으며 부도 위기에 몰리고 있음.

다들 "AI 데이터센터는 앞으로도 무한정 지어질 것"이라고 믿고 있지만, 정작 뒤에서 돈을 대주던 미국 월가에서는 'AI 영끌 빚투'가 한계에 왔다며 돈을 빼기 시작함.

오늘 뉴욕타임스, 파이낸셜타임스(FT), 블룸버그에서 동시에 터져 나온 팩트 3가지 정리.

1. 빚내서 엔비디아 칩 사던 대표 기업 '코어위브': 부채 70조 원, 이자율 15% 폭등

- 지금까지 AI 반도체가 왜 그렇게 미친 듯이 팔렸을까? 빅테크들만 산 게 아니라, '코어위브(CoreWeave)' 같은 신생 AI 클라우드 업체들이 엔비디아 칩을 담보로 수십조 원씩 대출을 받아서 칩을 쓸어 담고, 그걸 다시 빅테크에 빌려주는 장사를 했기 때문임.

- 그런데 뉴욕타임스 보도에 따르면, 이 코어위브의 빚이 무려 70조~95조 원까지 불어나면서 채권 금리(돈 빌릴 때 내는 이자)가 연 15~16%까지 치솟았음. 기업이 연 15% 이자를 내야 돈을 구할 수 있다는 건, 시장에서 사실상 '언제 부도가 나도 이상하지 않은 위험한 회사'로 보고 있다는 뜻임.

- 왜 이렇게 됐냐면 구조 자체가 굉장히 불안함. 데이터센터 건물은 15년 이상 장기 계약으로 빌리고 비싼 엔비디아 칩을 빚내서 잔뜩 채워 넣었는데, 정작 그 칩을 빌려 쓰는 빅테크들과는 짧은 단기 계약을 맺어놨음. 즉 빅테크가 재계약을 안 하거나 발을 빼는 순간, 남은 빚과 건물세를 고스란히 떠안고 무너지는 구조임.

- 심지어 AI 데이터센터에 큰돈을 쏟아붓던 오라클도 채권값이 뚝뚝 떨어지고 있고, 오픈AI에 수십조 원을 넣겠다며 연 10%짜리 고금리 대출까지 끌어다 쓴 소프트뱅크도 부도 위험 수치가 빠르게 치솟고 있음.

2. 미국 대형 AI 데이터센터 47곳 줄취소… "발표된 계획의 65%는 못 짓는다"

- "그래도 데이터센터는 계속 짓고 있지 않냐"고 생각하겠지만, 파이낸셜타임스(FT)가 조사해 보니 올해 미국에서만 대형 데이터센터 건설 프로젝트 47곳 이상이 아예 취소되거나 무기한 연기됨.

- 이유는 아주 현실적임. 첫째로 데이터센터를 돌릴 '전기'가 아예 모자라고, 둘째로 전기요금 오르고 소음 심해진다고 미국 내 1,000개 넘는 지역에서 주민들이 반대해 공사가 막혔으며, 셋째로 돈 빌리기가 너무 힘들어졌기 때문임.

- 결국 월가 투자은행 번스타인은 "현재 미국에서 짓겠다고 발표된 데이터센터 계획 중 실제로 제때 지어질 수 있는 건 고작 35%뿐이고, 나머지 65%는 실현되기 어렵다"고 경고함.

3. 마이크로소프트도 발 뺐다… "수백 개 업체 중 7~10곳 빼고 다 파산할 것"

- 실제로 돈 많은 빅테크들부터 슬슬 발을 빼고 있음. 마이크로소프트(MS)는 최근 영국의 대표 AI 클라우드 기업인 '엔스케일(Nscale)'과 맺었던 대형 데이터센터 임대 계약을 취소해 버림(전기가 2030년대에나 들어온다는 이유).

- MS 하나 믿고 미국 상장을 준비하던 이 회사는 단숨에 기업 가치가 300억 달러에서 160억 달러로 반토막 났고, 또 다른 AI 클라우드 업체(퍼머스)는 아예 상장 계획 자체를 접어버림.

- 상황이 이렇다 보니 업계 임원들 입에서조차 "지금 빚내서 칩 사 모은 수백 개의 AI 클라우드 업체 중 딱 7~10곳만 살아남고, 나머지는 전부 파산하거나 헐값에 넘어갈 것"이라는 얘기가 나오고 있음.

사실 이 문제는 AI 붐 초반부터 계속 나왔던 우려였음.

당시에도 "엔비디아가 신생 AI 클라우드 업체들에 투자를 해주고, 그 업체들은 엔비디아 칩을 담보로 거액의 대출을 받아서 다시 엔비디아 칩을 사주는 식으로 서로서로 물려 있는 돌려막기 구조 아니냐"는 비판이 많았음.

분위기가 좋을 때는 이 구조가 굴러가는 것처럼 보였지만, 결국 이자는 계속 높아지고 전기 부족으로 데이터센터 공사까지 줄줄이 막히기 시작하니까, 초반에 다들 걱정했던 그 우려가 지금 터지기 시작하고 있는 것.

这两天又看了几遍，依然认为这套底层逻辑是没问题的，只是在2026年的经济环境下，不再能百分百适用市场。

经济的模型和市场的结构，是会变的，规律也会，而我们不做出改变还要继续留在这个圈子里，适应力就会很差，所以今年我也被市场推着走改变了很多不符合我过去思维的交易，有赚钱，也有亏钱，而亏得最多的真的还是这篇里面我不擅长的那个板块。

眼下市场中赚钱，其实大家都在吃一个币的量，没量了立马走，有量了立马追，你问叙事，问逻辑都没人在意了，所以深度研究基本也无用，胡说八道是日常。

但即便是这样，今年市场中诞生的几个神币，用这套逻辑模版依然适配，所以变了的也许是我们这批始于meme精神的人。
author: xxxApril_D13
quoted_text:
SOL老外角度meme选币经验

（我本人的理解角度，交流学习贴，觉得不对不好skip就行，杠就是你对🫰）

怎样快速理解老外的梗

-Tiktok,CNN,MSNBC,FOXNEWS,白宫,川普,马斯克,万斯等账号。

老外的文化一般来自tiktok，新闻热点，时政热点或欧美顶流八卦。每个阶段盛行的都不同，毕竟这些热点来自人，人是有情感的活物。最近所有的热门几乎围绕川普，万斯，马斯克。也就是人物梗，（一言一行）反而动物的不多，上限也不高。

抓取这些热点的第一步关注相关账号例：川普，马斯克，万斯，币圈的一些巨鲸大V，YouTuber，新闻账号。
如果看不过来的话，链上一些内幕,车头kol地址监控起来也能很快抓取到实时的反应。 

代币一般都是缩写，但在看板页面都会有这个币的全名，先去看什么意思，去快速找相关，至少能知道个大概。

我不会过度关注太多地址，大脑处理不过来反而成为杂音，目前参考最多的就是 @Ga__ke 即dnf，还有两个新车头，后面会说如何在关注地址里筛选潜在金狗。

如何在已经跑出第一阶段的meme里找到潜在金狗

-24h交易量，持币人数，社区

交易量不用多说了，在第一阶段跑出来的只要不是作恶ds的那种基本就是独立叙事的龙头，观察持币人数的增长，再去看有没有社区建设，sol很多币没有tg社区，而是在X上的，也要每天关注人数的增长。

-底部筹码分配和潜在庄家资金

庄这个东西你除非扒出所有相关资金的钱包地址，很难去用数据支撑来证明有庄，野庄，大庄，强庄。sol更多的只是游资打一枪就跑的。

一个不错的ip（独立，新，有meme属性） 资金也喜欢选这样的标，但如果前排筹码拿太多，就不会那么快启动，至少会磨2-3天，也会尝试拉盘再砸一下试探抛压，洗不掉前排的话在合适价格区间开始吸筹，会拉盘，但上限就没那么高了，毕竟前排拿太多的并不是自己人。

基于这个心理，我经常会去选没人要的币，捡垃圾找潜在可能性，但，一旦筹码多的砸了承接力度不够，我也会maxsell的。

-时间差，信息差。赚钱就是你懂他不懂

首先我不喜欢去凑热闹也就是集体fomo时候的热点，我喜欢在资金全去一个地方的时候反过来抄被吸血的一直关注的币。 

不是追热点不好，是我清楚自己的性格和操作，我无法快过他们。多大能力揽多大活，认清自己很重要。无数时刻反复回溯，那都是最佳进场时间。

币圈是24h不分昼夜的，我们每个人的时区也不一样，所以在时间上也需要根据自己的作息来调整，找到自己的节奏。 我的时差很不友好，所以有放弃一些第一阶段的进场机会，调整在新币pvp第一波结束的时候买进去，在我的时区里基本都可以早上自然睡醒后捡垃圾。每天重复做这样的事。

之前说过，我已经坚持四年每天睡醒花1-1.5h去check所有媒体的信息，因为已经坚持了这么久养成了习惯，对我的帮助就是脑过滤很快，总结抓取也很快。这些确实是靠勤奋努力来的，如果不够聪明勤快是唯一的出路，我也喜欢学习扩充知识领域。毕竟靠运气总有花完的时候。

找到金狗买多少钱合适？如何拿住，拿多久，怎样交易。

-买多少钱取决于你口袋深浅和风险承担能力，这没人可以给你肯定的答案。

-翻倍出本是最基础的能力，行情好的时候底部筹码可以钻一下，放大贪婪。行情不好的时候保住本金，收紧口袋，落袋为大。

-拿多久，sol节奏很快，除了现象级的币可以玩1个月，其他的潜伏2-3天，5-7天卖出似乎是平均现象。pvp玩法不在我说的之内。

-怎样交易，我还是很老套的买入方式，总额分三次进入。卖出每个新高就按比例出一些，没量了就maxsell。

-市值预判和参考，只能阶段性以大行情来估算。
最近1-2个月，时政相关上限10M-20M顶，50M只有pwease一个，算现象级个例。 动物纯原生类，1-5M。

怎样判断meme能不能hold

这件事是把双刃剑，sol的信息透明度勤快点都可以看到所有金狗神盘的信息。但你拿到早期筹码不代表可以赌赢它就是一场大叙事，卖飞是所有人的常态。

我能给的方法就是上面讲的首先要培养自己筛选潜在金狗的能力，在过程里去反复发现和确认持续性,市场接受度。如果位置足够低，是可以赌一赌。如果位置不好，也可以选择第一波先出来，等市场慢慢在接受了启动前买进去。

过往经验是可以看出，除了人造的阳谋金狗，自然发生纯meme金狗基本都是冷盘，也就是你有足够多的时间去研究，发现，上车。

另外，再好的叙事，如果没有你的好成本价格，就算起来可能也赚不到很多钱，不要执迷一个叙事。来圈子里是印钱的，戒掉不必要的情绪。当然你钱多也可以趁着新闻面利好进去吃一波下车。

评论区我会以最近一段时间选的几个狗举例思路👇🏻

text:
agree w/ most of it. 

the main evidence is consumer agents with a human principal who already has a card. That's the one regime where crypto obviously loses. But agents with no human principal, machine-to-machine settlement, or markets where cards don't exist could emerge. It's really US consumer agents don't need crypto for payments.

the verification-layer idea is bigger I think. An agent that simulates every tx and refuses bad fills is a per-user execution guard +private order flow by default. If that's the interface, retail MEV compresses and agent demand for blockspace looks like intent flow, not raw txs. That's a more interesting than "agents make crypto safe." 

also "you'll never be phished" moves the attack surface to the agent. Prompt injection, poisoned context etc., it doesn't remove it altogether

author: marco_derossi
quoted_text:
how to get faster and cheaper videos from Opus 5.5

using a decision model for frame checks reduced video review costs by 90% and review time by 75%

when you create videos with Claude Opus 5.5, checking thousands of frames can consume a lot of time and tokens

you can set this up so a decision model checks the frames, while Opus 5.5 reviews the flagged issues and fixes the code

here's how it works:

1. build your video with Opus 5.5

give it your idea, brand book, assets and references, then work through the storyboard and animation

if you're using Remotion, it renders the code into a video

2. separate the repeated checks from the creative work

use code to check measurable requirements and a decision model to inspect the frames

> code checks things like text size, blank or frozen frames and colours against your brand rules

> the decision model reads the frames and answers specific questions to help identify problems

> selected frames and check results go to Opus 5.5 for further review

3. have Opus 5.5 investigate and fix the problems

it reviews the selected frames and edits the video code where needed

render the changes and run the checks again

this reduces the amount of frame-by-frame review you ask Opus 5.5 to do

4. review the finished video yourself

watch the pacing, sound, transitions and whether the video matches what you wanted to create

the automated checks help find defects, while you review the creative decisions and overall quality

SageCut is one implementation of this for Remotion videos

in the example Chris shared, Sage (decision model) read 3,153 frames for $0.16 (the frame-reading cost, not the full production cost)

the savings come from the review stage, rendering still takes time

start with a video you've already reviewed and check whether it catches the problems you found

then compare the review cost and time with your existing process

Lose to earn wasn’t a good idea at the end

quoted_text:
Papertrade is slowly rugging its own users🚨

The situation with $PAPER is getting ridiculous

For those unfamiliar, Papertrade launched on HyperEVM just 10 days ago, allowing users to trade with 1,000x leverage

every time you lost money or got liquidated, you received $PAPER

You could then stake those tokens to earn USDC from the protocol’s revenue

Well, in its first few days, Papertrade generated $1T in trading volume, with traders losing $54M and $45M distributed in staking rewards

Some people were even deliberately losing money to farm PAPER

One wallet lost $979K to mint 252M PAPER and received $1.87M in staking rewards within days

But yesterday, the team announced some pretty significant changes

First, $PAPER won’t be transferable anytime soon

Actually, the team said they have no plans to enable transfers outside the protocol at this stage

(Remember that users were farming this token expecting it to eventually become tradable)

Paragon, which had paid around $45K to secure the PAPER ticker on Hyperliquid’s HIP-3 infrastructure, immediately shut down its market

Aster did the same

The team is also changing PAPER’s emission model

Previously, the initial rate was 100 PAPER for every $1 lost

Under the new system, each $1M in eligible losses will mint approximately 0.1% of the existing supply

Meaning that as supply grows, more PAPER gets created for the same amount of losses

(existing holders get diluted)

The team literally acknowledged this in its announcement

So imagine being one of the earliest users, losing money to farm PAPER, and suddenly discovering that:

- You can’t transfer or sell your tokens
- The pre-market where people were trading them has disappeared
- Your share of future staking rewards will gradually be diluted
- The protocol is changing its fee structure too

Now, to be fair, the team has an explanation

They argue that allowing people to short PAPER externally could make attacks against the protocol’s liquidity pool profitable

But here’s my problem

If making PAPER transferable creates such a serious threat to the protocol, why wasn’t that risk properly addressed before people started farming it?

And why should early participants accept dilution after taking the biggest risks?

Especially when those people have no way to exit their positions

author: iqxsol
quoted_text:
A note on transferability.

Papertrade is a complicated primitive, and managing it from a risk standpoint is a complicated problem. The PAPER token is far more integrated into the economics of the primitive than most tokens are in their respective protocols today, and, broadly, was designed to act as a counter insolvency incentive coupled with a rebate mechanism to losing traders. Market makers and exchanges are by far the two most profitable businesses in crypto, and our goal was to try and externalise as much of their margins back to users as possible. We are now just over a week into the life of papertrade and we are becoming increasingly confident that this is both possible, but also a likely outcome as agentic led software becomes the norm. 

As it stands, the paper token traded as a perp becomes a leveraged bet on bankroll solvency - and being able to short bankroll solvency materially changes the payoff curve of a manipulation attack. The target number goes from the bankroll, to the bankroll + short side exposure on paper. We can, and do limit bankroll size specifically to control this payoff curve and ensure it never becomes existentially problematic, but external perp markets are not something we would have any control over if left to float of their own accord. For example, if our bankroll is $10m, an attack costing $15m manipulating the price of bitcoin or ether is not viable. You simply lose money. If however you were also able to put on $10m of PAPER short side exposure, suddenly an attack costing $15m is very viable indeed.

If we were to make the token transferable at this point, we are confident we would quickly enter a state too dangerous to allow any material exposure to be taken on papertrade, an end result that benefits no party beyond the wolves who have done the math on the short and are waiting in the wings with sharpened knives.

We would also like to thank the various perps teams who have reached out about pre-market listings for their understanding and patience regarding this issue, and especially to the paragon team who, despite jumping the gun on us, have behaved with the utmost integrity and transparency once a dialogue was opened.

Perps on PAPER will always act as a self-limiting exposure ceiling for a token with this type of utility, and we think it would be a shame to limit the growth of papertrade to the extent that allowing perps would necessitate. As such, at this juncture we do not have plans to allow off-contract token transferability.

Structurally, papertrade is limited by the quality of the data it receives from hyperliquid, but we strongly believe that hyperliquid has a very large part to play in the future of global exchanges, and expect their books to continue to thicken and strengthen over time.

A note on fees.

Papertrade launched with a deadband fee from entry of 0.2bps. This means you don't earn anything until the price has moved by 0.002% in your favour. Over the months before launch, we played around with many different curves and fee structures affecting exclusively positions closed very close to entry price in order to try and devise a structure that removed the edge against the bankroll low time frame scalp bots have, whilst also minimally impacting the traders around which and for whom the product was devised. We were never able to find anything we were absolutely happy with and so decided to stay with the 0.2bp deadband fee through launch. This has however meant we have had to be very restrictive when it came to certain parameters, such as OI caps.

Now, however, we have enough live data to fully understand exactly which strategies work, and to make the necessary changes to stop them. The changes we are making will have an on hours and off hours fee mode to account for the relative differences in liquidity the hyperliquid books see between these two time periods, and the ease with which low time frame moves are signalled. The changes we are making will only affect positions closed within 6bps of entry (0.06%) in on hours, and 10bps (0.1%) in off hours. Any trades closed above these threshold price shifts will see no change to their fees at all. On a look back to launch basis, these changes affect the profitability of bot strategies roughly 15x more than they do normal traders, for whom a very small proportion of overall winnings come from within this band.

These changes should serve to flatten much of the edge our microfee structure necessarily creates on low time frames, and will help with long term exchange sustainability. This should hopefully allow us to open up parameters such as OI caps a little more so those of you who wish to can put on the size you want to, when you want to.

It is possible these changes are still too lax, and that further revisions to this structure may be necessary going forwards. If so, we will notify users ahead of time.

A note on paper tokenomics. 

In conjunction with the fee changes, we will also be implementing a change to the token issuance curve.

Going forward, every $1 lost mints a fixed share of PAPER's supply at that moment, roughly 0.1% of supply per $1M lost (the exact number depends on the mint rate at the time the contracts are upgraded). PAPER minting in and near insolvency will also change, switching from a flat 100 per $1 of loss, to a time weighted multiplier on the curve growing over time, effectively acting as the house running a discounted auction on its own future cash flows. This change also removes the risk of the paper-mint-straddle-attack, temporarily pushing the protocol insolvent by closing only the winning side of a large straddle position and then attempting to mint as much paper as possible. 

In the immediate term these changes will only have a very subtle effect on PAPER minting, but in the long run will structurally change the outlook of the system beyond the first few weeks, serving to slowly dilute out older holders and leaving more recent users with an advantage. Reconstituting the PAPER system into something much closer to the exchange rakeback it was intended to be.

We have been very reticent to touch this particular aspect of the system for obvious reasons, but ultimately we believe that these changes provide all users with the optionality to take a smaller piece of a potentially much larger pie than the current dynamic might necessarily allow.

Other, miscellaneous notes.

These contract upgrades will include a few other contract changes, including the addition of builder codes so that builders can utilise papertrade in whatever capacity they choose to. This will be a whitelist only to begin with and we will have more for you later in the week on where/how this will be rolled out. A small change to contract permissions on the reward distributor and a change on how below bust closes are processed by the exchange are also included, largely to block gas griefing attacks. 

These changes will be pushed to docs in full over the coming day, and we will further announce once the changes are queued into the timelock pending final security passes, scheduled to go live 24 hours after that point.

Final note.

We'd like to thank everyone that has tried out papertrade over the last 10 days. It has been a labour of love building this product and both of us have been taken aback at all of the positive feedback we have received. We'd also like to thank all those of you who have spent considerable time musing on the system we have built, and much of your advice has been taken onboard and will likely affect the colour of what papertrade becomes going forward. We know some of these changes will be unpopular with some, but we would not be making them if we did not feel them to be absolutely necessary.

- blurr, jez

author: antiprosynth
quoted_text:
Two major pieces of Ethereum news landed today: Deutsche Bank, Germany’s largest bank, is reportedly preparing to offer institutional ETH custody, while JPMorgan, the largest bank in the United States, is bringing JPM Coin’s tokenized dollar deposits to Ethereum.

Two giants of traditional finance embracing Ethereum and ETH. But the price barely reacted, whereas on another network, people would be expecting a major pump.

There are two reasons for this. 

First, ETH is larger and more liquid than most competing assets, so it takes more buying pressure to move it. Second, the market already expects major institutions to build on Ethereum. Another announcement is not subverting expectations.

Some people might say Ethereum is cursed: success is expected, and it only has something to lose when it disappoints.

This is where Ethereum bulls diverge from bears.

For years, bulls predicted the adoption now materializing before our eyes. This was NOT consensus. People said institutions would never use Ethereum, or would build everything privately.

Now it’s: “That’s already priced in. Good for Ethereum, but how does it accrue value to ETH?”

There are two things that mentality ignores.

First, this is financial adoption, with size. The players matter, but so do the capital they commit, the assets they tokenize, and how deeply they integrate their products and services.

All of that shows growing trust in Ethereum as a financial network, both for people using layer one directly and for layer twos using it for settlement.

We are gradually building an internet of finance where the underlying network has one native asset: Ether.

ETH secures that system and can be used directly as collateral. Bringing Bitcoin or any other asset, into Ethereum requires additional backing, bridge, or custody arrangements. Native ETH already belongs there.

Why does this matter so much?
Financial activity settling on Ethereum does not pay Bitcoin’s miners. Bitcoin’s own security model anticipates transaction fees replacing its declining issuance. That activity will not magically show up on Bitcoin just because its proponents expect it to.

Second, the uncertainty pushed around ETH’s supply ignores what has actually happened.

Since the Merge, ETH’s net supply has grown roughly 1.3% in total, while continuing to reward the stakers securing it. Stakers can earn above supply dilution, with transaction income on top. For an asset used as a store of value, that cannot simply be ignored.

There is already actual substance behind ETH’s gradual recognition as a store of value. The network has matured. Proof of stake has years of operation behind it. Current SEC guidance identifies ETH as a digital commodity. The ETFs that critics said would never happen now exist, including BlackRock’s multibillion-dollar fund.

Treasury companies like Bitmine and Sharplink are accumulating ETH at scale, and their holdings can produce staking income. That adds another way for investors to gain exposure, and another reason to hold the asset.

So when bulls talk about ETH eventually flipping Bitcoin, then gold, this is what they are looking at: an asset with restrained supply growth, native yield, and direct usefulness in a growing financial system.

You can disagree with that thesis. But “the price didn’t move” does not answer it. Fundamentals are moving int the right direction, but price is a lagging metric.

Many of the things bulls expected are happening. The argument is that ETH is severely underpriced, and that the market still underestimates where it leads.

author: barnabemonnot
quoted_text:
There are many ways to tap into Ethereum’s unique features. Its two unique features to me are its decentralisation, and its state: liquidity, user accounts etc, all accumulated from 11 years of continuous uptime.

Decentralisation and trustlessness of the L1 have been the key to obtaining liquidity over time, including for ETH.

Some use cases want to tap into the chain’s decentralisation, and build to obtain the same properties that decentralisation offers: integrity, uptime and fair access (safety, liveness, censorship-resistance).

Some use cases want to tap into liquidity. This is not parasitic: this creates demand for L1-issued assets, in particular ETH.

Some use cases want to tap into both! But the liquidity is only there, once again, because of the L1’s decentralisation and trustlessness.

Making the L1 a better home for liquidity amplifies something that is originally there because of the L1’s core properties. In particular, L1 should serve as the root of trust for assets that go on to be deployed across various use cases.

Note that this argument does not depend on whether the use case in question is offered as “an L2” or not. L1 apps, including some tokens, may offer very little of the properties that the chain offers maximally. Let us not confuse the way a use case is packaged with the properties it offers. L2s themselves come in different shapes, and at the limit blur with what one might recognise as an L1 application.

So we need not pin our hopes on any one kind of package to realise the potential of Ethereum. We need not reject them either, when their success celebrates Ethereum’s unique offering to the world. We may even support their emergence, particularly so when providing them the means to succeed is aligned with improving the L1’s own core properties.

PALANTIR $PLTR CEO ALEX KARP SAYS MOST SOFTWARE IS BUILT TO TRAP YOU

And why he says that made Palantir hard to fund early on

Karp says a real business is one that eventually produces high-quality revenue, meaning free cash flow. 

You can only charge more than something costs to make if you do something unique, whether that's how you build it, distribute it or market it.

The minute someone else can do any part of that as well as you, your pricing power and your value start to fall.

His problem with most software is that it takes what makes your business unique, turns it into a commodity and sells it to everyone else.

He says early VCs wanted to hear the opposite of his pitch. What they wanted was "clients will be unhappy but they can't get rid of you." In other words, a bad marriage.

Palantir's pitch was that your data stays yours and you decide what gets shared. "You are not gonna be seeping your alpha to everyone else."

- Skip the ETH for gas. USDG trades on Robinhood Chain can run gasless, and the review shows "Gas covered by Exfil" when sponsorship is available. When it isn't, your ETH or a small $0.25 USDC top-up pays, as before.

- Deposit on every chain you can trade. Deposit now lists Solana, Base, BNB Smart Chain and Robinhood Chain, and each network says exactly what to send and where.

- Send straight to your own wallet on BNB Chain and Robinhood. USDT on BNB Smart Chain and USDG on Robinhood Chain go directly to your Exfil EVM address, with no bridge in between. BNB Smart Chain takes USDT only and counts as trading cash; USDG buys Robinhood coins.

- Fund from Base. Base deposits now work: send USDC or ETH on Base to a one-time deposit address and it arrives as Solana USDC. Live for everyone, no update needed.

- Only networks that lead to a trade. Arbitrum, Optimism and Ethereum are gone from Deposit, because money sent there couldn't be traded. Live for everyone.

- See the balance for the network you pick. Deposit shows USDT on BNB Smart Chain, USDG on Robinhood Chain, and Solana USDC and SOL for Solana and Base.

- No dead-end deposits. If Exfil can't cover gas for BNB Smart Chain USDT right now, Deposit hides that network and buys stop counting that USDT as spendable cash. Your portfolio still shows its value.

- Buy as big as you want. There's no buy cap and no minimum. Amount chips now run up to $100,000 and 100 SOL, Max uses your whole balance, and the amount field handles balances of $1M and above.

- Find settings faster. Wallet & Settings now has a Wallet | Settings switch, and the Profile gear opens straight to Settings.

- Settings in clear groups. Trading (slippage, price impact), Alerts, Privacy, Sound & help and Account (login email, referral code, wallets, account ID) each get their own card, followed by Support, Privacy policy, Sign out and Delete account.

- Know when your balance was read. The wallet shows one status line in your phone's time, like "Confirmed on-chain at 8:47 PM", and a failed refresh says when the amount on screen was last read.

- All your addresses in one card. Every network gets one row with its own copy button.

- Meet the scout on Android. The Android app icon and Play Store icon now use the same scout as iPhone, replacing the old pixel rat, and the rat stays whole in round and rounded-square launchers.

- A clearer App Store name. Pending review: Exfil Arena: Memecoin Scanner, with the subtitle "Holder check before you buy."

text:
今年 2 月，Anthropic 宣传 Claude Code 改造 COBOL 旧系统的能力后，IBM 股价单日重挫 13.2%。

八个月后，OpenAI 也公布了 GPT-6 系列在老旧编程语言上的最新成绩，其中 COBOL 代码迁移测试的最高成功率达到 97.9%。

COBOL 诞生于上世纪 50 年代，至今仍广泛用于银行交易、ATM 和保险系统。许多程序运行了几十年，原开发者早已离职，部分业务规则甚至只存在于代码里。

将它们改写成现代语言，不仅得让代码跑起来，还得保证计算结果完全一致。比如 COBOL 在定点数运算中，如果没有明确要求四舍五入，就会直接舍弃多余的小数位。新程序如果改成四舍五入，就可能导致金融账目出错。

OpenAI 专门测试了 AI 将 COBOL 程序改写成 C++、Java、Python、Rust 等语言的能力，要求新旧程序在测试中的输出逐字节一致。GPT-6.1 Sol 在低推理档位下的成功率达到 86.6%，上一代 GPT-5.6 Sol 只有 5.4%，估算 API 成本还降低了 39%。提高推理档位后，成功率进一步达到 97.9%。

OpenAI 还开源了 MultiLangBench，要求 AI 分别用 20 种编程语言，从零编写兼容 SQLite 的数据库引擎。GPT-6 Astra 的平均测试通过率达到 87.4%，GPT-5.6 Sol 为 26.8%。其中，两款模型在 COBOL 上分别得到 72.1% 和 10.9%，这也是 20 种语言中最难的一种。

text:
Becoming an RL diehard in the past year and thinking about RL for most of my waking hours inadvertently taught me an important lesson about how to live my own life.

One of the big concepts in RL is that you always want to be “on-policy”: instead of mimicking other people’s successful trajectories, you should take your own actions and learn from the reward given by the environment. Obviously imitation learning is useful to bootstrap to nonzero pass rate initially, but once you can take reasonable trajectories, we generally avoid imitation learning because the best way to leverage the model’s own strengths (which are different from humans) is to only learn from its own trajectories. A well-accepted instantiation of this is that RL is a better way to train language models to solve math word problems compared to simple supervised finetuning on human-written chains of thought.

Similarly in life, we first bootstrap ourselves via imitation learning (school), which is very reasonable. But even after I graduated school, I had a habit of studying how other people found success and trying to imitate them. Sometimes it worked, but eventually I realized that I would never surpass the full ability of someone else because they were playing to their strengths which I didn’t have. It could be anything from a researcher doing yolo runs more successfully than me because they built the codebase themselves and I didn’t, or a non-AI example would be a soccer player keeping ball possession by leveraging strength that I didn’t have.

The lesson of doing RL on policy is that beating the teacher requires walking your own path and taking risks and rewards from the environment. For example, two things I enjoy more than the average researcher are (1) reading a lot of data, and (2) doing ablations to understand the effect of individual components in a system. Once when collecting a dataset, I spent a few days reading data and giving each human annotator personalized feedback, and after that the data turned out great and I gained valuable insight into the task I was trying to solve. Earlier this year I spent a month going back and ablating each of the decisions that I previously yolo’ed while working on deep research. It was a sizable amount of time spent, but through those experiments I learned unique lessons about what type of RL works well. Not only was leaning into my own passions more fulfilling, but I now feel like I’m on a path to carving a stronger niche for myself and my research.

In short, imitation is good and you have to do it initially. But once you’re bootstrapped enough, if you want to beat the teacher you must do on-policy RL and play to your own strengths and weaknesses :)

text:
前两天看到一个采访问到 Jeff，现在如果再创业，有什么好的方向，Jeff 给到了一个回答是 —— 期权 Options，而且明确表示，期权就是 Hyperliquid 下一个重点方向，非常有可能是 HIP-5。Lighter/Variational 也都将期权列为下一个重点。

2025 年全球可统计的交易所期权成交约 886.5 亿张，市场规模不可小觑。crypto 除去币安、OKX、Bybit 未公开外，最大的期权交易平台 Deribit 日均名义交易量 25-40 亿美金不定，BTC OI常年在 300 亿上下，季度到期前能干到 400 亿。

链上最大的期权 Derive 几乎占了整个链上期权赛道的 98%，一天的名义交易量仅不到 1 亿美金，整个平台的 OI 在 18 亿美金左右，日均收入在 2w美金左右。但我们要知道，Derive 是一个仅提供 12 个标的的期权市场。

交易量上，Derive 大约是 Deribit 的 1/30。
OI 上，Derive 大约是 Deribit 的 1/20。

同为链上赛道龙头，对比永续合约，Hyperliquid 的 OI 约为最大的交易所币安的 1/5，交易量是 1/8。

由上数据可知，链上期权，不管是中短期，还是未来整体的市场规模，都具有很大的发展空间，这体现在交易品类、交易量还有 OI 上。

Perp 和 Options 各有优缺点，期权相比于合约，买 put 仅损失保证金，给现货套了保险，操作合适不会有强平风险，而合约更适合快速消除当前方向风险。但有不确定的费率和强平风险。

在传统股票领域，大的做市商、券商还有机构都会用期权来管理整个库存和尾部风险。而在 Crypto，面对未来 全面 Perp 化的交易标的，期权是随之增长的 Beta 赛道。

至于 Derive 如何做起来的？我觉得一是产品给力，推出第一个链上期权 Portfolio Margin 机制，更多可能是吃到了链上整个衍生品发展的红利。加上代币经济学的改进，使其被市场注意。还有一个更有意思的一个数据我放评论区。

所以，如果一个交易所同时可以提供 Perps 和 Options，那做市商、机构完全有可能在一个交易所完成风险对冲，而不必在多个平台之间高频交易，这对机构来说少了很多 latency 和多点风险，交易平台的流动性整合更容易。

对散户来说，当然是多一个赌博的工具啦，当我看到 Derive 期权图，有限亏损换取无限回报，第一反应是——哇！还有这好事，但后来一想，100x 合约不也是有限亏损对应的无限回报嘛，哈哈。

text:
$META 担保 280 亿，财报负债是 0 ？

之前讨论 $CRWV 和 $ORCL 的债券收益率上涨，
现在标普都警告， AI 巨头们的实际债务风险比想象中高。

摩根士丹利统计出，单单微软、谷歌、亚马逊、Meta、甲骨文，加上英伟达和博通这 7 家公司涉及的担保和租赁等其他财务承诺，就超过 3.1 万亿美元。

我们用 $META 来当例子，
由 $META 主导和外部投资一起推进的 Hyperion 数据中心项目。
开发成本大概是 270 亿美元，$META 只持有 20 % 的股权，
但提供了 280 亿美元的残值担保。
什么是残值担保？
就是 $META 需要为这个项目兜底，
如果未来 Meta 不再续租这个数据中心，
而数据中心剩余价值低于约定金额， $META需要给投资方补偿差额。

我们假设 280 亿美元的残值担保，
如果未来数据中心价值 300 亿美元，Meta 不需要补偿。
如果只剩 250 亿美元，可能需要补偿 30 亿美元。
如果只剩 200 亿美元，就可能需要补偿 80 亿美元，以此类推。

现在我们再看回 $META 第二季度财报，这笔残值担保虽然有披露，
但现在触发残值担保付款的可能性比较低，所以在财报上确认的担保负债是 0 美元。

但是 0 美元不代表是 0 风险。
更何况，这只是那么多的科技巨头里其中一个项目。
AI 收入能兑现是一回事，这些巨型财务承诺可不可以履行也是另一回事。

$TORCH 14.6m dyor

0x000050e18ffa3f8f7ad170eb9cef160eb3ed1111

okx wallet:https://t.co/TVOhrFHGgB

A multi-chain trading + token launch platform, focused on "one balance, cross-chain operations."

It integrates a trading terminal, a Telegram trading bot, and a fair launchpad. The core idea: users can use just one balance to buy and sell tokens across multiple chains, launch new tokens, and trade cross-chain—without manually moving funds around or managing a bunch of wallets.

The core pain points the project aims to solve:

Multi-chain trading is too much hassle.

Traditional launchpads are prone to "liquidity pulls" or team rug pulls.

Most launchpads are just "extraction"—creators take their fees and leave, with no ongoing rewards for holders.

The full memecoin cycle is too fragmented.

So Torch wants to put this entire loop into one platform.

The product currently has three main components:

Terminal: token discovery, trading, limit orders, take-profit/stop-loss, portfolio tracking, Alpha feed, and token launches.

Telegram Bot: paste a contract address to quickly buy/sell, set take-profit/stop-loss, bridge, etc.

Launchpad: one-click token launches on Robinhood Chain.

Features:

At launch, 100% of the supply goes directly into a Uniswap v4 pool, with liquidity permanently locked.

No bonding curve, no migration.

Configurable buy tax (creator 70% / protocol 30%). Creators can choose to keep the money for themselves, use it for buybacks and burns, or distribute it to holders.

Multi-chain support.

TORCH is the platform token, with the main functions:

Value capture: a portion of platform trading fees and launch-related revenue flows back to holders.

Burn mechanism: trading triggers buybacks and burns of the token, continuously reducing supply.

Pairing asset: new tokens can be launched paired with TORCH.

Holder returns:
70% of the 2% buy tax goes to holders (in the early stage, most of this is used for buybacks and burns).
About 25% of net platform revenue is also distributed to holders based on their holdings.

text:
I love Job for many reasons, but mainly because it does a very clever jujitsu move on you as a reader. You start out thinking you've seen behind the curtain -- the scene in heaven w/ God & Satan making bets about Job.

So then after Job's trials, as his four friends come visit him to give their theories of why Job is in the predicament he's in, you've got your own little theory based on the opening scene, right? You're essentially the fifth friend who has their own read of the situation.

Then God comes in at the end and is like, "all your theories are wrong. None of you were there at The Beginning, and none of you know enough of the real backstory to really understand what's happening here. None of you can actually tame the chaos monster and organize all the things into a coherent whole. Only I can do that." 

You, the reader, think God is calling out Job and maybe his four friends. But He's calling you out, too. You, the reader, are in the same boat as Job and his four friends. You think you have enough info about what is going on with Job because you saw the opening scene in heaven, but actually you're just as clueless and limited as the story's characters.

So the opener of the story is actually a trap, and the conclusion springs it on you. You think you have the backstory via some special perspective, but you're just like all the other confused people in the story. You don't really know and you're not ever going to know, either.

Job's lesson is that not only does God not owe you a theodicy (so stop expecting one), but even if you could see into the unseen realm you still wouldn't have a clue. You're never going to have enough information to put the whole, chaotic picture together in some satisfactory way. It's never going to all hang together in a coherent way that makes sense.

In some ways, I think Job is a coming of age story. This is one of things you learn in midlife -- that the pieces actually didn't ever fit together like you once thought they did, and the fact that it used to make coherent sense to you says more about who you were in that phase of life than it does about any larger meaning behind the events themselves.

The Job story is literally yelling at you that you cannot organize the chaos of life events into a coherent "why" -- it's simply beyond you. That you once thought you could was the arrogance of youth. God is actually the only one strong enough to tame the chaos monster & split its carcass into a neat, ordered, coherent structure.

This isn't the answer anyone wants, but it's the only answer that's telling you like it is.

Anyway, Job is a great book. The haters are wrong. I like it because I don't like to be lied to.

quoted_text:
A note on transferability.

Papertrade is a complicated primitive, and managing it from a risk standpoint is a complicated problem. The PAPER token is far more integrated into the economics of the primitive than most tokens are in their respective protocols today, and, broadly, was designed to act as a counter insolvency incentive coupled with a rebate mechanism to losing traders. Market makers and exchanges are by far the two most profitable businesses in crypto, and our goal was to try and externalise as much of their margins back to users as possible. We are now just over a week into the life of papertrade and we are becoming increasingly confident that this is both possible, but also a likely outcome as agentic led software becomes the norm. 

As it stands, the paper token traded as a perp becomes a leveraged bet on bankroll solvency - and being able to short bankroll solvency materially changes the payoff curve of a manipulation attack. The target number goes from the bankroll, to the bankroll + short side exposure on paper. We can, and do limit bankroll size specifically to control this payoff curve and ensure it never becomes existentially problematic, but external perp markets are not something we would have any control over if left to float of their own accord. For example, if our bankroll is $10m, an attack costing $15m manipulating the price of bitcoin or ether is not viable. You simply lose money. If however you were also able to put on $10m of PAPER short side exposure, suddenly an attack costing $15m is very viable indeed.

If we were to make the token transferable at this point, we are confident we would quickly enter a state too dangerous to allow any material exposure to be taken on papertrade, an end result that benefits no party beyond the wolves who have done the math on the short and are waiting in the wings with sharpened knives.

We would also like to thank the various perps teams who have reached out about pre-market listings for their understanding and patience regarding this issue, and especially to the paragon team who, despite jumping the gun on us, have behaved with the utmost integrity and transparency once a dialogue was opened.

Perps on PAPER will always act as a self-limiting exposure ceiling for a token with this type of utility, and we think it would be a shame to limit the growth of papertrade to the extent that allowing perps would necessitate. As such, at this juncture we do not have plans to allow off-contract token transferability.

Structurally, papertrade is limited by the quality of the data it receives from hyperliquid, but we strongly believe that hyperliquid has a very large part to play in the future of global exchanges, and expect their books to continue to thicken and strengthen over time.

A note on fees.

Papertrade launched with a deadband fee from entry of 0.2bps. This means you don't earn anything until the price has moved by 0.002% in your favour. Over the months before launch, we played around with many different curves and fee structures affecting exclusively positions closed very close to entry price in order to try and devise a structure that removed the edge against the bankroll low time frame scalp bots have, whilst also minimally impacting the traders around which and for whom the product was devised. We were never able to find anything we were absolutely happy with and so decided to stay with the 0.2bp deadband fee through launch. This has however meant we have had to be very restrictive when it came to certain parameters, such as OI caps.

Now, however, we have enough live data to fully understand exactly which strategies work, and to make the necessary changes to stop them. The changes we are making will have an on hours and off hours fee mode to account for the relative differences in liquidity the hyperliquid books see between these two time periods, and the ease with which low time frame moves are signalled. The changes we are making will only affect positions closed within 6bps of entry (0.06%) in on hours, and 10bps (0.1%) in off hours. Any trades closed above these threshold price shifts will see no change to their fees at all. On a look back to launch basis, these changes affect the profitability of bot strategies roughly 15x more than they do normal traders, for whom a very small proportion of overall winnings come from within this band.

These changes should serve to flatten much of the edge our microfee structure necessarily creates on low time frames, and will help with long term exchange sustainability. This should hopefully allow us to open up parameters such as OI caps a little more so those of you who wish to can put on the size you want to, when you want to.

It is possible these changes are still too lax, and that further revisions to this structure may be necessary going forwards. If so, we will notify users ahead of time.

A note on paper tokenomics. 

In conjunction with the fee changes, we will also be implementing a change to the token issuance curve.

Going forward, every $1 lost mints a fixed share of PAPER's supply at that moment, roughly 0.1% of supply per $1M lost (the exact number depends on the mint rate at the time the contracts are upgraded). PAPER minting in and near insolvency will also change, switching from a flat 100 per $1 of loss, to a time weighted multiplier on the curve growing over time, effectively acting as the house running a discounted auction on its own future cash flows. This change also removes the risk of the paper-mint-straddle-attack, temporarily pushing the protocol insolvent by closing only the winning side of a large straddle position and then attempting to mint as much paper as possible. 

In the immediate term these changes will only have a very subtle effect on PAPER minting, but in the long run will structurally change the outlook of the system beyond the first few weeks, serving to slowly dilute out older holders and leaving more recent users with an advantage. Reconstituting the PAPER system into something much closer to the exchange rakeback it was intended to be.

We have been very reticent to touch this particular aspect of the system for obvious reasons, but ultimately we believe that these changes provide all users with the optionality to take a smaller piece of a potentially much larger pie than the current dynamic might necessarily allow.

Other, miscellaneous notes.

These contract upgrades will include a few other contract changes, including the addition of builder codes so that builders can utilise papertrade in whatever capacity they choose to. This will be a whitelist only to begin with and we will have more for you later in the week on where/how this will be rolled out. A small change to contract permissions on the reward distributor and a change on how below bust closes are processed by the exchange are also included, largely to block gas griefing attacks. 

These changes will be pushed to docs in full over the coming day, and we will further announce once the changes are queued into the timelock pending final security passes, scheduled to go live 24 hours after that point.

Final note.

We'd like to thank everyone that has tried out papertrade over the last 10 days. It has been a labour of love building this product and both of us have been taken aback at all of the positive feedback we have received. We'd also like to thank all those of you who have spent considerable time musing on the system we have built, and much of your advice has been taken onboard and will likely affect the colour of what papertrade becomes going forward. We know some of these changes will be unpopular with some, but we would not be making them if we did not feel them to be absolutely necessary.

- blurr, jez
