author: cryptoleon
quoted_text:
A note on transferability.

Papertrade is a complicated primitive, and managing it from a risk standpoint is a complicated problem. The PAPER token is far more integrated into the economics of the primitive than most tokens are in their respective protocols today, and, broadly, was designed to act as a counter insolvency incentive coupled with a rebate mechanism to losing traders. Market makers and exchanges are by far the two most profitable businesses in crypto, and our goal was to try and externalise as much of their margins back to users as possible. We are now just over a week into the life of papertrade and we are becoming increasingly confident that this is both possible, but also a likely outcome as agentic led software becomes the norm. 

As it stands, the paper token traded as a perp becomes a leveraged bet on bankroll solvency - and being able to short bankroll solvency materially changes the payoff curve of a manipulation attack. The target number goes from the bankroll, to the bankroll + short side exposure on paper. We can, and do limit bankroll size specifically to control this payoff curve and ensure it never becomes existentially problematic, but external perp markets are not something we would have any control over if left to float of their own accord. For example, if our bankroll is $10m, an attack costing $15m manipulating the price of bitcoin or ether is not viable. You simply lose money. If however you were also able to put on $10m of PAPER short side exposure, suddenly an attack costing $15m is very viable indeed.

If we were to make the token transferable at this point, we are confident we would quickly enter a state too dangerous to allow any material exposure to be taken on papertrade, an end result that benefits no party beyond the wolves who have done the math on the short and are waiting in the wings with sharpened knives.

We would also like to thank the various perps teams who have reached out about pre-market listings for their understanding and patience regarding this issue, and especially to the paragon team who, despite jumping the gun on us, have behaved with the utmost integrity and transparency once a dialogue was opened.

Perps on PAPER will always act as a self-limiting exposure ceiling for a token with this type of utility, and we think it would be a shame to limit the growth of papertrade to the extent that allowing perps would necessitate. As such, at this juncture we do not have plans to allow off-contract token transferability.

Structurally, papertrade is limited by the quality of the data it receives from hyperliquid, but we strongly believe that hyperliquid has a very large part to play in the future of global exchanges, and expect their books to continue to thicken and strengthen over time.

A note on fees.

Papertrade launched with a deadband fee from entry of 0.2bps. This means you don't earn anything until the price has moved by 0.002% in your favour. Over the months before launch, we played around with many different curves and fee structures affecting exclusively positions closed very close to entry price in order to try and devise a structure that removed the edge against the bankroll low time frame scalp bots have, whilst also minimally impacting the traders around which and for whom the product was devised. We were never able to find anything we were absolutely happy with and so decided to stay with the 0.2bp deadband fee through launch. This has however meant we have had to be very restrictive when it came to certain parameters, such as OI caps.

Now, however, we have enough live data to fully understand exactly which strategies work, and to make the necessary changes to stop them. The changes we are making will have an on hours and off hours fee mode to account for the relative differences in liquidity the hyperliquid books see between these two time periods, and the ease with which low time frame moves are signalled. The changes we are making will only affect positions closed within 6bps of entry (0.06%) in on hours, and 10bps (0.1%) in off hours. Any trades closed above these threshold price shifts will see no change to their fees at all. On a look back to launch basis, these changes affect the profitability of bot strategies roughly 15x more than they do normal traders, for whom a very small proportion of overall winnings come from within this band.

These changes should serve to flatten much of the edge our microfee structure necessarily creates on low time frames, and will help with long term exchange sustainability. This should hopefully allow us to open up parameters such as OI caps a little more so those of you who wish to can put on the size you want to, when you want to.

It is possible these changes are still too lax, and that further revisions to this structure may be necessary going forwards. If so, we will notify users ahead of time.

A note on paper tokenomics. 

In conjunction with the fee changes, we will also be implementing a change to the token issuance curve.

Going forward, every $1 lost mints a fixed share of PAPER's supply at that moment, roughly 0.1% of supply per $1M lost (the exact number depends on the mint rate at the time the contracts are upgraded). PAPER minting in and near insolvency will also change, switching from a flat 100 per $1 of loss, to a time weighted multiplier on the curve growing over time, effectively acting as the house running a discounted auction on its own future cash flows. This change also removes the risk of the paper-mint-straddle-attack, temporarily pushing the protocol insolvent by closing only the winning side of a large straddle position and then attempting to mint as much paper as possible. 

In the immediate term these changes will only have a very subtle effect on PAPER minting, but in the long run will structurally change the outlook of the system beyond the first few weeks, serving to slowly dilute out older holders and leaving more recent users with an advantage. Reconstituting the PAPER system into something much closer to the exchange rakeback it was intended to be.

We have been very reticent to touch this particular aspect of the system for obvious reasons, but ultimately we believe that these changes provide all users with the optionality to take a smaller piece of a potentially much larger pie than the current dynamic might necessarily allow.

Other, miscellaneous notes.

These contract upgrades will include a few other contract changes, including the addition of builder codes so that builders can utilise papertrade in whatever capacity they choose to. This will be a whitelist only to begin with and we will have more for you later in the week on where/how this will be rolled out. A small change to contract permissions on the reward distributor and a change on how below bust closes are processed by the exchange are also included, largely to block gas griefing attacks. 

These changes will be pushed to docs in full over the coming day, and we will further announce once the changes are queued into the timelock pending final security passes, scheduled to go live 24 hours after that point.

Final note.

We'd like to thank everyone that has tried out papertrade over the last 10 days. It has been a labour of love building this product and both of us have been taken aback at all of the positive feedback we have received. We'd also like to thank all those of you who have spent considerable time musing on the system we have built, and much of your advice has been taken onboard and will likely affect the colour of what papertrade becomes going forward. We know some of these changes will be unpopular with some, but we would not be making them if we did not feel them to be absolutely necessary.

- blurr, jez

text: 国际清算银行（BIS）10 月 19 日发布第 1385 号工作论文，比较传统银行、Wise 和 Remitly 等金融科技平台及稳定币的跨境支付成本，指出稳定币并非解决跨境支付成本问题的“万能药”。研究发现，在传统银行电汇的小规模样本中，外汇兑换加价约为 2% 至 4.7%，相比之下，从美国向部分发达市场汇款 1 万美元，金融科技平台的费用中位数约为 40 至 60 美元。报告认为，稳定币在部分实施资本管制的新兴市场具有汇率优势，但这更多源于资本管制及美元需求造成的市场价差，而非区块链技术本身的效率提升。https://t.co/EjrN93vMtY

text:
我觉得卡牌收藏界的Hyperliquid正在诞生！🧐 @Collector_Crypt

8月份香港那次 #BTCAsia 大会，让我真正感受到宝可梦卡牌🃏收藏的火爆，以及金明老师的卡牌10倍的投资回报，也让我触动比较大！

作为Z时代，新收藏品类，这几年爆发力，肉眼可见的正在走向主流，尤其是香港很多商场，包括广州正佳广场，基本都有一层楼，专门做卡牌店铺以及玩家对战。

而今天看到 solana:CARDSccUMFKoPRZxt5vt3ksUbxEFEcnZ3H2pd3dKxYjp 创下新高，心里十分激动和开心，这次主要的刺激原因是PumpFun的集成，导致ADU日活，爆发性增长，单日突破了3157人(如👇图1)！

今天正好趁着创新高，讲讲前不久团队做的投研笔记👇！

📝 先说结论：作为Solana链上的卡牌 Gacha 项目，产品是个现金牛，护城河在后端，代币还得再观察。🧐

咱们先看数据：

• 团队只有 8 个人
• 第二季度 GMV 4.061 亿美元
• 净营收 3220 万美元
• 人均创收 400 万美元

整体来看，8 个人能干出这个量级，跟早期的Hyperliquid有的一拼，团队效率杠杠滴。

🤔产品解决的痛点：

传统卡牌交易里，买到一张卡只是开始。鉴定、保管、找买家、议价、收款、寄送，每一步都要花时间。卡越贵，对信任的要求越高。

Collector Crypt 通过链上方式，有效解决了上述痛点。他们把卡放在金库里，让对应的链上凭证自由流转。只要用户暂时不提走实物，卡牌换多少次主人，都不用反复寄快递。抽到不想要的卡，还可以在72小时内卖回给平台，回购金额按卡牌的保险估值计算，然后再按照85%、90%、93% 的比例来回购。

对于用户来说，这个体验感十分不错，享受了多巴胺抽卡的刺激，但却不用操心怎么处理抽到的卡，而且抽到稀有款，还能大赚一笔，这种天然有成瘾性。

对于平台来说，用户卖回卡，卡又进入金库；用户拿到钱，可以离开，也可以继续买卡包。一张卡能够参与很多轮交易，平台就在这些交易中赚取差额，可谓是无敌好生意。

🎯聊聊项目的优势：

1️⃣门槛降低了。以前抽卡基本是大鲸鱼在玩，现在新增了 50、100、250 美元的价位，还接入了 Jupiter 入口，小资金玩家也能进来体验。

2️⃣全链上透明。从实体卡牌评级到抽取记录，都能在 Solana 上查。抽到不想要的卡，还能按保险估值的 85%~93% 卖回平台，等于有个流动性兜底，传统实体抽卡根本做不到。

3️⃣金库自己运营了。今年春天把金库转成内部运营，不再依赖第三方（比如 PSA）排队积压，兑换更快、成本更低，还补贴运费。从NFT数字卡到拿到实体卡，这个闭环顺畅多了。

🎯再聊聊护城河，这是我最看重的：

很多人觉得壁垒是网页前端或者玩法，我不这么看。真正的门槛是后端的库存管理和物理循环。

为什么？开放卡池有个致命弱点，便宜的卡被抽光，池子就被掏空了，之前就有竞争对手因此崩盘。想撑住卡池深度，就得有庞大的实物库存：

• 资金门槛高，要从线下展会、eBay、批量货源持续补货
• 采购节奏难，卡牌市场虚高的时候不能硬着头皮追高进货

再看它的循环：用户抽卡 → 不要的卡折价卖回 → 评级卡回到机器 → 平台拿钱再去市场补货。

这套东西已经跑了数亿美元 GMV，不是写几个智能合约就能抄走的。

还有一个数据：第二季度 TCG 赛道（Collector Crypt、Courtyard、Phygitals 等）总 GMV 7.936 亿美元，它自己就占了 51.2%，超过半数，未来马太效应会更强，如👇图3。

📊潜力和风险：

• 第三季度毛利约 2500 万美元，8 个人的团队，现金流相当充沛。
• 前期刻意把赔率调得对用户有利，先抢规模、再谈变现，现在还在吃市场的阶段。

最关键的是 solana:CARDSccUMFKoPRZxt5vt3ksUbxEFEcnZ3H2pd3dKxYjp 代币。

产品很强，但代币经济学价值捕获比较弱，公开数据统计，第三季度用于 solana:CARDSccUMFKoPRZxt5vt3ksUbxEFEcnZ3H2pd3dKxYjp 回购的金额约为 56.7 万美元，相当于同期毛利润的 2.2%，这个比例，太低了。

值得注意的是，10月29日有一波代币解锁，后续 Tokenomics 怎么更新，一定要盯紧，据说要开启大比例回购方案。一旦开启回购模式，整个代币的估值逻辑就会不一样了。反过来，没有任何价值捕获，那就只是个故事。

总结一下：

• 优势：团队高效、赚钱能力强、卡池透明、回收有流动性
• 护城河：线下供应链 + 实物库存 + 正向回收循环
• 潜力：份额过半，就看代币能不能真正赋能

纯个人研究笔记，非投资建议，DYOR🙏

text:
Over the past few months, the @Nethermind Client team has been focusing on almost everything BUT performance - authoring, supporting and reviewing EIPs for Glamsterdam, championing Hegota headliner - Frame Transactions, researching state bloat, and much more.

That's not changing - we are still being heavily involved in Ethereum roadmap. But AI has unlocked a whole new level of productivity for us, and we're now pushing hard on several fronts:

1. zk guest program - coming soon to @eth_proofs. Very promising, very performant.
2. RPC refresh - Geth compatibility, major performance improvements, and more. Few projects already got a feeling of what we are shipping - and it is looking very good.
3. Client hardening with AI - Node MCP for users and our custom CoreMCP for developers, helping us ship faster and build a much more stable client.
4. Innovative node optimizations and advanced plugins - unlocking capabilities that could be extremely useful for many projects across the ecosystem, including support for new chains.

And that's just the beginning.

As a "side effect," we've also significantly improved the node's performance at the tip of the chain - before even getting into the Glamsterdam hard fork, which should unlock a whole new level of throughput.

Nethermind is the fastest #Ethereum execution client, and the only one pushing beyond 1.5 GGas/s in p50 block throughput at the tip of the chain.

With the next fork, we expect that ceiling to go even higher - based on Sepolia data, potentially around 3x higher.

And we're definitely not done.

We want to change the rules of the game. The AI-powered tools we've built in-house are giving us enormous leverage, and we're confident this advantage will only grow over time.

Performance is good. 🚀

text:
马斯克刚在一段访谈里扔出了一个非常反常识的工程暴论，把算力中心搬上太空，芯片根本不该追求低温冷静，反而应该专门设计在高温状态下狂飙，而且几万亿参数的大模型压根不在乎宇宙辐射带来的那几个数据错误。
他在视频里当场算了一笔极硬核的物理账，在没有空气对流的太空里，芯片散热全靠热辐射，

只要把芯片的工作温度按开尔文温标拉高 20%，整个散热器的重量就能直接砍掉一半，

至于太空高能粒子打穿内存造成的随机位翻转，在几万亿参数的神经网络面前根本不痛不痒。

平时我们在地球上建数据中心、攒高配工作站，默认铁律是散热越猛越好、数据越准越好，机房恨不得泡在液冷池里，传统航天芯片更是要花几百倍的成本加装厚重的防辐射装甲，生怕宇宙射线把哪一个 0 撞成了 1 导致整套系统当场死机。

但老马直接用第一性原理把这两座大山全给掀了，他点破了一个从来没人敢捅破的底层差异：传统软件写的是死板的启发式规则，错一个字符整行代码就崩了，

但几万亿参数的大模型本质是一张极其庞大的概率网，里面偶尔被宇宙射线撞歪几个数字，就像在太平洋里扔了一颗石子，模型自带的容错弹性直接就给消化掉了。

这就像你在战场上派人送一封绝密军令，传统程序是一个独行信使，挨一枪任务就彻底失败，所以你得给他穿上几百斤重的防弹铁甲，

而多万亿参数的大模型是一支浩浩荡荡的百万大军，哪怕路上擦破几个士兵的皮毛，大部队照样按原定路线平推过去，既然队伍本身就不怕擦伤，你干脆把那身笨重的铁甲和降温水箱全扔了，轻装上阵才能跑得最快。

说白了，这不只是在聊怎么把算力送上近地轨道，更是给所有做系统架构、带技术团队的人上了一堂极透彻的冗余清理课，很多时候把我们拖垮的根本不是核心难题，而是我们习惯性把上一代系统的保命规矩，原封不动地背到了新一代架构身上，大模型既然天生具备模糊容错的本事，工程重心就该从死保每一个字节不出错，全面转向怎么把硬件压榨到物理极限。

不过听老马畅想太空高温算力时，从另外一个角度看，他手里握着 SpaceX 的星舰运力和 xAI 的庞大算力需求，鼓吹轻量化太空计算中心本就最符合他的商业版图，况且在真实的模型推理中，如果宇宙射线恰好撞翻了浮点数里的指数位，或者打中了负责调度显存的底层控制代码，照样会引发数值溢出或整机崩溃，在关键控制层做内存屏蔽依然省不掉。

这就是三流的工程是在旧规则里堆料加固，一流的工程是看清新物种的脾气，把不再需要的安全感直接砍掉一半。 https://t.co/QhKuCAHI6W
author: AYi_AInotes
quoted_text:
花了1个多小时深度复盘了10个月涨粉7万+、跑完近两亿曝光之后，我才彻底想通：在 X 上做个人品牌，本质上不是文科写作，更像是一门严密的信息工程学， 就像马斯克当年拒绝相信火箭必须昂贵一样，你必须敢于推翻所有道听途说的做号常识， 而只有当你把内容拆成注意力抓取、信息密度压缩与可迁移价值这三个基本构件时，增长就不再是一门碰运气的玄学，而是一套可以稳定复现的工业流水线。

早在 2014 年，马斯克在 SpaceX 总部创办学校时，对着一群孩子讲过一段极少公开的镜头：
让我们来看看火箭的物理学和经济学，与其接受别人说的不可能，不如把它拆解到最基础的原材料，看看物理法则真正允许什么。

正是这种思维造出了可回收火箭，而如果把这套第一性原理用到今天做 X 自媒体上，你会发现全网绝大多数的运营教程全在带你走弯路。

几乎所有人在教你追热点、发短推、讨好算法，但如果你把这套系统的底层逻辑拆到最基本的粒子，真相正好完全相反。

最先被物理学击碎的常识，是所谓的追逐热门奇观。
 很多人以为几百万曝光的娱乐热点是做号的捷径，但后台的转化数据极其残酷：路过看热闹的人转化率只有可怜的千分之八；

在 X 这个高认知密度的人群里，信息压缩才是你唯一的产品，别人关注你从来不是因为你说了什么俏皮话，而是因为你替他读完了最难懂的原文，并把几十个小时的信息差提炼成了一张可以当场抄作业的硬核底牌。
更反直觉的真相，在于长短推文对信任建立的绝对分水岭。
 传统观念总觉得大家在信息流里浮躁、文字越短越好，但数据证明不到一百四十个字的碎片短推，涨粉中位数几乎就是零，

真正能引发高倍收藏与关注的，永远是四百字以上、带有完整推演过程与架构图的深度长推。读者只有在你的长文里看清了你思考的骨架，才会判定你是一个值得长期置顶的资产。

而在算法层面，最顶级的流量密码从来不是在结尾求赞求转发。
 在平台的推荐机制里，权重最高的正向动作是读者把你的推文复制链接发给同事，以及在评论区引发高质量的深度辩论，

当你给出的框架足够硬、留下的判断足够犀利，读者自然会把你当成整个行业的翻译官和吹哨人。

以前大家以为自媒体是比拼文笔的修辞游戏，用第一性原理拆开才发现： 文字只是导线，情绪只是包装，真正产生核聚变的，永远是你向读者交付的认知密度。
大家在刷推时，最能让你毫不犹豫点击关注并设为特别关注的博主，往往具备哪一个特征？我先说，只要一个人能持续把我看不懂的技术内幕拆成大白话，并且敢在第一句话就亮出极其锋利的独立判断，我当场就会按下关注。 https://t.co/ieV7kC2P8n

A note on transferability.

Papertrade is a complicated primitive, and managing it from a risk standpoint is a complicated problem. The PAPER token is far more integrated into the economics of the primitive than most tokens are in their respective protocols today, and, broadly, was designed to act as a counter insolvency incentive coupled with a rebate mechanism to losing traders. Market makers and exchanges are by far the two most profitable businesses in crypto, and our goal was to try and externalise as much of their margins back to users as possible. We are now just over a week into the life of papertrade and we are becoming increasingly confident that this is both possible, but also a likely outcome as agentic led software becomes the norm. 

As it stands, the paper token traded as a perp becomes a leveraged bet on bankroll solvency - and being able to short bankroll solvency materially changes the payoff curve of a manipulation attack. The target number goes from the bankroll, to the bankroll + short side exposure on paper. We can, and do limit bankroll size specifically to control this payoff curve and ensure it never becomes existentially problematic, but external perp markets are not something we would have any control over if left to float of their own accord. For example, if our bankroll is $10m, an attack costing $15m manipulating the price of bitcoin or ether is not viable. You simply lose money. If however you were also able to put on $10m of PAPER short side exposure, suddenly an attack costing $15m is very viable indeed.

If we were to make the token transferable at this point, we are confident we would quickly enter a state too dangerous to allow any material exposure to be taken on papertrade, an end result that benefits no party beyond the wolves who have done the math on the short and are waiting in the wings with sharpened knives.

We would also like to thank the various perps teams who have reached out about pre-market listings for their understanding and patience regarding this issue, and especially to the paragon team who, despite jumping the gun on us, have behaved with the utmost integrity and transparency once a dialogue was opened.

Perps on PAPER will always act as a self-limiting exposure ceiling for a token with this type of utility, and we think it would be a shame to limit the growth of papertrade to the extent that allowing perps would necessitate. As such, at this juncture we do not have plans to allow off-contract token transferability.

Structurally, papertrade is limited by the quality of the data it receives from hyperliquid, but we strongly believe that hyperliquid has a very large part to play in the future of global exchanges, and expect their books to continue to thicken and strengthen over time.

A note on fees.

Papertrade launched with a deadband fee from entry of 0.2bps. This means you don't earn anything until the price has moved by 0.002% in your favour. Over the months before launch, we played around with many different curves and fee structures affecting exclusively positions closed very close to entry price in order to try and devise a structure that removed the edge against the bankroll low time frame scalp bots have, whilst also minimally impacting the traders around which and for whom the product was devised. We were never able to find anything we were absolutely happy with and so decided to stay with the 0.2bp deadband fee through launch. This has however meant we have had to be very restrictive when it came to certain parameters, such as OI caps.

Now, however, we have enough live data to fully understand exactly which strategies work, and to make the necessary changes to stop them. The changes we are making will have an on hours and off hours fee mode to account for the relative differences in liquidity the hyperliquid books see between these two time periods, and the ease with which low time frame moves are signalled. The changes we are making will only affect positions closed within 6bps of entry (0.06%) in on hours, and 10bps (0.1%) in off hours. Any trades closed above these threshold price shifts will see no change to their fees at all. On a look back to launch basis, these changes affect the profitability of bot strategies roughly 15x more than they do normal traders, for whom a very small proportion of overall winnings come from within this band.

These changes should serve to flatten much of the edge our microfee structure necessarily creates on low time frames, and will help with long term exchange sustainability. This should hopefully allow us to open up parameters such as OI caps a little more so those of you who wish to can put on the size you want to, when you want to.

It is possible these changes are still too lax, and that further revisions to this structure may be necessary going forwards. If so, we will notify users ahead of time.

A note on paper tokenomics. 

In conjunction with the fee changes, we will also be implementing a change to the token issuance curve.

Going forward, every $1 lost mints a fixed share of PAPER's supply at that moment, roughly 0.1% of supply per $1M lost (the exact number depends on the mint rate at the time the contracts are upgraded). PAPER minting in and near insolvency will also change, switching from a flat 100 per $1 of loss, to a time weighted multiplier on the curve growing over time, effectively acting as the house running a discounted auction on its own future cash flows. This change also removes the risk of the paper-mint-straddle-attack, temporarily pushing the protocol insolvent by closing only the winning side of a large straddle position and then attempting to mint as much paper as possible. 

In the immediate term these changes will only have a very subtle effect on PAPER minting, but in the long run will structurally change the outlook of the system beyond the first few weeks, serving to slowly dilute out older holders and leaving more recent users with an advantage. Reconstituting the PAPER system into something much closer to the exchange rakeback it was intended to be.

We have been very reticent to touch this particular aspect of the system for obvious reasons, but ultimately we believe that these changes provide all users with the optionality to take a smaller piece of a potentially much larger pie than the current dynamic might necessarily allow.

Other, miscellaneous notes.

These contract upgrades will include a few other contract changes, including the addition of builder codes so that builders can utilise papertrade in whatever capacity they choose to. This will be a whitelist only to begin with and we will have more for you later in the week on where/how this will be rolled out. A small change to contract permissions on the reward distributor and a change on how below bust closes are processed by the exchange are also included, largely to block gas griefing attacks. 

These changes will be pushed to docs in full over the coming day, and we will further announce once the changes are queued into the timelock pending final security passes, scheduled to go live 24 hours after that point.

Final note.

We'd like to thank everyone that has tried out papertrade over the last 10 days. It has been a labour of love building this product and both of us have been taken aback at all of the positive feedback we have received. We'd also like to thank all those of you who have spent considerable time musing on the system we have built, and much of your advice has been taken onboard and will likely affect the colour of what papertrade becomes going forward. We know some of these changes will be unpopular with some, but we would not be making them if we did not feel them to be absolutely necessary.

- blurr, jez

text:
The Stages of Civilizational Collapse
 Jean-Michel’s Ten Years in Paris.

Meet Jean-Michel. Fifty-eight, Paris, 11th arrondissement. Thirty years at the prefecture. An apartment nearly paid off, savings in an assurance-vie, a vote for the left. The state has always taken care of him.
Here are his next ten years.

2027 – Small decay. The metro breaks down twice a week. His doctor's next appointment is in four months. His favourite brasserie closes – rent, rules, taxes, and the owner had enough when the windows got broken one more time. It reopens as a kebab shop. His daughter, an engineer, leaves for Montreal. In Marseille, the drug gangs settle their accounts with Kalashnikovs – but Marseille is far away. Everyone shrugs.

2028 – Disorder becomes normal. On New Year's Eve his neighbor's car burns, along with hundreds of others. His wife's bag is snatched on the metro, and she stops taking it after nine. In the summer riots, police in Lyon come under fire from weapons of war. The news calls it "a feeling of insecurity."

2029 – The bill. The government falls again. The rating agencies downgrade France again. One week, the lenders stop pretending, and interest on the debt becomes the biggest line in the budget. One Monday morning, a notification: withdrawals from his assurance-vie are "temporarily suspended" – under a 2016 law nobody read. That night, a police patrol in the 18th arrondissement is met by a teenager with a Scorpion submachine gun.

2030 – Austerity. His salary frozen. His pension de-indexed. An "exceptional solidarity contribution" on savings. Property tax doubled. The garbage collectors strike for six weeks, and rats run through the courtyard. His wife's bag is stolen for the third time. The neighbor from the fourth floor is beaten up coming out of the metro at Place de la République.

2031 – The exodus. The doctors, the engineers and the entrepreneurs leave – quietly, one family at a time. Transfers abroad are capped, "temporarily." The good restaurant where he took his wife for their anniversaries is boarded up. His son, thirty, still lives at home. The apartment is worth a third less, and nobody is buying.

2032 – Paralysis. Governments last weeks. Every reform triggers a general strike. One night, someone fires fireworks through the window of the apartment downstairs. The family puts out the fire in time. Now the first-floor windows are boarded up. A police station in the suburbs is overrun and burned; the officers escape through the back. Jean-Michel stops watching the news.

2033 – Services break. Blackouts in winter. Schools closed one day a week "for lack of staff." The police no longer come for a burglary – you file it online. Two streets from home, Jean-Michel is stopped at gunpoint for his phone. He hands it over and says nothing. Neither does anyone else. His building installs a steel door.

2034 – Fragmentation. Whole neighborhoods are now openly run by armed gangs, and the city negotiates with them to get the trash collected. Militias from both political extremes fight in the streets. After a football match, the riots reach the Louvre. One wing burns. Luckily, not the one with the Mona Lisa.

2035 – Street guerrilla. Shootings in broad daylight. A bombing at a train station. A politician assassinated outside his home. Napoleon's tomb at Les Invalides is looted. Armored vehicles at Place de la République, curfew at nine. Jean-Michel's son joins a militia "for protection." Jean-Michel doesn't ask which one.

2036 – The failed state. Paris can't pay its civil servants. Whole districts are held by armed groups. The euro is "under review." An international administration arrives, with conditions. The state still exists, on paper.

Jean-Michel, sixty-eight, packs two suitcases and applies for a visa – to Poland.

Science fiction? French police have already faced rioters and gangs armed with Kalashnikovs and Scorpion submachine guns – in Paris, Marseille and Lyon. The first stages are not a prediction. They are the news.

It won't come as a revolution. It will come one notification, one closed shop, one burned car at a time. And every step will be explained away – until the last one.

🎯 Collapse bingo. How many of these will happen in France over the next ten years?
author: BillAckman
quoted_text:
The Louvre is next.

Someone has suggested that the Louvre's magnificent and priceless works of art should be moved to Poland. To keep them safe – but also so they can be appreciated in a civilized environment.

A year ago today, thieves walked into the Louvre in broad daylight and walked out with the crown jewels – in seven minutes. Activists had already thrown cake and soup at the Mona Lisa. Only the glass saved her.

It may sound like a joke. Until you imagine if they were to burn the Mona Lisa.
Notre Dame burned after all…

We are talking about the heritage of Our Civilization.
Can the French government be trusted to protect it?

Centuries of Western genius, in a country that can no longer protect its own streets.
We would take good care of her.
Civilization is best kept by the people who would never throw soup at it.

i wrote a blood shader for my 2003 crimsonland port and somehow ended up implementing a small optics department.

beer–lambert absorption, fresnel reflections, separate soil and liquid normals, volume-weighted coagulation, hdr beam reflections.

the enemy: blood that looks like a red vinyl sticker. derive normals from a blood decal’s alpha and you give every splatter a tiny cliff. congratulations, you’ve invented embossed ketchup.

so the shader separates the surfaces:
- soil/corpse normals handle diffuse lighting with no blood bevel.
- a separate, smoothed liquid normal handles reflections.

blood becomes an optical layer over wet ground. light passes through it, hits the substrate, and passes through it again. wavelength-dependent absorption eats green and blue first; deeper pools swallow more of the remaining red.

every splatter also carries its own age. freshness decays exponentially with a 45-second time constant, weighted by deposited volume. a fresh drop doesn’t magically rejuvenate an entire ancient puddle.

as it ages, the blood darkens and gets rougher. sharp weapon reflections spread out and fade.

passing beams are finite light sources: reflected eye rays intersect their height plane, and the highlights can push past sdr white into edr.

all this so you can shoot spiders on a pentium-era dirt texture.

shown: the same splatter coagulating from fresh → 15s → 45s → 180s

How do people read this then just... go on with their day as usual?

“25 AI agents inhabit a digital Westworld, unaware that they are living in a simulation. They go to work, gossip, organize socials, make new friends, and even fall in love.”

Here’s a mindblowing example of how autonomous AIs are now, and how ridiculous it is to say that the AIs "only do things we tell them to do”:

POV: you tell the Westworld character “Isabella Rodriguez” to host an entire Valentine’s Day party in two days. This is a complex act, certainly something only humans, and not toasters, can do, right?

- Isabella proceeds to invite friends and customers when she sees them at Hobbs Cafe or elsewhere. 
- Isabella then spends the afternoon of the 13th decorating the cafe for the party. 
- Maria, a frequent customer and close friend of Isabella’s, arrives at the cafe. Isabella asks for Maria’s help in decorating for the party, and Maria agrees. 
- That night, Maria invites Klaus, her secret crush, to join her at the party, and he gladly accepts. 
- On Valentine’s Day, five agents, including Klaus and Maria, coordinate to show up for the party together at the right time (5pm), and they enjoy the festivities.

You told Isabella to host a party, but then she - and the other AIs - went and made a million other decisions entirely on their own - things you didn't explicitly tell them to do.

Autonomous AIs are here.

And -- tapping the sign -- this is another example where science fiction is becoming reality, and why “you watch too much sci-fi” is a stupid dunk.

This digital Westworld - “Smallville” - is now open source, meaning there will soon be thousands of these Westworlds, with thousands or millions of autonomous AIs populating them.

Makes you think, doesn’t it?

text:
In one day, I've made more progress on my own mathematical projects than in an entire decade. Once you have a good instinct for what should work, delegating mathematical work to AI makes it easy to solve problems and show the results. Before I even start reading anything, I let the agents explore and bootstrap the problems using my custom skills and agentic harness. This eliminates a lot of dead ends, especially in algebra.

Combining this with computer algebra produces a real system that auto-corrects itself, improves, generalizes, and produces genuinely novel reasoning. There are stochastic parrots at the bottom of each LLM, but on top, there is much more going on due to RL and other training techniques. I guess that I am not doing anything immediately useful to humanity, except perhaps teaching. So I can freely explore the landscape.

I suspect there will be more and more mathematicians using frontier models, training smaller ones, and exploring these new skills and tools.

SAIR has launched the Open Models for Mathematics initiative. You can sign in and start enjoying the power of not-so-small LLMs. I am now training models to do recurrent inference and comparing them with models trained in the vanilla way on my Heyting arithmetic library. So far, the work is not completely conclusive, but the models are learning, and it's so awesome to see the experiments work!

And it's not only an engineering job. Sometimes you still have to prove some really nice theorems. So it's still our good old mathematical work, but now incredibly accelerated with model prompting. And we are only at the beginning.

It's quite impressive to imagine how far we might get in a year's time. But we need to keep building a community of mathematical builders so that they can stay in the loop, not necessarily understanding every single epsilon, but navigating the conceptual landscape.

text:
The NFL and the Philadelphia Eagles almost killed Jalen Hurts for a Week 5 international showcase.

​The full details of what happened behind closed doors in London just surfaced, and the negligence is staggering.

​Before kickoff in London, Hurts was in a hospital bed until 4:00 AM undergoing emergency vascular testing. Medical staff instructed him not to sleep because sleep was considered an active health risk.

​Instead of shutting down their $255 million franchise quarterback, the team cleared him to play 60 minutes of brutal, high-impact collision football on zero sleep.

​Then, they loaded him onto a pressurized, 8-hour transatlantic flight back to Philadelphia.

​Every doctor on the planet knows that long-haul flights and cabin pressure are the exact triggers that cause lower-extremity blood clots to break free. The Eagles spent days assuring the public it was just a "minor, superficial calf clot".

​Now the truth comes out: the clot dislodged, shot through his bloodstream, and caused multiple pulmonary emboli in his lungs.

​Hurts is officially out for the season, placed on blood thinners where taking a single routine tackle could cause a fatal internal hemorrhage.

​He isn't just lucky to play football again, he is lucky to be alive.

​When the NFL preaches "player safety," remember this moment. They ran a human being into the ground for television ratings in the UK, almost lost him to a preventable medical catastrophe, and cratered their entire season in the process.

​Who inside that building signed off on letting him play and board that flight?

DeepSeek Open-Sources Its Inference Framework: Toward a Future of Truly Universal Access

The capability boundaries of large models are defined by the models themselves, but serving ultra-large-scale models at a reasonable cost also depends on a middle layer that has long gone unnoticed by the public: the inference framework.

Training is how a model learns; inference is how it becomes useful to people. Faced with today's enormous volume of user requests, the inference framework orchestrates and schedules vast compute clusters, and its efficiency directly determines the compute cost and power consumption of AI services.

DeepSeek has long been committed to pushing inference performance to its limits. Building on our earlier open-sourcing of a series of large models, the TileLang compiler toolchain, and our inference operator library, we have decided to go further and fully open-source our internal inference framework, DeepInfer.

"Do good together with the many; share skill so that the many may be skilled." By sharing our internal deployment experience, we hope to help developers and enterprises optimize throughput and latency for large-scale inference, so they can efficiently build private and public cloud deployments, lower compute costs, and reduce energy consumption, bringing intelligence to a broader population at a lower price and making large models truly accessible to all. We will also continue to support the community in optimizing large-scale deployments, and we welcome you to join us in open source.

DeepInfer

Using DeepInfer, we have achieved high-throughput, low-latency large-scale inference serving for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. Going forward, inference code and subsequent optimizations for new DeepSeek models will continue to be released here.

DeepInfer inference framework: An inference engine that integrates high-performance operators with deep optimizations. It supports distributed inference, speculative decoding, SWA Bounded Replay, structured output, and more, and is compatible with both NVIDIA and Huawei Ascend platforms.
deepseek-recipe encoding/decoding component: A production-grade token encoding/decoding component, open-sourced alongside DeepInfer. It is fully aligned with the processing logic of DeepSeek's official API, so the community gets an API experience consistent with our official deployment.

quoted_text:
A note on transferability.

Papertrade is a complicated primitive, and managing it from a risk standpoint is a complicated problem. The PAPER token is far more integrated into the economics of the primitive than most tokens are in their respective protocols today, and, broadly, was designed to act as a counter insolvency incentive coupled with a rebate mechanism to losing traders. Market makers and exchanges are by far the two most profitable businesses in crypto, and our goal was to try and externalise as much of their margins back to users as possible. We are now just over a week into the life of papertrade and we are becoming increasingly confident that this is both possible, but also a likely outcome as agentic led software becomes the norm. 

As it stands, the paper token traded as a perp becomes a leveraged bet on bankroll solvency - and being able to short bankroll solvency materially changes the payoff curve of a manipulation attack. The target number goes from the bankroll, to the bankroll + short side exposure on paper. We can, and do limit bankroll size specifically to control this payoff curve and ensure it never becomes existentially problematic, but external perp markets are not something we would have any control over if left to float of their own accord. For example, if our bankroll is $10m, an attack costing $15m manipulating the price of bitcoin or ether is not viable. You simply lose money. If however you were also able to put on $10m of PAPER short side exposure, suddenly an attack costing $15m is very viable indeed.

If we were to make the token transferable at this point, we are confident we would quickly enter a state too dangerous to allow any material exposure to be taken on papertrade, an end result that benefits no party beyond the wolves who have done the math on the short and are waiting in the wings with sharpened knives.

We would also like to thank the various perps teams who have reached out about pre-market listings for their understanding and patience regarding this issue, and especially to the paragon team who, despite jumping the gun on us, have behaved with the utmost integrity and transparency once a dialogue was opened.

Perps on PAPER will always act as a self-limiting exposure ceiling for a token with this type of utility, and we think it would be a shame to limit the growth of papertrade to the extent that allowing perps would necessitate. As such, at this juncture we do not have plans to allow off-contract token transferability.

Structurally, papertrade is limited by the quality of the data it receives from hyperliquid, but we strongly believe that hyperliquid has a very large part to play in the future of global exchanges, and expect their books to continue to thicken and strengthen over time.

A note on fees.

Papertrade launched with a deadband fee from entry of 0.2bps. This means you don't earn anything until the price has moved by 0.002% in your favour. Over the months before launch, we played around with many different curves and fee structures affecting exclusively positions closed very close to entry price in order to try and devise a structure that removed the edge against the bankroll low time frame scalp bots have, whilst also minimally impacting the traders around which and for whom the product was devised. We were never able to find anything we were absolutely happy with and so decided to stay with the 0.2bp deadband fee through launch. This has however meant we have had to be very restrictive when it came to certain parameters, such as OI caps.

Now, however, we have enough live data to fully understand exactly which strategies work, and to make the necessary changes to stop them. The changes we are making will have an on hours and off hours fee mode to account for the relative differences in liquidity the hyperliquid books see between these two time periods, and the ease with which low time frame moves are signalled. The changes we are making will only affect positions closed within 6bps of entry (0.06%) in on hours, and 10bps (0.1%) in off hours. Any trades closed above these threshold price shifts will see no change to their fees at all. On a look back to launch basis, these changes affect the profitability of bot strategies roughly 15x more than they do normal traders, for whom a very small proportion of overall winnings come from within this band.

These changes should serve to flatten much of the edge our microfee structure necessarily creates on low time frames, and will help with long term exchange sustainability. This should hopefully allow us to open up parameters such as OI caps a little more so those of you who wish to can put on the size you want to, when you want to.

It is possible these changes are still too lax, and that further revisions to this structure may be necessary going forwards. If so, we will notify users ahead of time.

A note on paper tokenomics. 

In conjunction with the fee changes, we will also be implementing a change to the token issuance curve.

Going forward, every $1 lost mints a fixed share of PAPER's supply at that moment, roughly 0.1% of supply per $1M lost (the exact number depends on the mint rate at the time the contracts are upgraded). PAPER minting in and near insolvency will also change, switching from a flat 100 per $1 of loss, to a time weighted multiplier on the curve growing over time, effectively acting as the house running a discounted auction on its own future cash flows. This change also removes the risk of the paper-mint-straddle-attack, temporarily pushing the protocol insolvent by closing only the winning side of a large straddle position and then attempting to mint as much paper as possible. 

In the immediate term these changes will only have a very subtle effect on PAPER minting, but in the long run will structurally change the outlook of the system beyond the first few weeks, serving to slowly dilute out older holders and leaving more recent users with an advantage. Reconstituting the PAPER system into something much closer to the exchange rakeback it was intended to be.

We have been very reticent to touch this particular aspect of the system for obvious reasons, but ultimately we believe that these changes provide all users with the optionality to take a smaller piece of a potentially much larger pie than the current dynamic might necessarily allow.

Other, miscellaneous notes.

These contract upgrades will include a few other contract changes, including the addition of builder codes so that builders can utilise papertrade in whatever capacity they choose to. This will be a whitelist only to begin with and we will have more for you later in the week on where/how this will be rolled out. A small change to contract permissions on the reward distributor and a change on how below bust closes are processed by the exchange are also included, largely to block gas griefing attacks. 

These changes will be pushed to docs in full over the coming day, and we will further announce once the changes are queued into the timelock pending final security passes, scheduled to go live 24 hours after that point.

Final note.

We'd like to thank everyone that has tried out papertrade over the last 10 days. It has been a labour of love building this product and both of us have been taken aback at all of the positive feedback we have received. We'd also like to thank all those of you who have spent considerable time musing on the system we have built, and much of your advice has been taken onboard and will likely affect the colour of what papertrade becomes going forward. We know some of these changes will be unpopular with some, but we would not be making them if we did not feel them to be absolutely necessary.

During our analysis of @_Qubic_  Wallet, we found that the wallet uses the same non-cryptographically secure Math.random() stream for account seed generation and dejaVu values exposed in network packet headers, potentially enabling private key recovery through network observations.

🔍 Root Cause

A shared, non-cryptographically secure random stream → Account seed generation + Network-visible header values

⚠️ Hypothesized Attack Flow

1️⃣ Collect dejaVu values from bridge/peer traffic or the plaintext bridge-to-peer link.
2️⃣ Recover the 128-bit PRNG state using 6 consecutive observations.
3️⃣ Reconstruct the 55-character seed and verify it against the public key exposed in balance requests.
4️⃣ Recover the private key and forge a SchnorrQ signature to transfer assets.

Our PoC validated the technical feasibility of this recovery chain. Actual exploitability depends on network trust boundaries, observation continuity, call alignment, and other consumers of Math.random().

🛡️ Security Recommendations

Use cryptographically secure randomness for key generation, conduct comprehensive external security audits before deployment, and review trust boundaries around random number sources and protocol header fields.

People seem to be misinterpreting the message.

The crux of the issue is not the prosecutors or how they found me, but the fact that Venue required them to involve me in the first place.

Venue, the law that states you have to try a crime in the district where it is committed, doesn't make sense when applied to crypto. Crypto transactions happen everywhere and nowhere, it's applying a framework that doesn't fit.

Butttt, defendants can still get their case dismissed because of it, even if they are guilty. So the prosecutors are forced to bring someone in because the alternative was the hacker would be let free.

This was not an attack on crypto, it was an attack on a guy who stole it. The prosecutors are good guys forced to temporarily inconvenience someone because of a law that doesn't make sense.

顶部仓位管理的mindset：

一、顶部仓位管理的mindset，需要同时容纳几组看似冲突、实际可以共存的判断：

1.我可以长期看好，也可以高位降低仓位。

2.我可以认为股价还会继续涨，也可以承认当前风险暴露已经过大。

3.我可以接受卖早，也可以通过保留核心仓，让剩余仓位继续参与长期成长。

4.我可以尊重强趋势，同时承认趋势越成熟，风险收益比可能越差。

5.我可以给基本面足够的兑现时间，同时要求估值和仓位不断接受重新评估。

6.我可以保持很高的conviction，同时始终对反证保持开放。

7.我可以承认自己无法预测顶部，同时提前让仓位为顶部做好准备。

8.我可以接受卖出后的遗憾，同时坚持事先制定的卖出纪律。

9.我可以保留上涨的参与权，同时保留下跌后的行动权。

二、最终要形成几个条件反射：

1.顶部最大的特征之一，就是让你越来越不想卖。

2.底部不会让你买得舒服，顶部同样不会让你卖得舒服。

3.底部允许买早，顶部也要允许卖早。

4.不要追求最高点，卖在顶部区域已经足够优秀。把最后15%到20%的上涨慷慨送给别人。

5.不要问“还能不能涨”，要问“这个价格应该持有多少”。

6.越涨，越要主动寻找反证。

7.不要预测明天涨还是跌，也不要预测最后一根大阳线，让仓位提前为反转做好准备。

8.长期逻辑决定核心仓，估值、周期、趋势和风险收益比决定进攻仓。

9.卖出规则在冷静时制定，在兴奋时执行。

三、顶部管理的成熟，在于同时容纳两个事实：

1.股价可能继续上涨，风险也可能正在同步上升。

2.最终用仓位解决这两者之间的矛盾。

不猜顶，只管理仓位。

Today we sent live the RiseX Market, and an user just executed the first purchase at $3.33 / point.

Points earned via our RiseX USDC Vault can be traded on Shift's Points Marketplace without the need of locking 100% of your collateral or having your return capped at 2x.

How does it work?
Shift accumulates points via its strategies, including RiseXUSDC. These points are then distributed to our users in the form of "Shift Wrapped Points" with an added bonus, coming from us or our partners (or a mix).

Via Shift's Points Marketplace you can trade the points (buy or sell them) on @arbitrum, directly receiving USDC for your sales.

How is this different from a normal points OTC Marketplace?
OTC Marketplaces have four issues that we try to solve:

1. Trust: many users would like to buy points or sell their points, but they do not trust the intermediary, which is generally a telegram group chat or an individual. Here, every trade is guaranteed and backstopped by Shift. 

2. Capital Efficiency: another thing that users don't like is locking their capital for weeks or months, waiting for the points to become transferrable or to be converted in tokens. This doesn't happen with Shift. 
Since the points are wrapped by Shift, we immediately transfer them to the buyer once the trade is executed, and the seller immediately receives his USDC.

3. Wait time: OTC markets are generally dependent on their manager to be up and awake. If they're not (timezone, lack of time, lack of commitment) you may struggle to place an order or a trade. Shift's market is live 24/7 and completely independent from Shift's team availability.

4. Transparency: with OTC chats you generally are never sure of being properly matched with counterparties. Who is the counterparty? Is the middleman really acting in your best interest? 
This is not an issue with our Points Marketplace, since everything is handled like an orderbook.

One last reminder:
To earn points, you can deposit in each of the vaults.
For RisexUSDC, there is also a Pendle Pool available. You can LP in the pool or buy/mint YTs (or buy PTs if you don't want points) to accelerate your point accrual even more!

text:
@base has led @solana in DeFi TVL for 10 straight days, the first time since 2023.

But it's not as big a deal as it sounds. Here's why:

• Base's lead comes from one app. @Morpho holds ~$4.4B of Base's $6.16B, and ~97% of Base's growth over the last 30 days ($258M of $265M) went into it.

• Solana didn't really lose money. Its TVL is down ~7%, and SOL's price is down ~6%. The tokens are still there, they're just worth less.

• Solana still holds ~3x more stablecoins ($15.8B vs $5.1B on Base). Most of it just isn't deposited in DeFi apps, so TVL doesn't count it.

So if Morpho has a bad week, Base loses its lead. And if SOL's price goes back up, Solana could take the spot back without anyone moving a dollar.

If you're earning yield on Base, check who runs your Morpho vault and how much of the yield comes from token rewards.

Next time you see a chain ranking, ask two questions. Did TVL just follow the token price? Is one app doing all the work?

author: Alvin0617
quoted_text:
A note on transferability.

Papertrade is a complicated primitive, and managing it from a risk standpoint is a complicated problem. The PAPER token is far more integrated into the economics of the primitive than most tokens are in their respective protocols today, and, broadly, was designed to act as a counter insolvency incentive coupled with a rebate mechanism to losing traders. Market makers and exchanges are by far the two most profitable businesses in crypto, and our goal was to try and externalise as much of their margins back to users as possible. We are now just over a week into the life of papertrade and we are becoming increasingly confident that this is both possible, but also a likely outcome as agentic led software becomes the norm. 

As it stands, the paper token traded as a perp becomes a leveraged bet on bankroll solvency - and being able to short bankroll solvency materially changes the payoff curve of a manipulation attack. The target number goes from the bankroll, to the bankroll + short side exposure on paper. We can, and do limit bankroll size specifically to control this payoff curve and ensure it never becomes existentially problematic, but external perp markets are not something we would have any control over if left to float of their own accord. For example, if our bankroll is $10m, an attack costing $15m manipulating the price of bitcoin or ether is not viable. You simply lose money. If however you were also able to put on $10m of PAPER short side exposure, suddenly an attack costing $15m is very viable indeed.

If we were to make the token transferable at this point, we are confident we would quickly enter a state too dangerous to allow any material exposure to be taken on papertrade, an end result that benefits no party beyond the wolves who have done the math on the short and are waiting in the wings with sharpened knives.

We would also like to thank the various perps teams who have reached out about pre-market listings for their understanding and patience regarding this issue, and especially to the paragon team who, despite jumping the gun on us, have behaved with the utmost integrity and transparency once a dialogue was opened.

Perps on PAPER will always act as a self-limiting exposure ceiling for a token with this type of utility, and we think it would be a shame to limit the growth of papertrade to the extent that allowing perps would necessitate. As such, at this juncture we do not have plans to allow off-contract token transferability.

Structurally, papertrade is limited by the quality of the data it receives from hyperliquid, but we strongly believe that hyperliquid has a very large part to play in the future of global exchanges, and expect their books to continue to thicken and strengthen over time.

A note on fees.

Papertrade launched with a deadband fee from entry of 0.2bps. This means you don't earn anything until the price has moved by 0.002% in your favour. Over the months before launch, we played around with many different curves and fee structures affecting exclusively positions closed very close to entry price in order to try and devise a structure that removed the edge against the bankroll low time frame scalp bots have, whilst also minimally impacting the traders around which and for whom the product was devised. We were never able to find anything we were absolutely happy with and so decided to stay with the 0.2bp deadband fee through launch. This has however meant we have had to be very restrictive when it came to certain parameters, such as OI caps.

Now, however, we have enough live data to fully understand exactly which strategies work, and to make the necessary changes to stop them. The changes we are making will have an on hours and off hours fee mode to account for the relative differences in liquidity the hyperliquid books see between these two time periods, and the ease with which low time frame moves are signalled. The changes we are making will only affect positions closed within 6bps of entry (0.06%) in on hours, and 10bps (0.1%) in off hours. Any trades closed above these threshold price shifts will see no change to their fees at all. On a look back to launch basis, these changes affect the profitability of bot strategies roughly 15x more than they do normal traders, for whom a very small proportion of overall winnings come from within this band.

These changes should serve to flatten much of the edge our microfee structure necessarily creates on low time frames, and will help with long term exchange sustainability. This should hopefully allow us to open up parameters such as OI caps a little more so those of you who wish to can put on the size you want to, when you want to.

It is possible these changes are still too lax, and that further revisions to this structure may be necessary going forwards. If so, we will notify users ahead of time.

A note on paper tokenomics. 

In conjunction with the fee changes, we will also be implementing a change to the token issuance curve.

Going forward, every $1 lost mints a fixed share of PAPER's supply at that moment, roughly 0.1% of supply per $1M lost (the exact number depends on the mint rate at the time the contracts are upgraded). PAPER minting in and near insolvency will also change, switching from a flat 100 per $1 of loss, to a time weighted multiplier on the curve growing over time, effectively acting as the house running a discounted auction on its own future cash flows. This change also removes the risk of the paper-mint-straddle-attack, temporarily pushing the protocol insolvent by closing only the winning side of a large straddle position and then attempting to mint as much paper as possible. 

In the immediate term these changes will only have a very subtle effect on PAPER minting, but in the long run will structurally change the outlook of the system beyond the first few weeks, serving to slowly dilute out older holders and leaving more recent users with an advantage. Reconstituting the PAPER system into something much closer to the exchange rakeback it was intended to be.

We have been very reticent to touch this particular aspect of the system for obvious reasons, but ultimately we believe that these changes provide all users with the optionality to take a smaller piece of a potentially much larger pie than the current dynamic might necessarily allow.

Other, miscellaneous notes.

These contract upgrades will include a few other contract changes, including the addition of builder codes so that builders can utilise papertrade in whatever capacity they choose to. This will be a whitelist only to begin with and we will have more for you later in the week on where/how this will be rolled out. A small change to contract permissions on the reward distributor and a change on how below bust closes are processed by the exchange are also included, largely to block gas griefing attacks. 

These changes will be pushed to docs in full over the coming day, and we will further announce once the changes are queued into the timelock pending final security passes, scheduled to go live 24 hours after that point.

Final note.

We'd like to thank everyone that has tried out papertrade over the last 10 days. It has been a labour of love building this product and both of us have been taken aback at all of the positive feedback we have received. We'd also like to thank all those of you who have spent considerable time musing on the system we have built, and much of your advice has been taken onboard and will likely affect the colour of what papertrade becomes going forward. We know some of these changes will be unpopular with some, but we would not be making them if we did not feel them to be absolutely necessary.

- blurr, jez

text:
Helium和IO之后，我一度觉得DePIN这个赛道难了，尤其是面向Retail的DePIN，消费级硬件跟云厂商能力差距太大，规模化了也干不成太多事儿，永远都是“代币补贴”，找不到真实PMF

不过后来Pi居然真的上了大所，Grass也比我预想的成功不少，算是被小打脸一波

Grass跑通的原因我记得之前Tweet写过，人家卖的就不是算力，是住宅带宽和IP，这玩意在AI大规模数据抓取时是真的有用，真的有需求（单一Source IP太容易被封）

这两天在EchoHunt上看到 @Acurast，稍微研究了下，是在探索相对Make Sense的一个方向 - 如果说Grass证明了家用PC分布式最值钱的是住宅IP，那全球几十亿部手机，分布后最大的优势是啥？

优势必然不是算力，而是每一部手机上自带的硬件安全芯片，这玩意平时只用来解锁和刷脸，多少有点浪费。要是连起来，能不能当成一个特定场景下的云来用？

手机里芯片都有硬件级的TEE 和Attestation，天然能向网络证明：我是一台真机，代码在Enclave 里跑，没被篡改。

这跟服务器算力市场有本质区别。后者很大程度依赖节点自报配置，刷量和造假一直是老问题（懂的都懂）。Acurast是每台设备由硬件自证身份。对DePIN来说，"可验证"比"规模"更稀缺。

数据层面：累计接入超过 33 万台手机，链上交易突破 11 亿笔。今年1月主网和 TGE 上线，Binance Alpha 和合约、Bybit、Bitget、Kraken 等都已上线。10月15号还刚上了Bithumb的韩元对

当然，别指望手机网络跑什么大型的去中心化训练/推理之类，应该未来主打的场景是轻量推理、预言机、链上自动化、带宽和住宅 IP之类，有点像是Grass的带宽/IP之外，再多了一层可验证的计算能力。

但和所有 DePIN 一样，最终要回答的问题还是：主网后的付费需求，能不能跑赢节点激励的通胀。

有闲置手机想自己跑个节点感受一下的，可以试试，多少是个猪脚饭，万一跑出来点啥还能加个鸡腿也说不定

吴说获悉，区块链安全公司慢雾（SlowMist）发布 Qubic 钱包漏洞分析报告称，Qubic Wallet 使用不具备密码学安全性的 Math.random() 生成账户种子，同时将同一随机数序列的部分输出写入网络数据包的 dejaVu 字段，可能使攻击者通过网络观测恢复用户私钥。慢雾在本地概念验证（PoC）中发现，连续获取 6 个 dejaVu 数值即可在特定条件下还原伪随机数生成器的 128 位内部状态，进而重建 55 字符账户种子、推导私钥并验证匹配。该攻击路径的实际可利用性仍取决于网络访问权限、观测连续性及随机数调用顺序等条件，尚不能确认此前攻击者采用了相同手法。此前 Qubic 于 10 月 18 日披露，因部分钱包种子随机性不足，1,404 个钱包被盗约 2.94 万亿枚 QU。

quoted_text:
Quantum Tier List (2026)

Everyone says their chain is quantum ready but only a few can prove it.

👇 I ranked 34 "quantum" projects including the 28 on @Mars_DeFi's list based on
• quantum safety
• upgradability
• testnet/mainnet
• age + size
• privacy feature

S
.@QRLedger - every wallet has used XMSS feature, a hash-based signature quantum computers can't crack, it has been live since 2018, with multiple audits.

A
.@QuantusNetwork - uses quantum-safe ML-DSA signatures by default, but mainnet only launched this September.
.Abelian - quantum-safe lattice signatures since 2022, but its own custom design haa no public crypto audit.
.@tidecoin - uses Falcon, a quantum-safe signature, on every transaction since 2020, but it's a tiny network.
.@cellframenet wallets use Dilithium, a quantum-safe signature, by default, but adoption is small.
.@QoreChain - every transaction needs a quantum-safe ML-DSA signature, but mainnet only went live in June this year.
.@NeptunePrivacy - spending uses hash-based proofs, but it's a young chain.
.@NEARProtocol - quantum-safe ML-DSA keys are live since Jul 2026, and you can switch your account to them anytime.
.@Algorand - quantum-safe Falcon accounts are live since Aug 2026, and you can move an existing wallet over.

B
.@Starknet - its proofs are quantum-safe, but your wallet keys aren't yet, and the safe wallet is just a demo.
.@solana - an outside team built a quantum-safe vault you can opt into, the chain itself isn't quantum safe.
.@NervosNetwork - an optional quantum-safe lock exists, but you have to move funds into it.
.@trondao - quantum-safe Falcon and ML-DSA keys are being tested on its testnet.
.@tezos - testing quantum-safe ML-DSA accounts on a special testnet.
.@QANplatform - is integrating quantum-safe Dilithium signatures, but still on testnet only.
.@quipnetwork - building earky stage quantum-safe accounts for coins on other chains, still on testnet.
.@Aptos - its quantum-safe SLH-DSA accounts are coded but still waiting for a governance vote to switch it on.
.@SuiNetwork - made its first quantum-safe transaction on a dev network this month, and mainnet is targeted for 2027.
.@Tensorcash - you can create quantum-safe ML-DSA addresses, but it's a small, new network.
.Bitcoin BIP-360, a proposal for quantum-safe addresses, is still a draft

C
.@ethereum - still researching quantum-safe upgrades, most likely years away.
.@zksync - its proofs are quantum-safe, but user accounts aren't.
.@Zcash - plans for quantum-safe signatures, but nothing shipped yet.
.Qoneqt - claims a quantum-safe vault, but can't verify anything yet.
.@injective - said last week it started building toward a quantum future, but no details yet.
.@monad - quantum-safe keys are still on their roadmap.
.@aztecnetwork no quantum plan or anything substantial published yet but Mars included it in his list
.@mindnetwork_xyz - focuses on encryption, not quantum-safe signatures but seems they frame that as quantum
.@NexusMutual - security-focused imo, no quantum plan
.@Qubic - quantum-themed only, maybe to join the hype, but little real quantum-safe tech.
.@GeeqOfficial - only security claims, no quantum details
.AME Chain - claims to be quantum-secure, little public proof
.QuStream - quantum claims, little public detail

Bottom line:
Most of crypto still runs on keys a quantum computer could break. Only one project here clears every bar today and that's @QRLedger.
But there's room for growth and tech like this would take years to perfect👌

text:
As I head to Europe for GTC Berlin, I keep coming back to a question: what good is building the future if our children don’t have a stake in it?

As a father of three, this is personal. I want my kids to grow up knowing they can help build something and own a piece of it. But that opportunity shouldn’t depend on whether their parents already have money.

Watching the unrest in France, I worry about what happens when people lose faith that the system has a place for them. Ownership won’t solve every grievance. But I believe capitalism is stronger when more people participate in its upside, rather than watch it from the outside.

That’s why @altcap work with Invest America, @MichaelDell and Susan Dell’s gifts, and Elon’s pledge here deserve real credit. Different efforts, united by a powerful idea: give children a stake in the future before they’re old enough to feel excluded from it.

A first investment can teach something a lecture cannot. You own a small piece of a business. You can watch it grow, weather setbacks and learn what patience means. Compounding becomes something you experience, not just something you’re told about.

Everyone wants equity. Not just a seat at the table, but a share in what gets built.

Let’s start the kids young.

👶💪🚀🇺🇸

author: AnselFang
quoted_text:
A note on transferability.

Papertrade is a complicated primitive, and managing it from a risk standpoint is a complicated problem. The PAPER token is far more integrated into the economics of the primitive than most tokens are in their respective protocols today, and, broadly, was designed to act as a counter insolvency incentive coupled with a rebate mechanism to losing traders. Market makers and exchanges are by far the two most profitable businesses in crypto, and our goal was to try and externalise as much of their margins back to users as possible. We are now just over a week into the life of papertrade and we are becoming increasingly confident that this is both possible, but also a likely outcome as agentic led software becomes the norm. 

As it stands, the paper token traded as a perp becomes a leveraged bet on bankroll solvency - and being able to short bankroll solvency materially changes the payoff curve of a manipulation attack. The target number goes from the bankroll, to the bankroll + short side exposure on paper. We can, and do limit bankroll size specifically to control this payoff curve and ensure it never becomes existentially problematic, but external perp markets are not something we would have any control over if left to float of their own accord. For example, if our bankroll is $10m, an attack costing $15m manipulating the price of bitcoin or ether is not viable. You simply lose money. If however you were also able to put on $10m of PAPER short side exposure, suddenly an attack costing $15m is very viable indeed.

If we were to make the token transferable at this point, we are confident we would quickly enter a state too dangerous to allow any material exposure to be taken on papertrade, an end result that benefits no party beyond the wolves who have done the math on the short and are waiting in the wings with sharpened knives.

We would also like to thank the various perps teams who have reached out about pre-market listings for their understanding and patience regarding this issue, and especially to the paragon team who, despite jumping the gun on us, have behaved with the utmost integrity and transparency once a dialogue was opened.

Perps on PAPER will always act as a self-limiting exposure ceiling for a token with this type of utility, and we think it would be a shame to limit the growth of papertrade to the extent that allowing perps would necessitate. As such, at this juncture we do not have plans to allow off-contract token transferability.

Structurally, papertrade is limited by the quality of the data it receives from hyperliquid, but we strongly believe that hyperliquid has a very large part to play in the future of global exchanges, and expect their books to continue to thicken and strengthen over time.

A note on fees.

Papertrade launched with a deadband fee from entry of 0.2bps. This means you don't earn anything until the price has moved by 0.002% in your favour. Over the months before launch, we played around with many different curves and fee structures affecting exclusively positions closed very close to entry price in order to try and devise a structure that removed the edge against the bankroll low time frame scalp bots have, whilst also minimally impacting the traders around which and for whom the product was devised. We were never able to find anything we were absolutely happy with and so decided to stay with the 0.2bp deadband fee through launch. This has however meant we have had to be very restrictive when it came to certain parameters, such as OI caps.

Now, however, we have enough live data to fully understand exactly which strategies work, and to make the necessary changes to stop them. The changes we are making will have an on hours and off hours fee mode to account for the relative differences in liquidity the hyperliquid books see between these two time periods, and the ease with which low time frame moves are signalled. The changes we are making will only affect positions closed within 6bps of entry (0.06%) in on hours, and 10bps (0.1%) in off hours. Any trades closed above these threshold price shifts will see no change to their fees at all. On a look back to launch basis, these changes affect the profitability of bot strategies roughly 15x more than they do normal traders, for whom a very small proportion of overall winnings come from within this band.

These changes should serve to flatten much of the edge our microfee structure necessarily creates on low time frames, and will help with long term exchange sustainability. This should hopefully allow us to open up parameters such as OI caps a little more so those of you who wish to can put on the size you want to, when you want to.

It is possible these changes are still too lax, and that further revisions to this structure may be necessary going forwards. If so, we will notify users ahead of time.

A note on paper tokenomics. 

In conjunction with the fee changes, we will also be implementing a change to the token issuance curve.

Going forward, every $1 lost mints a fixed share of PAPER's supply at that moment, roughly 0.1% of supply per $1M lost (the exact number depends on the mint rate at the time the contracts are upgraded). PAPER minting in and near insolvency will also change, switching from a flat 100 per $1 of loss, to a time weighted multiplier on the curve growing over time, effectively acting as the house running a discounted auction on its own future cash flows. This change also removes the risk of the paper-mint-straddle-attack, temporarily pushing the protocol insolvent by closing only the winning side of a large straddle position and then attempting to mint as much paper as possible. 

In the immediate term these changes will only have a very subtle effect on PAPER minting, but in the long run will structurally change the outlook of the system beyond the first few weeks, serving to slowly dilute out older holders and leaving more recent users with an advantage. Reconstituting the PAPER system into something much closer to the exchange rakeback it was intended to be.

We have been very reticent to touch this particular aspect of the system for obvious reasons, but ultimately we believe that these changes provide all users with the optionality to take a smaller piece of a potentially much larger pie than the current dynamic might necessarily allow.

Other, miscellaneous notes.

These contract upgrades will include a few other contract changes, including the addition of builder codes so that builders can utilise papertrade in whatever capacity they choose to. This will be a whitelist only to begin with and we will have more for you later in the week on where/how this will be rolled out. A small change to contract permissions on the reward distributor and a change on how below bust closes are processed by the exchange are also included, largely to block gas griefing attacks. 

These changes will be pushed to docs in full over the coming day, and we will further announce once the changes are queued into the timelock pending final security passes, scheduled to go live 24 hours after that point.

Final note.

We'd like to thank everyone that has tried out papertrade over the last 10 days. It has been a labour of love building this product and both of us have been taken aback at all of the positive feedback we have received. We'd also like to thank all those of you who have spent considerable time musing on the system we have built, and much of your advice has been taken onboard and will likely affect the colour of what papertrade becomes going forward. We know some of these changes will be unpopular with some, but we would not be making them if we did not feel them to be absolutely necessary.

- blurr, jez

text:
给一点 Deepinfer推理侧的速度锐评
1. 感觉 git repo 本身，对我们这样研发来说意义不太大，有一点点吧，但是好些东西没开。但是论证了我 kern 的想法，per model per repo 。
2. 精华本身在 zhihu 那篇文章，这篇文章很有价值，https://t.co/iEXBU3ac11。主要是确定了一些 ds 内部的并行，decode 侧就还是经典的 wideep，ep64 什么的。
有价值的就在几个 load balancer，第一个是分桶（这个其实是比较生产的），不知道开源 router 有没有人做，但生产来说，其实之前 together 就探索过一下。
prefill 的路由策略很有意思，不做任何的 cache aware，靠池化兜底。
dp group 直接用 compute tokens 作为负载 平衡的指标，dp 组内，也是。这个有点什么的味道，我想不起来了。可能和 hash 那边的一些东西有关，maybe 是，bitmap 什么的，我只是说思想好吧。
fifo，这里有个有意思的，它也做了一个估计器，其实前不久我也做了一个（只不过链接失效了hh）,我当时是想给 pp 做的，但是我觉得无论 ep pp，这个思路是一致的，不固定 chunk size，然后固定“耗时”，总之就是一个离线你先跑出来嘛，然后给个表，然后让 scheduler 去估到合适的时间，组 batch。

当然我有一个想法是，prefill 到底是 pp 还是 ep，当然现在模型训成 每一个 Layer 都不一样的，那天生也就对 pp 不友好，那也没招。但是 ep 要完整做完 ds 这一套，需要不少流量和 prefill worker。总的来说在中小部署我看好 pp（几个 prefill worker 这种），大部署我才看好 ep。

decode 和我想的也差不多，就是一个 kv cache + num running 的组合是吧。当然具体怎么调配就是一个 case by case 的事情。

eplb 呢，就是冗余换 lb 吧。不过有个在线的 eplb，不知道开源出来没有。这里的 trade off 就是，eplb 会占用更多显存是吧，但是呢它也能提升吞吐，而且越复制收益越小，所以要找到一个比较合适的点。也是 case by case 的。

然后是 router 的pd 动态扩缩容，prefill 还是  整体compute tokens，deocde 是 num running。

kv cache 呢就是 3fs，然后 3天的 ttl，能换到 0.5 - 1% 的命中率。kv cache 管理由 decode 主导？这样输出也能被 hit。

关于 I/o，精华是这句，换入从 shm 到 HBM 在 engine 进程内的线程里做，目标是实现逐层 H2D （Host-to-Device） 传输与前向计算重叠，由于 CUDA copy engine 对于 KVCache Block 细粒度的拷贝性能不佳，换入使用 GDR 实现，用 RDMA 网卡就能打满 PCIe 带宽，并且不占 SM。
这个我有空后面再讲吧。

dspark 变长验证，这个真上了，挺好的。

异步调度，先忽略。

ds弄了一个结构化输出库，good!

为了防止说我在蹭，我截个图，我之前思考过的路由策略，开源我的 thinking content !

链上竟然有26亿美元没人领？涉及600万个钱包!
这些人都去哪了？他们为什么不要了啊？
啥家庭啊！哪能这么造啊！
老6啊，你去哪了?

看亏友分享了一个挺有意思的网站：@0xEnsp1re开发的HiddenFunds：https://t.co/lHHWUNpISS，它专门追踪那些还留在链上但没有完成领取、赎回或者迁移的资产。大家有空可以查查自己的老钱包，说不定真有意外收获。

看了下数据，不是有点意外，是太他么意外了。
全网约26亿美元遗留资产，涉及600多万个钱包。覆盖了203条网络、218个数据源，统计出超过864万个尚未处理的仓位。其中约88%需要用户自行领取（很多人忘了），8%需要项目方协助，剩下约4%可能再也没办法追回。

主要的钱包情况是

1、钱不是没了，而是操作只做了一半。

一些早期代币的质押用户，发起解质押后，冷静期过了但是一直没有Claim的解质押资产，比如Solana，网站统计有约2.61亿已经解除质押却没有提取，数据显示有13.1万个钱包。有些400多万美金的领取时间是21年，卧槽。真服了这些人。
类似的还有：
TRON：9707万美元
NEAR：6129万美元
Polkadot：2561万美元
Babylon：1011万美元

光是公链质押这一类，遗留资金就高达4.8亿美元。有些人可能是忘了，有些可能是钱包丢了，还有些可能根本不知道需要再操作一次。
其他的大金额就是未完成的代币兑换，MATIC 换 POL，MKR 换 SKY，RNDR 换 RENDER，FTM 换 S 等

2、熟悉的DeFi协议，还有以太坊质押相关的
比如Lido，竟然有近7000万没有领取。其中有个钱包，已经很久没有链上活动，却还有超过200万美元的提款没有Claim。啥家庭啊，200多万美元都不领？

再看看其他协议：
Lido：6990万美元
Pendle：6680万美元
PancakeSwap：4880万美元
EigenLayer：4820万美元
Polygon PoS Bridge：4040万美元
zkSync Lite：3600万美元
dYdX v3：3220万美元

3、跨链的L2，关门的链，

尤其是Arbitrum、Optimism、Base、zkSync、Scroll等L2。从L2向Eth主网提款，部分流程还需要在主网执行最后一步确认。很多用户可能前面的操作都完成了，却一直没有完成最后一步。如果只看钱包余额，未必能发现这些资产。

还有一些早期DeFi协议，前端关闭了，项目转型了，甚至大家已经忘记项目叫什么名字，但合约里可能还有钱可以取。

触目惊心，触目惊心，触目惊心，有钱人的世界不理解也是正常的。但是还是想说
老6啊，你去哪了?

text:
Recently, the Nigerian X timeline was awash with concern over the spike in kidney failure.

Much of it was linked to fake drugs and drinks, toothpastes, etc.

But there's an aspect that people hardly are aware of: the contribution of Nigerian doctors to the kidney disease scourge.

My recent experience makes me believe that doctors contribute a major percentage to Nigeria's organ failure crisis.

I have a habit of painstakingly researching on procedures my family goes through in any hospital. That curiosity has saved us many times.

Yesterday, my 9yr old daughter was sick and had high fever, so I rushed her to a hospital in Yaba.

After routine tests, she was given Artemether & Augmentin 'starts' around 8pm. Then I was asked to buy ACT and Augmentin tabs to follow up subsequently.

As we left the hospital, I asked the doctor when we are to start with the tablets. He said, "this night".

My ears tickled. I knew that can't be right. So I waited a few minutes till the doctor's chief came around. I walked up to him & told him what the other doctor instructed. He said no, that it is the following morning that we will start the tabs.

Throughout the night, me and my wife battled to keep my girl's temperature from crossing 40°C. The thing hovered between 38° - 39.5°. No sleep for us as we tepid-towelled her every 20mins. Why? The doctor we met earlier whom we made a clear report of high fever did not give the girl any direct fever antidote (like 'paracetamol start').

So today's morning we rushed her back to the hospital. Met a different doctor who immediately prescribed 50mg Diclofenac (Voltaren) suppository. I went to buy it.

While on the way, I made enquiries. Three pharmacists I asked (including the pharmacist of this hospital) all exclaimed & asked who wants to give 50mg Diclofenac suppository to a 9yr old as first-line treatment for fever.

I checked reputable medical websites & they affirmed that the ceiling for adolescents & children below 15yrs is 25mg in divided doses, that 50mg & above should not be used for that age range.

I got the drug, went back to the hospital, & expressed my concerns to the doctor. He asked what am I saying, that my 9yr old could actually take up to 90mg but that he reduced it to 50mg. I told him that I learnt that the 50mg should be cut into two and one 25mg administered as a dose. I told him that 50mg is high only for the nurses to 'add mouth' and scold me, asking if I am teaching the doctor his job. I stormed out of the room where they were.

Left to my fate, I had to quickly make a decision. I'm aware that paracetamol start could be given, but there's no way those nurses will agree to give it since I had fallen out with them.

My next option to quickly arrest the fever became Ibuprofen. At least I can get the syrup & accurately calculate my daughter's dose based on her weight. I left to get the ibuprofen. Meanwhile the girl's temperature had gotten to 40.5°C. The doctors and nurses looked away from us (most likely wishing us the worst in their hearts so they can gloat if we run into a crisis).

I returned with the syrup, calculated the dose as 15ml & gave my girl. After about 40mins she began to sweat. Her temperature dropped to 38°, and we left the hospital to our home. Her temperature is now normal.

Thankfully, she is stable, and we'll continue with the other medications that she was given.

The point is, if I was not well informed,

1. We would have given the girl ACT and Augmentin tabs less than 2hrs after her injection of the same.

2. The doctor would have given her the 50mg Diclofenac suppository.

The question is, how many people take their prescriptions without scrutinising them? Many of them might be inappropriately calculated dosages, and people end up leaving hospitals with compromised/damaged organs while seeking for good health. 

Some Nigerian doctors may be contributing to Nigeria's organ failure crisis more than we imagine.
