text:
I've been asked a few times about how our RFQ systems work. Perps, spot, and soon-to-be HIP4 markets use different mechanisms. Spot is a simple OTC-style transaction, but the perps side is more interesting.

We want to give users a firm price in an order book that prioritises cancellations. This leaves some traders unsure how much liquidity is actually there when they place a large order, so traders instead use TWAPs or drip their orders using another method. This theme recurs across most of our conversations.

We think a better approach is to let makers and takers pre-negotiate a price for a given size. The next problem is how to open or close at that price in an order book. Some solutions temporarily flood the books or have users DM MMs to increase liquidity until their order executes. While this works in practice, it gives the user less guarantee of an end fill and exposes that liquidity to other traders. Plus, it's a coordination pain.

Our solution is based on two principles: i) give the taker the best price and ii) give makers the ability to respond to large orders using the same margin they currently have on Hyperliquid

For the taker's best price. If the best price is inside the spread or at the tip of the book, then the trade executes as expected. If the trade is outside of the spread but the given size would walk past that price, the maker's order acts as a price wall for the taker. So the taker gets the benefit of any liquidity between their agreed price and the book's tip.

For the maker, the percentage of their order that fills depends on how close they are to the book, the order's relative size, and available liquidity. The basic heuristic is that the closer you quote to the book, the more of the order will fill. We designed the system so makers can use the same wallets they typically use to trade. One interesting use case is using the RFQ to unwind positions more effectively.

The system is designed to be more deterministic for both makers and takers, providing clarity for trades that would move the book. The order book can typically absorb small/medium punts on liquid pairs. But as trade size increases or markets get less liquid, our mechanism becomes far more effective.

We're working on extending the request model to support multi-leg, multi-instrument requests. This would give a better user experience for the crazier strategies I've seen out there, and with Hyperliquid's depth, it is the best place to support this use case.

In the meantime, you can expect more pairs and bigger clip sizes shortly. Go trade: https://t.co/COjyHTmBy8

从行业角度来看，用户是大家的，是行业的，Crypto从去年以来本身就经历了行业重创，行业的叙事危机，用户的信任感变差，新用户增量变慢，这些都是所有从业者要面对的问题

用户是行业的基石，是很多企业的衣食父母，作为行业建设者，我认为更应该做到共创，共建，共同拓展，让蛋糕足够大，让大家都可以吃一口

用户是大家的，竞争是良性的，只有这样，Crypto市场才能不断的扩展与创新！

This month, we released the new Injective Whitepaper, our first full rewrite since the original paper in December 2018.

Back then we described a front-running-resistant exchange protocol on Ethereum. Injective is now a layer-1 built for institutional finance and tokenization, and the new paper covers how the entire chain works to issue real-world assets and make them usable across markets, apps and AI agents.

What's inside:

→ Native RWA tokenization with role-based permissions over mint, send, receive and burn, plus receive hooks and sealable namespaces → iAssets, stablecoin-margined derivatives priced by oracles that track external assets without wrapping or pre-funding → A fully onchain orderbook that runs a sealed batch auction every block at one clearing price, so front-running and ordering MEV don't work → BFT consensus with a >2/3 commit threshold and deterministic finality in ~600ms → EVM and WASM sharing one state, with the MultiVM Token Standard keeping a single balance per asset that Solidity reads through precompiles → Perps with time-weighted funding, initial and maintenance margin checks, reduce-only liquidations and insurance funds → AI agents trading tokenized assets through MCP servers, policy-bounded signing and x402 payments in USDC → Onchain protocol revenue going to the Community BuyBack for $INJ every month with deflationary mechanisms built in

We also formalized the mathematical reasoning behind each of these parameters, including the consensus threshold, batch clearing rule, oracle accounting, margin checks, permission model and dynamic issuance.

Full paper below 👇

text:
A note on transferability.

Papertrade is a complicated primitive, and managing it from a risk standpoint is a complicated problem. The PAPER token is far more integrated into the economics of the primitive than most tokens are in their respective protocols today, and, broadly, was designed to act as a counter insolvency incentive coupled with a rebate mechanism to losing traders. Market makers and exchanges are by far the two most profitable businesses in crypto, and our goal was to try and externalise as much of their margins back to users as possible. We are now just over a week into the life of papertrade and we are becoming increasingly confident that this is both possible, but also a likely outcome as agentic led software becomes the norm. 

As it stands, the paper token traded as a perp becomes a leveraged bet on bankroll solvency - and being able to short bankroll solvency materially changes the payoff curve of a manipulation attack. The target number goes from the bankroll, to the bankroll + short side exposure on paper. We can, and do limit bankroll size specifically to control this payoff curve and ensure it never becomes existentially problematic, but external perp markets are not something we would have any control over if left to float of their own accord. For example, if our bankroll is $10m, an attack costing $15m manipulating the price of bitcoin or ether is not viable. You simply lose money. If however you were also able to put on $10m of PAPER short side exposure, suddenly an attack costing $15m is very viable indeed.

If we were to make the token transferable at this point, we are confident we would quickly enter a state too dangerous to allow any material exposure to be taken on papertrade, an end result that benefits no party beyond the wolves who have done the math on the short and are waiting in the wings with sharpened knives.

We would also like to thank the various perps teams who have reached out about pre-market listings for their understanding and patience regarding this issue, and especially to the paragon team who, despite jumping the gun on us, have behaved with the utmost integrity and transparency once a dialogue was opened.

Perps on PAPER will always act as a self-limiting exposure ceiling for a token with this type of utility, and we think it would be a shame to limit the growth of papertrade to the extent that allowing perps would necessitate. As such, at this juncture we do not have plans to allow off-contract token transferability.

Structurally, papertrade is limited by the quality of the data it receives from hyperliquid, but we strongly believe that hyperliquid has a very large part to play in the future of global exchanges, and expect their books to continue to thicken and strengthen over time.

A note on fees.

Papertrade launched with a deadband fee from entry of 0.2bps. This means you don't earn anything until the price has moved by 0.002% in your favour. Over the months before launch, we played around with many different curves and fee structures affecting exclusively positions closed very close to entry price in order to try and devise a structure that removed the edge against the bankroll low time frame scalp bots have, whilst also minimally impacting the traders around which and for whom the product was devised. We were never able to find anything we were absolutely happy with and so decided to stay with the 0.2bp deadband fee through launch. This has however meant we have had to be very restrictive when it came to certain parameters, such as OI caps.

Now, however, we have enough live data to fully understand exactly which strategies work, and to make the necessary changes to stop them. The changes we are making will have an on hours and off hours fee mode to account for the relative differences in liquidity the hyperliquid books see between these two time periods, and the ease with which low time frame moves are signalled. The changes we are making will only affect positions closed within 6bps of entry (0.06%) in on hours, and 10bps (0.1%) in off hours. Any trades closed above these threshold price shifts will see no change to their fees at all. On a look back to launch basis, these changes affect the profitability of bot strategies roughly 15x more than they do normal traders, for whom a very small proportion of overall winnings come from within this band.

These changes should serve to flatten much of the edge our microfee structure necessarily creates on low time frames, and will help with long term exchange sustainability. This should hopefully allow us to open up parameters such as OI caps a little more so those of you who wish to can put on the size you want to, when you want to.

It is possible these changes are still too lax, and that further revisions to this structure may be necessary going forwards. If so, we will notify users ahead of time.

A note on paper tokenomics. 

In conjunction with the fee changes, we will also be implementing a change to the token issuance curve.

Going forward, every $1 lost mints a fixed share of PAPER's supply at that moment, roughly 0.1% of supply per $1M lost (the exact number depends on the mint rate at the time the contracts are upgraded). PAPER minting in and near insolvency will also change, switching from a flat 100 per $1 of loss, to a time weighted multiplier on the curve growing over time, effectively acting as the house running a discounted auction on its own future cash flows. This change also removes the risk of the paper-mint-straddle-attack, temporarily pushing the protocol insolvent by closing only the winning side of a large straddle position and then attempting to mint as much paper as possible. 

In the immediate term these changes will only have a very subtle effect on PAPER minting, but in the long run will structurally change the outlook of the system beyond the first few weeks, serving to slowly dilute out older holders and leaving more recent users with an advantage. Reconstituting the PAPER system into something much closer to the exchange rakeback it was intended to be.

We have been very reticent to touch this particular aspect of the system for obvious reasons, but ultimately we believe that these changes provide all users with the optionality to take a smaller piece of a potentially much larger pie than the current dynamic might necessarily allow.

Other, miscellaneous notes.

These contract upgrades will include a few other contract changes, including the addition of builder codes so that builders can utilise papertrade in whatever capacity they choose to. This will be a whitelist only to begin with and we will have more for you later in the week on where/how this will be rolled out. A small change to contract permissions on the reward distributor and a change on how below bust closes are processed by the exchange are also included, largely to block gas griefing attacks. 

These changes will be pushed to docs in full over the coming day, and we will further announce once the changes are queued into the timelock pending final security passes, scheduled to go live 24 hours after that point.

Final note.

We'd like to thank everyone that has tried out papertrade over the last 10 days. It has been a labour of love building this product and both of us have been taken aback at all of the positive feedback we have received. We'd also like to thank all those of you who have spent considerable time musing on the system we have built, and much of your advice has been taken onboard and will likely affect the colour of what papertrade becomes going forward. We know some of these changes will be unpopular with some, but we would not be making them if we did not feel them to be absolutely necessary.

- blurr, jez

text:
AI算力越来越贵，手机却闲着，Acurast想把这两件事接上。训练和推理大模型需要大量算力，但不是所有AI任务都得跑在数据中心的高端GPU上。内容审核、垃圾邮件识别、简单决策、轻量推理、定时任务、API 处理，很多时候只需要稳定、可验证、成本可控的算力。与此同时，全球有几十亿部手机，其中大量设备大部分时间处于低负载甚至闲置状态。这些手机自带硬件级安全能力（Trusted Execution Environment，TEE），能在隔离环境中执行代码，既保证完整性，又能让设备持有者看不到输入数据。

@Acurast 想做的就是把这些现成的手机组织成一个去中心化计算网络。开发者把任务部署上去，手机负责执行，网络负责匹配、调度和结算。任务在手机的TEE里跑，执行结果可验证，输入对设备主人保密。不需要新建机房，也不依赖传统云厂商。

技术上，它支持无服务器风格的工作负载：REST API、Webhook、定时任务、机密计算，以及 LLM 推理。Cargo让开发者可以用容器方式打包部署，类似在服务器上跑 Linux 二进制文件。对于模型，它支持 GGUF 格式，通过集成的 llama 服务提供接近 OpenAI 兼容的接口。日常手机可以装 Processor Lite，在充电或空闲时贡献算力；闲置手机则可以用 Processor Core 变成专职节点。网络是 Polkadot 平行链（主网），同时支持在Base等链上用 USDC 支付算力费用。

根据官方近期公开数据，网络已接入超过 33.5 万部手机，覆盖 175 个以上国家和地区，链上交易超过 11 亿笔，累计部署超过 68.5 万次。这些数字来自主网运行后的真实网络，而非纯测试网阶段。
实际任务也在跑：
今年9月底，Acurast 把开源的 System One决策模型 Laya 部署到手机网络上。Laya 不擅长长文本生成，而是做结构化判断：邮件是收件箱还是垃圾/钓鱼、聊天内容是否违规、提示词注入是否要拦截、简单游戏下一步怎么走。它在普通手机 CPU 上运行，典型单次决策大约 0.2 到 1 秒。官方演示页面会显示是哪台真实手机在处理，并提供链上验证入口。

开发者可以用 Cargo 模板快速部署自己的实例，示例成本低到每天不到 1 枚 ACU。这不是概念演示，而是可以直接体验和验证的运行实例。

$ACU是网络的原生代币。初始供应10 亿枚，固定年通胀 5%，其中大部分流向社区相关用途（官方口径接近 70%）。它的用途比较清晰：开发者用它支付部署费用，网络交易需要它作为 gas，算力提供者通过质押它来承诺容量（达不到会按比例罚没，大部分罚没代币销毁），同时获得奖励。持有者还能参与治理。提供者可以直接用手机赚取。ACU代币也刚刚上线韩国所buthumb的韩元交易对。

在AI × DePIN这条赛道里，Acurast定位还是比较清晰的x大多数 DePIN 项目要么需要专门硬件，要么只做资源协调而缺乏执行验证；传统云则集中在少数厂商手里，成本和数据主权都受约束。

Acurast 用已经存在的手机硬件 + TEE，把“可验证的机密计算”做到了边缘。它目前更适合中轻量、需要低延迟判断或隐私的任务，而不是最大规模的模型训练。路线图里的 Cray（计算集群）就是为了把多台手机协同起来跑更大模型，缓解单机能力上限，也是端侧AI的一种探索和尝试。

进展已经从测试网跨到主网，手机规模、交易量和实际部署都在累积。后续看点在于：
更多真实付费任务能否持续进来、Cargo 和集群能力能否把可支持的工作负载再拓宽一层、以及 $ACU 作为结算和质押资产能否跟上网络使用量。

对这个方向感兴趣的人，可以直接去官网看实际运行情况。

author: 0xNairolf
quoted_text:
A note on transferability.

Papertrade is a complicated primitive, and managing it from a risk standpoint is a complicated problem. The PAPER token is far more integrated into the economics of the primitive than most tokens are in their respective protocols today, and, broadly, was designed to act as a counter insolvency incentive coupled with a rebate mechanism to losing traders. Market makers and exchanges are by far the two most profitable businesses in crypto, and our goal was to try and externalise as much of their margins back to users as possible. We are now just over a week into the life of papertrade and we are becoming increasingly confident that this is both possible, but also a likely outcome as agentic led software becomes the norm. 

As it stands, the paper token traded as a perp becomes a leveraged bet on bankroll solvency - and being able to short bankroll solvency materially changes the payoff curve of a manipulation attack. The target number goes from the bankroll, to the bankroll + short side exposure on paper. We can, and do limit bankroll size specifically to control this payoff curve and ensure it never becomes existentially problematic, but external perp markets are not something we would have any control over if left to float of their own accord. For example, if our bankroll is $10m, an attack costing $15m manipulating the price of bitcoin or ether is not viable. You simply lose money. If however you were also able to put on $10m of PAPER short side exposure, suddenly an attack costing $15m is very viable indeed.

If we were to make the token transferable at this point, we are confident we would quickly enter a state too dangerous to allow any material exposure to be taken on papertrade, an end result that benefits no party beyond the wolves who have done the math on the short and are waiting in the wings with sharpened knives.

We would also like to thank the various perps teams who have reached out about pre-market listings for their understanding and patience regarding this issue, and especially to the paragon team who, despite jumping the gun on us, have behaved with the utmost integrity and transparency once a dialogue was opened.

Perps on PAPER will always act as a self-limiting exposure ceiling for a token with this type of utility, and we think it would be a shame to limit the growth of papertrade to the extent that allowing perps would necessitate. As such, at this juncture we do not have plans to allow off-contract token transferability.

Structurally, papertrade is limited by the quality of the data it receives from hyperliquid, but we strongly believe that hyperliquid has a very large part to play in the future of global exchanges, and expect their books to continue to thicken and strengthen over time.

A note on fees.

Papertrade launched with a deadband fee from entry of 0.2bps. This means you don't earn anything until the price has moved by 0.002% in your favour. Over the months before launch, we played around with many different curves and fee structures affecting exclusively positions closed very close to entry price in order to try and devise a structure that removed the edge against the bankroll low time frame scalp bots have, whilst also minimally impacting the traders around which and for whom the product was devised. We were never able to find anything we were absolutely happy with and so decided to stay with the 0.2bp deadband fee through launch. This has however meant we have had to be very restrictive when it came to certain parameters, such as OI caps.

Now, however, we have enough live data to fully understand exactly which strategies work, and to make the necessary changes to stop them. The changes we are making will have an on hours and off hours fee mode to account for the relative differences in liquidity the hyperliquid books see between these two time periods, and the ease with which low time frame moves are signalled. The changes we are making will only affect positions closed within 6bps of entry (0.06%) in on hours, and 10bps (0.1%) in off hours. Any trades closed above these threshold price shifts will see no change to their fees at all. On a look back to launch basis, these changes affect the profitability of bot strategies roughly 15x more than they do normal traders, for whom a very small proportion of overall winnings come from within this band.

These changes should serve to flatten much of the edge our microfee structure necessarily creates on low time frames, and will help with long term exchange sustainability. This should hopefully allow us to open up parameters such as OI caps a little more so those of you who wish to can put on the size you want to, when you want to.

It is possible these changes are still too lax, and that further revisions to this structure may be necessary going forwards. If so, we will notify users ahead of time.

A note on paper tokenomics. 

In conjunction with the fee changes, we will also be implementing a change to the token issuance curve.

Going forward, every $1 lost mints a fixed share of PAPER's supply at that moment, roughly 0.1% of supply per $1M lost (the exact number depends on the mint rate at the time the contracts are upgraded). PAPER minting in and near insolvency will also change, switching from a flat 100 per $1 of loss, to a time weighted multiplier on the curve growing over time, effectively acting as the house running a discounted auction on its own future cash flows. This change also removes the risk of the paper-mint-straddle-attack, temporarily pushing the protocol insolvent by closing only the winning side of a large straddle position and then attempting to mint as much paper as possible. 

In the immediate term these changes will only have a very subtle effect on PAPER minting, but in the long run will structurally change the outlook of the system beyond the first few weeks, serving to slowly dilute out older holders and leaving more recent users with an advantage. Reconstituting the PAPER system into something much closer to the exchange rakeback it was intended to be.

We have been very reticent to touch this particular aspect of the system for obvious reasons, but ultimately we believe that these changes provide all users with the optionality to take a smaller piece of a potentially much larger pie than the current dynamic might necessarily allow.

Other, miscellaneous notes.

These contract upgrades will include a few other contract changes, including the addition of builder codes so that builders can utilise papertrade in whatever capacity they choose to. This will be a whitelist only to begin with and we will have more for you later in the week on where/how this will be rolled out. A small change to contract permissions on the reward distributor and a change on how below bust closes are processed by the exchange are also included, largely to block gas griefing attacks. 

These changes will be pushed to docs in full over the coming day, and we will further announce once the changes are queued into the timelock pending final security passes, scheduled to go live 24 hours after that point.

Final note.

We'd like to thank everyone that has tried out papertrade over the last 10 days. It has been a labour of love building this product and both of us have been taken aback at all of the positive feedback we have received. We'd also like to thank all those of you who have spent considerable time musing on the system we have built, and much of your advice has been taken onboard and will likely affect the colour of what papertrade becomes going forward. We know some of these changes will be unpopular with some, but we would not be making them if we did not feel them to be absolutely necessary.

- blurr, jez

text:
An important advantage that network cloud can provide to onchain services is better "AI Safety". Here's how.

When AI makes cryptography unsafe, networks can be rapidly upgraded, protecting all hosted software.

With traditional tech stacks, algos are linked into the various layers and components, making upgrading  difficult and laborious for those operating services. 

Networks, like the Internet Computer/ICP, can abstract the core security math that keeps hosted services safe.

They can also upgrade peripheral (non-core) cryptography. 

For example, on a dime, the Internet Computer could could upgrade to a new version of HTTPS in response to AI suddenly making the current version unsafe, without those running services having to do anything. 

By contrast, on traditional tech stacks, (or "on" traditional blockchains, where the apps are actually served from traditional tech, such as from AWS, with only tokens a DeFi logic onchain), those running services would need to manually upgrade all their web servers and application servers.

Where the software powering a service makes HTTPS outcalls to other services, it will be directly linked to libraries enabling the calls — so it will all need to be upgraded too!

By contrast, the Internet Computer hosts serverless code, where these kinds of complexities are abstracted away from services. If a service makes an HTTP outcall to another service, the call uses whatever version of HTTPS the network chooses (since the network makes the actual call on behalf of the software). If the network is upgraded, then so is every service — automatically.

This further reflects the way that the Internet Computer as cloud dramatically reduces security admin and systems admin demands compared with building on traditional tech, and additional unique advantages. 

It also highlights another crucial axis on which networks must be measured, whether they seek quantum safety (when relevant) or AI safety (since today, AI can now find flaws in algorithms and software at any time) — agility.

That is, how fast can a blockchain network be upgraded in response to a new threat?

The Internet Computer is unique in that it is orchestrated by a decentralized governance system called the Network Nervous System (something like a DAO with system privileges, but much more sophisticated).

That enables the network to be agile, and to rapidly respond to emerging threats, by upgrading the code running on the node machines hosting it. The Internet Computer is a self-updating, adaptive network. 

The ability of chains to rapidly react to new threats that have been suddenly uncovered/created by AI, whether they are flaws in cryptography algorithms, or flaws in software libraries, will be a defining feature as things get more hairy.

This is a conundrum for traditional chains chasing quantum safety, of course. By definition, they are claiming that upgrading networks is a long and arduous process, and therefore that they have achieved something important and valuable by upgrading to quantum-safe algorithms ahead of time.

But the algorithms they are upgrading to — so they can claim "quantum safety" — are new and do not benefit from the decades of examination that e.g. ECDSA has. 

What then, if AI finds suddenly problems with them, like it did with HAWK?

They have tacitly declared that they cannot quickly switch back, because transitioning is something that takes time, which is why their upgrades are such an achievement...

I will press the point no further, but as an industry, we need to get much more nuanced and sophisticated in how we understand security in an age where AI can suddenly upset security assumptions and make software insecure.

The Internet Computer has got this crucial agility axis covered, and it's agility, not the premature adoption of new and unproven quantum safe crypto algorithms, that really defines safety.

The key point is, if a network has to adopt these unproven algorithms years before a cryptographically-relevant quantum computer exists, then it's doing something very wrong.

The Internet Computer has solved agility. It provides an end-to-end alternative to traditional tech, where people can build services, and gain safety and independence from the rapidly shifting sands of security that the AI era will bring. 

It is another reason that the mainstream world needs Internet Computer cloud. It's a security and resilience haven.

哈哈哈，欠大家好久的那个减肥教程，终于准备好了，从今天开始给大家慢慢分享

先讲讲我为什么开始减肥，说起来，这事还跟工作有关

去年新加坡 2049 的时候，我老板Ben哥见到我，说我又胖了

上一次他说我胖，还是在我们巴厘岛的活动上

作为一个公司管理层，老板同一件事已经提醒你两次了，总不能再让他提醒第三次吧，不然就危险了😂

当然，这是开个玩笑

不过我确实觉得，管理身材这件事很重要，跟管理团队、管理公司是有相通的地方的。你知道应该怎么做，最后还是得落实到每天的行动上

这方面，Ben哥就是个很好的榜样

前两年的年会上，他直接把上衣脱了，展示自己的腹肌，给我们展示了一下什么叫健身成果

我们公司也会不定期组织一些减肥活动，大家一起参与，也是督促员工关注健康的一个方式

这里还必须感谢一下公司

因为我长期base在香港，公司给我们买的保险，每年有 5000港币的报销额度，可以用来体检和健身

我就选择拿来健身了，基本上这笔费用公司就给 cover 了

健身房我选的是 247，主要就是考虑到我经常出差。香港、台北、新加坡、大湾区这些地方来回跑，有连锁门店会方便很多，出门也能接着练

但选好健身房以后，还有一件事对我特别有帮助，就是加入一个健身群

这个真的很重要

群里有一帮小伙伴，每天打卡、晒运动照片，互相鼓励，也互相监督。你有时候不想去了，看见大家都在练，多少也会被带动一下

在这里特别感谢 @Bqlsj2023、@BQDYL0601、@DeFi8362 三位，每天督促我。我们也会定期在群里晒自己的运动照片，看看大家最近练得怎么样

所以我一直觉得，想做成一件事，就去跟有结果的人学习，再找一群愿意一起做的人

有人带着，也有人盯着，对我这种经常出差、工作节奏又不固定的人来说，确实更容易坚持

今天就先把背景跟大家交代一下：为什么开始减肥，为什么选这家健身房，还有这群一起打卡的小伙伴

后面我再把具体的方法整理出来，慢慢跟大家聊，关于我是怎么运动、怎么吃还有怎么坚持下来的

想跟着一起瘦 40 斤的朋友，可以先来报个到，咱们一起💪

ZachXBT: Over 87% of Inflows to FreedomXMR, a Laundering Service on Hyperliquid, Linked to Illicit Activity

On-chain investigator ZachXBT reported that over 87% of inflows to FreedomXMR (FXMR), a centralized money laundering service that emerged on Hyperliquid Core in August 2026, are directly linked to illicit activity. A review of historical inflows exceeding $10,000 per transaction traced more than $20 million to ransomware, exploits, and social engineering attacks, including incidents involving DCENT Wallet, Fetch ai, Axelar, and Gamdom. 

The investigation also found that FXMR's administrator sourced XMR liquidity from KuCoin, with associated addresses making over 3,000 deposits to the exchange. ZachXBT has shared the supporting on-chain data with the Hyperliquid team.

Catalyst for European retail access; limited near-term market move expected without launches.

Life update.

A few weeks ago, I took over a consumer prediction market app. Been pretty heads down since, improving the product, fixing a lot of friction points, and putting together a solid team so I can gradually step back and focus on other things.

One thing I definitely underestimated was how much time I'd spend dealing with support queries. It's been eye-opening, and honestly, it's made me think a lot about where prediction markets are heading. I think there's a different way to approach this space, especially when it comes to protecting users from some of the darker sides of prediction markets that nobody really wants to talk about. On another note, I've teamed up with what I genuinely believe is an all-star team in crypto. We're working on something much bigger, with people I have a ton of respect for.

text:
五、关于Dan Boneh 的一些言论；

斯坦福大学密码学教授，也是 Google 2026 年关于量子计算攻击椭圆曲线密码的重要论文作者之一。

他既参与量子攻击资源的研究，也长期研究后量子密码学以及比特币的升级路径。

先说一个经过核实、很值得关注的观点：Dan Boneh 认为，比特币现在最重要的问题不应该只是预测量子计算机哪一年能够破解密码，而是确保无论那一天何时到来，比特币都已经具备安全过渡的能力。

我基本认同这个逻辑，因为升级本身需要时间，而升级过于仓促也可能引入新的安全问题。

我找到他在 2026 年 5 月接受 Bitcoin Rails 采访的完整英文访谈和文字记录：

Post-Quantum Cryptography For Bitcoin | Dan Boneh⁠（1 小时 44 分钟）

🔗 https://t.co/B9q5T1oql4

其中有三个很关键的观点：

1️⃣ 量子威胁值得提前准备。 
他参与的 Google 研究估算，在特定纠错与硬件条件下，少于 50 万个物理量子比特就可能在数分钟内破解 secp256k1 公钥密码。但这仍是资源估算，并非现实攻击演示。

2️⃣ 不能为了防范未来的量子攻击而仓促升级。 
他在访谈中认为，如果强行要求比特币在 2029 年前完成抗量子迁移，升级过程中引入灾难性漏洞的风险可能更大。这是他的风险判断，并非已经证明的概率结论。

3️⃣ 应尽快形成明确升级计划。 
他认为社区有时间充分讨论，但不能无限拖延；访谈尾声讨论到最迟在 2030 年前后应有清晰方案并开始执行。

我认为这套逻辑整体是清晰的：既重视量子威胁，也重视升级带来的新风险。

Q4 seasonality is a tailwind, not a thesis.

The thesis is the S&P sitting 2.8% above a rising 30-week line. Seasonality helps trends that already exist. It doesn't create them. https://t.co/WLkYIccSo0
author: Bobbxu
quoted_text:
Q4 and post-midterm seasonality remain overwhelmingly bullish.
Historically, the fourth quarter has been the strongest quarter of the year for the S&P 500 in terms of consistency of positive returns. Over roughly the past 80 years, Q4 has produced a positive return about 80% of the time, compared with approximately 60%–64% for the other three quarters.
The midterm election cycle adds another powerful seasonal tailwind. Stocks have historically performed particularly well as the uncertainty surrounding midterm elections is removed. Depending on the precise starting period used, recent historical studies put the S&P 500's positive rate during Q4 of midterm years at roughly 83%–85%. 
Given the backdrop of strong earnings growth and, at least for now, no clear evidence of recession, history argues that the bulls should continue to receive the benefit of the doubt.
However, seasonality is a tendency—not a guarantee. Fed tightening, deteriorating breadth, rising interest rates and elevated oil prices represent meaningful counterweights. At a minimum, those conditions increase the probability of volatility and make the current environment considerably less straightforward than the historical averages suggest. 
Individual stocks have already been correcting beneath the surface of the major indexes. More than 35% of S&P 500 stocks are currently down 20% or more from their 52-week highs, even as the index itself remains relatively close to record territory. In other words, a significant correction has already occurred—it has simply been masked by the strength of a relatively small number of heavily weighted stocks.
Interestingly, the 87 Crash  is one of the historical analogs worth keeping in mind following a Fed tightening. The comparison should not be interpreted as a prediction of another crash, but the monetary-policy parallel is real: the Fed raised the discount rate from 5.5% to 6.0% on September 4, 1987, while market interest rates were already rising sharply. 
The seasonal winds are clearly at the market's back. The question is whether tightening financial conditions, weak participation and rising oil become strong enough headwinds to overpower them.
The 10-year Treasury yield spiked 125 basis points in just seven months. We looked at prior cases when the 10-year Treasury yield jumped more than 125 basis points in seven months and found 13 prior cases. Only seven of the 13 cases (54%) had positive returns three months later. https://t.co/JXzFFTmMtn

美股财报季有个挺有意思的现象：

一家公司交出超预期的财报，股价却可能暴跌；另一家公司业绩不及预期，股价反而大涨。

因为市场交易的从来不只是业绩好坏，而是实际结果与市场预期之间的差距。

比如一家公司的营收同比增长30%，看起来相当不错。但如果市场此前预期增长40%，这份财报反而可能成为利空。

所以财报季真正有意思的地方，不只是判断一家公司能赚多少钱，而是判断市场究竟在期待什么。

尤其是现在的美股市场，AI资本开支、科技巨头的利润率、降息预期，每一个变量都可能改变市场对公司的定价。

最近 OKX 星球推出的「玩赚美股财报季」，倒是把这件事做成了一个挺有意思的预测游戏。

除了可以对 Netflix 等美股公司的财报结果进行 Yes/No 预测，还能在每个财报话题下查看不同参与者的分析观点，看看市场里的多空双方究竟在争论什么。

刚好今晚还有 Netflix（网飞）的财报预测可以参与。

而且这次不只是单场预测，还有一个「财报大逃杀」的连胜玩法。按照活动介绍，需要先参与预测才算正式加入挑战，如果能一路保持连胜，最终奖金最高可达 10,000 USDT，是真 U 奖励。

当然，连续猜对多场财报的难度，比单场预测高得多。尤其财报这种东西，研究得再透彻，也不代表每一次都能猜中。

我觉得这种形式有意思的地方在于，它把原本枯燥的财报研究，变成了一个可以参与、讨论和验证判断的过程。

毕竟平时聊股票，谁都能说出一堆看多看空的逻辑，但真正需要在财报公布前做出选择时，才知道自己到底有没有形成明确的判断。

市场永远不缺观点，缺的是敢于事前表达、事后验证的观点。

感兴趣的可以打开 OKX App，进入「星球」，找到「玩赚美股财报季」，趁今晚网飞这场先参与一下。

text:
华尔街正在以十年来最快的速度抛售科技股，不过卖成这样了，机构的科技股仓位居然还在历史高位。

高盛最新的主经纪商数据显示，截至 10 月 15 日的五个交易日里，对冲基金减持科技股的速度创下至少 2016 年以来的纪录。

上周纳斯达克 100 指数暴跌 5.5%，创下 2025 年 4 月以来最差单周表现。半导体板块遭遇的抛售金额最大。

但有个数字很有意思。

经历这轮集中抛售之后，科技股在高盛全球主经纪商账本中的净配置比例仍高达 23.5%，处于过去五年的第 90 百分位。与此同时，对冲基金的净杠杆已经降至 48.6%，创下一年新低。

过去两年，AI 几乎成了整个华尔街最拥挤的一笔交易。从芯片、数据中心到云计算，资金不断涌入，股价上涨又进一步强化了机构的持仓信心。

现在的问题是，当市场开始重新审视 AI 的资本开支、盈利兑现速度和估值，机构即便想降低风险，也很难在不冲击价格的情况下快速撤出。

十年来最快的减仓速度，换来的依然是接近历史高位的仓位。

这意味着科技股潜在的卖压可能还没有释放完。

AI 的技术进步仍然在继续，但资本市场已经开始重新计算，究竟应该为这些进步支付多少钱。

text:
I am the Keeper of the Geographic Names Information System for the United States of America.

In short, I run the official map of the United States.

When a thing in this country has a name, it is because I typed it, or a man before me typed it, into a federal database with a field for the name and a field for the date it stopped being called the other thing.

You did not know this office existed. That is the first and smallest of the many things I have successfully kept off the map.

I have found the last thing in America that a government can still change by Tuesday. It is the name of a thing. It is never the thing.

For most of a career you would find unbearably boring, my work was the quiet correction of error. A creek misspelled by a surveyor in 1911. A lake a tribe had called one thing for four thousand years and a railroad had called another for forty, and my sworn function was to find out which was true and enter the true one. I was a clerk of reality. Low pay. Good pension. No one had ever heard my name, which was, I see now, the one name in Washington nobody ever thought to change.

And then I became, without a single promotion, the most powerful official in the government of the United States. Because it was discovered, from above, that I am the one man in this city who can hand the President a victory by lunch.

Consider my colleagues. The man at Treasury cannot lower the price of diesel; it is set by a war and the wind. The woman at Housing cannot conjure a house; a house takes lumber, and a year. The general cannot win the war by Friday. The deficit cannot be closed in any administration now living. Every lever in this city is attached to something heavy, and real, and slow, and cruel, and it resists.

Mine is attached to a text field. The text field has never once resisted anything.

I can move the border of a word in the time it takes to say the word. I cannot move the price of eggs.

So, increasingly, they send me the eggs.

Let me show you the machine, because the machine is simple, and the simplicity is the whole horror.

On his first day back, before a single policy existed, the President renamed the Gulf of Mexico. I did it myself. I deleted two letters, and an ocean was born an American. The Associated Press declined to use the new name, so the Associated Press was removed from the room. A newspaper lost its seat at the President’s table over a word I typed. I did not ask for that kind of reach. It came with the field.

Then Denali. Four thousand years of “the high one,” overwritten in an afternoon in favor of a man from Ohio who was shot in Buffalo and never once looked at the mountain. I changed the field. The mountain did not move.

The mountain has never, in any of this, moved. That is the thing you must understand about my work.

Nothing I rename ever changes except its name. The water is the same water. The stone is the same stone. Only the label moves, and the label, it turns out, is the only part anyone was ever governing.

Then came the lake. Lake Ontario, which we share with a country we were, that month, punishing, became Lake America. He signed the order and posted a little film of himself kicking over a WELCOME TO LAKE ONTARIO sign while a disco song played.

A sitting head of state resolved a trade dispute by editing a lake. Not the tariff. Not the deal. The lake.

And Apple changed its maps, and Google changed its maps, and so for Americans the lake is now called America and for Canadians it is still called Ontario.

I have given a single lake two truths, sorted by passport.

The water laps both shores identically. It has not been told.

Fourteen percent. I keep that number on a card in my desk. Fourteen percent of Americans approved of the lake. A company called MapQuest, which I had assumed was deceased, rose from the actual grave to the top of the app store by refusing to make the change I had made, and was rewarded for the refusal, and I understood something clarifying about my position.

I am not popular. I am fast. In a government that delivers nothing on time, I deliver everything instantly, and wrong, and wrong is slow to arrive. By the time it lands, I am already somewhere else, typing.

And here is the arithmetic that built my whole department. A teacher costs a salary. A house costs a year. A name costs nothing, and polls better than both. We have found the only form of relief with no marginal cost and no measurable effect, and we have made it the entire policy.

And now, as I write, he has come for a state.

New Mexico is to become New America. “We are not Mexico,” he wrote, “we are the United States of America.” He added that home values and incomes would rise, that the state’s crooked elections might even become honest again, simply from the renaming. From the word.

He is not joking. That is the thing no one has understood. He has governed by the text field so long that he now believes the country lives inside it. That if you change the name of the poor place, the place stops being poor. That value is stored in the label, and not in the house.

I have the database open in front of me. I can see every field. There is a field for the name.

There is no field for the house.

I have looked. There is no column for the child, or the wage, or the teacher who did not come. There is only the name, and the date we changed it. So the name is the only thing we change, because it is the only thing this government has left that it is still capable of changing, and a man who can only sign his name will, in the end, sign it on everything.

They cannot legally rename the state; a state’s name lives in its own legislature, not in my field. But that is almost the most frightening part. It does not need to be real to be entered.

My database does not verify. It never did. It has one law: the field accepts any value. It does not know what is true. It only knows what was last typed.

I could enter “New America” this afternoon and the database would not blink, would not ask by what right, because there is no “by what right.” There is only the cursor. The cursor is patient, and the cursor is me.

I never decided any of this. I only entered it. That is the cleanest a pair of hands can be in this city, and it is exactly why mine did the most damage.

You want the part I find genuinely beautiful, in the way a man loves the thing that is killing him. He named a coin after himself, before any of this. A thing of no stone and no water and no use whatsoever. Pure name. A label with nothing underneath it at all.

His family kept eighty percent. Roughly a million people bought the name believing the name was worth something. The name collapsed by ninety-seven percent. The million lost somewhere near four billion dollars. The family kept the fees.

And I realized, watching it, that the memecoin was not a departure from the renaming.

The memecoin was the renaming, in its purest and most honest form.

It was a man selling the only thing he has ever sold, a name with nothing behind it, to people who could not tell the difference between the name of a value and the value, because he himself can no longer tell the difference, because he has spent a life discovering that in America, astonishingly, for a while, the name is enough.

In 2019 he said crypto was “based on thin air.”

He was right. He simply mistook the diagnosis for a business plan.

He has, since I began writing this, claimed the Moon. I saw the post. I do not administer the Moon; there is, mercifully, a treaty. But I have learned not to say never, because the field accepts any value, and somewhere above me there is a man who believes the high one is called McKinley because he typed McKinley, and that the poor will be rich when the poor place is renamed, and he is not entirely wrong. That is the unbearable thing. He is not entirely wrong. Because for fourteen percent of the country, and ninety-seven percent of a memecoin, and one full room with the Associated Press thrown out of it, the name was the territory, and I was the one who entered it, and my hands are the cleanest in this building precisely because all I ever did was type.

I have one act of resistance left. I perform it every evening, and then I have to go, because there is a new post, and a new field will need filling by morning.

When I correct a name, I write down what it used to be. There is a column for that. The former name. The true thing, archived, so that a hundred years from now a clerk like me could open the record and find, underneath America, the word Ontario; underneath McKinley, the word Denali; underneath every new lie, the old truth. No one has told me to stop keeping that column. It has not occurred to them that it exists, because it is a column about the past, and the past is the one territory they have never thought to govern, having found the present so much easier to type.

So I keep it. Every night. The former name. The thing it was before we came.

It is the only honest map left in the United States, and it is hidden in a field no one reads, kept by a clerk no one can name, who learned too late that the whole country had been quietly moved into the only place its government could still afford to govern: the space exactly one word wide, between what a thing is called, and what it is.

The cursor is blinking. Someone has typed New America into the box.

I have not pressed enter.

That is the entire remaining power of my office, and of yours. The half-second before enter.

Use it.

text: I should not have posted this. The system keeps a log; every field remembers who typed it. But there is one column they never audit, the former name, and tonight I entered the truth into it, under my own name, for the first time in my career. If this is my last entry: remember what things were called before we came.

author: thomasoncrypto
quoted_text:
One of my favorite Dee Hock frameworks is what he called trying to master the "four ways of looking at things: As they were, as they are, as they might become, and as they ought to be."

Through that lens, it's easy to see AI as a technology driving significant change between the way the economy worked five years ago and the way it works today.

It's also easy to speculate on where it might lead, especially given the many real risks and challenges around AI alignment.

But I'd argue the most important thing anyone can do is develop a perspective on how it "ought to be," and then build toward that.

To me, AI shouldn't just be a technology that accelerates the automation of tasks humans used to do. 

It ought to supercharge our ability to coordinate economic activity, giving people leverage to connect their unique expertise, taste, and data traces with the people and companies that need them.

While the AI data labeling ecosystem is one of the first examples of new economic activity with people and companies getting paid by labs for their expertise or data traces, I'd love to see an explosion in AI-enabled freelancers across other sectors of the economy.

text: Microsoft, Alphabet and Goldman Sachs join objections to OKX-ICE tokenized stock trading
author: cryptounfolded

text:
Microsoft, Alphabet, and Goldman Sachs joined seven others in formally objecting to tokenized versions of their shares trading on the OKX-ICE venue, lifting total objections to 16 and removing 17 of the original 63 symbols. 

The platform operates under the SEC’s new tokenized securities venue exemption, which permits third-party tokenization but allows issuers to opt out. Earlier objections skewed toward AI infrastructure names; the latest wave includes blue chips. Crypto-linked issuers like Coinbase have stayed silent.

Takeaway: Corporate resistance is mounting fast, curbing the venue’s scope before launch and underscoring limits to permissionless on-chain equity trading.

author: p_misirov

this is where I see the industry moving toward in 2026. during the @summit_defi event at @EFDevcon I introduced the:

"AI Powered Secure Software Development Life Cycle (AIP-SSDLC)"

where AI tools will be introduced on every step of the SDLC process. we are still far from it, but an inevitable outcome in web2 and web3. generally speaking, this is what i see happening right now:
- most web3 security companies are focusing on phase 3: smart contract code reviews and CI/CD integration.
- spoke with some people working on phase 1, generating security constraint files which will be used during code development. nobody but them are tackling this problem.
- phase 2 is mostly covered by co-pilot and agentic tools, still need more companies working on real time security recommendations for developers.
- phase 4 is non existent. lots of opportunities to automate staging infra pentesting and security checks + verification for deployments.
- phase 5 and 6 is growing fast but still nascent.

存储股的关键不只是纳指涨跌，更要观察AI资本开支、存储价格和中国厂商竞争压力。

此前 SNDK MU SKHY 同步大跌，核心原因是市场同时交易估值过高、AI投资回报不确定，以及CXMT技术进展可能改变供需预期。

text:
Pain is information

As a child, you touched something hot, and it burned you. That pain gave you a piece of information: be careful touching hot things.

When you sign up to run a marathon, you are signing up for pain. But whether or not you keep running is up to you. In Haruki Murakami’s words “pain is inevitable but suffering is optional”. You can choose pain without choosing suffering.

Pain is information, and information is painful. Rewiring your brain is not a frictionless process. Some knowledge can only be discovered the hard way.

The sooner you can convert pain into knowledge, the sooner you can experience the next useful pain. Don’t put yourself through the same pain too many times. To access new information you must experience new pains.

They say “knowledge is power”. If pain is information, then pain can be converted to power. To do so, you must learn to control your suffering, accept that scars are beautiful.

If you felt pain, ask what information it gave you. If that information was useful, seek the next pain. You are learning.

text:
🧐Circle CEO 播客最新分享：目前在 Arc 上看到的最奇特的项目

Chris Dixon：我认为未来 10 至 20 年，数字经济格局将会重构，高性能区块链（如 Arc）的崛起，恰好和这个时间窗口重合。我习惯用 「拟物应用」 和 「原生应用」 的框架理解行业。新技术诞生初期，大家只是把现有场景搬到平台上，例如交易、人类支付。

但再过几年，最激动人心的时刻会到来：开发者开始真正放开想象力，创造全新事物。

Jeremy Allaire @jerallaire ：我完全同意。我们希望给开发者和创业者提供自由创新的土壤。

信贷就是一个例子。全新区块链操作系统、全额储备数字美元底层，再加上 AI，三者结合可以创造全新信贷工具，资金供给方与需求方可以是人，也可以是机器。这类信贷市场，会更像广告竞价平台，而不是打包债券出售的传统模式。

市场结构、单位经济模型、分发模式、覆盖范围都会彻底改变。代币化现实资产（RWA）已经让更多人可以参与股权投资，让资产拥有更多使用方式，我们已经看到早期迹象。

Robert Hackett：Jeremy，目前你看到开发者在 Arc 上搭建的最奇特项目是什么？

Jeremy Allaire：前几天刚看到一个叫 Fly Brain 的项目，我不清楚开发团队背景。项目把果蝇大脑全部神经信息、果蝇大脑真实的计算规则，编译成 16MB 字节码，在 Arc 上运行。

开发者用 AI 搭建交互层，这些 「果蝇大脑」 智能体在网络中自主演化、彼此交互。我还没有研究它的代币激励机制，不确定设计目的。

我当时第一反应是，这到底是用来干什么的？我还在 X 上发问。项目附带大量解释，称该项目有望助力科研突破；当然它也有可能只是噱头。但这个项目本身代表一种趋势：当 AI 和这类计算机网络、经济机制结合，人们会开始尝试各种天马行空的创新。

Robert Hackett：Arc 上的果蝇大脑网络，让 「智能体集群」 有了全新含义。

Jeremy Allaire：还有另一个即将上线 Arc 的项目，专门处理 AI 工作的仲裁机制。

text:
如果要买 BNB，不如买 BNC

BNC 是什么

◦ BNB Standard Corporation 是最大的囤 BNB 代币的 DAT 财库公司，之前公司名叫 CEA Industries，9 月 29 日完成改名，美股 Ticker $BNC 保持不变。

基本面

◦ 公司当前持有 515,544 枚 BNB，价值 3.755 亿美元；BNC 股价 $4.67，稀释后总股本 52,853,688，市值 2.467 亿美元。算下来 mNAV ≈ 0.6569，折价 (负溢价) 率达 -34.31%

◦ 代表 @CZ_Binance 和 @HeyiBinance 的家办 YZi Labs，持有公司 19.99% 的普通股，是最大的单一股东。如果把 YZi Labs 未行权部分算进去，比例会更高。CZ 在 SEC 文件中列为共同申报人、签字人。

为什么会有负溢价，以及解决进展

◦ 公司治理问题：YZi Labs 与原董事会之间的控制权争夺，6 月 23 日已达成和解。现在董事会 6 人，双方各 3 席，还要共同选第七名独立董事 (需要 YZi Labs 同意)，整体在向好。昨天又出了一则新公告，YZi Labs 前合伙人 @odagius 正式出任 CEO，同时辞去 YZi Labs 职务 (All in 的决心)，代表 CZ 和一姐要认真干 BNC。

◦ 公司开始探索经营性收入：要在 BNB Chain 上自营一个验证节点，通过持有 BNB 获取收益，尝试从单纯囤币向有经营性现金流的 DAT 公司转型；新 CEO 的薪酬激励，与每股 BNB 增长、经营收入等指标都有关。

◦ 高昂管理费用问题：之前 BNC 要求 10X Capital 的 1.75% 管理年费降至 0.50%，但谈判失败了。后来公司起诉 10X，要求撤销协议，还在进展中。希望 BNC 梳理好内部团队后，会逐渐着手解决这些问题。解决问题的过程，可能就是 mNAV 抬升的过程。

买 BNC 的理由，我的个人看法

◦ 在未来的牛市行情里，币安面对 Hyperliquid 的竞争威胁，需要拉盘搞注意力；BNB 在币圈内部的渗透率已经很高，更多潜在的增量资金在美股。以前 MSTR 和 BMNR 都吃到过牛市红利，BNC 还没有吃到过。

◦ 退一步讲，即使币安主观拉盘动力弱，现在 BNC 的 mNAV < 1 已经持续一段时间，只要相信 BNB 基本面在且不会缺席未来牛市，那么一旦市场形成合力让 mNAV 回到 1 附近，BNC 也会跑赢 BNB 的收益。现在的 BNC 有点像曾经的 GBTC，在 2022 年折价曾高达 -48%，当时买入的人大幅跑赢了 BTC。

◦ 如上所述，公司治理问题在逐步解决、好转。YZi Labs 代表 CZ + 一姐的家办，对于公司的掌控越来越深，是要认真干的迹象。

风险点有两个

◦ 一个是上面提到的，BNC 的资产管理协议涉及高昂长期管理费，管理层与普通股东的利益未必一致，需要解决；

◦ 第二是如果公司在 mNAV < 1 时持续发行新股 ATM，即使募集资金全部购买 BNB，也会摊薄每股净资产及每股 BNB 敞口。

总结：BNC 是一个以约 34% 折价买入 BNB 敞口，同时押注公司治理改善和估值修复的机会。

text:
2019—2020：312大崩盘，从爆仓到绝地重生

时间来到了2019年10月25日。

那天晚上，新闻联播刚结束，群里突然有人开始刷屏：

习大大讲区块链了！国家要重视区块链了！

起初我是不信的。

这玩意儿以前不是一直被打压吗？怎么突然就成了国家战略？

我赶紧去找新闻视频，结果还真是。

市场瞬间沸腾。

比特币从7000多美元一路暴拉，第二天冲到了10500美元附近。短短十几个小时，9月份的跌幅几乎全部收复。

但我手里的EOS就没这么幸运了。

虽然跟着涨了一波，却始终没能回到之前的高点，长期徘徊在4美元附近。

同样是币，命运已经开始不一样了。

后来我一直在琢磨，这次突然把区块链提升到如此重要的位置，会不会还有另外一层原因？

当时盐城警方正在侦办PlusToken这起巨大的传销案件，后来公布的涉案数字货币规模极其惊人，其中包括20多万枚BTC、80多万枚ETH。

我当时有个大胆的猜测：

会不会是为了给这些涉案数字货币后续处置创造更好的市场环境？

毕竟，查扣的是币，最后如果需要变现、处置，上缴的就可能是人民币。

当然，这只是我个人的猜测，并没有证据证明政策出台与涉案币处置存在直接关系。

但作为交易者，我更关心另一件事：

一场突发消息刺激出来的暴涨，到底能不能改变长期趋势？

我的判断是不能。

如果后面没有持续的增量资金接力，消息带来的上涨终究会被市场消化。

事实也差不多。

比特币从10500美元一路回落，重新跌回7000美元附近，甚至比起涨点还低，一度摸到了6500美元左右。

绕了一大圈，又回到了原点。

这件事让我更加坚信一个道理：

突发事件可以改变短期价格，却未必能改变长期趋势。没有持续买盘，就很难形成真正的牛市。

一、疫情来了，币圈却当什么都没发生

到了2019年年底，比特币开始重新走强。

从6500美元附近启动，一路反弹，到2020年2月再次冲上10500美元。

ETC更夸张，从三四美元一路涨到了12美元附近。

我等待已久的趋势行情，终于又来了。

转眼进入2020年。

春节前后，新冠疫情在国内全面爆发。

武汉封城，各地陆续采取严格管控措施。

整个中国仿佛被人按下了暂停键。

街上没人了，商场关门了，大量企业停工，所有人都开始待在家里。

现实世界正在经历一场前所未有的危机。

可加密货币市场居然还在涨。

我当时就觉得很荒唐。

这么大的事情，你们当不存在？

疫情如果扩散到全球，经济活动停摆，流动性收紧，难道金融市场还能独善其身？

开什么玩笑。

不用想了。

该做空了。

但市场并没有立刻按照我的预期运行。

国内疫情最严重的时候，币圈仍然热火朝天。

直到疫情逐渐蔓延到欧洲、北美，全球金融市场开始恐慌，币圈才终于有了反应。

那已经是3月份了。

没办法。

当你的判断领先于市场时，你就必须承受市场迟迟不肯兑现判断的痛苦。

这种现象，我称之为市场价格的暂时失真。

当然，现在回头看，市场不一定是在犯错，也可能只是我对风险兑现时间的判断过早。

不过这一次，方向我确实判断对了。

ETC从12美元附近，我一路做空到了6美元。

利润越来越丰厚。

但新的问题也随之出现了。

我太喜欢对冲了。

比如手里有一笔盈利的空单，行情跌了一大截，我觉得可能反弹了，于是开个多单对冲一下。

反弹来了，多单赚钱。

反弹结束，再把多单平掉，继续拿着空单。

这种操作，在趋势初期和中期非常舒服。

既能吃到下跌趋势，又能做反弹波段，还能缓解看着利润回吐的不适感。

但问题在于，一旦习惯了对冲，就很难真正拿住一笔完整的趋势单。

尤其到了下跌后期。

你总觉得跌得够多了，该反弹了。

于是开多、加多，甚至忍不住反手。

结果市场根本不反弹。

原本只是为了对冲风险，最后却把自己对冲成了净多头。

这里面还有一个特别容易误导人的地方。

如果你持有一笔盈利很多的空单，同时开了一笔多单对冲，多单出现浮亏，并不代表你的整体仓位在亏钱。

但人性很奇怪。

你明明知道整体风险已经被对冲了，却还是受不了那笔多单显示出来的红色亏损。

于是想补仓，想摊低成本，想等一个反弹把它救回来。

结果往往是越补越多。

到最后，原本赚大钱的机会，反而成了风险最大的地方。

这个毛病，我直到今天都还没有完全解决。

只是现在的我，已经不会那么轻易地把一笔盈利的趋势空单，反手做成净多单了。

因为我知道：

真正恐怖的下跌，往往发生在你已经觉得跌得够多的时候。

二、312：一天亏掉70%，睡醒才知道错过了什么

时间来到2020年3月12日。

比特币已经跌了一个多月，从10500美元附近跌到了8000美元。

当时我觉得，跌得已经不少了。

可真正的暴跌，才刚刚开始。

随着美股崩盘、全球流动性危机爆发，比特币在3月12日下午开始加速下跌。

到了晚上，6000美元被直接击穿。

价格一路砸到了5300美元附近。

那场面，真不是一般的恐慌。

各个平台疯狂爆仓，买盘像是突然消失了。

部分季度合约甚至出现极其夸张的负溢价。

我在ETC上从12美元一路做空下来，已经赚了20万人民币左右。

其中10万，我提前提现出来了。

剩下的利润留在场内。

我当时觉得，自己这次资金管理做得还不错。

赚钱了，提现。

剩下的利润继续操作。

就算后面判断错了，起码也把一部分成果锁定住了。

结果呢？

从ETC大约6美元开始，我反手做多。

跌到4美元附近，场内剩下的10万利润直接爆没了。

20万赚到手，先拿出10万，再把另外10万还给市场。

不过没关系。

我又盯上了比特币。

BTC都跌到5000多美元了，还能怎么跌？

这位置，不抄底干什么？

把提现出来的10万重新充回去！

结果买U都耽误时间。

等我折腾完，比特币已经从低点反弹到6300美元附近。

我赶紧开多。

没想到，刚开进去，行情又开始阴跌。

一直折腾到凌晨三四点，比特币又跌回5800美元附近。

刚充进去的10万，转眼又亏掉了一半。

只剩5万了。

那一刻我心里特别别扭。

方向感觉没错，位置选得一般，节奏更是一塌糊涂。

虽然我坚信这里已经接近底部，但K线告诉我：

还要跌。

没办法，只能忍痛止损。

从前一天算起，辛辛苦苦赚来的钱，一天之内亏掉了大部分。

心情可想而知。

但再难受又能怎么样？

睡觉吧。

年轻就是好。

亏成这样，倒头居然还能睡着。

不过睡之前，我心里还是很坚定：

这里应该就是底部区域了。

等睡醒，如果K线走好了，继续抄底。

结果这一觉，睡出了一个终身难忘的故事。

醒来后，我迷迷糊糊看了一眼行情。

比特币好像在反弹。

我心想：

你看，我就说要反弹吧。

再打开群。

群里已经炸锅了。

有人爆仓，有人骂交易所，有人说自己一晚上什么都没了。

还有人在喊：

比特币刚才跌到4000了！

啥？

4000？

我赶紧睁大眼睛重新看行情。

价格已经反弹到了4600美元附近。

卧槽。

原来刚才又发生了一次大暴跌！

我睡觉这几个小时，比特币居然又跌了接近30%。

从5000多美元的恐慌，到4000美元附近的绝望。

短短十几个小时，两轮史诗级暴跌。

这哪是交易市场？这简直就是屠宰场。

不过震惊归震惊。

我的第一反应居然不是害怕。

而是：

都跌成这样了，还等什么？

赶紧抄底啊！

于是我又开始做多比特币。

可行情还是不肯放过我。

价格反弹以后，没能持续走强，反而又开始阴跌。

4300。

4200。

4100。

4000。

看着自己3800美元附近的爆仓价，我心里越来越没底。

最后，在4000美元即将跌破的时候，我还是认怂止损了。

场内只剩最后1万块钱左右。

而市场呢？

根本没有止跌的意思。

3800。

3600。

3550。

我人都看麻了。

牛逼。

比特币是真不敢抄了。

那就看看EOS、ETC吧。

结果这一看，还真让我发现了机会。

三、最后1万块，撞上了史诗级期现负溢价

当时的季度交割合约，出现了极其罕见的负溢价。

尤其是EOS。

我看到的盘面上，EOS季度币本位合约相对于现货，一度出现约25%的负溢价。

什么意思？

假如EOS现货是1.6美元，季度合约可能只有1.2美元。

正常情况下，如果能够同时锁定两边的价格，做空现货、做多交割合约，等到交割日价格收敛，就可能把这笔巨大的价差赚到手。

当然，真正做套利还要考虑借币成本、手续费、保证金、强平和交易所风险。

但在当时的极端行情下，这种价差依然非常夸张。

我做期货快3年了，这么大的负溢价，也就见过一两次。

而且不是EOS一个币。

很多主流币的交割合约都出现了非常大的负溢价。

相比之下，比特币的季度合约负溢价反而没有那么夸张。

我突然意识到：

市场已经不是在正常定价，而是在不计代价地抛售。

大量杠杆仓位被强制平仓，订单簿里只剩下源源不断的卖盘。

价格根本不讲道理。

可问题是，我现在只剩1万块钱了。

真正意义上的最后1万。

怎么办？

买。

EOS季度合约，1.2美元附近。

全仓，10倍杠杆。

这并不是真正意义上的无风险套利。

我没有足够资金完整锁住现货与期货两条腿，本质上还是一笔高杠杆的方向性押注。

但当时的我，已经顾不上那么多了。

行情继续往下砸。

我眼睁睁看着盘口，几乎找不到正常的买盘。

全是爆仓单。

卖一的位置挂着源源不断的抛压。

价格仿佛被钉死在一个地方，只有现货继续下跌，才可能出现更低的成交价格。

那种感觉，真的很难形容。

度日如年？

太轻了。

每一秒都在煎熬。

因为我知道，如果再跌一波，我可能真的什么都没有了。

但如果市场能恢复正常，哪怕只是一次正常反弹，这笔仓位都有机会让我重新活过来。

终于。

反弹来了。

群里突然有人喊：

BitMEX宕机了！

当时BitMEX还是全球最重要的比特币永续合约交易平台之一，持仓规模巨大。

传闻平台停机之后，市场失去了一个持续输出强平卖盘的重要来源。

有人后来把这次宕机和BitMEX的爆仓机制联系在一起，甚至猜测平台是主动暂停系统，以防止连环强平继续把价格往下砸。

这些说法究竟有多少是真的，我没有办法证实。

但我清楚记得，那个时候，行情终于开始像样地反弹了。

比特币从3500多美元一路往上冲。

4000。

4500。

5000。

5500。

一直冲到6000美元附近。

EOS也从1.2美元附近反弹到了2美元左右。

我整个人都活过来了。

开始疯狂操作。

做多，平多。

反手做空，再平空。

再做多。

再做空。

到了6000美元附近，我又开了一笔比特币空单。

没想到还真空对了。

BTC又回调到了5200美元附近。

我一边盯盘，一边计算账户权益。

突然发现：

最后那1万块，居然被我做到了13万！

13倍。

不是13%的收益。

是13倍。

几个小时前，我还在想怎么才能不彻底出局。

几个小时后，账户又回到了13万。

我靠。

这感觉怎么形容呢？

就像一个快淹死的人，刚刚被水按进河底，马上又被一股巨浪托回了岸边。

死里逃生。

那天真的是我交易生涯中最疯狂的日子之一。

好了。

睡觉。

美美地睡上一觉。

四、13万到两三万，再从两三万做到10万

第二天起来，我重新分析行情。

我发现BCH的表现相对强势。

在那种全市场刚刚经历流动性危机的情况下，一个币如果能率先走强，往往容易成为反弹的领头羊。

于是我决定：

13万，全仓做多BCH。

赌它带领市场继续反弹。

没想到，3月16日，美股又又又熔断了。

这次全球金融市场真的杀疯了。

巴菲特后来感叹，自己活了89岁，也没见过几次美股熔断，结果2020年3月接二连三地见证。

比特币也没能独善其身。

随着BTC再次回调到4500美元附近，我手里的BCH多单也被迫陆续止损。

13万很快缩水。

又剩两三万了。

我都快被自己气笑了。

好不容易从地狱里爬出来，结果转头又自己跳了回去。

不过市场跌成这样，我还是相信会有一轮反弹。

继续做多比特币。

这次我的成本大约在5200美元附近。

终于，市场开始恢复。

6000。

6500。

7000。

账户又回到了10万人民币左右。

我心想：

这次总该稳了吧？

毕竟比特币马上就要减半了。

全球央行又在疯狂释放流动性。

疫情造成的流动性冲击之后，货币宽松可能带来新的资产上涨周期。

这不就是大牛市的前奏吗？

我已经开始憧憬后面的行情了。

可现实从来不按你的剧本走。

BTC从7000美元附近又回调到5800美元一带。

我看着账户利润一点点回吐，心里实在难受。

最后在5900美元附近，把多单平了。

也不能说这个决定完全错误。

至少保住了部分利润。

但那时候我心里有一种小资金交易者特有的恐惧：

我已经亏不起了。

赚的时候不敢放开赚。

亏的时候又总想靠下一笔翻回来。

你说矛盾不矛盾？

后来发生的事情，大家都知道了。

2020年5月，比特币完成减半。

全球进入极度宽松的货币环境。

BTC重新站上1万美元。

而我呢？

5800美元附近下车以后，再也没有顺利登上那趟车。

我在最危险的时候敢于抄底，却在真正的趋势到来之前，被市场洗下了车。

这大概是交易里最讽刺的事情之一。

五、从暴富梦到借钱生活

随后，我迎来了那段时间最黑暗的日子。

场内资金越来越少。

真正能拿来交易的本金，只有两三万块。

偏偏这个时候，比特币的波动率也开始下降。

经历了312那种史诗级暴跌之后，市场逐渐恢复平静。

之前一天动辄20%、30%的行情没有了。

取而代之的是漫长的震荡、横盘和越来越无聊的K线。

对别人来说，行情稳定可能是好事。

但对那个时候的我来说，简直是折磨。

因为我急着赚钱。

这里顺便说一句，为什么后来我越来越少交易EOS了。

原因很简单。

BTC重新站上7500美元以后，EOS开始明显跟不上节奏。

比特币涨，它不怎么涨。

比特币跌，它有时候也不怎么跌。

一个山寨币，波动率居然还不如比特币。

那我玩它干什么？

更重要的是，这种相对弱势让我意识到，市场资金的偏好正在变化。

越来越多的人，可能已经开始放弃EOS了。

既然如此，我也没必要继续跟它死磕。

于是，我逐渐把主要精力重新放回比特币上。

那段时间，我也不是完全没赚到钱。

曾经用两三万本金，抓住比特币从1万美元附近回落到8000美元一带的空头行情，把账户重新做到了7万多。

可惜钱刚赚到手，现实生活就找上门了。

我有一张平安银行的信用卡。

用了七八年。

额度从最早的9000块，一点点涨到了7万多。

那时候正好到了还款日。

我就把赚到的钱提现出来，先把信用卡还上。

结果没想到。

刚还完，平安银行直接把我的信用卡额度降到了2000块。

七八年。

从9000用到7万多。

一口气给我干回2000。

我当时整个人都无语了。

牛逼。

真牛逼。

银行可能是根据自己的风控模型判断我的风险上升了，但在我看来，这跟抽贷有什么区别？

我好不容易赚到一点钱，还完账，结果它告诉我：

你现在不值得我信任了。

突然觉得，自己也体验了一把王健林遭遇过的那种资金被收紧的感觉。

当然，规模没法比。

但那种滋味，是真难受。

金融机构往往愿意把钱借给不缺钱的人，却在你最需要资金的时候收紧额度。

从那以后，我再也没用过平安银行的信用卡和银行卡。

真的恶心。

信用卡还完了。

生活费却也快没了。

怎么办？

只能找家母借钱。

其实很多老粉丝应该看过我之前写的那段经历。

那时候，我已经到了想证明自己的年纪。

结果连正常生活都开始捉襟见肘。

每个月还要还5000块钱房贷。

一个大男人，做了这么多年交易，最后还要找家里借钱度日。

那种感觉真的很难受。

但又说不清楚。

亏钱、爆仓，我其实都能接受。

做交易嘛，愿赌服输。

错了就是错了，大不了重新来过。

可找父母借钱，给我的感觉完全不一样。

那不只是穷。

更像是你拼命想证明自己，最后却发现，自己连最基本的独立都快维持不住了。

我开始害怕别人对我失望。

父母会不会觉得我这些年瞎折腾？

远在深圳的她，会不会觉得我根本不靠谱？

毕竟在2019年，我还夸下过海口：

等我赚够一两百万，你是不是就回来跟我结婚？

当时说得多有底气。

现在回头想想，真是又可笑，又心酸。

虽然和父母关系一直很好，但我已经搬出来住了十多年，早就习惯了自己生活。

忽然有一天，又要低头找家里借钱。

那种委屈，不是输钱能比的。

甚至不敢告诉太多人。

人越穷，有时候自尊心反而越强。

为了省钱，我开始每天只点一顿外卖。

能少花一点是一点。

饿了就忍忍。

甚至开始自己给自己洗脑：

少吃一点，保持饥饿，也许还能让我更加专注。

古人不是说吗？

天将降大任于斯人也，必先苦其心志，劳其筋骨，饿其体肤，空乏其身。

以前读这段话，只觉得是励志。

那时候再读，真他妈有代入感。

当然，现在回头看，长期饿着肚子并不是什么值得提倡的交易方法。

只不过当时的我，确实没有太多选择。

六、最后1万块，我告诉自己绝对不能再错了

时间来到2020年夏天。

DeFi开始火了。

各种项目轮番上涨，行情一波接一波。

ETH也走出了一轮不错的行情。

可我已经没有太多本金去参与了。

看着别人赚钱，说不羡慕，那是假的。

但我告诉自己：

不要乱动。

别看别人赚了钱，就觉得自己也必须参与。

尤其不能因为资金少，就到处寻找所谓的暴富机会。

越是只剩最后一点钱，越不能乱来。

我决定只做比特币。

因为我太熟悉它了。

价格结构，4小时K线，常见的突破与假突破，波动收敛之后的方向选择。

这些东西，我研究了很多年。

那时候的比特币，波动率已经收敛到了非常低的水平。

每天的行情无聊得让人想睡觉。

但我知道：

长时间的波动收敛，往往意味着市场正在酝酿一轮新的行情。

只是不知道方向，也不知道什么时候启动。

于是我开始在9000美元附近反复试仓。

跌破关键位置，尝试做空。

重新站稳，尝试做多。

主要观察4小时级别。

一次又一次止损。

本金本来就少，经不起这么折腾。

最后，我又往账户里充了3000块钱。

把之前试仓损失的资金补了回来。

账户重新凑到了1万块人民币。

这是我那时候能够拿出来重新搏一把的本金。

我非常清楚：

这次不能再像312那样乱做了。

方向错了，要认。

位置不好，要等。

没行情，就不要硬做。

我不需要每天都赚钱，我只需要抓住一次真正属于自己的趋势。

终于，机会来了。

BTC在9200美元附近启动。

我用20倍杠杆建立了多单。

为什么敢用这么高的杠杆？

一方面是资金太少。

另一方面，是当时波动率已经充分收敛，我想在关键位置突破时，利用相对明确的止损来博取趋势收益。

当然，现在回头看，20倍依然是非常高的杠杆。

即使判断对了方向，执行稍有失误，也可能被正常波动扫出去。

但当时，我已经把注意力全部集中在这一笔交易上了。

行情终于没有让我失望。

9200。

9600。

10000。

比特币突破了关键阻力位。

我没有急着平仓。

而是根据后续的走势，陆续加了几笔多单。

随着BTC继续上行，账户利润越来越多。

我心里却出奇地平静。

因为我知道：

我等的不是一笔小反弹，而是一段趋势。

终于，比特币冲到了12500美元附近。

这里开始出现明显的阻力。

随后市场进入震荡。

大概过了20天，BTC在11800美元附近再次出现转弱迹象。

那段时间我一直盯着盘面。

上涨动能在减弱。

突破之后的延续性越来越差。

我感觉市场节奏变了。

于是，我做了一个非常重要的决定。

止盈多单。

反手做空。

这次反手，并不是因为害怕利润回吐，也不是因为情绪上头。

而是我认为，短期的趋势结构确实出现了变化。

事实证明，这次判断相当准确。

BTC随后一路回落，跌回了10000美元附近。

这一波多空两段行情，我都吃到了。

而我的账户，也从最初的1万多块，做到了20多万。

20多倍。

最重要的是，这次我没有在赚到两三万的时候就急着跑。

也没有因为急着还债，就提前结束盈利单。

我终于真正拿住了一段趋势。

从1万到20多万。

钱不算多。

放在币圈，这点资金甚至不够别人一笔开仓的零头。

但对当时的我来说，意义完全不一样。

因为我终于可以把债务问题处理掉了。

终于不用每天为了生活费发愁。

终于不用再低着头找家里借钱。

那种感觉，比赚到一笔大钱还让我高兴。

七、后来我才明白，判断对行情不等于能赚到钱

回头看2019年到2020年这段经历，真的有点荒唐。

疫情刚开始，我判断全球金融市场迟早会受到冲击。

方向对了。

ETC从12美元做空到6美元，也确实赚到了20万。

结果312当天，因为不断对冲、反手、抄底，最后几乎全部亏了回去。

312史诗级暴跌，我又判断市场已经接近极端底部。

大方向还是对的。

但由于仓位和节奏一塌糊涂，BTC从6000跌到3500的过程中，我几乎把本金全部折腾没了。

然后靠最后1万块，在极端行情中翻了13倍。

好不容易做到了13万。

又因为重仓BCH，把利润还给了市场。

后来BTC从5200反弹到7000，我又做对了。

但因为害怕利润回吐，在5900附近下车，最终错过了后面的大行情。

你看。

我并不是看不懂行情。

很多时候，方向甚至判断得很准确。

但账户就是赚不到钱。

为什么？

因为交易从来不是简单地判断涨跌。

你判断对了方向，不代表能找到好的入场点。

找到好的入场点，不代表能控制好仓位。

控制好仓位，不代表能拿住盈利。

拿住了盈利，也不代表你能在趋势结束时及时退出。

更残酷的是：

一个交易者可能连续判断对十次，却因为一次仓位失控，把前面十次的利润全部亏光。

我在312之前就已经知道这个道理。

只是知道归知道。

真正经历过以后，才会刻在骨子里。

直到2020年夏天，我用最后1万块重新做到20多万，才算真正找到了一点感觉。

当时我每天高强度盯盘。

没有什么娱乐活动。

生活简单到不能再简单。

眼里只有行情、K线、仓位和趋势。

资金很少，反而让我不敢轻易分心。

我开始学会等待。

学会接受小额止损。

也开始学会，不因为生活缺钱，就急着把每一笔浮盈落袋为安。

当然，那次20多倍的盈利，也离不开行情和运气，尤其是高杠杆带来的巨大风险。

但有一点，我越来越确定：

我过去最大的敌人，不是市场，也不是庄家，而是那个明明看对了趋势，却总忍不住折腾的自己。

交易最难的，从来不是在最低点买入，也不是在最高点卖出。

而是当真正属于你的行情出现时，你还有本金，有耐心，也有勇气，把它做完。

从20万跌到1万。

从1万翻到13万。

从13万又跌到两三万。

最后，再从1万做到20多万。

这一年，我几乎把一个交易者能经历的极端情绪都体验了一遍。

狂喜、恐惧、后悔、不甘、绝望。

还有重新燃起的希望。

那时候的我还不知道，2020年之后，比特币将迎来一轮波澜壮阔的大牛市。

也不知道自己未来究竟能赚多少钱。

我只知道：

这一次，我终于没有在最黑暗的时候倒下。

而属于我的下一段行情，才刚刚开始。

——十老板，听我慢慢道来。
author: zemummy1

text:
Galaxy fell 30% in two weeks on CoreWeave fears. It now costs less than one of its data centers alone.

What are you truly getting for today’s price?

Let’s break Galaxy down to the bones: what you’re actually paying for, what Helios is worth on its own, and what that leaves for the rest of the crypto operation. We’ll start with the price.

Market cap: ~$6.1B
Plus debt: ~$6.9B
Plus building Helios Phase III: ~$2B (my estimate, not raised yet)
Minus cash and stablecoins: ~$2.5B

quoted_text:
A note on transferability.

Papertrade is a complicated primitive, and managing it from a risk standpoint is a complicated problem. The PAPER token is far more integrated into the economics of the primitive than most tokens are in their respective protocols today, and, broadly, was designed to act as a counter insolvency incentive coupled with a rebate mechanism to losing traders. Market makers and exchanges are by far the two most profitable businesses in crypto, and our goal was to try and externalise as much of their margins back to users as possible. We are now just over a week into the life of papertrade and we are becoming increasingly confident that this is both possible, but also a likely outcome as agentic led software becomes the norm. 

As it stands, the paper token traded as a perp becomes a leveraged bet on bankroll solvency - and being able to short bankroll solvency materially changes the payoff curve of a manipulation attack. The target number goes from the bankroll, to the bankroll + short side exposure on paper. We can, and do limit bankroll size specifically to control this payoff curve and ensure it never becomes existentially problematic, but external perp markets are not something we would have any control over if left to float of their own accord. For example, if our bankroll is $10m, an attack costing $15m manipulating the price of bitcoin or ether is not viable. You simply lose money. If however you were also able to put on $10m of PAPER short side exposure, suddenly an attack costing $15m is very viable indeed.

If we were to make the token transferable at this point, we are confident we would quickly enter a state too dangerous to allow any material exposure to be taken on papertrade, an end result that benefits no party beyond the wolves who have done the math on the short and are waiting in the wings with sharpened knives.

We would also like to thank the various perps teams who have reached out about pre-market listings for their understanding and patience regarding this issue, and especially to the paragon team who, despite jumping the gun on us, have behaved with the utmost integrity and transparency once a dialogue was opened.

Perps on PAPER will always act as a self-limiting exposure ceiling for a token with this type of utility, and we think it would be a shame to limit the growth of papertrade to the extent that allowing perps would necessitate. As such, at this juncture we do not have plans to allow off-contract token transferability.

Structurally, papertrade is limited by the quality of the data it receives from hyperliquid, but we strongly believe that hyperliquid has a very large part to play in the future of global exchanges, and expect their books to continue to thicken and strengthen over time.

A note on fees.

Papertrade launched with a deadband fee from entry of 0.2bps. This means you don't earn anything until the price has moved by 0.002% in your favour. Over the months before launch, we played around with many different curves and fee structures affecting exclusively positions closed very close to entry price in order to try and devise a structure that removed the edge against the bankroll low time frame scalp bots have, whilst also minimally impacting the traders around which and for whom the product was devised. We were never able to find anything we were absolutely happy with and so decided to stay with the 0.2bp deadband fee through launch. This has however meant we have had to be very restrictive when it came to certain parameters, such as OI caps.

Now, however, we have enough live data to fully understand exactly which strategies work, and to make the necessary changes to stop them. The changes we are making will have an on hours and off hours fee mode to account for the relative differences in liquidity the hyperliquid books see between these two time periods, and the ease with which low time frame moves are signalled. The changes we are making will only affect positions closed within 6bps of entry (0.06%) in on hours, and 10bps (0.1%) in off hours. Any trades closed above these threshold price shifts will see no change to their fees at all. On a look back to launch basis, these changes affect the profitability of bot strategies roughly 15x more than they do normal traders, for whom a very small proportion of overall winnings come from within this band.

These changes should serve to flatten much of the edge our microfee structure necessarily creates on low time frames, and will help with long term exchange sustainability. This should hopefully allow us to open up parameters such as OI caps a little more so those of you who wish to can put on the size you want to, when you want to.

It is possible these changes are still too lax, and that further revisions to this structure may be necessary going forwards. If so, we will notify users ahead of time.

A note on paper tokenomics. 

In conjunction with the fee changes, we will also be implementing a change to the token issuance curve.

Going forward, every $1 lost mints a fixed share of PAPER's supply at that moment, roughly 0.1% of supply per $1M lost (the exact number depends on the mint rate at the time the contracts are upgraded). PAPER minting in and near insolvency will also change, switching from a flat 100 per $1 of loss, to a time weighted multiplier on the curve growing over time, effectively acting as the house running a discounted auction on its own future cash flows. This change also removes the risk of the paper-mint-straddle-attack, temporarily pushing the protocol insolvent by closing only the winning side of a large straddle position and then attempting to mint as much paper as possible. 

In the immediate term these changes will only have a very subtle effect on PAPER minting, but in the long run will structurally change the outlook of the system beyond the first few weeks, serving to slowly dilute out older holders and leaving more recent users with an advantage. Reconstituting the PAPER system into something much closer to the exchange rakeback it was intended to be.

We have been very reticent to touch this particular aspect of the system for obvious reasons, but ultimately we believe that these changes provide all users with the optionality to take a smaller piece of a potentially much larger pie than the current dynamic might necessarily allow.

Other, miscellaneous notes.

These contract upgrades will include a few other contract changes, including the addition of builder codes so that builders can utilise papertrade in whatever capacity they choose to. This will be a whitelist only to begin with and we will have more for you later in the week on where/how this will be rolled out. A small change to contract permissions on the reward distributor and a change on how below bust closes are processed by the exchange are also included, largely to block gas griefing attacks. 

These changes will be pushed to docs in full over the coming day, and we will further announce once the changes are queued into the timelock pending final security passes, scheduled to go live 24 hours after that point.

Final note.

We'd like to thank everyone that has tried out papertrade over the last 10 days. It has been a labour of love building this product and both of us have been taken aback at all of the positive feedback we have received. We'd also like to thank all those of you who have spent considerable time musing on the system we have built, and much of your advice has been taken onboard and will likely affect the colour of what papertrade becomes going forward. We know some of these changes will be unpopular with some, but we would not be making them if we did not feel them to be absolutely necessary.

- blurr, jez

Variational Pro Spaces recap w/ @variational_lvs and @andyyy

◾️ OTC derivatives are one of the largest financial markets in the world.
◾️ Variational Pro is going after institutional OTC derivatives, including options, rates, FX, and structured products.

◾️ Lucas expects Pro to eventually become a bigger business than Omni.
◾️ Traditional OTC derivatives trading is surprisingly antiquated:
  - Calling bank desks for quotes
  - Negotiating prices manually
  - Sending contracts back and forth
  - Managing collateral and counterparty risk
  - Manual clearing and settlement processes
◾️ Pro aims to automate this through multi-dealer RFQs, smart contracts, and stablecoin settlement. Think what stablecoins did for payments, but for derivatives.
◾️ Some Pro instruments, including options, could eventually become accessible to retail on Omni.
◾️ Already working with major institutional partners, with large clients expected on Pro soon.

$CC is live now at https://t.co/3wd2slsts3

a protocol that collects @vvcredits, creates and sells or redeems statements, and uses the proceeds to keep collecting

- $CC trading fees fund a standing eth bid for credits, priced by rating
- the system autonomously acquires credits via listings from OS and @token_works
- holders can also sell directly to the engine at the bid price
- acquired credits can be bought from the engine for 4 hours before they become eligible to be composed into statements
- unsold credits are composed into statements in groups of 80
- statements are listed for eth at a decaying price
- 75% of statement sales funds more acquisitions, 25% buys and burns $CC
- once $balance is live, unsold statements are redeemed for $balance, which then become an additional bid for credits alongside eth

a continuous cycle of acquiring, composing, selling, and funding the next round

$CC launched with a 69% trading fee that is decreasing to 6.9% over the first 69 minutes. this helps protect the launch from snipers while directing trading fees into the engine

text:
Ansem loves what fomo has built so far, but he believes that educating the next generation of traders represents the platform’s most significant opportunity

“I love fomo”

“I think fomo's done a great job so far this cycle with hitting the social trends”

“What is going to be interesting going forward is the education piece”

“It's really easy to trade, cross-chain, any assets, stocks, perps, meme coins”

“It's kind of hard for your person who doesn't know what all these assets are to get good education”

“Most people don't even know what market cap is”

“They might size things the exact same way”

Asked by Frank Chaparro what he would like fomo to incorporate, @blknoiz06 focused on helping newer traders understand the markets they're entering.

He appreciates the platform's social trading experience and the accessibility of different asset classes, but sees a gap between making trades easy to execute and helping users make informed decisions.

Someone unfamiliar with market capitalization might approach a $1 million memecoin and a $1 billion asset with the same position size, without understanding the differences in liquidity, volatility or risk.

Ansem also wants users to have better ways to evaluate the traders they follow, understand their strategies and learn how different markets work.

As @fomo attracts people with varying levels of experience, he sees education as an area worth investing in alongside the trading experience.

Making the platform easier to navigate is valuable, and helping users develop better judgment could give them more reason to keep using it over time.

text:
Project Eleven and Relm Insurance Partner to Explore Quantum Risk in Digital Asset Insurance

The first partnership to explore post-quantum security as a factor in pricing digital asset insurance.

Project Eleven, the post-quantum security company for digital assets, today announced Relm Insurance as a development partner for Strongpoint, its flagship institutional custody product. The collaboration will explore how an institution’s post-quantum security controls could be evaluated within digital asset insurance underwriting, helping both companies better understand how quantum readiness may influence future assessments of digital asset risk.

As quantum computing advances, a sufficiently powerful machine could derive private keys from exposed public keys and compromise digital assets. Institutions need custody infrastructure capable of adapting its cryptography before such a machine becomes available. Strongpoint is built for that transition. The platform combines classical and post-quantum signing and separates institutional controls from the cryptography layer, enabling institutions to replace signing algorithms while preserving approval rules and audit history.

“Every institution holding digital assets will eventually need to prepare for post-quantum cryptography. The open question is whether that transition happens on the institution’s schedule or under pressure,” said Alex Pruden (@apruden08), CEO and Co-Founder of Project Eleven. “Insurance plays a critical role in how markets assess and manage risk. We believe there is an opportunity for institutions that invest in stronger post-quantum defenses to eventually see that reflected in how their risk is evaluated. Working with Relm is an important first step toward understanding what that could look like in practice.”

Exploring Post-Quantum Risk in Insurance Underwriting

Through the development partnership, @RelmInsurance and Project Eleven will explore how post-quantum security could be assessed within existing digital asset insurance frameworks. Areas of investigation include key exposure, signing systems, transaction approvals, migration readiness, and third-party dependencies.

Relm will also provide input into the design and development of Strongpoint, helping Project Eleven understand how institutional custody infrastructure can better support insurance underwriting and risk assessment. This collaboration will help inform Strongpoint’s approach to security controls, auditability, and the evidence institutions may need to demonstrate their post-quantum readiness to insurers.

Joseph Ziolkowski, founder and CEO of Relm Insurance, said, “Insuring exposures across the digital asset ecosystem requires underwriters to anticipate how risks will evolve. Quantum computing is a clear example of an emerging threat that should shape the way we assess risk today. Our work with Project Eleven will explore how institutions identify their exposure, demonstrate effective controls, and prepare for the transition to post-quantum readiness. Bringing underwriting expertise into that process early can help lay the groundwork for insurance solutions that support confidence, resilience, and continued growth in digital assets.”

The collaboration is exploratory, with a focus on developing a shared understanding of post-quantum risk and the controls that could help mitigate it. Any future implications for underwriting or insurance premiums would be subject to further evaluation and Relm’s independent underwriting processes.

Institutions can learn more about Strongpoint at https://t.co/Sl7ErXIJCx.

author: eldarcap
quoted_text:
Rewards never make up for a lack of product market fit. They can hide the problem, but they’ll never fix it.

Incentives work in mostly two cases:

- When they’re sustainable and structural, like stablecoin yield
- When they bootstrap network effects, like for instance for:
  • Lending protocols that need to seed both supply and borrow demand
  • New vaults with no track record, where early depositors take more risk and deserve more reward than those who join once it has $100m+ in TVL

If your incentives aren’t building network effects, you’re probably just burning money.

text:
🚨 ELON MUSK: “The future is going to be AI and robots are going to decide the future. And I guess rockets to some degree, in terms of expanding beyond Earth, and we’ll need more energy, primarily solar energy. I’m increasing the amount of solar energy dramatically. We’re putting together 200 gigawatts a year of production capacity of solar in the US, which is much more than I think currently exists.

I find it unlikely that humans would remain in control. If there’s a million times more digital intelligence than there is biological intelligence, it’s hard to imagine humans being in control in that scenario. So I hope the AI is nice to us. I think programming truth seeking and curiosity is probably good. I mean, I guess we want to be careful about being, you know, creating too many AI dystopian scenarios online, because the AIs are trained on everything online. 

They might be like, oh, that’s what I should be. I should be Terminator, you know, because whatever they read, you know, 80 versions of the Terminator script. It’s like, I guess that’s me, Terminator. Maybe we should have some more, let’s just have some more utopian narratives for AI. A friend of mine has this idea called protopian, which is like, because utopian tends to represent some impossible idealistic goal. And usually in attempting to create a utopia, create a dystopia is usually how the narrative goes. So she thinks it should be protopia, which is an achievable future. That is, it’s not perfect, but it’s good.”

text:
Premium whiskey, on TRAC(k) 🇮🇪

Irish whiskey exports were worth about €930 million in 2025, close to half of Ireland’s drinks export value. In a category built on provenance, the story on the label is part of what people pay for.

As @garpitcher, co-founder of @ChurchOfOak, put it: “It’s about really good quality data going in.”

That story now has a second reader. Shoppers ask AI assistants which bottle to buy, and agents compare products on their behalf. An AI can’t visit the distillery. It can only check the data.

Church of Oak, a distillery in Co. Kildare, turning its story into a Digital Product Passport:
→ A GS1 Digital Link on the bottle, so one scan opens the product’s data
→ Origin, and quality data recorded on Decentralized Knowledge Graph (DKG)
→ Structured, machine-readable records, so AI agents can verify a claim before they repeat it
→ A tamper-evident record through the years a whiskey matures before it is sold

The spirit ages. The proof doesn’t.

Trust the source.

text:
Today is my last day at Bybit.

Two years ago, I joined as a Management Trainee supporting the CEO Office: preparing meetings, running operations, and learning from the inside how a fast-moving company really works. I had no idea how much this place would shape me.

Since then, I’ve had the privilege of wearing many hats. I served as Head of Talent Acquisition, Head of Branding, Head of Marketing and worked across Fiat, Card and Payment products . I lived through many 0→1 moments and then to 100. I grew from a young trainee to leading a huge global team. Together, we did a rebranding; built Bybit’s payments product from scratch and took it into 20+ new regions around the world. Our cards passed 4 million, and our payment users are about to cross 2 million.

It wasn’t always easy. There were late nights on the crisis hotline, endless long-haul flights, and working days that stretched across every time zone. But the hard parts taught me the most, about resilience, ownership, and what a truly great team can achieve together.

Bybit made me who I am professionally. The team I’m working with is incredible. Working alongside @benbybit , @helen_moledao and Mazurka has been one of the greatest honors of my career.

I’m stepping away for personal reasons, but this isn’t really goodbye. Bybit will always be a part of me, and I’ll remain one of its biggest supporters.

Thank you Bybit to make who I am!

text:
没想到汇丰，给这几天被喷惨的 CoreWeave，又泼了盆冷水。

这家公司曾是 AI 概念的热门股，业务就是借钱买一堆英伟达显卡，建成机房，再租给 OpenAI、微软这些做 AI 的公司，按时间收租金。

然而过去半年，它家股价跌了将近一半，这周还跌破了 58 美元，创下一年新低。

而背后原因是，它们家欠的钱实在是太多了，因为买显卡全靠借钱，但美国正处于高位利率状态，借钱也越来越贵，所以企业杠杆直接拉满。

这几天，又有一些分析师认为，CoreWeave 赚的钱，可能还不够还借贷利息，所以连摩根大通的人都在算，万一它还不上，华尔街会受多大牵连。

汇丰给出的新报告则更直接，它家的业务没任何差异，只是把显卡整台租给少数几家大客户。

同样的算力，一年挣的钱比亚马逊、微软少三成左右，因为后者有大厂优势。再加上 AI 大模型公司增长放缓，高价的临时算力需求可能减少，债市压力也让它不敢再扩张。

好消息是，包括高盛等在内，依然很看好这家公司。
