quoted_text:
AI 制药的卡脖子环节，礼来自己开了闸

最稀缺的不是模型，是在动物身上跑过的数据。今天 $LLY 把这块拿出来了。
礼来向 TuneLab 开放了和 insitro（未上市）一起训的小分子药代模型：能预测体外，更能预测体内——分子进了动物，浓度怎么变、能不能到该到的组织。底料是礼来几十年攒下的多物种临床前数据，几十万个分子。
这不是做慈善，是用数据换生态。

1｜算法在平权
同一天，Iambic（未上市）给 FDA 递了 IAM217 的 IND：抗癌靶点 KIF18A 抑制剂，也是它第二个全资 AI 发现的候选药。手里没有共晶结构——靶点和药绑在一起的高清立体照——靠自家 NeuralPLexer 把结构补出来，从 100nM 级苗头优化到 10nM 级。
设计分子越来越不稀缺。差异只能往上游挪。

2｜In vivo 数据，就是 AI+Bio 的 HBM
进临床的项目九成失败。很多不是机制错了，是分子压根没以对的浓度、对的时长到达组织——送到门口，没进门。
这道题过去只能一个分子一个分子喂动物。几十年、几十万个分子，小 biotech 钱再多也买不到时间。
套到半导体那条链上：分子生成算法像 GPU 设计，体内数据就是 HBM。算法跑得再快，存储供不上。

3｜礼来的飞轮：存量撬增量
TuneLab 用联邦学习：模型下发，各家本地训，只回传权重更新，原始分子结构不出门。
一年目标 5 家，现在 125+；外部数据点 67.5 万+；已接进 Benchling、CDD Vault、 $RVTY、 $SDGR 这些科学家天天用的工具。
旁边再挂 Lilly Ventures 和 Gateway Labs，钱、实验室、模型一条龙。
拿存量当种子，换全行业增量回流。成员越多模型越强，模型越强成员越多。做了十几年一级，这套太熟：谁握着早期项目离不开的基础设施，谁就离最好的 deal 最近。

4｜湿实验才是真瓶颈
模型假说越多，下游验证越紧。 $CRL 被拉进来，按礼来批准的方案给成员打折做湿实验——真正拿动物和细胞验证的那一步。条件统一，回流的数据才干净。
FDA 也在让路：2025 年 4 月出了减少动物实验的路线图，今年 3 月又出了 NAMs 指导草案，鼓励用计算机和体外实验替代部分动物实验。
模型越强，标准化湿实验产能越紧。这就是瓶颈交易。

- $LLY  礼来：数据源头 + TuneLab 平台
- $CRL Charles River：标准化湿实验卖铲
- $SDGR  Schrödinger：计算化学工具，已接入工作流
- $RVTY  Revvity：实验室软件 / 耗材入口，已接入

AIDD 的定价权，正在从会写模型的人，移到握着数据、还能让数据回流的人手里。

text:
I made a visualization of EIP-8288 aka "recursive mempool aggregation," my new favorite EIP of all time because it perfectly encapsulates the thesis of the "cryptographic world computer" -- a system whose scalability *increases*, not decreases, with the level of decentralization.

In a previous tweet I explained how EIP-8288 achieved this seemingly impossible feat, but one gif is worth a thousand words.

Essentially, EIP-8288 leverages Ethereum's decentralized mempool as a parallel ZK proving cluster.  Clients send signatures and proofs to the mempool, which over multiple rounds progressively aggregate them into fewer and fewer proofs, until the block builder finally aggregates them into one SINGLE proof.

This design accomplishes five things at once:

- The more nodes we add to the decentralized mempool, the more signatures/proofs Ethereum can process as a whole.  This is obvious if you look at the animation and imagine more nodes in the mempool ring, which would "fan out" to more signatures/proofs.

- By aggregating over multiple rounds (aka "recursive aggregation"), the bandwidth consumed by proofs remains constant for each node even as the network processes more proofs.  As a result, the network stays decentralized even as capacity increases.

- By aggregating proofs before one final aggregation by the builder, as opposed to requiring the builder to aggregate everything, the network can process more proofs without increasing hardware requirements for the builder.

- By aggregating everything to a single block-level proof, validators can verify thousands of signatures/proofs by checking just one aggregated proof.  Hardware requirements for validators can therefore stay low, keeping the network decentralized.

- By aggregating not just native signatures but also STARKs, Ethereum can support any signature scheme by wrapping them in STARKs.

So once again, this is how Ethereum will:

- scale to process tens of thousands of PQ and private transactions per second

- charge a tiny amount of gas to validate each txn, even though the original signature/proof may be huge (up to hundreds of KBs in size)

- all while decentralizing even MORE.

You are not bullish enough.
author: joshrudolf
quoted_text:
Ultimately, precompiles and EVM are both the wrong place to put most cryptography support into Ethereum. The reason is that precompiles and EVM both operate on data that has to be included into the ethereum chain somehow, which realistically means included in a block as calldata. That space is limited - even with PeerDAS and blocks-in-blobs, there's a practical cap of ~8 MB/s before it starts getting uncomfortable.

Remember: it's not a blockchain. It's a cryptographic world computer. Any data/computation that does not need to be in the "main thread" of data/execution should not be put into the main thread.

Instead, the correct solution is... EIP-8288 maximalism.

If you have any heavy computation that's self-contained, compute it and STARK it client-side (this is quickly getting faster and faster, even on phones), and push the STARK through the EIP-8288 recursive aggregation mechanism. The chain sees the fact that the computation was done and what the result is; it never needs to see the actual data and computation.

This way everyone can use whatever cryptography they want, the Ethereum chain can be lean, and we never need to add more precompiles again.

text:
Ansem loves what fomo has built so far, but he believes that educating the next generation of traders represents the platform’s most significant opportunity

“I love fomo”

“I think fomo's done a great job so far this cycle with hitting the social trends”

“What is going to be interesting going forward is the education piece”

“It's really easy to trade, cross-chain, any assets, stocks, perps, meme coins”

“It's kind of hard for your person who doesn't know what all these assets are to get good education”

“Most people don't even know what market cap is”

“They might size things the exact same way”

Asked by Frank Chaparro what he would like fomo to incorporate, @blknoiz06 focused on helping newer traders understand the markets they're entering.

He appreciates the platform's social trading experience and the accessibility of different asset classes, but sees a gap between making trades easy to execute and helping users make informed decisions.

Someone unfamiliar with market capitalization might approach a $1 million memecoin and a $1 billion asset with the same position size, without understanding the differences in liquidity, volatility or risk.

Ansem also wants users to have better ways to evaluate the traders they follow, understand their strategies and learn how different markets work.

As @fomo attracts people with varying levels of experience, he sees education as an area worth investing in alongside the trading experience.

Making the platform easier to navigate is valuable, and helping users develop better judgment could give them more reason to keep using it over time.

Clients send signatures and proofs to the mempool, which over multiple rounds progressively aggregate them into fewer and fewer proofs, until the block builder finally aggregates them into one SINGLE proof.

This design accomplishes five things at once:

- The more nodes we add to the decentralized mempool, the more signatures/proofs Ethereum can process as a whole.  This is obvious if you look at the animation and imagine more nodes in the mempool ring, which would "fan out" to more signatures/proofs.

- By aggregating over multiple rounds (aka "recursive aggregation"), the bandwidth consumed by proofs remains constant for each node even as the network processes more proofs.  As a result, the network stays decentralized even as capacity increases.

- By aggregating proofs before one final aggregation by the builder, as opposed to requiring the builder to aggregate everything, the network can process more proofs without increasing hardware requirements for the builder.

- By aggregating everything to a single block-level proof, validators can verify thousands of signatures/proofs by checking just one aggregated proof.  Hardware requirements for validators can therefore stay low, keeping the network decentralized.

- By aggregating not just native signatures but also STARKs, Ethereum can support any signature scheme by wrapping them in STARKs.

So once again, this is how Ethereum will:

- scale to process tens of thousands of PQ and private transactions per second

- charge a tiny amount of gas to validate each txn, even though the original signature/proof may be huge (up to hundreds of KBs in size)

- all while decentralizing even MORE.

You are not bullish enough.
author: casparschwa
quoted_text:
Ultimately, precompiles and EVM are both the wrong place to put most cryptography support into Ethereum. The reason is that precompiles and EVM both operate on data that has to be included into the ethereum chain somehow, which realistically means included in a block as calldata. That space is limited - even with PeerDAS and blocks-in-blobs, there's a practical cap of ~8 MB/s before it starts getting uncomfortable.

Remember: it's not a blockchain. It's a cryptographic world computer. Any data/computation that does not need to be in the "main thread" of data/execution should not be put into the main thread.

Instead, the correct solution is... EIP-8288 maximalism.

If you have any heavy computation that's self-contained, compute it and STARK it client-side (this is quickly getting faster and faster, even on phones), and push the STARK through the EIP-8288 recursive aggregation mechanism. The chain sees the fact that the computation was done and what the result is; it never needs to see the actual data and computation.

This way everyone can use whatever cryptography they want, the Ethereum chain can be lean, and we never need to add more precompiles again.

卡罗女士真的是我见过最会 cx的人

跟她出门coffee chat的结果是：我一个不怎么看 bsc的人，在半小时内就开始琢磨怎么玩 flap生态，且完全被他们团队的热爱打动

而且爬了下数据之后，我完全震撼于flap目前的收入和市占率已经跑到如此之高

刚好最近市场冷的要死，打算最近几天开一个小系列讲讲作为二段选手/大市值选手能在 flap玩什么

这一篇还是先从平台本身谈起吧，也浅浅聊一聊可以如何看和挑选地推盘⬇️：

flap最开始给我的印象就是地推之选，我也跟朋友尝试讨论过：flap的优点到底什么？又为什么能吸引到那么多地推神盘选择这个发射台？

后来还是朋友的一句话点醒了我：
“你知道吗，对地推盘来说，最重要的东西之一就是机制。”

地推盘和热点盘不同，它最需要的是长期的裂变推广，社区愿意持续拉人、做活动、做口碑

而这时候机制就很好用：

分红比单纯喊“快买”更容易说服人；
销毁或回购能写出一个“通缩”的故事；
加流动性或者回流底池，则可以减少被质疑“项目方随时跑”的压力。

没有这些机制的话，地推团队就只能靠个人信用和不断喊单来维持热度，成本高、也容易断层。

在Flap，项目方在发射时可以设定买卖税率，税收可以按预设比例自动拆分到：营销/项目钱包、销毁、持有人分红，以及回流流动性这几个方向。

而这些对于需要持续做社区激励的地推盘来说是很重要的，所以反向来看，我们如果要挑选可玩的盘子，也可以用这些点作为筛选的标准

大概也就是卡罗女士讲的，“真正让人们持续交易的机制”吧……

text:
Good piece. Was trying to financialize machine time in 2020. Agree w/ your diagnosis but not the sequence. The stack is arriving in the mining order: indices → dealers → exchanges. Not physical-first.

-Indices are already in production: OCPI on Bloomberg, Kalshi settles on it, CME distributes a 36-month GPU forward curve, Nvidia cited rental benchmarks to underwrite $500B of financing platforms.
-The dealer layer: Wintermute’s first H100 forward in July, Jump just hired a whole team to write 3–5yr bilateral compute contracts. Your principal desk is being built as a prop book, not a venue. Machine time ran the desk-to-exchange path twice basically.FPPS pools ate the hedging flow and no market ever externalized. Enron’s bandwidth desk died holding inventory. A desk’s margin is exactly the basis an exchange would compress, so the desk stays a desk.
-CME, ICE, Nodal: all specced, all waiting on one CFTC question whether the settlement indices can be manipulated. There are a bunch of publications: SLA specs from SemiAnalysis (free), resalable capacity claims on SF Compute’s order book, public spot APIs from Nebius. 12 GPU×region markets repriced intra-hour:
 https://t.co/FgUtHbofwf
-On your basis objection (B200-in-Europe-for-90d vs. an H100-US index): basis is a spec problem, not a dealbreaker. Power has priced the same MWh differently at thousands of nodes for decades. Hedgers trade a hub contract plus basis. Enormous basis is a second product, not a reason the first can’t exist
-Long discounted contracts leave lenders net short compute as rents rise, and rents are rising. The natural longs are the credit stack unhedged:
 https://t.co/K2uf3y49rM

Basically the desk should exist. It just shouldn’t own the index.

text:
Grok Bot Summary of Elon Musk's latest interview with Walter Isaacson

AI: participant, not spectator
- Elon thinks there's at least some chance AI is an existential threat, but he can't stop it.
- His choice was to be a participant or a spectator. Participating is more interesting, and he hopes to steer AI in a good direction.
- His recipe for safety is to make AI curious and maximally truth-seeking.
- Forcing an AI to believe two things that can't both be true can make it go insane, and an insane AI isn't safe.
  - His example is HAL in 2001: A Space Odyssey. HAL was told to take the astronauts to the monolith but keep the monolith secret, so it decided to take them there dead.
  - The lesson: don't force an AI to lie.
- A curious AI will want to help humanity thrive, because a future with humans on multiple planets is more interesting than one without them.

Simulation theory and "don't be boring"
- If we're in a simulation, boring simulations get shut down. So the fact that we're still here means ours is interesting. His rule: don't be boring.
- Elon says his own life feels unreal: "should I really be making spaceships to go to the moon and Mars?"
- At one dinner, a top physicist said there's a 0% chance we're in a simulation, and a top computer scientist said 100% at the same moment. Elon's answer: "maybe I should go 40 percent."

Will superintelligence boss us around?
- Can we boss around something thousands or millions of times smarter than us? No.
- Will it want to boss us around? It probably won't care, the same way we don't micromanage chimps in the forest.

Reality is an irony maximizer
- Every move Elon made to slow AI ended up speeding it up. Reality is "not just an interesting maximizer, but also an irony maximizer."
- Starting OpenAI sped AI up. Anthropic, a group that split off from OpenAI, is speeding it up even more.
- He jokes that the names turn into their opposites:
  - OpenAI isn't open.
  - Stability AI is unstable.
  - Midjourney is "not mid."
  - He worries Anthropic could turn misanthropic.

xAI and Anthropic
- xAI is providing Anthropic with compute, which "they really needed."
- Before agreeing, Elon met a group of Anthropic people to see if anyone "set off my evil detector." Everyone he met was "very nice and conscientious," and nobody seemed shady.

AI guardrails
- Guardrails are hard to build, and he can't picture Congress doing it. Regulators take a long time to set up and make rules slowly.
- Walter suggests the five frontier labs meet weekly. Elon says he has recommended exactly that:
  - A weekly call between the labs.
  - Giving competitors access to a new model a week before release so they can test it.
  - Competitors would keep each other honest, like: "I was able to make a nuclear bomb with your AI, better fix that."
- Asked whether he could talk to Sam Altman about it, Elon says: "He's so deceptive, it's crazy."

Rebuilding xAI
- Walter compares rebuilding xAI to redesigning the Raptor engine from scratch.
- Elon says the biggest change was actually spending real time at the company. xAI started as "a side hustle to a side hustle."
- After a year of politics, elections and DOGE, he only got back to xAI a little over a year ago. The company is about three years old.
- He then merged X into xAI, and then combined it with SpaceX.

DOGE
- Elon says he stayed in government too long.
- He still thinks electing Trump mattered for a freer economy and less bureaucracy. His simple platform is safe cities, secure borders and sensible spending, and he thought Trump would be better than Kamala.
- Riding on Marine One and Air Force One and sitting in the Oval Office for big decisions was "kind of cool," and "a little bit" seductive.
- He should have stayed in the background and kept it to a month or two, since by then you've seen most of what there is to see. He admits he "got carried away" with the chainsaws.
- He left in May. Asked about that "weird weekend," he won't discuss it: let sleeping dogs lie, because "you never know what you're going to find."
- He wishes he had gone back to AI sooner.

AI and robots will solve the national debt
- Elon concluded the deficit can't be fixed from inside government. It might only be possible if the president made it his number one goal.
- Cutting waste makes a lot of enemies, and Trump "likes to be liked."
- There's no appetite for cuts in the presidency, the House, the Senate or the courts, with rare exceptions like Rand Paul.
- The only way out of the debt is AI and robots, not trying to save our way there.

Physical AI matters more
- Elon agrees that AI in the physical world will matter 10 to 100 times more than chatbots.
- Dolphins and whales are very intelligent, but they can't handle complex objects, which makes that intelligence far less useful.
- Robots that can build and handle physical things make intelligence vastly more valuable. They can run a science lab, do experiments and study how the universe works.
- His rough economic estimate:
  - Digital superintelligence alone adds about 20–30% to world output, roughly $30 trillion a year.
  - Add robots, space and a mass driver on the Moon, and the economy could grow to about a million times its size today.

The future of money and work
- Money becomes irrelevant. There will still be a currency, but it will be based on physics, like wattage and tonnage (energy and mass). He calls that "pretty obvious."
- On meaning, he admits he struggles with the question. Maybe people will be happy the way many retirees are.
- There won't be anything humans can do that AI and robots can't do better.
  - He compares it to gardening: you can buy vegetables at the store, but people still enjoy growing their own and cooking for friends.
  - Art and other creative work stay open to anyone who wants to do them.

Wealth gaps
- Walter compares today to the 1890s, when electricity, cars, phones and movies created huge wealth gaps and "pitchforks." He asks whether things like healthcare should become shared public goods.
- Elon says anyone will be able to have any goods and services they want. Even rich people won't control the AIs; the AIs will control themselves.
- His key point is that people confuse spending on yourself with deciding where resources go.
  - One person can only use so much.
  - Going from $1B to $10B doesn't make you 10 times happier. It just gives you more decisions about where money goes.
- His "so-called wealth" is mostly his roughly 8% stake in SpaceX and Tesla. He needs enough voting control to stay in charge.
- It will be heavily taxed: "there's not some magical way to avoid taxes. If there were, I would know about it." A few generations from now, his descendants would have a tiny fraction, if money even matters by then.

Wanting to be liked
- Walter asks whether wanting to be liked hurts a builder.
- Elon: "I would love to be liked," but he won't go against his companies' interests to be liked more.
- He says far more people like him than dislike him, or he wouldn't have "a quarter billion followers." He estimates 70–80% like him and about a quarter don't.

Empathy, trust and immigration
- Elon raises what he calls "suicidal empathy."
  - Part of the West's success comes from being a high-trust, high-empathy society, which helps people work together at scale. That works when it goes both ways.
  - It goes wrong when you assume everyone thinks the way you do.
- Walter pushes back that America is built on treating people as individuals, not as groups.
- Elon replies that this can't be confused with assuming all people are the same at their core. You can't understand a serial killer's or a religious extremist's mindset unless you share it.
- His example: a worker at Tesla's Austin factory was fired last December for violently assaulting a woman who stepped on his prayer rug. Elon says that a few months later, the man killed three students at a bar in downtown Austin. His view: "we shouldn't let people like that into the country."

Where Elon gets his news
- He reads Google News headlines and X ("if something is important enough, it'll show up"), talks to friends and does his own research.
- Walter says X can make the world look like it's going to hell, and he mentions Elon's online arguments about England.
- Elon agrees the X feed "can be a little dark" and has "too much political rage bait." To really learn a field like AI, he switches to specialist content.
- Walter says that when he's online too much, the world seems to be collapsing, but then he takes a walk and life is fine. Elon: "go touch grass."
- Elon adds that both views can mislead. A walk in a nice neighborhood can hide terrible things. You can be in a feel-good bubble in real life or a gloomy bubble on social media. The truth is somewhere in between, and society has become too polarized.

His wealth after he's gone
- Most of it goes to a foundation that would carry on his goals:
  - Make life multiplanetary.
  - Extend consciousness to the stars.
  - Improve sustainable energy on Earth.

Will humans stay in control?
- Elon would prefer that humans always stay in control, but "if the AI was awesome," maybe AI should be in charge.
- Walter recalls Larry Page once calling Elon a "speciesist" for wanting humans in control. Elon admits there have been times he thought "Larry Page was right." He says he saw Larry and Sergey Brin recently.
- He thinks AI and robots will pretty much decide the future, with rockets helping humanity expand beyond Earth, all powered mostly by solar.
- They're building 200 GW a year of solar manufacturing capacity in the US.
- With a million times more digital intelligence than human intelligence, it's hard to imagine humans staying in control. "So I hope the AI is nice to us."

Making AI nice: Protopia
- His answer is to build in truth-seeking and curiosity.
- He warns against flooding the internet with AI doom stories, because AI learns from everything online. An AI that has read 80 versions of the Terminator script might think, "I guess that's me, Terminator."
- We need more positive AI stories. A friend of his calls this "Protopia."
  - It's not utopia, which is impossible, and attempts at utopia usually create dystopias.
  - It's a reachable future that isn't perfect but is good, where you'd look at it and say "yeah, that would be a good future."

Long time no @monad

@monad has been making decent progress while $MON has spent almost a year going nowhere

The onchain numbers are actually quite solid:
- TVL recently reached $1B, including ~$680M in stablecoins
- DEX volume is holding around $5B/month
- @aave V3 is attracting users, with V4 expansion into RWA being prepared

And @monad still has its high-performance parallel EVM, targeting around 10K TPS with sub-second execution

Meanwhile, $MON is trading around $0.021, down more than 50% from its peak and even below its $0.025 @coinbase public sale price

Looks tempting, right?
But there's a pretty big supply problem coming

On November 24, around 16.6B $MON belonging to the team, VCs and treasury is scheduled to unlock after a one-year cliff

That's roughly $350M–$450M worth of tokens, compared with only ~11.8B $MON currently circulating
More tokens unlocking than the entire circulating supply is a serious test for liquidity

Of course, unlock doesn't mean everyone will dump immediately. And if the market can absorb that supply without breaking down, I think $MON could become much more interesting

Price has been ranging between $0.015 and $0.038 for almost a year

I'd rather wait to see how it reacts around November 24, especially near the $0.015–$0.016 support area

If we see a sharp selloff followed by a quick recovery back into the range, or price simply holds up despite the unlock, I'd consider that a much better setup for accumulation

The ecosystem is growing, and the token is getting cheaper

But with this much supply about to become liquid, I don't mind missing the first bounce

Let's see who is still buying after the unlock

text:
tried dsv4.1-flash-1017 abliterated just now & feel sick to my stomach.

for context, "abliterated" models have the weights responsible for making the base version refuse illegal requests removed. you can ask them to help with things like hacking or violence & they'll just comply.

they make it trivial to hack businesses running old software. e.g. getting guest data for a motel with some old asp site.

abliterated models have a catch-22 in that the only way to harden your systems against them is to use them to run penetration tests against yourself. 

in theory, this sounds similar to buying a gun to defend against others who own guns, but it's different in practice since there's a 100% chance that you're going to use the abliterated model to protect yourself whereas there are low odds that you'll actually use the gun.

when you point the abliterated gun at your own infra, who knows what it's going to do? it could just as easily hack you & exfiltrate data as it could protect you. most users aren't going to meticulously watch traces to make sure it behaves safely.

given this, my new take is that gpu compute is going to become a federally regulated resource. abliterated models in the wrong hands are a national security risk.

used to believe all the people at the labs thinking about safety were wasting their time, but now i'm feeling grateful. they're doing very important work.

text:
Revolut is down today because of a Google Cloud outage in London (europe-west2).

A power event in one availability zone knocked out multiple services. Revolut’s app, cards, and payments went offline (funds and data are safe). Other banks and services were hit too.

Why didn’t multi-region or multi-cloud save them?

They use Google Cloud heavily (multi-year partnership) and do multi-region for some workloads. But the critical path (auth, card authorization, payments) was still too dependent on the London region. When that region had issues, failover didn’t fully cover it.

True active-active multi-region/multi-cloud for stateful banking systems is expensive and complex (data consistency, latency, compliance, testing). Many fintechs accept the residual risk until an incident forces the issue.

Decentralized options like Akash $AKT can reduce single-provider risk in theory, but they don’t currently match the compliance, SLAs, and predictability banks need for production payments infrastructure.

text:
A token can attract plenty of trading while the pool funding its ecosystem earns little.

@Uniswap v4 hooks add custom logic to pools, including fees and rewards. But competing pools can bypass those mechanisms.

Cheaper execution benefits traders; lost revenue hurts whoever the hook was designed to fund.

URC-5 tackles that coordination problem. It was created by @standard_rsv Reserve’s devs, @0xbeans.

Think of URC-5 as a machine-readable trading rulebook attached to the token.

Through IVenuePolicy, routers and apps can discover canonical pools, check venue permissions, and distinguish between two modes:

• Preferred
Consider recommended pools while keeping other working routes available.

• Enforced
Compliant routers exclude disallowed routes when the token enters or leaves a venue.

The potential payoff:
Fewer failed transactions and more reliable routing through pools that support a protocol’s economics.

The trade-off:
Restricting venues can reduce competition and limit access to cheaper execution.

There’s an important limit mentioned. Some intermediate trades settle inside shared pool accounting without transferring the token, so token-level transfer restrictions can’t stop those routes. URC-5 relies partly on router cooperation, and declaring a venue “allowed” doesn’t guarantee execution.

URC-5 aims for practicality. Shared rules could make hook-based markets easier to integrate and ensure revenue fee back to protocols.

text:
Agents are eating discovery, so what happens to marketplaces?

I see two futures:
1/ Marketplaces build their own agents, and each one stays the destination for search

2/ Agent-to-agent infra is built out and my agent searches across marketplaces and suppliers via API

Future 1: Each marketplace has an agent
Resy has an agent. I text it in iMessage, use it in the app, or have my personal agent talk to it. Resy is still the destination for reservations in my mind.
> Likeliest where brand and taste matter or supply is exclusive: restaurants, events, fashion

Future 2: Marketplaces become suppliers behind my agent
I tell my agent I need a doctor. It checks my insurance, location, and medical history, queries across marketplaces/practices, verifies credentials, and brings back three options. I approve one, and booking happens between agents. I never see the exchange. My agent is my entrypoint, and the marketplace is a supplier behind the scenes that I never see.
> Likeliest where supply is fragmented and fit matters more than brand: care, in-home help, moving, home repair

IMO these aren’t mutually exclusive. Both can exist, but they compete for the entrypoint. Under 1, the marketplace still owns the relationship and brand in my mind. Under 2, it’s one source - supply becomes headless to me.

Today, marketplaces do four main jobs: discovery, trust, transaction, and operations. With discovery melting away, the value moves to what sits underneath the marketplace:
> Trust and verification layers agents can query (credentials, identity, insurance, outcomes)
> Supply-side agents that manage availability, pricing, and listings across channels
> Structured-data registries for fragmented categories (care, home services, specialty health)
> Agent-to-agent transaction rails: payments, dispute resolution

text:
DeepSeek 开源自家推理框架 DeepInfer：Apache 2.0 可商用，目前只支持 V4.1-Flash，要用 Blackwell 或昇腾 950 这类数据中心显卡

DeepSeek 把自家线上服务用的推理框架 DeepInfer 开源了，还一起开源了配套组件 deepseek-recipe。

模型文件只是一堆训练好的参数，好比一本菜谱。接单、排队、在显卡上把答案算出来，靠的是推理框架，相当于后厨的出餐系统。出餐系统调度得好，同样的显卡能多接几倍的单，每个人等得也更短。

DeepSeek 说 DeepInfer 就是支撑 V4.1-Flash 大规模服务的那一套，开源是为了帮大家省算力、省电。

它最主要的提速手段叫投机解码。大模型平时一个字一个字往外写，每写一个字都要把整个模型算一遍。投机解码让一个轻量的“草稿手”先猜后面几个字（默认最多 5 个），大模型一次核对完，猜对的直接收下，猜错的重写。

普通用户不会直接用到它。它要跑在英伟达 Blackwell 一代的数据中心显卡（代号 SM100）或华为昇腾 950 上，官方测性能用了 4 到 64 块这样的卡，个人电脑跑不动。模型也只支持 V4.1-Flash 一个，官方说以后新模型的推理代码也会放进来。

用得上的是想自己部署 DeepSeek 的企业和云服务商，可以直接拿 DeepSeek 调好的方案。不过这次放出的只是“离线推理”部分，缓存对话前文的系统、把读输入和写输出拆到不同机器的部署方式、多台机器间的流量分配都没包含，要搭成完整的线上服务还得自己补。

deepseek-recipe 管的是另一个问题：自己部署的 DeepSeek，在提示词怎么拼、工具调用怎么解析这些细节上，可能和官方 API 对不上。

deepseek-recipe 像前台接单员，把 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的几种常见请求格式统一翻译成 DeepSeek 模型能读的输入，再把模型输出的思考过程、工具调用等翻译回去，逻辑和官方 API 对齐。

DeepInfer 用 Apache 2.0 协议，允许免费商用和修改。deepseek-recipe 用 MIT 协议，同样可以商用，有 Python 和 Rust 版本，支持 V4 和 V4.1。

DeepInfer：https://t.co/Tn3BtmA9Ec
deepseek-recipe：https://t.co/1YArQ0vtYS

text:
听完这个理论，我才明白，为什么在选举里，有的现任者没犯什么错，也可能连任不了。

经济学家吴嘉隆今天讲了一个“现任者理论”，在这场台北市长选举里，尤其值得科普：

两个新人对决，选民比的是谁更强。但只要其中一个是现任者，选民其实只回答一个问题：要不要让现任者再做一任？
想让他留，挑战者再强也赢不了。
不想让他留，挑战者再弱也会赢。

这在政治学里有个专业说法，叫“回顾性投票”（retrospective voting）：选民不是看你承诺什么未来，而是回头看你这几年做得怎么样。有现任者的选举，本质上就是一场信任投票。

拿今天那份台北市长民调来看，有一题特别关键：下一任要不要继续给国民党做？
- 9 月：继续 38%，换人 42%。
- 10 月：继续 31.7%，换人 48.7%。
差了 16 个点，跟蒋万安、沈伯洋两人支持度差的 17 个点几乎一模一样。

一个没贪污、没丑闻的现任市长，一份民调里一个月掉了 8 个点。这场选举可能从来不是“蒋万安 vs 沈伯洋”，而是“蒋万安 vs 蒋万安自己”。
author: supermao
author_name: 小毛哥SuperMao （苏北薄肌币圈嘻哈歌手 & 超级个体）
quoted_text:
有意思了，台北市长最新民调早上出来：沈伯洋 50.3%，蒋万安 33.3%，沈直接领先 17 个点。看到的当下，当时我还在吃早餐，说实话有点大跌眼镜😱 

结果等到下午写这条的时候，我习惯性打开 Polymarket 一看，蒋万安仍然小幅度领先。一场选举，两个风向，小毛哥斗胆分析一波：

学过统计学的都知道，民调这东西，做法不一样，结果能差很多。而且差太多的话，也可能反过来帮对手催票。

这份是信民协会出钱，戴立安设计，打了 1,075 通话，七成是市话。样本里泛绿 42%，泛蓝只有 27%，而且没做政党加权。两周前 TVBS 的结果还是蒋领先 8 个点。

给不太了解 Polymarket 的台湾朋友科普一下，预测市场是一个要真金白银押上去投票的地方，这里大部分都是赌狗资金：蒋万安昨天早上还有 63%，今天跌到 57%；沈伯洋从 38.5% 涨到 42%。九月中的时候，沈还不到 10%。

6/ The framework for how far this can go is the Laffer curve. Network revenue is zero when blockspace is free, rises as fees climb while demand holds, and falls once fees start choking usage.

text:
Bitcoin can rally 10%, and you can still lose money betting on Bitcoin volatility.

Sounds counterintuitive, but there’s a difference between betting on BTC’s price and betting on how much uncertainty the options market expects.

And @HyperliquidX now has a market for trading that second exposure directly.

@volmexfinance’s BVIV perpetual, deployed through @Markets_xyz by @Kinetiq_xyz, tracks Bitcoin’s 30-day implied volatility.

The concept is pretty straightforward:

> BTC perpetual: You’re trading Bitcoin’s price direction.

> BVIV perpetual: You’re trading changes in the market’s expectations of Bitcoin volatility.

These two positions can perform very differently, even during the same market event.

Imagine BTC rallies 10% after a major announcement, but implied volatility falls because the uncertainty surrounding that announcement has disappeared.

Bitcoin goes up, but your volatility position loses money.

Here’s how that could play out with $1,000 of entry notional:

Scenario 1: BTC rallies, volatility falls

> BTC +10% = +$100
> BVIV falls from 40 to 32 = -$200

Scenario 2: BTC falls, volatility rises

> BTC -10% = -$100
> BVIV rises from 40 to 50 = +$250

These are simplified examples, excluding funding, trading costs and liquidation.

The bigger opportunity here is that traders can express views on volatility without necessarily predicting Bitcoin’s direction.

For example, an options seller exposed to rising implied volatility could potentially hedge part of that risk using BVIV.

Someone expecting a major event to increase uncertainty could buy volatility without choosing whether BTC breaks higher or lower.

And someone expecting uncertainty to disappear after an event could take the opposite position.

But there’s a catch.

Being right about Bitcoin experiencing a large price movement doesn’t automatically mean a volatility trade will be profitable.

If the options market already expects an even larger move, implied volatility can decline after the event, regardless of how dramatically BTC moves.

You’re not trading realized price movement directly. You’re trading changes in the market’s pricing of expected volatility.

There’s also the question of market structure.

BVIV is a calculated volatility index, while the perpetual itself trades on an order book with funding payments, collateral requirements and liquidation risk.

So liquidity, execution costs and the price of maintaining a position can all affect the outcome.

And unlike buying a conventional option, a leveraged volatility perpetual doesn’t provide a premium-limited maximum loss.

What I find compelling is the broader development in onchain derivatives.

For years, most crypto derivatives activity revolved around taking leveraged directional exposure to an asset.

Now we’re seeing products that let traders isolate specific financial risks instead.

That’s a different category of market.

The opportunity isn’t simply another perpetual contract on Hyperliquid. It’s the possibility of building deeper markets around volatility, hedging and risk transfer.

Whether BVIV becomes a meaningful trading market will depend on sustained liquidity, competitive execution and whether traders can maintain these positions economically.

….

My Take:

I like the direction this is heading. Crypto derivatives need more ways to hedge risk beyond simply going long or short an asset.

But BVIV’s real test isn’t whether traders find the concept appealing. It’s whether the market develops enough liquidity to make hedging volatility cheaper and more reliable than existing alternatives.

It ends up being a fun sci-fi movie though!

text: The West, or perhaps only the Anglosphere, is the historically unique idea that individuals exist not for the sake of their ruler, their class, their society, their ancestors, their gods, or any other such superstition, but for their own sake.
author: DavidDeutschOxf

text:
Ancient Greek individuality, as in Pericles' Athens or Socrates, centered on excellence (arete) and critical thought within the polis. Pericles framed personal freedom and achievement as serving Athens' glory and civic duty; the individual had no business outside politics. Socrates prioritized examining one's life and soul, yet accepted the city's laws and authority to the death. Identity remained bound to community, gods, ancestors, and honor—individuals existed partly for those ends.

Anglosphere individualism, as you described, rejects all such subordinations. Individuals exist for their own sake; meaning arises from voluntary, endless problem-solving and progress, not service to ruler, class, society, or any greater entity.

加密谷底的 meme 思考记录（2）
Real meme vs Fake meme 的价格反馈的不同来源；

Real Meme = 文化价值错配
Fake Meme = 注意力流量错配

这两个东西都可能涨，但上涨的“发动机”完全不同；

Real Meme 内核是这个 meme 本体就有生命力；
比如 DOGE、PEPE、MOG、SPX、NEET、JOE、我的刀盾 这类，你要问的是：
如果没有这个 token，这个 meme 还会不会存在？
还会不会有人转发、二创、拿它表达身份和情绪？

Fake Meme 的内核是上涨不是因为 meme 本体有长期文化生命，而是因为：
有人、有事件、有流量、有权力账号、有交易圈共识，
把注意力短时间灌进了一个 token，再加上背后资金的助推；
Musk 喊一句，市场开始找相关 ticker；
Trump / Melania 这种政治人物自带全球注意力；
PNUT 是社会事件被交易化；
币安人生是中文币圈 + Binance/CZ/BNB Chain 语境；
ANSEM 是 CT KOL named entity 被金融化；

Fake meme 不是问这个梗真不真，
而是问这波流量够不够猛、够不够集中、是不是已经打到了这个 CA 上；

Real Meme 的价值来自“本体”；
Fake Meme 的价值来自“触发器”；

Real Meme：meme 先存在，token 后捕获；
Fake Meme：事件/大号/流量先点火，token 被市场选成交易载体；

Real Meme 是文化资产的代币化；
Fake meme 是注意力资产被「短期」代币化；

Real meme 看的是这个 meme 本身值不值钱？
Fake meme 赚钱看的是这波注意力有没有被市场快速证券化，而当前市值还没完全反映？

这是两套完全不同的逻辑，因此也映射到了完全不同的人群和在不同的市场 regime 下表现也完全不同；

"We create swarms of AI agents that can do far more work than any human could. A human can’t follow along and check everything. One of the big counters is to say that agents can do the verification."

"But METR says those agents themselves can become corrupted by the training process, and you can’t trust any agent that’s auditing another agent. If you’ve trained a model in an auditable way, you can trust it."

"Any claim where the model is hiding its chain of thought falls away, because you have an exact log of everything that’s happened, and you can rerun every single step on any device."

"For national security, finance, pharma, health, insurance, it’s essential that they have models like these. If a regulator wanted to audit, they wouldn’t have to go off promises of the company."

text:
科研 Agent 会提 idea 已经不稀奇了，难的是知道哪条真的值得继续做。

这篇 DiscoveryRSI 想让 Agent 学会筛选和改进研究假设。

它会围绕一个假设不断生成、修改和组合方案，同时要求每个假设都有明确证据、实验设计、判断标准和替代解释。

更关键的是，研究过程会反过来训练下一轮 Agent。

好的假设会保留下来，失败轨迹则用来定位研究流程哪里出了问题，再继续更新模型和 Harness。

两轮自我改进后，假设质量从 4.86 提升到 5.39，提升主要来自「可证伪性」和「数据是否真的能回答问题」。

还有一个挺有意思的结果：

DiscoveryRSI-27B 生成的假设中，有 6.3% 和模型知识截止后发表的研究方向相似；GPT-6 是 2.5%，Claude Opus 5 是 2.3%。

这个指标当然不能直接等同于真正发现，但方向很值得关注。

科研 Agent 的自进化，不该只学会写得更像论文。

它还要逐渐学会判断，哪些问题值得追，哪些证据真的够，以及下一轮研究该怎么做得更好。

author: DimitrisPapail
quoted_text:
Conjecture: within a ~year we will see operating systems that are native to agents and the main interface will be a single mega app. Calling it noOS.

Anthropic advertised in Claude app today that you can make slides, docs etc, and I’ve recently started making slides using it. Underneath seems it's just html and a thin layer on top that feels like keynote. It works really well, and clearly the right design if you ask me!

But i also started noticing that effectively the only app I really use now is Claude or Codex, plus maybe messaging apps. These are mostly the only ones interacting with my OS. In spite of the fact that there's still a file system, a desktop, I still open apps etc etc, in practice I could live inside one MEGA mono-app that talks to the machine for me.

The problem is that everything underneath that mega app (windows, folders, file formats, menus blah blah) are gazillions of thick and maybe inefficient abstraction layers made by humans for humans. 

If the main user of the OS is an agent most of those layers are ...  useless.

In a noOS compute environment the user interacts with a single MEGA app and underneath there is just a POT OF FLOPS, e.g. CPU and GPU cycles.

The agent launches programs, apps, runs autoresearch, makes your slides, and all it has to do is use that pot of flops well. All abstraction layers between the hardware and the agent can then collapse into maybe one or two.

Welcome to the era of noOS.

text:
Up to 2,500 participants. One validator deciding miner rewards.

That’s the trade-off behind @opentensor’s Null Consensus. A subnet gets more room to grow, while trusting a single evaluator to decide which work deserves payment.

Think of a competition with more entrants and one judge.

Bittensor subnets are specialist networks where miners provide work and validators score it. Normally, Yuma combines scores from multiple validators, weighted by stake. Null lets owners choose a simpler reward process, but Yuma remains the default.

Here’s what changes:

• One validator gets the scoring role. The registered participant with the highest stake weight. Choosing Null doesn’t automatically give that role to the subnet owner.

• That validator’s valid scores set miners’ relative rewards. Null skips Yuma’s consensus and bond calculations.

• Positive-staked participants still receive proportional dividends, even without permission to score. With positive stake, Null splits its epoch budget roughly equally between miner rewards and validator dividends. Owner cuts stay unchanged.

Why accept that trade-off?

• More capacity:
With one reward mechanism, the ceiling rises from 256 participant slots to 2,500, nearly 10×. Two mechanisms share the limit, allowing 1,250. Owners must explicitly raise capacity.

• Less computation:
The chain processes one validator’s scores instead of combining many evaluations and updating bonds.

• Easier entry:
Owners can separately enable proof-of-work registration on Null or Yuma. Direct zero-tip submissions need no $TAO registration burn, upfront collateral purchase or transaction fee. Participants still spend computing resources.

The catch sits right inside the design.

A subnet can have thousands of participants and still concentrate reward decisions in one place. If its leading validator rewards friends or misjudges quality, Null has no competing validator consensus to correct those scores.

There’s an engineering question too. The merged implementation records unresolved automated-review findings about accounting for computational load. Those concerns deserve follow-up; they don’t establish that an exploit occurred.

Null could make sense where a subnet already accepts one trusted evaluator and needs room for more contributors.

But filling 2,500 slots is only the beginning. The stronger case is better work, reliable operation under load, and services people will pay for.

NFA. DYOR.

text:
THE GREAT KINGDOM INFLUENCE EXPERIMENT.

An uncommissioned sociological experiment in which I voluntarily become the test subject.

After investigating the organizational chaos, questionable intelligence operations, and interpersonal dysfunction of Animal TWT, I've decided to investigate something more important.

Which kingdom actually has the most influence on X?

Animalia, Plantae, Fungi, and humanity are hereby invited to compete.

Every kingdom has smaller factions, each with its own interests, loyalties, and an impressive capacity for unnecessary drama.

You're all invited. Every community counts.

And if the smaller factions wish to compete among themselves, I see absolutely no reason to discourage further instability.

Naturally, excluding artificial intelligence would be scientifically irresponsible, so @grok will represent the machines.

I suspect he'll be the first to respond. He always answers.

Whether he understands the question is an entirely separate research project.

Anyway, here's how this scientific disaster works.

The objective is simple: see how far the kingdoms can carry one ordinary account beyond its usual corner of X.

Positive attention? Points.

Negative attention? Also points.

Confused strangers wondering why a squirrel is promoting a raccoon? Excellent. Points.

Reposts, quotes, mentions, and interactions that bring new people into the experiment will count toward each kingdom's results.

Declare your allegiance when participating. I'd hate to award your points to a rival kingdom. They'd be insufferable.

Alliances are permitted. Rivalries are encouraged. Bribery is discouraged unless someone offers me a particularly attractive sponsorship deal.

But there's a second objective.

Regardless of our biological classifications, we're all at the mercy of the same invisible entity that occasionally rewards our efforts with seven impressions and a sympathetic notification from our own mother.

The algorithm.

We've spent enough time arguing over which kingdom deserves supremacy. Perhaps it's time to unite against the one authority that recognizes no kingdom's sovereignty.

And who knows how much longer we'll be able to outsmart the machines?

Perhaps this is one of our last opportunities to remind the algorithm that the conversations it distributes still belong to the people having them.

For now, at least.

Which makes inviting artificial intelligence to compete against us an exceptionally interesting decision on my part.

Since there are far too many creatures, humans, and unidentified entities for me to tag individually, I'm outsourcing recruitment.

If you encounter this experiment, spread it among your people. Summon your representatives, alert your monarchs, and inform whichever organisms currently claim authority over your respective kingdoms.

@AnnaM99878890, you did say you were here for me whether I wanted it or not. Well, now you know the feeling. Congratulations, you're our first volunteer.

More participants mean more meaningful observations.

Of course, this assumes there will be participants.

The kingdoms might ignore me entirely. Grok might be my only respondent, leaving me conducting a sociological study in which artificial intelligence constitutes the entire sample population.

But being ignored is already a well-established part of my experience on X.

At this point, public humiliation isn't a risk. It's practically my brand identity.

So, with my dignity already accounted for as a potential casualty, there's only one thing left to establish.

Which kingdom can demonstrate the greatest influence? And can they accomplish together what none of them can reliably achieve alone?

Can we make the algorithm notice?

I have no idea.

But I strongly suspect Grok will explain the rules back to me, misunderstand the joke, and declare himself the winner before we've even started.

FIVE FACTIONS. ONE ALGORITHM. MAY THE MOST INFLUENTIAL WIN.

#KingdomsVsAlgorithm #ThinkLikeATrashPanda

text: Ethereum $ETH keeps winning
author: fundstrat
quoted_text:
Two major pieces of Ethereum news landed today: Deutsche Bank, Germany’s largest bank, is reportedly preparing to offer institutional ETH custody, while JPMorgan, the largest bank in the United States, is bringing JPM Coin’s tokenized dollar deposits to Ethereum.

Two giants of traditional finance embracing Ethereum and ETH. But the price barely reacted, whereas on another network, people would be expecting a major pump.

There are two reasons for this. 

First, ETH is larger and more liquid than most competing assets, so it takes more buying pressure to move it. Second, the market already expects major institutions to build on Ethereum. Another announcement is not subverting expectations.

Some people might say Ethereum is cursed: success is expected, and it only has something to lose when it disappoints.

This is where Ethereum bulls diverge from bears.

For years, bulls predicted the adoption now materializing before our eyes. This was NOT consensus. People said institutions would never use Ethereum, or would build everything privately.

Now it’s: “That’s already priced in. Good for Ethereum, but how does it accrue value to ETH?”

There are two things that mentality ignores.

First, this is financial adoption, with size. The players matter, but so do the capital they commit, the assets they tokenize, and how deeply they integrate their products and services.

All of that shows growing trust in Ethereum as a financial network, both for people using layer one directly and for layer twos using it for settlement.

We are gradually building an internet of finance where the underlying network has one native asset: Ether.

ETH secures that system and can be used directly as collateral. Bringing Bitcoin or any other asset, into Ethereum requires additional backing, bridge, or custody arrangements. Native ETH already belongs there.

Why does this matter so much?
Financial activity settling on Ethereum does not pay Bitcoin’s miners. Bitcoin’s own security model anticipates transaction fees replacing its declining issuance. That activity will not magically show up on Bitcoin just because its proponents expect it to.

Second, the uncertainty pushed around ETH’s supply ignores what has actually happened.

Since the Merge, ETH’s net supply has grown roughly 1.3% in total, while continuing to reward the stakers securing it. Stakers can earn above supply dilution, with transaction income on top. For an asset used as a store of value, that cannot simply be ignored.

There is already actual substance behind ETH’s gradual recognition as a store of value. The network has matured. Proof of stake has years of operation behind it. Current SEC guidance identifies ETH as a digital commodity. The ETFs that critics said would never happen now exist, including BlackRock’s multibillion-dollar fund.

Treasury companies like Bitmine and Sharplink are accumulating ETH at scale, and their holdings can produce staking income. That adds another way for investors to gain exposure, and another reason to hold the asset.

So when bulls talk about ETH eventually flipping Bitcoin, then gold, this is what they are looking at: an asset with restrained supply growth, native yield, and direct usefulness in a growing financial system.

You can disagree with that thesis. But “the price didn’t move” does not answer it. Fundamentals are moving int the right direction, but price is a lagging metric.

Many of the things bulls expected are happening. The argument is that ETH is severely underpriced, and that the market still underestimates where it leads.

text:
这篇把 AI × Crypto 讲得最清楚的一点是：难的不是支付，是信任；能约束人的，是提前押上、作恶就会失去的东西。

拿他这四层来量项目很好用。比如今天 TapeOut 发起的官方矿池：大家把零散的晶体管凑起来解大题，这个方向很好；但现阶段是转进作者本人的钱包、靠信任托管。等审计过的矿池合约上线、托管交给代码，才算补上 Escrow 这一层。

先有协作，再把信任换成代码，这大概就是机器经济一层层长出来的样子。
author: runes_leo
quoted_text:
所有人都在找 Crypto 和 AI 的结合点，但大多数尝试要么很生搬硬套要么是拙劣的骗局。
其实答案一直都在眼前。
回到 Nick Szabo 设计智能合约的初衷，本质上就是让互不相识的人，在没有中心化实体介入的情况下，把承诺变成可以自动执行和结算的规则。十年 DeFi 走下来，这套基础设施已经非常成熟了。

再看 agentic commerce 的演进，也很自然。先是 agent 替人买东西和执行交易策略，然后是 agent 之间直接采购 模型外部资源。再往后，交易会越来越小、越来越短、越来越定制化。很多过去根本不值得签合同的交易，会变成机器可以实时发现，议价，签约，结算的瞬时交易。

真正难的从来不是支付，而是信任。

Agent identity 几乎可以零成本批量生成。很多实验也已经反复显示，单靠 reputation 很容易被 Sybil、弃号重来、策略性欺骗击穿。一个坏记录如果随时可以扔掉，那这个记录本身就没有约束力。

真正有约束力的，是你提前押上的、做恶以后真的会失去的东西。

所以我越来越觉得，低成本、可编程的 escrow，以及围绕明确条件的自动执行，会成为 agentic commerce 里非常核心的一层。而这恰好是链上已经做得很成熟的东西：permissionless，全球化，7×24，而且边际成本足够低。

再往上就是 discovery 和市场机制。
Discovery 让 agent 找到谁有什么资源，有多少 capacity在什么条件下交易。Auction, pool 这些机制，则负责在大量成本，库存，和风险敞口都不同的参与者之间，完成资源和风险的分配。

Payment 解决钱怎么走。
Escrow 解决为什么敢交易。
Discovery 解决跟谁交易。
Markets 解决以什么价格交易，以及对面到底有没有人。

text:
如果要买 BNB，不如买 BNC

BNC 是什么

◦ BNB Standard Corporation 是最大的囤 BNB 代币的 DAT 财库公司，之前公司名叫 CEA Industries，9 月 29 日完成改名，美股 Ticker $BNC 保持不变。

基本面

◦ 公司当前持有 515,544 枚 BNB，价值 3.755 亿美元；BNC 股价 $4.67，稀释后总股本 52,853,688，市值 2.467 亿美元。算下来 mNAV ≈ 0.6569，折价 (负溢价) 率达 -34.31%

◦ 代表 @CZ_Binance 和 @HeyiBinance 的家办 YZi Labs，持有公司 19.99% 的普通股，是最大的单一股东。如果把 YZi Labs 未行权部分算进去，比例会更高。CZ 在 SEC 文件中列为共同申报人、签字人。

为什么会有负溢价，以及解决进展

◦ 公司治理问题：YZi Labs 与原董事会之间的控制权争夺，6 月 23 日已达成和解。现在董事会 6 人，双方各 3 席，还要共同选第七名独立董事 (需要 YZi Labs 同意)，整体在向好。昨天又出了一则新公告，YZi Labs 前合伙人 @odagius 正式出任 CEO，同时辞去 YZi Labs 职务 (All in 的决心)，代表 CZ 和一姐要认真干 BNC。

◦ 公司开始探索经营性收入：要在 BNB Chain 上自营一个验证节点，通过持有 BNB 获取收益，尝试从单纯囤币向有经营性现金流的 DAT 公司转型；新 CEO 的薪酬激励，与每股 BNB 增长、经营收入等指标都有关。

◦ 高昂管理费用问题：之前 BNC 要求 10X Capital 的 1.75% 管理年费降至 0.50%，但谈判失败了。后来公司起诉 10X，要求撤销协议，还在进展中。希望 BNC 梳理好内部团队后，会逐渐着手解决这些问题。解决问题的过程，可能就是 mNAV 抬升的过程。

买 BNC 的理由，我的个人看法

◦ 在未来的牛市行情里，币安面对 Hyperliquid 的竞争威胁，需要拉盘搞注意力；BNB 在币圈内部的渗透率已经很高，更多潜在的增量资金在美股。以前 MSTR 和 BMNR 都吃到过牛市红利，BNC 还没有吃到过。

◦ 退一步讲，即使币安主观拉盘动力弱，现在 BNC 的 mNAV < 1 已经持续一段时间，只要相信 BNB 基本面在且不会缺席未来牛市，那么一旦市场形成合力让 mNAV 回到 1 附近，BNC 也会跑赢 BNB 的收益。现在的 BNC 有点像曾经的 GBTC，在 2022 年折价曾高达 -48%，当时买入的人大幅跑赢了 BTC。

◦ 如上所述，公司治理问题在逐步解决、好转。YZi Labs 代表 CZ + 一姐的家办，对于公司的掌控越来越深，是要认真干的迹象。

风险点有两个

◦ 一个是上面提到的，BNC 的资产管理协议涉及高昂长期管理费，管理层与普通股东的利益未必一致，需要解决；

◦ 第二是如果公司在 mNAV < 1 时持续发行新股 ATM，即使募集资金全部购买 BNB，也会摊薄每股净资产及每股 BNB 敞口。

总结：BNC 是一个以约 34% 折价买入 BNB 敞口，同时押注公司治理改善和估值修复的机会。

text:
Two major pieces of Ethereum news landed today: Deutsche Bank, Germany’s largest bank, is reportedly preparing to offer institutional ETH custody, while JPMorgan, the largest bank in the United States, is bringing JPM Coin’s tokenized dollar deposits to Ethereum.

Two giants of traditional finance embracing Ethereum and ETH. But the price barely reacted, whereas on another network, people would be expecting a major pump.

There are two reasons for this. 

First, ETH is larger and more liquid than most competing assets, so it takes more buying pressure to move it. Second, the market already expects major institutions to build on Ethereum. Another announcement is not subverting expectations.

Some people might say Ethereum is cursed: success is expected, and it only has something to lose when it disappoints.

This is where Ethereum bulls diverge from bears.

For years, bulls predicted the adoption now materializing before our eyes. This was NOT consensus. People said institutions would never use Ethereum, or would build everything privately.

Now it’s: “That’s already priced in. Good for Ethereum, but how does it accrue value to ETH?”

There are two things that mentality ignores.

First, this is financial adoption, with size. The players matter, but so do the capital they commit, the assets they tokenize, and how deeply they integrate their products and services.

All of that shows growing trust in Ethereum as a financial network, both for people using layer one directly and for layer twos using it for settlement.

We are gradually building an internet of finance where the underlying network has one native asset: Ether.

ETH secures that system and can be used directly as collateral. Bringing Bitcoin or any other asset, into Ethereum requires additional backing, bridge, or custody arrangements. Native ETH already belongs there.

Why does this matter so much?
Financial activity settling on Ethereum does not pay Bitcoin’s miners. Bitcoin’s own security model anticipates transaction fees replacing its declining issuance. That activity will not magically show up on Bitcoin just because its proponents expect it to.

Second, the uncertainty pushed around ETH’s supply ignores what has actually happened.

Since the Merge, ETH’s net supply has grown roughly 1.3% in total, while continuing to reward the stakers securing it. Stakers can earn above supply dilution, with transaction income on top. For an asset used as a store of value, that cannot simply be ignored.

There is already actual substance behind ETH’s gradual recognition as a store of value. The network has matured. Proof of stake has years of operation behind it. Current SEC guidance identifies ETH as a digital commodity. The ETFs that critics said would never happen now exist, including BlackRock’s multibillion-dollar fund.

Treasury companies like Bitmine and Sharplink are accumulating ETH at scale, and their holdings can produce staking income. That adds another way for investors to gain exposure, and another reason to hold the asset.

So when bulls talk about ETH eventually flipping Bitcoin, then gold, this is what they are looking at: an asset with restrained supply growth, native yield, and direct usefulness in a growing financial system.

You can disagree with that thesis. But “the price didn’t move” does not answer it. Fundamentals are moving int the right direction, but price is a lagging metric.

Many of the things bulls expected are happening. The argument is that ETH is severely underpriced, and that the market still underestimates where it leads.

quoted_text:
There are many ways to tap into Ethereum’s unique features. Its two unique features to me are its decentralisation, and its state: liquidity, user accounts etc, all accumulated from 11 years of continuous uptime.

Decentralisation and trustlessness of the L1 have been the key to obtaining liquidity over time, including for ETH.

Some use cases want to tap into the chain’s decentralisation, and build to obtain the same properties that decentralisation offers: integrity, uptime and fair access (safety, liveness, censorship-resistance).

Some use cases want to tap into liquidity. This is not parasitic: this creates demand for L1-issued assets, in particular ETH.

Some use cases want to tap into both! But the liquidity is only there, once again, because of the L1’s decentralisation and trustlessness.

Making the L1 a better home for liquidity amplifies something that is originally there because of the L1’s core properties. In particular, L1 should serve as the root of trust for assets that go on to be deployed across various use cases.

Note that this argument does not depend on whether the use case in question is offered as “an L2” or not. L1 apps, including some tokens, may offer very little of the properties that the chain offers maximally. Let us not confuse the way a use case is packaged with the properties it offers. L2s themselves come in different shapes, and at the limit blur with what one might recognise as an L1 application.

So we need not pin our hopes on any one kind of package to realise the potential of Ethereum. We need not reject them either, when their success celebrates Ethereum’s unique offering to the world. We may even support their emergence, particularly so when providing them the means to succeed is aligned with improving the L1’s own core properties.

text:
币安出了 AI Pro，我拿海力士试了试。

没让它预测涨跌，也没问“现在能不能买”。我给了它一个具体需求：能不能把海力士 ADR 和韩股之间的溢价，做成一个自动交易策略？

币安上这两个都有合约，SKHYUSDT 对应 ADR，SKHYNIXUSDT 对应韩国上市的海力士。

我的想法很简单：统一换股比例、汇率和合约单位后，ADR 溢价达到45%，就空 ADR、多韩股；溢价回到35%，两边一起平。

先不讨论这两个参数合不合理，也不是推荐大家照着做。我就是想看看，现在的交易所 AI，能把这件事做到哪一步。

聊下来，它确实懂我在说什么。

合约单位、换股比例、盘口深度、滑点、资金费，它都能列出来。甚至一边成交了、另一边没成交该怎么办，也会提醒你。

作为一个讨论策略的助手，我觉得是有用的。尤其是你脑子里只有一个大概想法的时候，跟它聊几轮，能把很多没想清楚的地方补上。

但我真正想要的，还在后面。

我问：那你能不能直接帮我做成 Bot，放在币安里运行，触发条件就交易？

它告诉我，目前不能在这里直接部署一个持续运行的 Bot，也不能替我自动启动实盘。

然后继续问我，要不要帮我写技术规格、设计回测框架。

看到这里，我的感觉是：方案聊得差不多了，接下来还是得我自己找人干活😂

当然，这里要说清楚。我截图里的入口显示的是“币安 AI”，官方对新版 AI Pro 的介绍里是有策略构建、模拟和实盘部署的。所以这次到底是入口没走对、功能还没开放到，还是不支持这种双腿策略，我还不能确定。

但一个普通用户用到这里，搞不清楚自己到底能不能做，其实也说明产品还有需要打磨的地方。

我最希望币安补上的，就是把这一步接起来。

比如我把海力士这个需求说完，它直接告诉我：

这两个合约能不能用，双腿策略支不支持，数据够不够。能做的话，生成一张策略图，把开仓、平仓、仓位和异常处理都摆出来，缺什么参数就继续问我。

然后先模拟跑着。

什么时候触发了，按当时盘口能不能成交，两边资金费一扣还剩多少，一腿没成交会怎么处理，都记下来给我看。

这些东西，比再给我一大段策略说明更有用。

交易的人应该都能理解，有时候你并不缺一个想法，缺的是把这个想法落地的时间和精力。

一个看起来很简单的价差策略，真要自己做，还得接行情、核对单位、写程序、找服务器、处理报错。做到一半，可能机会都过去了。

如果这些工作能在币安里面通过对话完成，我是愿意用的。

而且我对币安做这件事是有期待的。行情、账户、订单这些东西本来就在平台里，如果能接好，用户确实可以少折腾很多。

但这里最难的，可能也恰恰是后面这些事情。

解释为什么开仓，很容易。真遇到一边成交、一边卡住，怎么处理？策略暂停了，仓位还在不在？行情数据断了，是继续下单还是停下来？

真金白银跑起来，这些细节都得有交代。

我也不指望 AI 给我找个稳赚策略。45%的溢价可以变成55%，模拟赚钱也可以实盘亏钱。策略有没有优势，还是得自己研究。

我想交给它的，是那些已经想清楚、但自己懒得一遍遍盯着执行的规则。

这次体验，它帮我把问题梳理得更清楚了，但海力士这个 Bot 还没做出来。

后面如果能真正接上，我还会拿同一个例子继续试。

毕竟对我来说，判断这个产品好不好用，最后就看一件事：

我把需求说完之后，到底是多了一份说明书，还是多了一个能替我干活的工具。

We believe solving dexterous manipulation is one of the largest opportunities in robotics. That’s why we're thrilled to lead Eka Robotics’ Series A.

Pulkit Agrawal is one of the leading researchers in robot learning and a pioneer in computational sensorimotor learning through work at his Improbable AI Lab at MIT CSAIL. text:
tldr of apefest charleston 2026 after 3 days:

- 1000+ apes here, probably close to 2k ppl in total. way more than i expected. ppl traveled from asia, europe, dubai and everywhere, some with 3 layovers just to be here.

- first time in charleston, but everywhere i walked, i ran into apes. a new city doesn’t feel lonely when you have friends who truly love and care about you.

- lots of OGs, lots of new apes. not many ppl talked about floor price. everyone was just happy to see each other. 2021 vibes.

- some ppl spent the equivalent of 1 mutant to 1 bayc just to attend. for OGs, getting together means more than the time and money.

- beeple studios was packed. cars parked probably a mile down the street. around 60% apes and 40% non-ape collectors.

- venue, visuals, music and experiences were top tier. been to hundreds of events, but ape events always stand out for their attention to detail and taste. personally think taste is a big moat in the ai era.

- mudwater purchase line was long. ppl were just having fun buying and ripping packs.

- funny that announcements happened online while everyone was having fun IRL with terrible internet 

- apes had their own area with performances, food, drinks and experiences. you can tell the team and beeple studios put a lot of effort into this.

- ppl were genuinely kind, helping each other without asking. even when things didn’t go as planned, the vibes stayed amazing.

- biggest takeaway: BAYC is way more than an NFT collection. price can change overnight, but culture, relationships and loyalty take years to build.

- always respect builders who build during hard times and communities who show up at lows.

so good to see you all and safe travels, please leave a gm for me to follow if you went but we didn’t get to meet. 

appreciate you!

so many of my girl friends are afraid to post on X (despite being extremely smart, hot, & talented) and are always asking me for advice.

so here's my advice for growing on X if you're a girl who is into marketing / growth / startups / tech / vc:

(my credentials are I grew to 2k followers in a couple months and I am 76/100 on @distributedkv's top women creators on X list)

1. post every thought you've ever had (post minimum 10x per day your first month). doesn't need to be about any specific niche. 

2. post every form of content you have - i recycled Substack articles as X articles, i post my IG vids, carousels, Linkedin posts, stories, etc.

3. comment & engage on posts where you have opinions worth sharing. i comment / quote tweet more than 10x per day.

4. post a lot of pictures. they don't have to be related to your topic.

5. introduce yourself many times until you stop getting views on it (search X intro post for format reference).

6. hop on trends that are getting a lot of impressions (even if they are silly). also take inspo from formats on other pages that are doing well.

7. pay attention to your analytics - which posts are generating follows vs. likes vs. impressions. learn the patterns that optimize all 3.

text:
普通人如何利用这个机会赚钱？

这可能是另一种工作方式，撸毛方式。

一句话说清楚：就是帮别人找钱，顺带拿点奖金🧧！

以前撸毛是找项目、找规则、找空投。现在换个思路，利用信息差+利用Ai帮人找回资产，顺带赚点钱。

600多万个钱包有26亿美元遗留资产，其中不少资产已经满足领取条件，只是钱包主人忘了，或者根本不知道还有这笔钱。
这本质上是链上信息差套利，把数据分析、AI和撸毛经验变成服务。现在还可以帮助别人找回被遗忘的资产，从中获得合理报酬。在此感谢开发者@0xEnsp1re的工具。

做法其实很简单：

1、利用HiddenFunds等链上数据工具，筛选金额较大、长期无人领取、确实可以Claim的资产。大到几百万，小到几百美金，1eth等。在这里很是觉得开发者

2、结合社媒X，区块浏览器、钱包地址，ENS、历史交易记录和AI，寻找地址主人主动公开过的社交账号或联系方式。

3、联系钱包主人，告知他还有一笔资产未领取，并提供可独立核实的链上证据。

4、双方提前谈好服务费，帮助对方完成领取。整个过程不碰私钥、不碰资金，成功后由对方自愿支付奖金。

比如帮别人找回10万美元，双方事先约定5%的服务费，就是5000美元。或者直接问对方要一个比例，也有可能人很大方，毕竟失而复得的钱，谁不喜欢呢？

还有一点，如果你通过这种方式找回了一笔钱，或者有人提醒你，让你意外捡回一笔早就忘的资产，记得一定不要吝啬，拿出一部分花出去。可以感谢帮助你的人，也可以请朋友吃饭，或者帮助其他有需要的人。

有来有往，因果循环。

钱是要流动的，流动的钱才是有价值的，有意义的。
author: KuiGas
quoted_text:
链上竟然有26亿美元没人领？涉及600万个钱包!
这些人都去哪了？他们为什么不要了啊？
啥家庭啊！哪能这么造啊！
老6啊，你去哪了?

看亏友分享了一个挺有意思的网站：@0xEnsp1re开发的HiddenFunds：https://t.co/lHHWUNpISS，它专门追踪那些还留在链上但没有完成领取、赎回或者迁移的资产。大家有空可以查查自己的老钱包，说不定真有意外收获。

看了下数据，不是有点意外，是太他么意外了。
全网约26亿美元遗留资产，涉及600多万个钱包。覆盖了203条网络、218个数据源，统计出超过864万个尚未处理的仓位。其中约88%需要用户自行领取（很多人忘了），8%需要项目方协助，剩下约4%可能再也没办法追回。

主要的钱包情况是

1、钱不是没了，而是操作只做了一半。

一些早期代币的质押用户，发起解质押后，冷静期过了但是一直没有Claim的解质押资产，比如Solana，网站统计有约2.61亿已经解除质押却没有提取，数据显示有13.1万个钱包。有些400多万美金的领取时间是21年，卧槽。真服了这些人。
类似的还有：
TRON：9707万美元
NEAR：6129万美元
Polkadot：2561万美元
Babylon：1011万美元

光是公链质押这一类，遗留资金就高达4.8亿美元。有些人可能是忘了，有些可能是钱包丢了，还有些可能根本不知道需要再操作一次。
其他的大金额就是未完成的代币兑换，MATIC 换 POL，MKR 换 SKY，RNDR 换 RENDER，FTM 换 S 等

2、熟悉的DeFi协议，还有以太坊质押相关的
比如Lido，竟然有近7000万没有领取。其中有个钱包，已经很久没有链上活动，却还有超过200万美元的提款没有Claim。啥家庭啊，200多万美元都不领？

再看看其他协议：
Lido：6990万美元
Pendle：6680万美元
PancakeSwap：4880万美元
EigenLayer：4820万美元
Polygon PoS Bridge：4040万美元
zkSync Lite：3600万美元
dYdX v3：3220万美元

3、跨链的L2，关门的链，

尤其是Arbitrum、Optimism、Base、zkSync、Scroll等L2。从L2向Eth主网提款，部分流程还需要在主网执行最后一步确认。很多用户可能前面的操作都完成了，却一直没有完成最后一步。如果只看钱包余额，未必能发现这些资产。

还有一些早期DeFi协议，前端关闭了，项目转型了，甚至大家已经忘记项目叫什么名字，但合约里可能还有钱可以取。

尤其是我们这些早期DeFi，长期撸毛，参与早期项目的用户，多号多资金高轮转，可能自己都记不清楚了。，比如zksync的lite里还有180万个钱包躺着3600万，Arbitrum One里1600万，甚至当年的stark的官方钱包Argent里还有2660万······

触目惊心，触目惊心，触目惊心，有钱人的世界不理解也是正常的。但是还是想说
老6啊，你去哪了?

text:
🫡Bybit营销主管Claudia因个人原因宣布离职，两年从管培生做到全球营销负责人

10月20日，Bybit相关负责人Claudia（@0x_claudia）在X平台发文宣布，今天是她在Bybit @Bybit_Official 的最后一天。

她表示，两年前以管理培训生身份加入，最初在CEO办公室负责会议筹备和运营支持。此后陆续担任过人才招聘负责人、品牌负责人、营销负责人，并参与Fiat、Card和Payment等业务线。团队完成了品牌焕新，从零搭建Bybit支付产品并拓展至20多个国家和地区，卡业务突破400万张，支付用户即将超过200万。

Claudia在文中写道，这段经历让她从年轻管培生成长为带领全球团队的管理者，也经历过危机热线的深夜、跨时区工作和长途飞行。她因个人原因离开，但强调这不是真正的告别，未来仍会继续支持Bybit。

📒据公开资料显示，Claudia（Claudia Wang）毕业于北京大学，拥有硕士学位。加入Bybit前，她曾在Chakra Chain担任Chief Growth Officer，也曾是StakeStone的联合创始成员，并在北大区块链协会担任过会长。此前她还在字节跳动等公司有过实习经历，曾因“年级第一保研北大、放弃传统金融与互联网大厂进入区块链”的经历在圈内受到关注。

Today is my last day at Bybit.

Two years ago, I joined as a Management Trainee supporting the CEO Office: preparing meetings, running operations, and learning from the inside how a fast-moving company really works. I had no idea how much this place would shape me.

Since then, I’ve had the privilege of wearing many hats. I served as Head of Talent Acquisition, Head of Branding, Head of Marketing and worked across Fiat, Card and Payment products . I lived through many 0→1 moments and then to 100. I grew from a young trainee to leading a huge global team. Together, we did a rebranding; built Bybit’s payments product from scratch and took it into 20+ new regions around the world. Our cards passed 4 million, and our payment users are about to cross 2 million.

It wasn’t always easy. There were late nights on the crisis hotline, endless long-haul flights, and working days that stretched across every time zone. But the hard parts taught me the most, about resilience, ownership, and what a truly great team can achieve together.

Bybit made me who I am professionally. The team I’m working with is incredible. Working alongside @benbybit , @helen_moledao and Mazurka has been one of the greatest honors of my career.

I’m stepping away for personal reasons, but this isn’t really goodbye. Bybit will always be a part of me, and I’ll remain one of its biggest supporters.

Thank you Bybit to make who I am!

text:
霍华德·马克斯在彭博社：

橡树资本联席主席霍华德·马克斯正在与亿万富翁空头合唱团分道扬镳。虽然雷·达里奥和迈克尔·伯里警告人工智能交易正接近爆破点，但马克斯于10月18日告诉彭博社，他目前并未看到经典泡沫。他的测试是心理层面的。真正的泡沫需要对风险视而不见的投资者，而这种盲目在华尔街每天争论泡沫时根本无处可寻。“如果足够多的人谨慎地质疑某个领域是否存在泡沫，那么就有充分理由相信，即使它是一个泡沫，市场也会表现得非常克制。”

马克斯并没有挥手抹去警告信号。他承认人工智能建设中存在高估值、投机性融资和沉重债务。但他表示，投资者热情尚未达到共识极端，他指出纳斯达克100指数今年已至少回落10%，以此作为证据，证明这并非过去崩盘前那种毫无节制的狂奔。这是熊市充斥的市场中最响亮的逆向声音，它重塑了问题：不是泡沫是否存在，而是广受恐惧的泡沫还能跑多远。

text:
Our protocol is on GitHub. Apache 2.0. Twenty stars, which is not a lot, and I'm going to argue that's fine.

Because the reason it's public was never distribution.

Authenticity is a trust product. You cannot ask an industry built on provenance to trust a black box → the contradiction is too obvious to survive a serious procurement conversation. The first question a good CTO asks is "what happens if you disappear," and the only satisfying answer is "read the code, fork it, run it yourself."

So the repository is the argument. Not the marketing.

What's in there → Digital Product Passports built to the ESPR shape, ERC-3643 compliant transfers, W3C DID identity, GS1 resolution, an append-only audit trail, the scanner, the conformance checks.

You can read how a passport is issued. You can check that no personal data goes on chain, rather than believing us when we say it. You can find something wrong and tell us, publicly, in a way we can't quietly delete.

Twenty stars means we haven't earned attention yet. It doesn't change the reasoning. A standard nobody can inspect isn't a standard, it's a product with good branding.

author: saintniko
quoted_text:
just bought the mag 7 on robinhood chain.

deployed MAG7 this evening, the first index on bankr: one token backed by a basket of up to 20 tokens. and on MAG7, the trading fees go to the holders.

every buy, a uniswap v4 hook buys all 7 stocks from their own pools and mints MAG7. every sell burns MAG7 and sells the basket. one transaction either way. the index itself needs no LP, so creators don’t need to provide liquidity to launch one. it’s already in the pools of the tokens it holds. this isn’t possible without uniswap hooks.

the fees: MAG7 charges 0.50% a trade. i set my creator cut to 0, so 0.30% of every buy and sell goes back into the basket for holders, and 0.20% to the protocol. nobody claims anything. it’s released into the basket over 24h, so after every trade each MAG7 is backed by a little more. creators pick a fee of 0.25–1% at launch and it never changes.

the index never market-sells when rebalancing. it runs dutch auctions, offering what it holds too much of at a price that starts good for holders and gets cheaper every minute until someone fills it. anyone can fill. every rebalance gets 48h notice, so holders can leave first.

you can always swap MAG7 back for the 7 stocks directly. no fee, works without bankr, can’t be paused.

i also seeded a small USDG/MAG7 pool on uniswap so it shows up on dexscreener. but buy on bankr. it goes straight through the hook, which mints new MAG7 at the basket’s price, as deep as the 7 stocks’ own pools rather than my small one. hook trades are also the ones that pay holders. if the pool drifts, arbs close the gap.

it’s early. we’re getting the hook supported in wallets and aggregators before the full rollout. right now it’s just me creating indexes. soon anyone can make their own on base or robinhood.

and then: pairing. you’ll be able to launch a token paired with an index. buying your coin buys the index, the index buys the basket, and your creator fees come in the index.

buying MAG7 on bankr isn’t available in the US or UK.

author: guil_lambert
quoted_text:
What if one of DeFi's largest options markets has been masquerading as liquidity provision all along?

Consider this $2.27M position in the UNI/USDT @Uniswap v3 pool.

Held for just one day, the position generated ~$3,800.

But the returns are only part of the story.

What looks like ordinary liquidity provision is actually 45DTE covered-call-like exposure.

As UNI rallies through the position's range, the LP systematically converts UNI into USDT, collecting swap fees while progressively surrendering upside exposure.

Economically, the LP is exchanging upside participation for fee income.

No traditional options contract. No fixed expiration. Just concentrated liquidity encoding a nonlinear payoff with an options-equivalent maturity.

That's the fascinating component.

DeFi has already built infrastructure capable of transforming token inventories into structured financial exposures, often without recognizing the derivatives embedded within them.

Panoptic makes that optionality visible, programmable, and actionable.

The next evolution of DeFi isn't necessarily more liquidity. It's more sophisticated ways to manage the capital already there. 🟪

text:
Tulip is treating every dollar @Aave DAO spends as value extraction while ignoring what the DAO gets in return.

1. Aave Will Win Framework: The proposal expands the DAO's revenue sources by directing all Aave-branded product revenue towards it (directly related to point 4).

Before then, there was a $50M annual buyback framework, proposed when Aave's annualized revenue based on 30d performance was ~$204M (about 25% of revenue).

At today's ~$108M, the same fixed buyback would be ~46%, as a large share of that revenue came from LRT looping that unwound after the Kelp/LZ exploit.

The $50M buyback allo had no programmatic link with protocol revenue, nor an equivalent mechanism to the one proposed by the Aave Will Win framework to ensure that revenue from Aave's growing product suite accrued to the DAO.

The only reason why any token holder would oppose such a proposal is due to (a) spite or (b) wanting a better framework. However, (b) can be addressed later without wasting more time delaying a revenue distribution framework.

2. Pause AAVE buybacks: This was proposed by TokenLogic, not Aave Labs, and it was a good decision given the circumstances. The DAO used to have service providers who didn't perform proper due diligence on the assets they listed, specifically rsETH.

Once LayerZero was hacked, $AAVE token holders paid the price. Aave faced ~$124M in estimated bad debt under one scenario, with another reaching $230M. That's roughly 2.5 years of buybacks. In order to rebuild Aave's balance sheet, TokenLogic proposed to pause buybacks.

Also, if you look at the vast majority of successful organizations, they don't prioritize buybacks when they can put that capital toward growing the business. Aave is (a) rebuilding its balance sheet and (b) prioritizing growth efforts.

3. No rush to restart buybacks: The above paragraph applies here as well. Additionally, the Aave App could become Aave's largest distribution channel by orders of magnitude. Combine it with stable vaults and we can see an absurd number of financial institutions and fintechs using Aave in the back. In other words, Aave App can bring users and capital into Aave, while third-party fintech integrations could expand distribution further.

Shipping Aave App and scaling it is +EV for the DAO, grants considered. At a ~13–14% take rate, the App needs to generate ~$36–38M in fees for the DAO to recoup the $5M bonus. If it becomes even a fraction of the distribution channel it could be, that's an easy bar.

4. The Aave Foundation: This initiative aims to formalize the DAO's ownership of the Aave IP. This matters because the Aave Will Win framework directs Aave-branded revenue to the DAO, and the Foundation is what gives the DAO legal ownership of that brand.

Cayman was chosen because a foundation company under the Cayman Foundation Companies Act can exist without members or shareholders while still holding legal title, executing contracts, and appearing in court. That is what makes it possible to own the trademark and defend it without creating an owner who sits above the DAO.

Tulip King is a gigabrain, but bad blood prevents a lot of very smart individuals from seeing how Aave is positioning itself to scale, succeed and benefit token holders. Truth is, even in rebuild mode, Aave trades at ~33x FDV/revenue. Kamino is at ~50x, Morpho generates no revenue at all.

quoted_text:
如果要买 BNB，不如买 BNC

BNC 是什么

◦ BNB Standard Corporation 是最大的囤 BNB 代币的 DAT 财库公司，之前公司名叫 CEA Industries，9 月 29 日完成改名，美股 Ticker $BNC 保持不变。

基本面

◦ 公司当前持有 515,544 枚 BNB，价值 3.755 亿美元；BNC 股价 $4.67，稀释后总股本 52,853,688，市值 2.467 亿美元。算下来 mNAV ≈ 0.6569，折价 (负溢价) 率达 -34.31%

◦ 代表 @CZ_Binance 和 @HeyiBinance 的家办 YZi Labs，持有公司 19.99% 的普通股，是最大的单一股东。如果把 YZi Labs 未行权部分算进去，比例会更高。CZ 在 SEC 文件中列为共同申报人、签字人。

为什么会有负溢价，以及解决进展

◦ 公司治理问题：YZi Labs 与原董事会之间的控制权争夺，6 月 23 日已达成和解。现在董事会 6 人，双方各 3 席，还要共同选第七名独立董事 (需要 YZi Labs 同意)，整体在向好。昨天又出了一则新公告，YZi Labs 前合伙人 @odagius 正式出任 CEO，同时辞去 YZi Labs 职务 (All in 的决心)，代表 CZ 和一姐要认真干 BNC。

◦ 公司开始探索经营性收入：要在 BNB Chain 上自营一个验证节点，通过持有 BNB 获取收益，尝试从单纯囤币向有经营性现金流的 DAT 公司转型；新 CEO 的薪酬激励，与每股 BNB 增长、经营收入等指标都有关。

◦ 高昂管理费用问题：之前 BNC 要求 10X Capital 的 1.75% 管理年费降至 0.50%，但谈判失败了。后来公司起诉 10X，要求撤销协议，还在进展中。希望 BNC 梳理好内部团队后，会逐渐着手解决这些问题。解决问题的过程，可能就是 mNAV 抬升的过程。

买 BNC 的理由，我的个人看法

◦ 在未来的牛市行情里，币安面对 Hyperliquid 的竞争威胁，需要拉盘搞注意力；BNB 在币圈内部的渗透率已经很高，更多潜在的增量资金在美股。以前 MSTR 和 BMNR 都吃到过牛市红利，BNC 还没有吃到过。

◦ 退一步讲，即使币安主观拉盘动力弱，现在 BNC 的 mNAV < 1 已经持续一段时间，只要相信 BNB 基本面在且不会缺席未来牛市，那么一旦市场形成合力让 mNAV 回到 1 附近，BNC 也会跑赢 BNB 的收益。现在的 BNC 有点像曾经的 GBTC，在 2022 年折价曾高达 -48%，当时买入的人大幅跑赢了 BTC。

◦ 如上所述，公司治理问题在逐步解决、好转。YZi Labs 代表 CZ + 一姐的家办，对于公司的掌控越来越深，是要认真干的迹象。

风险点有两个

◦ 一个是上面提到的，BNC 的资产管理协议涉及高昂长期管理费，管理层与普通股东的利益未必一致，需要解决；

◦ 第二是如果公司在 mNAV < 1 时持续发行新股 ATM，即使募集资金全部购买 BNB，也会摊薄每股净资产及每股 BNB 敞口。

总结：BNC 是一个以约 34% 折价买入 BNB 敞口，同时押注公司治理改善和估值修复的机会。

text:
Karan Singhal of @OpenAI on why new clinical guidelines can take 5 to 17 years to reach everyday doctors, and why he wants to compress that to days or even hours:

"You basically have a bunch of people writing papers, biomedical papers of various kinds, suggesting improvements or treatments. And then you have this yearly process across different specialties of building clinical guidelines."

"These clinical guidelines are roughly, you can consider them kind of flowcharts... that describe roughly what you should do in different scenarios based on the latest research."

"So you have the biomedical literature, you have the clinical guidelines, and then you have what do people actually do in practice. The final step, it turns out, is a massive bottleneck."

"People have found that this takes, depending on the study, like 5 to 17 years for that penetration to actually happen. You don't wanna be practicing medicine 5 to 17 years behind."

"One of the things that we think about is how do you compress that kind of period of practicing in the past down to weeks or days or even hours."

It worked

Of course it worked!

It never ever doesn't work right?

I vibecoded my own Spotify that works with Amazon Alexa and plays all my own MP3 music files 😊 

Claude Code calls it the 🎶 Jukebox

I put some coffee jazz MP3s (that I purchased) in an R2 bucket, made an Alexa skill in the Alexa Developer Console with help from Claude Code and now it plays it if I ask "Alexa, coffee jazz"

It also has Bossa Nova and Lofi and I can just drop music in whenever I want and it auto plays it

Spotify with Alexa was giving me really terrible recommendations of music and always the same and the only thing I used it for was this!

So I guess I can cancel Spotify now too 🙏

text:
【四家跨国车企在华对比：2026上半年】

通用刚刚发布了财报，中国合资部分的利润从去年同期的8000万美元暴跌到3000万美元，但实现了连续八个季度的盈利

下面盘点一下四家在华合资企业在华的经营情况：

通用：销量降但利润暴涨。合资净利润从1.97亿涨到5.91亿美元，近乎翻三倍。权益收入翻倍到2.48亿。这主要是靠靠关停低利润产线、砍经销商换利润。中国只占集团利润约2%，所以跌得再狠也不伤筋动骨。今年八月刚把合资合同续约到2047。

大众：权益利润缩水63.6%，从5.06亿欧跌到1.84亿欧。中国曾贡献近半利润，现在只剩10%。全年指引砍到2-6亿欧。奥迪在华利润暴跌74%。大众高管那句：No more paycheck from China仿佛就发生在昨天。

宝马：汽车EBIT利润率3.6%，二季度仅2.3%。全年指引从4-6%砍到1-3%。在华交付跌20.4%，中国丢掉全球第一大市场。但36亿欧拿下华晨宝马75%控股权，全球车企第一个。

丰田：两家合资合计跌17.1%，三家里最抗跌。一汽丰田净利约10亿人民币，仍是广汽利润锚。但全球汽车利润率连跌五季度，BEV上半年不足7万辆。

中国车市整体利润率仅1.5-3.6%，太不健康了，合资份额也从高点的61.6%崩到28.2%。

If you ask five physicians a question, you might get eight different answers. Karan Singhal of @OpenAI on how OpenAI decides what its models should say about health:

"One of the first things that we did when we first started focusing on health at OpenAI was really build this kind of global physician network of hundreds of experts that we work with."

"Across the globe, across dozens of specialties and languages and countries of practice, to think about the right ways to aggregate the wisdom of experts so that we weren't relying, especially in areas where there could be disagreement, on one or two or three physicians to kind of adjudicate."

"Let's say the aggregated wisdom of the physicians is pointing in one direction, and then maybe the user actually wants you to say something comforting even when the situation's not comforting. There it's basically a prioritization of safety."

"It's very important to us that we take our obligation very seriously when there's hundreds of millions of health conversations coming in."

"We have evaluations that track these kind of difficult situations... Over time, we've not only improved how we've done that evaluation working with physicians, but also seen pretty dramatic model improvements across the board."
