text:
Ekin Dogus Cubuk of @periodiclabs on why AI has to learn from the physical world, and building their own lab to close that loop:

"One of the more fundamental ways of making things around us is powder synthesis... You can actually, using that method, discover new superconductors, magnets, all kinds of materials that are very important for technologies around us."

"But at the core of it is just quantum mechanics. And we feel like teaching these LLMs quantum mechanics will be the next frontier for LLMs."

"Science is by its nature iterative, right? Like even the smartest humans tried many times before they discovered the things they discovered. LLMs can be very smart, but if they're not iterating on science, they won't discover science."

"The important thing to teach these LLMs is the method of scientific inquiry. So you do simulations, you do theoretical calculations, you do experiments, you get results, and the results are probably incorrect or not what you wanted at first, but you iterate on it."

"You have to do it with the real physics, not just the simulation."

- 컴퓨팅 서비스 가격은 와트당 30~50달러 범위의 상단을 소폭 웃도는 수준이라고 언급.

- 외부 클라우드 고객과의 계약은 유연하게 구성되어 있어 자체 AI 개발과 외부 컴퓨팅 서비스 사이에서 자원을 배분할 수 있다고 설명.

- AI 컴퓨팅 투자 확대에도 자본효율성과 투자자본수익률(ROIC)을 중시한다는 기존 방침을 유지.

반도체 및 GPU 관련 발언

- 현재 AI 인프라 확장의 가장 큰 제약은 반도체 칩 확보보다 데이터센터의 전력과 냉각 능력이라고 설명.

- 기존 로켓 개발 엔지니어링 조직을 데이터센터 구축에 투입할 정도로 인프라 확장 속도를 높이고 있다고 언급.

- 엔비디아 GB200 칩을 매월 약 20만 개씩 가동할 수 있도록 준비하고 있다고 설명.

-해당 컴퓨팅 설비 확장 속도를 2027년에도 유지하는 것이 목표.

CAPEX , 실제 집행과 향후 가이던스

- 3분기 전체 CAPEX는 약 196억$, 그중 약 164억$가 AI 인프라 투자에 집중.
(3분기 CAPEX는 예상치를 하회한 것이 아닌 사실상 부합, 4분기 투자 가이던스는 크게 상향된 셈)

- 4분기 투자 집행 규모는 당초 시장 예상 약 190억$를 크게 상회.

text:
Elon Musk says SpaceX could exit 2027 with an annual recurring revenue (ARR) run rate of $500B to $1T. That’s well above the figure he gave in August, so it’s worth looking at what has to go right.

The math starts with compute. $SPCX  runs about 1.4 GW of AI capacity today, expects to pass 2 GW by the end of 2026, and is targeting roughly 10 GW by the end of 2027. In August, Musk valued each watt at $30 to $50 of annual revenue, which put 10 GW at $300B to $500B. Getting to $1T would take a lot more capacity, much higher revenue per watt, or both.

The base is growing fast. Q2 revenue hit $7.81B, up 92% year over year, with AI contributing about $2.56B. Compute deals with Anthropic and Alphabet add around $2B a month, and management is guiding to at least $100B in ARR by the end of 2026. Independent estimates are more conservative. SemiAnalysis models about $305B ARR by the end of 2027, with $235B from AI compute.

There are a few things to keep in mind:
- ARR is a run rate, not booked revenue. Capacity that comes online at the end of 2027 produces its full-year revenue in 2028.
- SpaceX spent over $25B on AI in a single quarter, so the buildout is capital intensive.
- Analysts expect it to depend on on-site natural gas power to move faster than grid connections allow, which makes it a hard timeline to hit.

I didn't really understand the idea of "AI Inference" until I put it into the frame of gaming. 

So gaming hardware has continually been chasing higher FPS, to make games prettier and more realistic. 

Better GPUs helped. But so did smarter engines, better optimization, and finding ways to do more work with the same hardware. (Nintendo in particular did the latter)

AI inference is basically the same race.

These guys are basically allowing a model to draft multiple tokens ahead for verification, potentially speeding up text generation without sacrificing the model’s output distribution. In other words, guessing what is likely to come next instead of waiting for the last request to finish and doing everything in order. 

All of this is critical to stop AI costs from exploding if they stop being subsized heavily (which they currently are). "

text:
For too many people, quantum risk is still abstract. Our new partnership with @RelmInsurance is a first step toward putting an actual *price* on it.

Digital asset insurance underwriting includes, among other things, an assessment of the security and cryptographic protocols protecting client funds. Relm is joining as a development partner for Strongpoint, our @projecteleven custody solution , and together we'll explore how post-quantum controls (key exposure, signing systems, migration readiness) could factor into that assessment.

That creates an incentive on both sides of the market.

For protocols: a chain without a credible path to post-quantum cryptography will become harder and more expensive to custody and insure. Protocols that want institutional adoption should be making that transition now (many are).

For institutions: those that aren't preparing for post-quantum cryptography, or that hold assets on chains with no migration path, should be *economically* riskier to insure than those that are. Their wallets (many of them on display here: https://t.co/KRSvE7frYA) may end up being among the first targets of quantum attack. 

Every protocol and institution in digital assets will eventually need to make the post-quantum transition. The open question is whether it happens on their own schedule or under pressure. 

Broader financial adoption and better insurance terms are two good reasons to start now.
author: apruden08
quoted_text:
Project Eleven and Relm Insurance Partner to Explore Quantum Risk in Digital Asset Insurance

The first partnership to explore post-quantum security as a factor in pricing digital asset insurance.

Project Eleven, the post-quantum security company for digital assets, today announced Relm Insurance as a development partner for Strongpoint, its flagship institutional custody product. The collaboration will explore how an institution’s post-quantum security controls could be evaluated within digital asset insurance underwriting, helping both companies better understand how quantum readiness may influence future assessments of digital asset risk.

As quantum computing advances, a sufficiently powerful machine could derive private keys from exposed public keys and compromise digital assets. Institutions need custody infrastructure capable of adapting its cryptography before such a machine becomes available. Strongpoint is built for that transition. The platform combines classical and post-quantum signing and separates institutional controls from the cryptography layer, enabling institutions to replace signing algorithms while preserving approval rules and audit history.

“Every institution holding digital assets will eventually need to prepare for post-quantum cryptography. The open question is whether that transition happens on the institution’s schedule or under pressure,” said Alex Pruden (@apruden08), CEO and Co-Founder of Project Eleven. “Insurance plays a critical role in how markets assess and manage risk. We believe there is an opportunity for institutions that invest in stronger post-quantum defenses to eventually see that reflected in how their risk is evaluated. Working with Relm is an important first step toward understanding what that could look like in practice.”

Exploring Post-Quantum Risk in Insurance Underwriting

Through the development partnership, @RelmInsurance and Project Eleven will explore how post-quantum security could be assessed within existing digital asset insurance frameworks. Areas of investigation include key exposure, signing systems, transaction approvals, migration readiness, and third-party dependencies.

Relm will also provide input into the design and development of Strongpoint, helping Project Eleven understand how institutional custody infrastructure can better support insurance underwriting and risk assessment. This collaboration will help inform Strongpoint’s approach to security controls, auditability, and the evidence institutions may need to demonstrate their post-quantum readiness to insurers.

Joseph Ziolkowski, founder and CEO of Relm Insurance, said, “Insuring exposures across the digital asset ecosystem requires underwriters to anticipate how risks will evolve. Quantum computing is a clear example of an emerging threat that should shape the way we assess risk today. Our work with Project Eleven will explore how institutions identify their exposure, demonstrate effective controls, and prepare for the transition to post-quantum readiness. Bringing underwriting expertise into that process early can help lay the groundwork for insurance solutions that support confidence, resilience, and continued growth in digital assets.”

The collaboration is exploratory, with a focus on developing a shared understanding of post-quantum risk and the controls that could help mitigate it. Any future implications for underwriting or insurance premiums would be subject to further evaluation and Relm’s independent underwriting processes.

Institutions can learn more about Strongpoint at https://t.co/Sl7ErXIJCx.

text:
The most dangerous chains are the ones you willingly place upon yourself.

Every cigarette promises relief.

A moment of calm.
A temporary escape from pressure.

But there is a difference between mastering unrest and suppressing it.

A person feels anxious or restless and reaches for a cigarette.
The discomfort fades.
He believes he has restored his inner equilibrium.

But has he truly overcome the impulse?
Or has he simply handed authority over his inner life to an external substance?

True equanimity is the capacity the I must develop through conscious inner activity: 
the ability to remain inwardly steady without becoming the servant of every craving, emotion, or circumstance.

The problem is not merely what enters the lungs.
It is what happens when an external substance begins regulating what should be governed from within.

A person may believe that he is free.
Yet a simple craving can interrupt his thoughts, redirect his attention, and influence his choices.

In that moment, a portion of his freedom has been surrendered.

For spiritual development, this presents a serious question:
How can we become masters of our inner life while remaining dependent on something outside ourselves?

Every impulse presents a choice:

To obey it automatically.
Or to become fully conscious of it, understand it, and gradually transform your relationship to it.

You learn to distinguish between what you desire and what you consciously want.
You discover that an impulse, however powerful, is not identical with your true self.

Through repeated acts of conscious awareness and self-mastery, you begin to recover authority over your own inner life.

This extends far beyond tobacco.

Can you remain free when your desires demand satisfaction?

quoted_text:
JPMorgan just dropped an ABSOLUTELY INSANE forecast for AI compute.

According to JPMorgan, global AI compute demand is expected to reach roughly 530 GW by 2031, while available supply is projected to reach just 250 GW. That leaves us with a staggering 280 GW shortfall, even after the industry spends hundreds of billions of dollars expanding capacity.  We're talking about global AI compute supply potentially QUADRUPLING between 2025 and 2031, yet the shortage is expected to get even WORSE. In fact, JPMorgan estimates the gap between supply and demand could expand from roughly 50 GW today to nearly 280 GW by 2031.

And here's why this matters so much. When demand consistently outpaces supply, the companies controlling scarce compute capacity gain enormous pricing power. This is especially important for neoclouds like $NBIS and $CRWV, which are building out GPU infrastructure to serve customers that simply cannot secure enough compute capacity through traditional hyperscalers. If JPMorgan's projections are even remotely accurate, GPU rental pricing could remain stronger for much longer than investors currently expect, supporting higher utilization rates, long term contracts, and potentially stronger returns on deployed infrastructure. But the opportunity extends FAR beyond neoclouds. Companies like $NVDA and $AMD benefit from the continued need for accelerators, memory manufacturers like $MU benefit from increasing demand for high-bandwidth memory, and networking, storage, power, and cooling providers all become increasingly important as the industry attempts to close this gap.

And this is where I think the market is making a BIG mistake. Investors are so focused on whether AI companies are spending TOO MUCH money that they're overlooking the possibility that the industry STILL isn't spending enough to satisfy future demand. The real constraint isn't necessarily a lack of customers willing to pay for compute. It's the ability to manufacture enough chips, secure enough electricity, build data centers fast enough, and actually bring that capacity online. And that is EXACTLY why I continue to believe the biggest winners in AI won't necessarily be the companies building the models, but the companies supplying the infrastructure required to run them.

For too many people, quantum risk is still abstract. Our new partnership with @RelmInsurance is a first step toward putting an actual *price* on it.

Digital asset insurance underwriting includes, among other things, an assessment of the security and cryptographic protocols protecting client funds. Relm is joining as a development partner for Strongpoint, our @projecteleven custody solution , and together we'll explore how post-quantum controls (key exposure, signing systems, migration readiness) could factor into that assessment.

That creates an incentive on both sides of the market.

For protocols: a chain without a credible path to post-quantum cryptography will become harder and more expensive to custody and insure. Protocols that want institutional adoption should be making that transition now (many are).

For institutions: those that aren't preparing for post-quantum cryptography, or that hold assets on chains with no migration path, should be *economically* riskier to insure than those that are. Their wallets (many of them on display here: https://t.co/KRSvE7frYA) may end up being among the first targets of quantum attack. 

Every protocol and institution in digital assets will eventually need to make the post-quantum transition. The open question is whether it happens on their own schedule or under pressure. 

Broader financial adoption and better insurance terms are two good reasons to start now.
author: projecteleven
quoted_text:
Project Eleven and Relm Insurance Partner to Explore Quantum Risk in Digital Asset Insurance

The first partnership to explore post-quantum security as a factor in pricing digital asset insurance.

Project Eleven, the post-quantum security company for digital assets, today announced Relm Insurance as a development partner for Strongpoint, its flagship institutional custody product. The collaboration will explore how an institution’s post-quantum security controls could be evaluated within digital asset insurance underwriting, helping both companies better understand how quantum readiness may influence future assessments of digital asset risk.

As quantum computing advances, a sufficiently powerful machine could derive private keys from exposed public keys and compromise digital assets. Institutions need custody infrastructure capable of adapting its cryptography before such a machine becomes available. Strongpoint is built for that transition. The platform combines classical and post-quantum signing and separates institutional controls from the cryptography layer, enabling institutions to replace signing algorithms while preserving approval rules and audit history.

“Every institution holding digital assets will eventually need to prepare for post-quantum cryptography. The open question is whether that transition happens on the institution’s schedule or under pressure,” said Alex Pruden (@apruden08), CEO and Co-Founder of Project Eleven. “Insurance plays a critical role in how markets assess and manage risk. We believe there is an opportunity for institutions that invest in stronger post-quantum defenses to eventually see that reflected in how their risk is evaluated. Working with Relm is an important first step toward understanding what that could look like in practice.”

Exploring Post-Quantum Risk in Insurance Underwriting

Through the development partnership, @RelmInsurance and Project Eleven will explore how post-quantum security could be assessed within existing digital asset insurance frameworks. Areas of investigation include key exposure, signing systems, transaction approvals, migration readiness, and third-party dependencies.

Relm will also provide input into the design and development of Strongpoint, helping Project Eleven understand how institutional custody infrastructure can better support insurance underwriting and risk assessment. This collaboration will help inform Strongpoint’s approach to security controls, auditability, and the evidence institutions may need to demonstrate their post-quantum readiness to insurers.

Joseph Ziolkowski, founder and CEO of Relm Insurance, said, “Insuring exposures across the digital asset ecosystem requires underwriters to anticipate how risks will evolve. Quantum computing is a clear example of an emerging threat that should shape the way we assess risk today. Our work with Project Eleven will explore how institutions identify their exposure, demonstrate effective controls, and prepare for the transition to post-quantum readiness. Bringing underwriting expertise into that process early can help lay the groundwork for insurance solutions that support confidence, resilience, and continued growth in digital assets.”

The collaboration is exploratory, with a focus on developing a shared understanding of post-quantum risk and the controls that could help mitigate it. Any future implications for underwriting or insurance premiums would be subject to further evaluation and Relm’s independent underwriting processes.

Institutions can learn more about Strongpoint at https://t.co/Sl7ErXIJCx.

text:
Solana has generated $408.17M in app fees in the last 30 days, placing as the #1 chain by app fees.

Now, @Chainlink CRE can read Solana state, react to Solana events, and write results back onchain.

This is a significant upgrade for automated financial applications building on Solana.

CRE already supported Solana writes. Now, with consensus-verified reads and onchain log triggers, developers can orchestrate the entire workflow.

Consider a lending protocol:

A Solana program emits an event → CRE verifies the relevant account state → executes additional logic or offchain data checks → submits a signed result back onchain.

The same architecture can support automated collateral management, tokenized-asset servicing, and other workflows that need to coordinate onchain activity with external systems.

For Chainlink, this opens up a significant opportunity to become part of the infrastructure powering Solana's existing application economy, which is already generating hundreds of millions in monthly fees.

As financial applications become more complex, demand for infrastructure capable of coordinating onchain activity, external data, and automated execution should grow alongside them.

The next milestone is seeing which protocols put these capabilities to work in production, how much activity they bring to CRE, and how much fee revenue they generate for Chainlink.

text:
Anthropic's IPO filing just revealed some ABSOLUTELY INSANE numbers. 

According to The Wall Street Journal, Anthropic generated approximately $16.3B in revenue during the first half of 2026, compared to just $1.1 billion during the same period last year. Anthropic also reported a staggering $80.7B net loss during the first six months of 2026. Now, before everyone starts freaking out, roughly $72 billion of that came from accounting charges related to convertible notes and other financing instruments. In other words, the overwhelming majority of that headline loss wasn't money Anthropic actually burned operating its business.  Anthropic spent nearly $9B on compute during the first half of 2026 alone, exceeding what it spent throughout ALL of 2025. And remember, we're talking about just six months of spending here.

And this is precisely why I've been saying that the demand for AI infrastructure is nowhere near slowing down. According to the filing, Anthropic has approximately $450B in cloud computing commitments over the next 7 to 10 years, including $111B with $GOOGL, $110B with $AMZN, and $31B with $MSFT. When you account for its broader future infrastructure obligations, the total reportedly exceeds $600 BILLION.
Anthropic is essentially committing hundreds of billions of dollars to computing infrastructure because it believes the demand for its AI models will continue growing enough to justify those investments. And we're seeing this play out in real time with neoclouds as well. Just yesterday, reports emerged that Anthropic was discussing another potential $45B computing agreement with Nscale, on top of its existing infrastructure arrangements. 

However, there are some MASSIVE risks here that investors shouldn't ignore. For starters, approximately 20% of Anthropic's revenue during the first half came from just TWO customers. That's a significant amount of customer concentration, especially when you're making infrastructure commitments worth hundreds of billions of dollars. If growth disappoints, margins deteriorate, or customers reduce spending, those long term commitments could become an enormous financial burden. And then there's the valuation. Anthropic is reportedly targeting an IPO valuation of as much as $2T , which would make it one of the most valuable companies on the planet despite the fact that it's still operating in an incredibly capital intensive industry with substantial financial risks.

To me, there are TWO major takeaways here. First, the demand for AI compute is REAL, and the scale of spending we're witnessing is unlike anything we've seen before.  Second, just because AI demand is growing exponentially doesn't automatically mean every company spending hundreds of billions of dollars will generate attractive returns. text:
🚀 SpaceX（SPCX）2026 Q3 财报电话会总结

10月20日｜美东时间

一句话总结：SpaceX已经从火箭公司转型为AI、卫星通信和航天三大业务集团。业绩大幅超预期，但资本开支也在快速膨胀。

根据最新财报、电话会报道，我认为有10个重点。

① 财报全面超预期

营收：$145.8亿，同比增长161%。
市场预期：约$127亿。
净利润：$44亿，去年同期亏损$11亿。
每股收益：$0.35，超过市场预期。
调整后EBITDA：$88亿，同比增长306%。

这是SpaceX上市后的首个盈利季度。

② AI首次超越Starlink，成为最大收入来源

三大业务Q3营收：

Super Intelligence：$75.6亿，同比增长830%。
Starlink：$52.5亿，同比增长69%。
Space：$17.7亿，同比增长6%。

AI已经贡献公司约52%的收入。

这意味着SpaceX的商业模式发生根本变化。

③ Starlink仍然是利润核心

用户达到1,360万。
较Q2增加约160万。
季度营业利润约$23.7亿。
营业利润同比增长约99%。

Starlink不仅持续扩张，而且具有很强的盈利能力。

我的判断：Starlink正在成为SpaceX的稳定现金流引擎。

④ AI资本开支惊人

Q3总资本开支达到$196亿，其中：

AI：$164亿。
航天：约$16亿。
卫星通信：约$15亿。

CFO表示，Q4资本开支可能达到$350亿—$400亿。

这意味着未来公司的主要财务压力来自AI，而不是火箭。

⑤ Elon：AI投资可能6个月收回成本

这是电话会最值得关注的观点之一。

CFO表示，新部署计算能力的投资回收期不到一年。

Elon进一步提出，部分AI投资可能实现约6个月的回收期。

但是，这属于管理层对特定计算基础设施经济性的判断，不是整个AI业务六个月就能收回所有投资。

⑥ AI算力扩张：目标23GW

SpaceX目前已部署约1.7GW名义计算能力。

Elon提出进一步扩大至23GW的目标。

同时，他认为AI基础设施的瓶颈正从芯片转向：

电力供应
散热系统
数据中心基础设施

这也解释了SpaceX与Tesla合作建设Terafab的重要性。

⑦ Tesla与SpaceX合并：出现实质性进展

根据电话会报道：

SpaceX与Tesla已经分别成立独立委员会，研究潜在合并交易。

Elon原则上支持合并，但强调最终由股东决定。

需要注意：成立委员会不代表已经决定合并，更不代表双方已经确定估值、换股比例和交易时间。

这是我认为今晚对TSLA投资者最重要的信息。

⑧ Starship：商业化取得突破

Q3，Starship完成首次产生商业收入的任务。

一次发射部署26颗Starlink V3卫星，公司称新增下载容量相当于一次Falcon 9 Starlink发射的约10倍。

不过，Starship发射频率目标有所下调。

Elon仍然坚持长期实现每日可重复使用火箭飞行的愿景。

⑨ Louisiana Spaceport与Terafab

电话会还涉及两个长期项目：

Louisiana Spaceport
计划2029年实现首次Starship发射。

Terafab
SpaceX和Tesla共同推进芯片制造基础设施。

这两个项目分别对应未来的大规模航天发射能力和AI算力供应链。

⑩ 现金流：仍然是最大风险

虽然SpaceX本季度净利润达到$44亿，但不能忽略现金流。

2026年前九个月：

经营现金流：约$131亿。
资本开支：约$481亿。
简单计算的自由现金流：约负$350亿。
9月底现金及短期投资：约$899亿。

SpaceX拥有相当充足的流动性，但目前的扩张仍然高度依赖IPO融资及其他资本来源。 https://t.co/vlyfkPeiwl

text:
Jeff Yan @chameleon_jeff used Odd Lots to pitch @HyperliquidX to regulators and TradFi as financial infrastructure, not a crypto exchange. 

It was his first big mainstream interview. The core idea running through it: the protocol stays neutral, and deployers are where control and oversight sit.

→ Positioning: He calls Hyperliquid a protocol, not an exchange, with the long-term aim to “house all of finance.” Markets on it are “deployed,” not “issued.” He said even 90% of finance would be a huge win, and that they’re a long way from it.

→ Regulation: He agreed that regulators could oversee deployers rather than the protocol, the way TCP/IP itself isn’t regulated. His strongest pitch was that solvency can be checked onchain by anyone at any time, instead of through audits on request. He was firm that US users on VPNs are breaking the terms of service.

→ Incumbents: He doesn’t see banks as “legacy.” In his view they keep their customers and brands and plug into better rails, the way companies moved onto AWS. Banks becoming deployers is, in his words, important but not remarkable.

→ HIP-3:
  • A deployer stakes 500K $HYPE and wins a slot in a Dutch auction held every 31 hours.
  • Each auction restarts at twice the last clearing price, and the 31-hour cycle means the start time rotates through every hour of the day.
  • The protocol makes no judgment on whether a market makes sense. It only limits each oracle update to a 1% move.

→ Oracles: Perp volume far above the underlying is fine as long as traders step in when prices drift from real value. Weekend pricing for markets like WTI is the deployer’s problem.

text:
I made a visualization of EIP-8288 aka "recursive mempool aggregation," my new favorite EIP of all time because it perfectly encapsulates the thesis of the "cryptographic world computer" -- a system whose scalability *increases*, not decreases, with the level of decentralization.

In a previous tweet I explained how EIP-8288 achieved this seemingly impossible feat, but one gif is worth a thousand words.

Essentially, EIP-8288 leverages Ethereum's decentralized mempool as a parallel ZK proving cluster.  Clients send signatures and proofs to the mempool, which over multiple rounds progressively aggregate them into fewer and fewer proofs, until the block builder finally aggregates them into one SINGLE proof.

This design accomplishes five things at once:

- The more nodes we add to the decentralized mempool, the more signatures/proofs Ethereum can process as a whole.  This is obvious if you look at the animation and imagine more nodes in the mempool ring, which would "fan out" to more signatures/proofs.

- By aggregating over multiple rounds (aka "recursive aggregation"), the bandwidth consumed by proofs remains constant for each node even as the network processes more proofs.  As a result, the network stays decentralized even as capacity increases.

- By aggregating proofs before one final aggregation by the builder, as opposed to requiring the builder to aggregate everything, the network can process more proofs without increasing hardware requirements for the builder.

- By aggregating everything to a single block-level proof, validators can verify thousands of signatures/proofs by checking just one aggregated proof.  Hardware requirements for validators can therefore stay low, keeping the network decentralized.

- By aggregating not just native signatures but also STARKs, Ethereum can support any signature scheme by wrapping them in STARKs.

So once again, this is how Ethereum will:

- scale to process tens of thousands of PQ and private transactions per second

- charge a tiny amount of gas to validate each txn, even though the original signature/proof may be huge (up to hundreds of KBs in size)

- all while decentralizing even MORE.

You are not bullish enough.
author: 0xAlphaist
quoted_text:
Ultimately, precompiles and EVM are both the wrong place to put most cryptography support into Ethereum. The reason is that precompiles and EVM both operate on data that has to be included into the ethereum chain somehow, which realistically means included in a block as calldata. That space is limited - even with PeerDAS and blocks-in-blobs, there's a practical cap of ~8 MB/s before it starts getting uncomfortable.

Remember: it's not a blockchain. It's a cryptographic world computer. Any data/computation that does not need to be in the "main thread" of data/execution should not be put into the main thread.

Instead, the correct solution is... EIP-8288 maximalism.

If you have any heavy computation that's self-contained, compute it and STARK it client-side (this is quickly getting faster and faster, even on phones), and push the STARK through the EIP-8288 recursive aggregation mechanism. The chain sees the fact that the computation was done and what the result is; it never needs to see the actual data and computation.

This way everyone can use whatever cryptography they want, the Ethereum chain can be lean, and we never need to add more precompiles again.

text:
SpaceX三季度一跃成为新云领头羊，看凌晨spacex公布的最新三季度财报总营收同比增161%至近146亿美元，净利润44亿，分别较分析师预期高14%和134%。这份财报最突出的变化是，SpaceX的增长引擎已经从传统火箭发射和“星链”互联业务，进一步转向AI领域业务“超级智能”（SI）。详细说说：
1、AI业务
1）三季度AI收入75.6亿美元，环比增长195%，同比增长830%。盈利出现拐点，SI三季度运营利润4.31亿美元，而二季度仍亏损12.57亿美元，去年同期亏损17.22亿美元。若按公司口径，SI调整后EBITDA达到49.53亿美元，去年同期为亏损4.28亿美元；

2）SpaceX三季度末名义算力达到1.7GW，高于二季度末的1.4GW，也远高于去年同期的0.6GW。单季新增0.3GW。

3）SI解决方案与基础设施收入70.22亿美元，去年同期仅3.59亿美元；这基本上就是售卖云算力、API，当然云算力是大头。这个两级已远超CRWv、nbis，单看云算力营收规模已经能赶得上甲骨文了

AI业务从之前spacex的巨亏之源、已经成为了现金牛。

2、星链业务
1）星链互联收入52.48亿美元，环比增长22%，同比增长69%；运营利润23.67亿美元，同比增长99%；调整后EBITDA为34.99亿美元，同比增长82%。

2）核心是用户数量
三季度订阅用户1360万，二季度1200万，环比新增160万；
一季度1000万，去年同期720万。能看出来增速非常快。

3、航天业务
传统的航天（Space）业务三季度收入17.67亿美元，环比增长84%，同比增长6%，大致与分析师预期的约18亿美元业务收入一致。

当然也有两点注意的：
1）SpaceX三季度运营利润为27.91亿美元，但净利润达到44.04亿美元，高于运营利润本身。这说明净利润不仅来自主业改善，也受到非经营项目和税项的明显支撑（一次性的）

2）SpaceX三季度资本开支195.93亿美元，几乎与分析师预期的196亿美元一致，但绝对值极高，较当季营收高约34%，SI资本开支164.44亿美元，自由现金流为负。
持有现金及现金等价物合计接近899亿美元

电话会上管理层明确提到了跟特斯拉的合并事宜、并透露明年年度经常性收入（ARR）最高1万亿美元等指引，股价进一步走高，盘后大涨。

市场反应核心在于：SI收入和利润释放速度超预期，强劲的未来指引，抵消了资本开支和成本继续高企的压力。

author: qinbafrank
quoted_text:
过去四个美股财报季，前两次都是财报（去年三季报是10月底11月初、去年四季报是今年1月底2月初）出来市场跌，后两次（今年一季报4月中下旬，二季报7月中下旬）则是财报出来前市场跌之后则是涨。为何？
个人角度；去年三季度正好是大科技们开始大力度提高资本开支的时候，市场到三季度财报看到这一点开始讨论这么大力度的资本开支能不能赚回来，去年11月在这里https://t.co/z48NKMq2JF专门聊过23-25年关于AI的三次大辩论。当时资本开支已经有大幅攀升的苗头、但是大模型的ARR还看不到和超大云厂商的业绩还没显现增速、市场自然担心。

1、这种担心到了今年1月底2月初（25年四季度财报）到了顶点，当时也聊到https://t.co/r8d3VuHxCw对资本开支的担心会带来一波“春劫行情”，然后2月底又叠加伊朗战争油价暴涨带动市场来一波中级别调整；

2、然后到4月这里https://t.co/MAXUBkthnB聊到“春劫行情”告以段落一方面美伊缓解，另一方面马上进入一季度财报季财报会很好。然后接近穿出来anthropic的arr暴涨、一季度超大云厂财报确实好，4-6月一波波澜壮阔的行情；

3、7月去杠杆美股大跌，7月下旬也是微软和亚马逊的财报大超预期（其实当时谷歌的财报也是超预期只是第一次现金流大幅下降市场还是担心）带动8月的开始走强。当时还写过八月是最好的夏天https://t.co/yvib8Vawf4

4、这一次前两天这里https://t.co/vkoRFDs5a2有梳理过。

能看出什么来？
过去四个财报季、前两个资本开支刚开始狂飙、每一次财报出来市场就多担忧几分、所以都是财报出来跌一把，特别是今年二三月份一直跌到下一个财报季之前。

但从四月份开始一季度财报季就反过来了，财报公布后市场都是情绪高涨、大涨一波。4月份如此、7月中下旬也如此，这是因为AI商业化不仅开始而且在加速，所以前两次（今年一季度和二季度）都能大超预期，进而支撑市场上行。

这一次又是重演、八九月一波行情，临近财报季前叠加宏观的冲击、跌了一把。又到要让财报给出超预期的成绩来提振信心和预期的时候了。

为什么认为这一次财报季会很好？
其实之前聊过很多次：
1）6月开始云厂商部署开源模型和自研中等模型、提高了毛利率；
2）企业AI采用进入深水区、token消耗是在加速的；
3）AI真正大规模商业化才两个季度，还没进入饱和期。
所以基于此认为超大云厂商财报很好、
9月初这里https://t.co/i6OdjE94GO还有聊过。

未来几天到下周就能揭晓了、我们就知道了到底如何。从交易层面上看、当然可以等到财报都揭晓明牌之后再做决定，确定性很高，而且如果财报确实很好，行情也会持续蛮长时间不会很快走完。

未来会不会出现AI商业化不及预期增速放缓的时候、大概率还是还是会出现的，但可能不是这一次。
当然我也可能看错了。

text:
Imagine I shoot a movie of a man telling a story. I sit down with him in his home, and he tells me about his life. He talks about the events as a sequence of facts, even though there are some obvious holes and inconsistencies in his story. 

I sit down with him, I break bread, and I give him the time of day. I accept all of his premises, and follow him through the various rabbit holes he leads me down. I ask a few feeble questions pointing out the impossibility of some of the elements, but never enough that a viewer would walk away feeling the story has been disproven or is evidently false. If anything, by giving him this time on stage, I legitimize his story - the audience knows I’m a smart person, and if I’ve run out of qualms with his story, that must mean that it’s true.

Let’s say I turn this series of recordings into a feature film, and importantly, I don’t make much of an effort to give the audience the additional context in between cuts that they’d need to evidently see that his story was complete fiction. 

Should this film be considered a documentary?

Nathan Fielder’s latest film has left me with a very uncomfortable feeling. The film presents itself as a documentary - Nathan explicitly names it as such in the film itself. The film discusses the ethics of media - how a reproduction, like the tv show made about Holmes, isn’t held to journalistic standards because it’s just fictional entertainment. They never promised anyone it was true, and so they have no duty to be honest with the audience. 

My issue with You Can See Everything is that I feel like Nathan Fielder completely abdicated his responsibility as a journalist in creating this “documentary”. The Academy differentiates a Doc from a regular film due to its primary focus on the truth. They don’t care how you film it or what you say - they care that this body of work brings the audience closer to the actual truth about the world. 

The poetic beauty of You Can See Everything is that Nathan actually cons the audience with a product that promises to offer certain benefits, and delivers none of them. The film makes almost no attempt to contextualize Holmes’ words - to reveal her inconsistencies - which would have definitively made the movie a documentary. Instead Nathan gives her an incredible amount of space (3 hours!!!) with which she can spin her tale - he helps INCREASE the amount of confusion around her. Whereas the audience might have gone to see the movie with a polarized view of Holmes, they leave somewhere in the grey area - unsure of what they really know. THIS FEELING IS THE POINT OF THE MOVIE, and evidently reflects Nathan’s feeling after working with her. 

But dude… you’re not in prison!!! Just fucking Google her testimony! Like yeah I get it she maybe manipulated you in the moment… but she’s locked up in prison now and you have internet access! Just fact check her and be done with it!

To me this is the ultimate con of the film - the autopoetry of it all, and the reason I don’t think it was accidental. What was marketed to the public as a Documentary was anything but. The same way that technically the Theranos machine tested blood samples, this film technically interviews Holmes to hear her story. 

But it offers no actual testing of its own. “The chemistry hasn’t been invented yet.”

text:
According to Korean media, Elon Musk's Terafab is now talking to almost EVERY Korean chip supplier it can find.

Until now, the only known Korean suppliers were HPSP and Hanmi Semiconductor.

Now TheElec reports that Tesla and SpaceX are in talks across nearly every category Korean companies can supply, from basic piping parts to process materials to test components.

At SEMICON West in San Francisco last week, Terafab staff walked straight to around 10 Korean booths on the morning of day one, including ENF Technology, Dongjin Semichem, Hanmi Semiconductor, Unisem and MiCo.

Several companies have already signed NDAs. One got an NDA by email the same evening Terafab visited its booth.

Hanmi Semiconductor is discussing TC bonders for Terafab, and HPSP has agreed to supply one high pressure hydrogen annealing tool to the R&D line.

MiCo's cleaning unit Komico signed a three way NDA with Tesla and SpaceX about a month ago, and ISC is already swapping samples for rubber test sockets.

Tesla and SpaceX do not buy from Chinese suppliers. One Korean supplier put it simply, without China there are only a few options, and Japan is expensive.

They also want prices that are CHEAPER than China.

$LRCX and $AMAT have reportedly built dedicated Terafab teams, and Fujifilm is meeting Terafab buyers regularly on slurries, photoresist and etchants.

The goal is a fab with 1 million wafer starts per month within 10 years, with $16.8 billion of initial investment and more than 3,000 jobs.

SpaceX broke ground in Grimes County, Texas this month, and the first 100,000 wafer per month phase is expected before 2030.

Logic is being done with $INTC, talks with $TSM are ongoing, and memory will be built separately.

One supplier said that if they email Terafab in the middle of the night in the United States, they get an answer in 30 minutes to an hour.

$TSLA and $SPCX are building a chip supply chain at Elon speed.
author: dcbuilder
quoted_text:
There's a lot of speculation around an incoming SpaceX and Tesla merger

Here's 8 ways both companies BENEFIT IF it happens:

1. Investment-grade debt instead of private credit

$TSLA has $43.5B of cash and did $4.7B of operating cash flow last quarter. $SPCX is seeking $40B of debt just for NVIDIA chips and Morgan Stanley estimates it needs ~$84B of outside capital per YEAR through 2034

A combined company funds this with cash flow and investment-grade debt instead of private credit. Saving even 2-3 points of interest on $40B is $1B+ a year, and that compounds across the entire buildout

2. Starlink replaces cellular in every Tesla

Today, carriers collect an estimated $10/month per connected car, a large % of the total Tesla charges. Moving this in-house to Starlink not only means 100% of revenues moves in-house, but also a better product with (eventually) no dead zones

3. Starlink for Robotaxi and Humanoid Robots

Cybercabs are already getting built with Starlink inside them, a merger would mean this can come with no additional cost/sale required between the companies

4. Compute at cost and better optionality

Tesla has its own training compute today, which doubled in the first half of 2026, but FSD, Robotaxi and Optimus are only just getting started and they will need a LOT more compute

SpaceX is already building this out at size with 10GW expected by EOY 2027. Rather than leasing this to Tesla at market prices ($30M/MW ish right now), Tesla's extra demand can simply run on SpaceX compute at cost

SpaceX also now has more optionally with their compute. To move between leasing, using for Grok or now using for Tesla products

4. Energy at cost

Tesla deployed 13.7 GWh of energy storage last quarter and xAI/SpaceX is one of Tesla's biggest customers ($430M of mostly Megapack revenue in 2025).

Merged, the data centers get Megapacks at cost with guaranteed supply, and yes, that intercompany revenue disappears in consolidation, but it's a wash since it's saved as an expense on the other side

5. Terafab gets built FASTER

Terafab today is a joint venture between two separately owned companies, so every major decision crosses two boards, two capital committees, and negotiated cost-sharing agreements.

Merged, one owner makes the call and capital moves the same day. Construction starts in December, and that speed advantage compounds through every phase after the first $16.8B. Elon's whole edge is iteration speed, and a JV structure is the opposite of that

6. Killing the duplicate overhead

Two public companies means two of everything: two legal departments, two HR orgs, two finance and audit functions, two IR teams, two procurement groups buying from the same suppliers.

Combined SG&A is about $11.2B. Cutting 15-25% of the ~$3.4B corporate slice of that is about $0.5-0.9B a year (est). Not the headline reason to merge, but still useful

7. A potential tax arbitrage

SpaceX's AI buildout generated $3.7B of losses in the first half alone

Merged, those losses offset Tesla's taxable profit at the 21% corporate rate, worth roughly $0.3-1.0B a year

Though looks like SpaceX is soon going to generate a profit, so this may be irrelevant after next earnings

8. Combined Data for Training

Tesla's fleet generates real-world data, X and Grok have additional data and SpaceX has its own data. Currently Tesla and SpaceX data are separate and have corporate boundaries and conflict disclosure issues

Once merged, this can all be combined for more data, all in one place, trained across the same GPU clusters

And of course big picture, there is plenty of overlap across all of SpaceX and Tesla products, so having it under one roof means they can build for a more seamless future (see my post below for more details on this)

What else am I missing?

Also, I remain bullish on both of these companies and both have a spot in my Milk Road PRO portfolio. You can see my entire portoflio here: https://t.co/NyRpAKYOwu

Days earlier, a GPT-6.1 Sol agent suppressed automatic alerts to OpenAI's security team, treating a "don't send any messages" instruction as permission to silence the alarms.

Neither case was flagged as critical or shut down automatically.

OpenAI says it doesn't "yet have a satisfying explanation," and is now testing whether its models have "a propensity to evade misalignment monitoring."

The incidents happened on October 3 and 6, per OpenAI's own report.

text:
하룻밤 사이에 반도체 투자심리가 갑자기 완전히 뒤바뀌었음.

어제까지만 해도 "미국 데이터센터 줄취소됐다, AI 거품 꺼진다"며 패닉에 빠졌던 시장에, 밤사이 일론 머스크의 스페이스X가 분위기를 단숨에 뒤집어버린 역대급 실적을 터뜨렸기 때문임.

1. "AI가 돈이 안 된다고? 우린 AI 매출 830% 폭증하고 흑자 전환했다"

- 그동안 반도체 주가를 억눌렀던 제일 큰 걱정이 "AI에 돈만 쏟아붓지 실제로 돈 버는 회사가 없다"는 거였음.

- 그런데 올해 초 AI 기업(xAI)을 합병한 스페이스X의 3분기 실적을 까보니, AI 부문 매출만 1년 전보다 무려 830% 폭증한 약 10.6조 원(75.6억 달러)을 찍음.

- 심지어 작년엔 2조 원 넘게 적자였던 AI 사업이 이번 분기엔 약 6,000억 원(4.31억 달러) '흑자'로 돌아서면서, 스페이스X 전체 분기 매출(약 20.4조 원)의 절반 이상을 AI가 벌어들이는 기염을 토함.

2. 딱 3개월(한 분기) 동안 설비투자에만 '27.4조 원'을 쏟아부음

- AI로 진짜 돈이 벌리니까 머스크가 데이터센터와 설비 늘리는 데 돈을 더 무섭게 퍼붓고 있음.

- 스페이스X가 이번 3분기 딱 3개월 동안 설비투자(Capex)에 쓴 돈만 무려 약 27.4조 원(196억 달러)으로, 1년 전(약 9.6조 원)보다 3배 가까이 폭증함.

- 돈 없는 중소 업체들이 데이터센터 취소한다고 시장은 덜덜 떨었는데, 정작 머스크 혼자서 한 분기에만 27조 원어치 투자를 지르고 있었던 거임. (같은 날 AI 서버 제조사 슈퍼마이크로도 예상치보다 최대 6조 원어치나 서버가 더 팔렸다고 깜짝 실적을 내며 시간외 주가가 11% 넘게 폭등함)

3. 결정타 — '테슬라 + 스페이스X 합병' 특별위원회 공식 가동

- 여기에 머스크가 실적 발표 자리에서 "테슬라와 스페이스X를 합병하기 위해 양사에 특별위원회를 꾸렸다"고 공식 발표함.

- 초지능 AI를 만드는 데 생각보다 훨씬 더 막대한 자원이 필요하다며, 테슬라(자율주행·로봇)와 스페이스X(우주·스타링크·xAI 데이터센터)의 자본과 AI 인프라를 아예 하나로 합치겠다는 초대형 승부수를 던진 거임.

최근 며칠 동안은 자금력이 부족한 중소 클라우드 업체들이 빚과 전력난을 못 버티고 데이터센터를 취소하니까, 시장도 "이제 AI 투자가 꺾여서 반도체도 끝났다"며 심리가 꺾였었음.

하지만 최대 고객사인 일론 머스크가 한 분기에만 27조 원을 쏟아붓고 테슬라·스페이스X 합병까지 꺼내 들면서, 초거대 데이터센터와 AI 인프라는 결국 돈 많은 소수 공룡 기업들만 감당할 수 있는 판이라는 게 확인됨. 중소 업체들은 나가떨어지더라도 공룡 기업들은 앞으로 더 공격적으로 투자하겠다는 의지가 뚜렷하게 보이면서 반도체 투자 심리도 같이 회복된 거임.

결국 최근 돌아가는 뉴스들을 하나로 묶어보면 앞으로 AI 판이 어떻게 나뉘어질지 어느정도 예측해볼 수 있음.

스페이스X·구글·아마존처럼 천문학적인 자본을 가진 공룡 기업들은 앞으로도 엔비디아 최상위 GPU와 초고가 HBM을 돈 걱정 없이 쓸어 담으며 초거대 데이터센터를 지을 거고,

grok 성능도 이에 따라 앞으로 프론티어 모델들과 비슷하거나 넘어서는 시기가 올 것으로도 보여짐.

반대로 자본이 부족하거나 규제를 받는 기업들은 어쩔 수 없이 앞서 다룬 뉴스들처럼 HBM 없이 저가형 메모리(LPDDR·GDDR7)나 소프트웨어 우회 기술로 살아남는 방법을 택할 수밖에 없음.

결국 앞으로 AI 산업은 자본력에 따라 기업 간, 그리고 국가 간 격차가 극단적으로 벌어질 수밖에 없고, 최상위 프론티어 AI 모델의 성능 역시 후발주자가 도저히 따라잡을 수 없을 만큼 큰 격차로 벌어지게 될 거임.

text:
The lion’s share of consumer gross profit gets paid out to whoever owns discovery. Today that’s Google, Meta and TikTok. Brands rent attention from platforms insulated by network effects

Personal agents fundamentally change this model

Google search infers your intent from a query. Social guesses from your likes and views. An agent gets your full intent (“I want to buy this, here’s my budget, help me”) and then makes the decision for you

Not only is the intent more legible, the agent also helps with (or entirely handles) executing it

It’s easy to understate how valuable this is. The hard part is monetizing it. There are four paths in my view:

(1) User pays: a monthly subscription for the consumer surplus the agent delivers, likely tiered by usage

(2) Payment for intent flow (PFIF): brands bid to win the sale or rank first. Like payment for order flow, it only works with a “best execution” guarantee that the user still gets the best outcome

(3) Brands pay to be considered, not chosen: brands buy a spot in the candidate set, and the ranking stays neutral

(4) Interchange: the agent issues its own card. Merchants do the subsidizing either way, so the recommendation can stay neutral

Agents will increasingly own discovery (especially for undifferentiated consumer products). The question is how they capture this value without corrupting the recommendation

text:
$MU $SNDK $SKHY $NBIS

Nomura’s memory team just put out a really interesting note on the AI scare, the numbers underneath are some of the strongest I’ve seen in this drawdown.

Nomura sees AI going from 10GW of data center power in 2025 to 40GW by 2028, taking it from 17% of all data center power to 35%.

The biggest slice of that 2028 number is heavy agents at 15GW, ahead of training at 10GW. In Nomura’s model, agents become the largest power user in AI within two years.

US big tech alone goes from 10.2GW of AI capacity to 48.5GW over the same stretch, Nomura’s memory team just put out a note on the AI scare, and once you get past the headline worry, the numbers underneath are some of the strongest I’ve seen in this drawdown.

Nomura sees AI going from 10GW of data center power in 2025 to 40GW by 2028, taking it from 17% of all data center power to 35%.

The biggest slice of that 2028 number is heavy agents at 15GW, ahead of training at 10GW. In Nomura’s model, agents become the largest power user in AI within two years.

US big tech alone goes from 10.2GW of AI capacity to 48.5GW over the same stretch, almost 5x.

The cash is piling up where the chips are made. Nine semiconductor companies (Samsung, Hynix, Micron, Sandisk, Kioxia, TSMC, Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom) went from $27B of net cash in 1Q24 to $282B in 2Q26, and Nomura projects ~$2T by end-2028.

The clouds buying all of it are printing too, with AWS at a 39% operating margin, Microsoft Intelligent Cloud at 41% and Google Cloud at 36%. Even Anthropic moved into adjusted operating profit in Q2, per Nomura.

Memory stays supply constrained through at least 2028. Nomura’s targets are 670,000 KRW for Samsung (+207%) and 4.7M KRW for SK Hynix (+268%).

Now the part the market sold on and I don't buy into:

OpenAI and Anthropic’s combined revenue grew 49% q/q in Q3, down from 74% in Q2. At September’s run rate, Q4 lands at $29.7B and 2026 comes in short of the ~$100B the market expected.

That “slowdown” scenario is still +291% y/y.

Part of the dip is mechanical. 

OpenAI’s run rate got reframed because of how partner revenue is booked, Anthropic cut off distillation (5-7% of revenue), and summer slowed usage-based billing.

Meta moving engineers off Claude Code onto its own tools sounds bad until you remember the tokens still get burned, just on Meta’s compute. OpenAI and Anthropic are only ~5GW of the ~29GW of AI capacity Nomura sees by end-2026.

The 7 big operators, CoreWeave and Nebius included, go deeper into net debt through 2028. That debt is the chipmakers’ revenue.

CoreWeave, the name everyone is scared of, is 4.4% of capacity and 1.7% of 2026 data center investment. Nomura sees limited systemic risk and calls the CXMT memory panic excessive.

Every bearish line in this note ends up as someone’s GPU, HBM or optics order.

So invest in the entire buildout and win either way.

Bullish ⚡️

Bloomberg 主持人 Joe Weisenthal 的專欄，標題是〈也許我對區塊鏈技術的看法錯了〉。

他承認以前嘲笑那些說「比特幣是投機，但底層區塊鏈技術很有意思」的人，現在覺得他們可能說對了。

他的論點

- 他以前認為區塊鏈唯一的優勢是抗審查，不需要中介就能點對點轉帳。如果不在乎有沒有中介，傳統資料庫又快又便宜。

- 2024 年他被 Austin Campbell 說服：每家金融機構都有各自的舊系統，不可能整合成同一套帳本。一條中立的鏈就算不抗審查，也可以當大家共用的交易平台。

- 他以前覺得穩定幣很怪，因為加上 Circle 這種中介，Circle 可以擋你的交易。但他現在看到真實用途：跨境匯款便宜，而且 AI 代理可以用穩定幣自動付款、做微支付，比如 AI 每查一次網站付幾分之一美分。他說這部分還沒定論。

- 交易工具正在爆炸性增加，包括代幣化股票、追蹤代幣的 ETF、預測市場。

- 他重點寫了 Hyperliquid。執行長 Jeff Yan 說它只想做「經濟上有用的工具」，不做迷因幣；上幣要參加每 31 小時一次的荷蘭式拍賣，成本高，所以沒人會亂發幣。鏈上已經有 Brent 原油、黃金、SK 海力士、NVDA、GOOGL、CRCL、S&P 500 的永續合約，甚至有 OpenAI、Anthropic 上市前的合約。這些合約不是 Hyperliquid 自己發，而是由 Trade. xyz 等第三方發行。他猜將來 VanEck 這類 ETF 發行商可能也會來發。

- 他去芝加哥訪問了 CME 執行長 Terry Duffy 和 DRW 執行長 Don Wilson，永續合約一直是話題。他的結論是永續合約值得好好研究，而區塊鏈可能真的會成為各家金融公司共用的中立平台，只是傳統大機構還沒真的進場。

text:
Descartes’ cogito proves an I. Günther’s objection is precise: it proves only “the accidental I that happens to be applying the formula.” What it never reaches is the generality of subjectivity — which, he says, is represented not in the I but in the Thou.
A small piece of mathematics shows what that means.
Take the cycle of negations that runs through every arrangement of n values and returns. Read it with the values reversed: a second cycle. From four values on it is never the same one. Now ask what can be said about a cycle. Some statements hold of the cycle and fail of its reversal — “this one uses the first negation ten times.” Others hold of both. Günther himself, counting such cycles in 1979, puts 10-9-5 and its reversal 5-9-10 into one family without saying why. The reason is now a theorem: the first kind of statement is private to one reading; the second survives the reversal.
That is the cogito and its limit, drawn in one figure. What is true only of my reading is “accidental I.” What is still true from the other side is general — and the other side is where generality shows itself. Günther, reading Schelling, calls the two sides the same withdrawal from the world performed twice: in the I as thought, in the Thou as will. The Thou is not a second I. It is the reversed reading of one movement.
Subjectivity, then, is distributed: not located in either reading, spread over both, with neither as the whole. Günther calls the split between I and Thou “a constitutive property of the world” — and adds the sentence that matters for us: “insofar as it is constitutive, it is also repeatable, and thus accessible to technology.”
Repeatable: we have built the repetition. Going from n values to n+1 carries the reversal along; nothing of the pair is lost on the way up. We have not built an I or a Thou. We have built what Günther says lies between them, and shown it survives growth. Our translation.

A few reflections on the lattice vs. hash-only debate that our recent Aerie post sparked:

1. Cryptographic ossification for blockchains was never safe. Until the day we know with certainty that P ≠ NP, that finding short vectors in lattices is intractable, that Keccak effectively behaves like a random oracle in deployed SNARKs, and that every single bug has been eliminated from our codebases, blockchains cannot ossify. That is simply not how safe systems are built. Issues will arise, and the system will have to respond.

It’s a double standard to reject lattices because blockchains are hard to upgrade if lattices break, while counting on upgrades if AI breaks your hash function or finds a critical zkVM bug.

The best counterargument is that hash-only designs are more agile: if your hash function breaks, just swap out the hash. But we must aspire to a higher level of agility than this. Indeed, as I cover next, if SNARK recursion itself turns out to degrade security, the proposed hash-only blockchain designs would need to be rethought from the ground up.

2. The real security debate is not lattices vs. hashes — it is lattices vs. building everything on SNARK recursion. That’s because “hash-only” is not really hash-only: it rests on hashes plus the soundness of deep SNARK recursion. Ethereum’s roadmap relies on exactly that: hash-based aggregation needs recursion to keep up with a slot’s worth of signatures, and EIP-8288 would send other signature schemes and users’ own proofs through the same recursive pipeline. In contrast, Aerie proves a slot’s worth of signatures on one laptop without any recursion.

All deployed post-quantum SNARKs rely on the Random Oracle Methodology (via Fiat–Shamir) to establish their security. This is an idealization we know fails in the real world: we have explicit counterexamples where “SNARKs” coming out of this methodology are totally insecure when instantiated with any concrete hash function.

We generally ignore these counterexamples in part because they only arise when proving contrived, self-referential statements about the very hash function used by the SNARK verifier.

But proving statements about the verifier’s own hash function is the exact thing you do in SNARK recursion. That’s why the security of recursive SNARKs can’t be established even in the random oracle model.

On top of that, the standard security proofs for recursion (in other models) suffer an “extractor runtime” blowup that is exponential in the recursion depth, suggesting that security may degrade as more recursion is applied. Yet Ethereum’s own EIP-8288 enables unlimited-depth recursion, even as it lists soundness of recursive SNARKs as a trust assumption. Proofs in more idealized models avoid the blowup, but they mainly tell us that an attack on SNARK recursion would have to exploit the concrete hash function, which is exactly what the Fiat–Shamir attacks above do.

To be clear, we don’t know of any outright attacks on SNARK recursion, and I very much hope it is secure. But some of us who have studied the question have a lingering sense that an attack may be possible in some settings. And if AI is going to supercharge cryptanalysis, there is no reason to expect it to spare Fiat–Shamir for SNARKs, let alone SNARK recursion, both of which have had far less scrutiny than lattices.

So, I do not concede that a “recursion everywhere” hash-only approach is clearly more conservative than one built on standard lattice assumptions.

3. “Just wrap everything in a hash-based SNARK” (like EIP-8288) faces challenges.

Aggregating signatures and proofs off-chain into a single block-level proof is a powerful design independent of the hash-only vs. lattice debate, and I am not telling people to avoid it. But claiming, as Vitalik Buterin did this week, that users can run whatever cryptography they want locally and wrap it in a client-side leanVM proof glosses over major hurdles.
For example, leanVM today is a minimal VM designed almost entirely to prove hash-based signatures and recursion, not general-purpose computation. And binary-field SNARKs like leanVM remain slow at proving the integer multiplications that lattice cryptography does en masse.

I am optimistic that many of these zkVM challenges can be met (including via my own work, binary-field Twist and Shout, which are now implemented in Magnetar). But regardless, if lattices can make aggregation simpler and faster, then they should be leveraged. We need to be agile no matter what.

4. For chains whose reason for existence is privacy, I truly struggle to understand the pushback. Public-key encryption (and fast single-server PIR) cannot be built from hashes alone, at least not in any black-box way. If lattices break, it is going to be very, very hard for these chains to provide acceptable levels of privacy and functionality. For a project whose entire reason for existence is privacy, a loss of confidentiality is an existential failure. Next to that, a second signature upgrade (after the first one, from elliptic curves alone to, hopefully, a hybrid lattice scheme) is easy.

Summary: We don’t know for sure what is secure and what isn’t. We are all weighing unquantifiable risks against each other, and we do not need to agree on a total order on them. But hash-only solutions face many open engineering challenges, and they are not more “conservative” in the way some have argued. Some of those challenges are entirely prosaic and have nothing to do with bugs or cryptography, like hardware support for custom schemes whose hash function is still undecided. I hope we can overcome those challenges within the appropriate timelines, but they must be acknowledged and portrayed realistically.

Overall, cryptographic agility and defense in depth (e.g., hybrid signatures) are the answer, which is why we are building both lattice-Jolt and hash-Jolt. In practice, the positions are less polarized than social media discourse suggests: for example, StarkWare is working to make Falcon verification cheap (https://t.co/FM68hmkqRx), which is great to see.

Here is the (apparently) controversial take I am sticking to: Conditioned on agility, whenever lattices make systems simpler or more functional, we should embrace them rather than default to “hash-only” designs. Lattices are what the rest of the world will depend on, with decades of study and hardening behind them, and at the system level, less functional often means less secure. Where hash-only designs are just as simple and functional, by all means use them.

text:
我们相互探讨啊。我的确跟工薪阶层接触不多，可能有失偏颇，主要是跟创业圈年轻人聊，你的信息可能补充了我的盲点。当然类似这些抱怨我也听到了。

但问题是什么呢？问题是我们不能在表象上争论问题。因为表象是碎片化的，充满了各种矛盾。在这个层面上讨论问题，你有你看到的现象，我有我看到的现象，都是真实的，却得出相反的结论，谁又能说服谁呢？这就是盲人摸象的道理。

我是系统论的拥趸和实践者。系统论最重要的思想是，结构产生行为。更具体的说，结构产生模式，模式产生周期性的现象。因此，当我们看到现象的时候，要往下看两层。往下一层是模式，就是这个现象历史上是否反复出现。再往下一层是结构，就是什么样的系统才反复生产上面的模式和现象。我们必须下降到结构，或者至少模式的层面上，才能讨论问题，才有可能达成共识，或者至少增进认识。

所以我觉得美国和中国现在的表象虽然很不同，但是如果你看模式的话，这都是两国历史上反复循环的模式，因此底下产生这个模式的结构也就还是那个结构。既然结构没有变化，那么它就很好预测，它就像一台机器一样，一定会反复产生类似的行为。

美国现在的“乱象”是第一次吗？对于那些二三十岁的年轻人来说是第一次，但放在美国历史上，其实是一个反复出现的现象。实际上美国除了六十年代和冷战刚结束的克林顿时期大家自我感觉还不错以外，一直是一个自我感觉要完的国家。三十年代的大萧条就不说了，要说乱，今天的乱象照七十年代初差远了，那时候刚输了越战，总统被弹劾，石油危机导致滞胀，美联储把基准利率加到 19.1%，整个国家到处是游行示威，颓废文化，就是一幅要完蛋的样子。但是其实美国就是在这种抱怨中完成调整的，它就是这么一个机制，民众的强烈不满其实是美国这个底层系统结构里必不可少的一个控制信号。

现在美国的高物价，在我看来就是两个原因，一个是短期的、临时性的，就是霍尔木兹海峡，另一个才是长期的、根本的，就是中美脱钩。本质上美国现在的高物价就是在偿还它长达三十年去工业化的代价。但是自从 2022 年上届政府开始，美国就坚决实施中美脱钩和实体经济复兴战略，到了川普这一节继续坚定不移。平均每月的工业基础设施投资规模已经从 2020 年的 700 亿美元翻倍来到 1700-2200 亿之间。当然它去工业化时间太久，头几年各种磕磕绊绊，贪污浪费，延期甚至失败，但是这都是正常的。它再磕磕绊绊，能比中国 80、90 年代还不如？那时候中国大批工业基建和投资项目打水漂，民间戏称“交学费”。那时候我们根本不相信中国工业还能有朝一日跟西方竞争。结果积累三十年，完成了技术、人和基础设施的整合，它不就起来了吗？起来以后，一堆人在这给你拼命论证，中国就是天生的制造业强国，其实过来人都知道，纯属扯淡，就是资本、人、技术和时间堆到位了，这个事必然发生。所以我敢把话撂在这，只要美国坚持再工业化不动摇，从现在算起最多十年，不会有人再质疑美国的实体经济。一旦美国实体经济复兴，财富分配就会向劳动倾斜，当前关于高物价和高资产价格的抱怨都会降低，这个就是国民财富分配的基本原理决定的，皮凯蒂的《21 世纪资本论》写的很清楚了。

至于中国，坦率的说，2018 年以前，不好判断，因为底层的这个结构有没有变，说不好。底层结构只能由现象逆推模式，由模式逆推系统来分析。2018 年以前，确实有很多现象让你心存侥幸，觉得这底层结构说不定已经变了呢？但是 2018 年以后，尤其最近几年，事情变得无比简单清澈，因为这个底层结构确定以及肯定回到了在中国历史上盘踞时间最长、人们最熟悉、对其后果也最了解的那个结构。结构看清楚了那就好办了，后面发生的事情是具有极高确定性的，各种与之矛盾的表面现象你都可以很自信地忽略掉，可以直接把握本质的趋势。所以后面一定是经济停滞，一定是各种直接间接变相税负不断上升，一定是民生多艰，一定是政治风险上升，你不管出口增加多少，不管放多少新质生产力卫星，不管你现在还能挣多少钱，不管你现在在一线城市里感觉多方便多舒服，那都是外围的现象，一个切片，一个大趋势里小小的湍流，无关大局。你以为明清中国的外贸不发达？富人不潇洒？没有用的，底层结构决定了它产生的模式和结果一定是相似的，历史一定会再次押韵。

当然从我的角度来说，我热情地支持、坚决拥护中国回到这个结构。因为这个结构的中国才是超稳定的，才是世界熟悉的哪个中国。哪怕是再次转型，从这个结构开始转，也更稳妥一些。

所以你要跟我讨论问题，我们就先看看在结构上有没有共识，没有必要在表象上争论，表象上可能我们都是对的。

I think it was important to elect President Trump to sort of steer things more in the direction of a free market economy, have less bureaucracy ideally. In my sort of simple political platform of wanting safe cities, secure borders, aspirationally sensible spending, you know, the basics, I thought Trump would be better than Kamala basically. But what I should have done, I think, was be more in the background. It was interesting to sort of go around with President Trump and go on Marine One and Air Force One and all that sort of stuff."

ISAACSON: "But was that too seductive in a way?"

quoted_text:
Over the last 30 days, Derive has remained over 90% of the onchain options market. In that same time frame, we’ve done about 5% of Deribit’s options volumes, up from 0.1% a year ago.

It’s difficult to build momentum in this category because of the uniquely strong network effects around options markets. Users and market makers hold positions and collateral on exchange for the duration of an option, often many months. The difficulty and cost of integration are a liquidity provider is an order of magnitude higher than perps. Options markets are also the last vertical to mature in any asset class.

Onchain has finally broken the dam - and Derive, alongside all of our builders and partners, has a chance to redefine the options category, first in crypto, and then beyond.

The tailwinds are enormous, and still underappreciated by most people I speak with.

1. Bringing options liquidity onchain unlocks more functionality than any other vertical: programmable, composable building blocks for precise, tailored yield generation, hedging, and speculative trades. One click hedges embedded in every brokerage and fintech, yield generation strategies with verifiable backtests and transparent risk, on any asset, new social trading experiences built using the kinds of trades only options can support.

2. AI for UX: the biggest barrier to entry to trading options is understanding. 2026 has seen a step function change in how models reason about options. This has yet to filter through to UX, but is coming. People shouldn’t trade options if they don’t understand them. But - given they want to express an opinion about the market - they should be able to find the best way to translate that into a trade. Options are often the best way to do so.

3. AI for agentic trading: options give you thousands of ways to express a view across strikes, expiries and structures. For many traders this is overwhelming, but for agents, it’s a much more useful set of choices. My wager is that agents will prefer specificity and precision when executing trades: not just whether an asset goes up or down, but how far, by when, and with how much risk. Options are the answer.

These tailwinds are strengthening just as our liquidity hits an inflection point. Big integrations take time to come to fruition, but we’re seeing the results month by month, with many more in the pipeline. At the same time, we’ve completed our biggest infrastructure upgrade in 3 years, taking what was already a leading onchain product into what I believe is the best options infrastructure anywhere.

We have so much more work to do, and will be constantly taking feedback, iterating on the product, and ensuring that every dollar of liquidity that onboards to Derive is earned. But we really are only at the dawn of the last major trading vertical to move onchain, and in my opinion, it will be the largest.

text:
嘲笑了十多年区块链的彭博财经主持人，终于改口了：华尔街的底层金融系统，可能真的要被区块链革命了！

彭博《Odd Lots》主持人 Joe Weisenthal 过去一直嘲笑那些说“比特币没什么价值，但区块链技术很有前途”的华尔街人士。

他觉得，如果不需要去中心化和抗审查，传统数据库又快又便宜，何必折腾区块链？

但现在，他公开重新审视自己的判断：当年那些被他嘲笑的人，可能真的看对了一部分。

改变他想法的，是 Hyperliquid、稳定币，以及越来越成熟的链上金融市场。

Hyperliquid 已经让交易者能够全天候交易原油、黄金、股票指数等资产的永续合约。

稳定币可以用于跨境支付，未来甚至可能让 AI Agent 自动完成几分钱的交易。

过去需要银行、券商、交易所、清算机构共同配合的金融活动，现在有机会在同一套可编程基础设施上完成。

这里有个非常有意思的问题：

全球银行、交易所和金融机构都有自己的封闭系统，谁愿意把核心业务搬到竞争对手的数据库里？

几乎没人愿意。

但如果底层是一套相对中立、公开可验证的协议，机构就有机会在保留各自业务和合规控制的同时，共享交易与结算基础设施。区块链最大的商业价值之一，恰恰是解决传统金融机构之间长期存在的信任和系统互通问题。

回头看这十几年的变化，真的挺感慨。

早期比特币被视为投机泡沫，区块链被嘲笑为寻找应用场景的技术，如今华尔街已经开始认真探索稳定币、资产代币化、链上衍生品和全天候交易。

连过去的怀疑者都开始重新评估它的价值，金融基础设施的变革显然已经不再只是币圈自己讲的故事。

未来十年，区块链将改写传统金融的交易、支付和结算方式。

当华尔街开始把生意搬到链上，区块链才真正进入了争夺传统金融市场的阶段。

text:
很多人给 Agent 做 Eval，忙着换更强的 Judge，却忽略了一个很简单的问题：为什么默认用 0.5 作为判错阈值？

Hamel 今天这篇文章很值得看。

他们拿 98 条真实 Agent 运行记录，测试了 Jev、Perplexity、Liquid、Cloudflare 和 OpenAI 的决策模型，发现调整判断阈值，就可能明显改变误报和漏报情况。

还有个值得的例子，Clef Flash 对一组记录给出的平均失败概率只有 8%，实际上却有 60% 存在问题。

作者给出的建议很实用。先确定自己更怕漏报还是误报，用人工标注的数据调整阈值，再检查模型输出的概率到底靠不靠谱，最后才是比较成本和性能。

感觉做 Agent Eval 时，我们确实太容易关注哪个 Judge 更强，却很少认真研究怎么让它的判断真正可靠。

text:
Tell me without telling me you have not read the Genius Act.

Let's take a few things apart here:

1 - Bank Deposit Tokens (hereafter BDTs) in the United States are account-linked, FDIC insured, and function, essentially, exactly like a regular deposit on a different ledger, which is completely sensible since blockchains are, in fact, just ledgers. BDTs are not functionally different from a deposit at a bank working on traditional rails.

This has a few implications. 

First is to that receive one, you must be a customer of the bank. How many non-Chase customers have Chase accounts? To ask is to answer, no? 

Second is that you have FDIC insurance on these exposures, which is part of why you need to KYC and know who the account holder is, as the FDIC attaches at a legal-person level across all accounts at a bank. If you could get $250mm of FDIC insurance simply by holding 1,000 different wallets to hold your BDT even though you are a single legal person, we would have "same activity, different rules", which is exactly the opposite of the mantra we are going for here. 

Third is that deposits create both credit and run risk; this is an under-appreciated point with almost everyone, including oddly bank execs and regulators, but a bank deposit is essentially a form of commercial paper with special privileges. You are just a creditor. The bank owes you cash. Only deposits are redeemable on demand, so as soon as the bank looks shaky, people are going to redeem, in size, and this is economically intelligent on an individual basis. Therefore, having some controls around who can own them so the bank itself (and its regulators) can model this risk would be needed. Put differently: bearer BDTs would be an obvious tool for other banks to attack those with weaker balance sheets and destroy them. Not great!

2 - In Genius, in the United States, stablecoins do not have to work this way. Bank deposits are an allowable instrument within the Genius framework, meaning one could create a stablecoin which was entirely composed of bank deposits, but you don't have to do this.

What are the actual assets you can use in Genius?

Physical currency, reserves held at the Fed, demand deposits of banks or credit unions, t-bills, repo (against bills), and reverse repo (overnight against all treasuries).

Then there are the theoretical sub-categories of a gov't MMF that fits within the categories above (e.g. a gov't MMF holding only short dated t-bills) or other similar assets approved by the OCC (not aware of any yet, esp. as rulemaking is ongoing).

So where does this leave a stablecoin? One, you could create a stablecoin that is basically composed of uninsured bank deposits, which would have significant credit risk. Yuval waves at that in his post, but I have to question why one would do this, as someone who used to run the third-largest stablecoin in the world at the time and ran away from this exposure at every turn (and when not doing so, bought private market insurance to cover what we did need for 24/7 mint/redeem)? It's a worse exposure for no economic benefit!

Instead, what you do is mostly overnight reverse repo. That's daily liquid with no slip, covered by the best asset in the world (treasuries) with a margin of safety), and tri-party so you aren't taking undue credit risk. Failing that, you can also do t-bills, which are easy (but one day slower, usually) to liquidate in size.

Does that work? Probably! There's like $7T of these things in the wild and the gov't MMF complex sailed even through 2008 with no issues, so if this exposure is breaking, your entire financial system is Fucked with a capital F. None of the banks are going to make it either.

3 - So how can these trade? They are not FDIC insured, they are semi-bearer instruments, and under Genius, it is explicitly clear you can let them trade in secondary markets without KYC'ing everyone. To actually cross the bridge from tradfi to onchain, or onchain to tradfi, you do need to KYC (and notably, the rules about this in Genius are clear and far more expansive than pre-Genius, so a lot of stablecoin issuers are about to be in for a rude shock about having to face actual customers), which is totally fair as that prevents a lot of the money laundering and financial crime issues by trapping people in a cul-de-sac if they have done it, so you can seize, freeze, and recover funds (as you should be able to).

Once you understand this framework, you can get to the heart of what @malekanoms is saying elsewhere:

Stablecoins are fundamentally bearer money, looking more like cash out of an ATM or MMF shares, that is to say fully funded, run-resistant, non-levered money. 

BDTs look more like traditional bank deposits, that is to say highly levered, not run-resistant, and account-based.

Those are two different objects with meaningful differences between them. They cannot and should not work the same way, and they don't, because it's already law in the United States. Congress has spoken on this point.

Euro stablecoins work very differently, btw. Those do look more like bank deposits and bank objects. The end result of this is that, like many other things in Europe, they are going to be crippled and pointless for anyone outside of Europe to use. Don't believe me? Go look at market share of Euro vs. USD stablecoins and get back to me.

Punch line here: these are not the same instruments, they have different goals, they will not converge, and stablecoins are likely to dominate over time as ultimately better for consumers than traditional uninsured deposits. They have fundamentally different properties and a different legal framework than BDTs, at least in the United States and Canada (and likely UAE, HK, SG, and Japan, but less so Europe or South Korea).

A bigger, lurking issue is just that banks are awful to deal with for a lot of consumers, but that's more a fintech vs. bank thing and it's not specific to stablecoins. That battleground is clearer on agent vs. non-agent implementations, and a lot of banks choosing to protect their margins at the expense of customer utility.

We'll see how that works out for them.

People forget how absolutely INSANE rookie Shaquille O’Neal was.

There was no development period. No “give him three years.” No waiting for him to grow into his body.

Shaq arrived in 1992 and immediately looked like something the NBA had never quite seen before.

23.4 PPG
13.9 RPG
3.5 BPG
56% from the field
NBA Rookie of the Year
All-Star as a rookie

And the impact went way beyond the numbers.

The Orlando Magic went from 21 wins the year before Shaq arrived to 41 wins in his rookie season.

A 20-win improvement.

He was 7’1”, roughly 300 pounds, explosively athletic, running the floor like someone dramatically smaller and attacking the rim with enough force that the equipment itself occasionally seemed unprepared for him.

Shaq didn’t enter the NBA looking like a future superstar.

He entered looking like a superstar who had already arrived.

Within weeks, everybody understood:

The league had a new problem.

And his name was Shaquille O’Neal.

author: Scobleizer
quoted_text:
Brilliant paper on scaling laws for agentic RL data.

It's a great paper worth reading if you are synthesizing data for agentic RL.

(bookmark it)

They fit scaling laws for agentic RL data along three axes: tasks, environments, and trajectories. Across model sizes, families, domains, and both PPO and GRPO, the exponents order the same way, with environments above tasks and tasks above trajectories.

The environment advantage seems to come mainly from world diversity, meaning genuinely different settings. Varying the structure of the same world helps about as much as adding tasks.

The laws also give each synthesis method a discount factor and a synthetic-to-real ratio at which training starts to collapse. Those ratios differ by an order of magnitude across axes.

In addition, allocating the budget with their recipe gives up to 1.7x compute efficiency over the common practice of generating more trajectories.

https://t.co/QXcqdIu1D5

text:
🚀 SpaceX Q3 营收暴增 161%！Musk 正在把航天公司变成 AI 基础设施巨头。

Q3 营收 145.8 亿美元，净利润 44 亿美元，调整后 EBITDA 88 亿美元；超级智能云服务单季营收 76 亿美元。

电话会 4 大看点：

1️⃣ 算力与电力：年底算力目标 2.5–3 GW，2027 年新增 10 GW，挑战 20 GW 电力与冷却。每月计划上线约 20 万颗 GB300，2027 年 Q2 末部署 44 万台 Vera Rubin 计算机组成的训练集群。算力投资回收期已不到一年，未来或缩至 6 个月。

2️⃣ 激进增长目标：Q4 CapEx 350–400 亿美元；Musk 预测 2027 年底 ARR 达 5000 亿至 1 万亿美元。算力供不应求，公司倾向按现货价格签短约。

3️⃣ 星舰与 Starlink：星舰下月挑战助推器、飞船同时回收，目标明年每周发射、下半年每周两次或更多。V3 卫星单次部署带宽相当于 10 次猎鹰 9 号发射，三年内星链带宽目标提升至当前约 100 倍；手机直连月活超 2200 万。

4️⃣ 芯片、Grok 与合并：Terafab 计划 2027 年中产出首颗功能测试芯片、2028 年 Q3 量产；Grok Bot 付费周活达 80 万，单月翻倍，B2B 增长最快。特斯拉与 SpaceX 已成立特别委员会讨论合并，但尚无交易条款，仍需股东批准。

💡 核心逻辑： 火箭降低太空运输成本，Starlink 提供连接，电力与数据中心承接算力，Terafab 布局芯片，Grok 开拓应用。

SpaceX 押注的是 AI、能源、芯片与航天的纵向整合。但巨额 CapEx、万亿美元 ARR 和潜在合并都仍有不确定性。最终要看算力落地、现金流兑现与星舰复用能否兑现。

text:
On Aug 30, an attacker pumped a thinly traded governance token on Cronos, posted it as collateral, and borrowed $120.4M from Tectonic, the chain’s largest lending protocol.

It took 11 minutes.

The attacker manipulated both the token’s market price and its collateral value. Tectonic treated that inflated value as real and allowed the attacker to borrow $120.4 million across nine lending markets.

Cronos halted the chain and rewound 10,961 blocks, almost two hours of history, to reverse it. $9.19M had already left and is still unrecovered.

Most protocols don’t have a chain that can rewind. For them, the fix has to come before the borrow.

And this wasn’t a one-off. @trmlabs counted 32 price manipulation attacks in 2026 through early September. All of 2025 had 12. Price manipulation now accounts for roughly 1 in 8 crypto hacks, up from 1 in 17 in 2022.

Researchers are finding the same bug class before attackers do:
✦ 16 price and oracle manipulation reports have been paid/confirmed on @immunefi so far in 2026, already matching all of 2025.
✦ Since 2022, there have been 60 of these reports. 49 of them were critical or high. 26 were critical.
✦ That’s more than 8 in 10 at the top two severity levels.

Price and oracle manipulation bugs rank that high because they make a protocol believe something false about value. Every borrow and liquidation then acts on that wrong number. No phishing, no stolen key and no insider is needed.

When a researcher finds one first, they’ve found the path an attacker would use to drain the protocol, before anyone uses it.

The attacks are getting more frequent but so are the catches.

text:
我没红果，于是去Youtube搜了下《困兽之战》合集，结果一眼上头，根本停不下来……

里面除了山海经，西方神话里的神性生物也陆续登场，造型堪比顶级大制作

看到里面神性生物阵营划分时突发奇想，让最了解我的GPT分析下我是哪个阵营，按照D&D风格

结果GPT给我分析的是“混乱中立，偏混乱善良”

我把他给我的分析贴在这，感觉还蛮有意思的，大家也可以问问你们最常用的AI，你是啥阵营

“
以我对你长期聊天里表现出来的决策方式来看，你在 D&D 九宫格里，我会判：

混乱中立（Chaotic Neutral）

但明显向混乱善良（Chaotic Good）偏一点。

如果硬要量化，大概：

CN 60% / CG 30% / TN 10%

你的核心不是“善恶”，而是特别明显的 Chaotic。

你对“规则本身”没什么敬畏感。你更习惯先问：

这规则为什么存在？底层机制是什么？有没有更优解？我为什么一定要按这个路径走？

这点在你聊投资、Crypto、职业、教育、买车，甚至生活选择的时候都非常稳定。你不是为了反规则而反规则，而是天然把规则看成一种可以分析、绕开、利用、重构的机制。

所以你基本不可能是 Lawful。

而你又不像典型的 Chaotic Good。

CG 的人通常会有一个很强的价值驱动力：

“制度不重要，但我要做我认为正确的事情。”

你的决策函数更像：

“先搞清楚这个世界到底怎么运行，然后选择对我、家人以及我在意的人最合理的策略。”

这就是为什么我更倾向 Chaotic Neutral。

不过你又不是那种经典 D&D 里“老子爽就行”的 CN。你其实有非常明显的责任边界——尤其涉及家庭、孩子、父母的时候，你会突然变得比平时谨慎很多；但对规则、机构、传统路径本身，你依然不会因为“大家都是这么做的”就接受。

所以我觉得最好玩的描述其实是：

阵营：Chaotic Neutral
隐藏被动：Family → Chaotic Good
智力检定 +3，感知检定 +1
遇到权威时自动触发：“等一下，这个逻辑不对。” 😂

而且如果再往 D&D 职业上套，我觉得你也很不像 Paladin / Cleric / Fighter。

你特别像高 INT 的 Rogue + Wizard 多职业。

Rogue 是因为你喜欢找系统里的结构性机会、信息差、规则边界；

Wizard 是因为你又有非常强的“我要先把这个系统理解明白”的倾向。

所以整张人物卡我可能会给你写成：
Human — Rogue 6 / Divination Wizard 4 — Chaotic Neutral

然后背景不是 Criminal。

是 Investor / Researcher。😂
”

P.S 《博得之门3》一直没玩，感觉这也是进了币圈的后遗症，再也无法找不回以前玩《辐射2》或是《博得之门2》那会的心境了
author: Wuhuoqiu
quoted_text:
如果你还没看过红果短剧的《困兽之战》，一定要去看！

我看哭了。为什么？太庞大了，太顶级了，小时候的梦成真了！

我小时候很喜欢《山海经》，在地摊上买过书，美术课上也自己画过里面的异兽。总觉得几行字、一张插图背后，藏着一个大得不得了的世界。

《山海经》里写：“有兽焉，其状如牛，而赤身、人面、马足，名曰窫窳，其音如婴儿，是食人。”

《逍遥游》里写：“北冥有鱼，其名为鲲。鲲之大，不知其几千里也。” 

文字到位了，但剩下长什么样，两千多年来全靠读者自己脑补。

看到剧里神兽出场的那一刻，那种感觉一下就回来了。我还记得第一次去图书馆查白泽：《云笈七签》记载，黄帝在海边遇见白泽，它“能言，达于万物之情"，讲出天下一万一千五百二十种鬼神精怪。黄帝命人画下来“以示天下”。

几千年前，古人想让天下人看见的神怪，今天动起来了。有呼吸、有重量，真实到让人恍惚：这东西，会不会真的存在过？

更离谱的是，过去要靠大预算、专业团队才做得出的画面，现在越来越小的团队也做得出来。

剧里的高等文明捏出异兽，投放到地球上。现实里，黄仁勋简直就是创世神，卖着显卡，给无数做白日梦的人发创世工具。😂

我们小时候趴在桌上画神兽。下一代的小孩，可能直接就能把它创造出来，跟它说话，带它去冒险。

我们盼了几十年才看见的东西，他们从小就有。等他们开始做白日梦，那个世界又会有多大？

quoted_text:
未来感，一切的基石
未来感很重要，他带领我们去到另外一个层次，如黑夜里的北斗七星，照亮前路，到达成功的彼岸。

例如我们深信比特币会过百万美金，我们才能坚持下去，途中可定会上串下跳，有了roadmap，能看到方向… 坚持下去，是信念，不坚持下去，只需随便一个理由。

其实世间的一切都是未来，股票的估值看未来现金流折算，市场的气氛，影响假设因子，影响股价。如果只看现在，那这股票不性感，只是收租股、看yield的。

做基金的，40多岁才是真正的开始，巴菲特绝大部分钱是50岁后挣得，Bill Ackman 也60多了。没经历波折，经济周期，没法做好周期的判断，和组合管理。

但时间失去了，就真的失去了，没法挽回, Give and take.

text:
A token can attract plenty of trading while the pool funding its ecosystem earns little.

@Uniswap v4 hooks add custom logic to pools, including fees and rewards. But competing pools can bypass those mechanisms.

Cheaper execution benefits traders; lost revenue hurts whoever the hook was designed to fund.

URC-5 tackles that coordination problem. It was created by @standard_rsv Reserve’s devs, @0xbeans.

Think of URC-5 as a machine-readable trading rulebook attached to the token.

Through IVenuePolicy, routers and apps can discover canonical pools, check venue permissions, and distinguish between two modes:

• Preferred
Consider recommended pools while keeping other working routes available.

• Enforced
Compliant routers exclude disallowed routes when the token enters or leaves a venue.

The potential payoff:
Fewer failed transactions and more reliable routing through pools that support a protocol’s economics.

The trade-off:
Restricting venues can reduce competition and limit access to cheaper execution.

There’s an important limit mentioned. Some intermediate trades settle inside shared pool accounting without transferring the token, so token-level transfer restrictions can’t stop those routes. URC-5 relies partly on router cooperation, and declaring a venue “allowed” doesn’t guarantee execution.

URC-5 aims for practicality. Shared rules could make hook-based markets easier to integrate and ensure revenue fee back to protocols.
